the rapporteur. madam president, whom i congratulate on your election, ladies and gentlemen, almost 800 million people are now covered by the cotonou agreement, which, following on from the founding lomé agreement, has guided relations between the european union and the acp countries since 2000. i hope that they will become ever closer and mutually beneficial. the favourable opinion of my rapporteur, for which i ask the house to support me, concerns the first five-yearly review of the agreement, as provided for in article 95 of the agreement. despite the intentionally limited nature of the amendments introduced, since the stability of agreements of this type and size should be given priority, they are overall positive. they aim to improve the effectiveness of the implementation of the lomé/cotonou acquis, which is based primarily on the equality of the parties, respect for human rights, democracy, the rule of law and good governance. while the fall of the berlin wall and the end of the cold war allowed the reference to human rights to be welcomed and in 2000 it was possible to define a deepening of the political dimension of our relations, as well as the prioritisation of the fight against poverty and the improvement of the economic and financial partnership, the 2005 review reinforces the political dialogue aspect by providing for it to be conducted in a more systematic, structured and formal way, thus contributing to preventing and resolving crises. the fight against terrorism also deserves, because of its urgency and timeliness, to be inserted into the body of the agreement, as does the reference to the millennium development goals, linking the common eu-acp commitment to poverty reduction and to improving education and health levels, without which we cannot speak of real development. decentralised local authorities, the prevention of mercenary work, the promotion of traditional knowledge, the prevention of hiv/aids, malaria and tuberculosis and the encouragement of exchanges of young people and students are also part of this review, demonstrating a greater awareness on the part of the signatory parties of the specific problems and aspirations of the peoples of the acp countries. i also want to stress and welcome the fact that for the first time there is an explicit reference to national parliaments as beneficiaries of aid. the development of parliamentary capacity is essential for the good management of public affairs and for full public debate on the development policy choices and priorities of each beneficiary country. many of the countries to which the union sends substantial aid under the cotonou framework enter these funds in their budgets. however, the many complaints that the funds transferred have not always contributed effectively, to the extent necessary and desirable, to the promotion and full implementation of these values are not new. at the same time, there is frequent criticism that the internal application of european funds is often discriminatory and arbitrary, and that the objectivity and impartiality of the public administration are not properly guaranteed. where this happens, the situation is in direct contradiction with the fundamental principles underlying the allocation of funds by the european union, justifying in each case a greater demand on the part of the community institutions, in particular as regards the need for the effective involvement of all political forces and civil society in the beneficiary countries in the discussion and setting of priorities in the use of the aid provided. as i had the opportunity to propose to the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly, which adopted this suggestion in november 2005 at the edinburgh meeting, this national accountability and awareness-raising could take the form of an annual parliamentary debate in each national parliament of the beneficiary countries specifically on external aid. ideally, it should take place some time before the respective annual debates on the national budget. this measure would have the merit of promoting the strengthening of democratic institutions and enhancing better exercise of citizenship. the agreement and its main body thus create a spirit in favour of the crucial systematic involvement of parliaments in the planning, monitoring and evaluation of the impact of cooperation in their respective countries. it is up to us to persist, to promote and support this effort. despite the amendments, of which i have highlighted the most relevant, the acp side, through the minister of foreign affairs of cape verde, considered that further simplification of administrative procedures for access to the european development fund could have been done. i share his concern and i think it is appropriate to echo it here and to ask the council and the commission to consider this in future reviews. in conclusion, i would ask members to support this favourable opinion and i would urge parliament, the council and the commission to do everything possible to maintain and, where possible, increase in future the effort to provide the acp countries with sound and responsible aid.

in writing. this report should be seen in the context of the european union's policy objectives for the railway sector - for which the commission has already presented three legislative packages over the past few years - which is simply to complete the technical/legal framework to achieve, in stages, the total liberalisation of rail transport, i.e. its handing over to large private interests, to the detriment and at the expense of the dismantling of national strategic public undertakings. it is in this context that this proposal for a regulation on rail passengers' rights and obligations arises and should be understood. the report seeks, among other things, to extend the scope of the directive - that is, it does not deal only with the rights and obligations of passengers on international rail services, it includes national ones - it seeks to define the information to be provided to users, the compensation to be granted in the event of delay, accident or death, and to ensure the conditions for the use of this means of transport by persons with reduced mobility. in other words, the current definition of passenger rights is being carried out in the context of a process which calls into question one of their fundamental rights: the right to quality public transport.

in writing. the new partnership agreement with the republic of gabon - which entered into force on 3 december 2005 - is valid for six years and contains a protocol which reduces by 40% the fishing opportunities available to the different member states' fleets operating in these waters, including the portuguese fleet. and, as has been the case with other tuna fisheries agreements, the burden on shipowners is increasing, with shipowners now bearing 35% of the total burden (instead of 25%), obviously with a reduction in the community's contribution. perhaps this is the reason why the possibilities offered by the agreements are not being fully exploited, and why many long-distance fishing vessels are being destroyed, as is happening in portugal. this situation raises questions about the real impact of these agreements, which increase fleet costs and reduce fishing opportunities. it is worrying, particularly in relation to the portuguese fleet, that this agreement implies a breach of the existing proportionality in the distribution of possibilities with other fleets compared to the previous one, i.e. putting relative stability in question. portugal loses 50% of its fishing opportunities for surface longliners, leaving it with only 3 licences compared with 6 under the previous agreement.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report because the fight against obesity must be a political priority for the european union, given that 27% of men and 38% of women in europe are overweight. more worrying is childhood obesity: more than 5 million children (eu-25) are obese and some 300 000 new cases occur annually. it is urgent to reverse this trend. i agree with the general approach proposed: consumer information from childhood; restriction of television advertising; nutrition and health claims on food labelling; greater coherence between the common agricultural policy and health policies.
in writing. we welcome the adoption of this report, which, among other things, includes two key issues: the recognition that the promotion of healthy eating and physical activity should be a political priority of the member states and the european union as a key issue in the fight against obesity, and the recommendation that obesity be officially recognised as a chronic disease. obesity is the most common form of malnutrition, resulting from a disease of excessive fat storage and is associated with debilitating, progressive diseases and with a relative risk of increased mortality relative to the normal population, becoming a growing public health problem. as the report notes, second data for 2006 is that there are now more than 300 million obese people worldwide, a number that has more than doubled in the last 15 years. in addition to supporting the fight against the disease by providing patients with access to health services, medicines, psychological counselling and other services, it is therefore essential to adopt a prevention strategy, which involves promoting healthy eating and lifestyles, particularly affecting women and children, as studies have shown that they are particularly vulnerable to the disease.
in writing. cross-border traffic has increased, as has the number of accidents involving residents in other eu member states. an inquiry into the effects of the existence of different limitation periods and, in particular, the number of cases concerning personal injury of citizens in cross-border areas involving different limitation periods, may help to understand the situation. there are limitation periods ranging from as short as 12 months in some countries to 30 years or more in others, which can lead to injured parties being denied the exercise of their rights to compensation because they have not initiated legal proceedings in accordance with the applicable foreign legislation on limitation. the most vulnerable members of the community, including those who have been most seriously injured or who are otherwise unable to adequately protect their own rights, are at greater risk of their rights being restricted in this way. it may therefore be appropriate to find a practical and fair solution which helps victims and their representatives, but which does not make the cost of insurance unbearable and does not call into question the principle of subsidiarity or the search for countries where the costs for insurers are lower, as could be the case with the application of the principle of the country of origin of the insurers.
in writing. as the rapporteur points out, although it has long been proven that young women and girls are no less capable than men and boys in the field of education, there are a number of reasons that still put them at a disadvantage, particularly in higher education and lifelong learning. in 2004, eight out of ten female students in higher education in the eu member states completed their studies. this rate is higher than that of boys, of whom only three-quarters have completed them, proving that girls are not less motivated or capable than boys when it comes to education. but the proportion of girls who continued their studies or started an academic career is lower. while the ratio of women to men in university education is 59% to 41%, only 43% of those who complete doctorates and only 15% of those who obtain the title of university professor are women. these figures show the marked gender gap in lifelong learning and in the area of women's further education outside the academic sphere, confirming that both phenomena have the same causes, which are rooted in a persistent gender gap, also clearly visible in wage discrimination.
in writing. the historical relationship of some european countries with this region and the ties they maintain with it, whether in political, cultural or economic terms, require the european union as a whole to strengthen these same ties to the mutual benefit of the countries of the region and its member states. the heterogeneity of the region, the dispersion of its population and the specific problems arising from the insular nature of many of its member states require a flexible and balanced approach on the part of a europe which is already one of the main international donors. as a portuguese, i cannot but welcome the calls by the rapporteur for the commission to set up programmes to combat malaria in east timor. i believe, however, that this appeal should be extended to other infectious diseases which are also plaguing that country. i also welcome the call for attention to the specific problems of timor and i support the call for the european commission to support the timorese leaders in their efforts to build a democratic, stable, reconciled, free, prosperous and just society.
mr president, i would like to take this opportunity to congratulate the 'yes' vote in the referendum held yesterday in portugal on the decriminalisation of voluntary termination of pregnancy, carried out by a woman in the first 10 weeks of her pregnancy. this result puts an end to all the false obstacles that have been created up to now, including the holding of the referendum itself, so that the portuguese parliament does not exercise its legitimate legislative competence on this issue. we must now make up for the years and years lost. i would like to thank all the members of the european parliament, particularly those of the group of the european united left - green left, nordic left, who have shown their solidarity over the years with the struggle of portuguese women, many of whom have been unjustly and inhumanely accused in court of practicing abortion. the result achieved yesterday is an important victory for portuguese women and for all those who, like us, have been fighting for decades for the end of clandestine abortion, for the defence of women's health and for a free, conscious and responsible motherhood/fatherhood.
i would also like to congratulate the rapporteurs, mrs jackson and mr blokland, on the work they have done. 49% of eu municipal waste is landfilled. 18% is incinerated and only 33% is recycled or composted. the european environment agency forecasts that paper, glass and plastic waste will increase by around 40% by 2020. in this context, the revision of the waste framework directive should contribute to the reduction of the environmental and socio-economic impacts resulting from waste management by taking into account the whole life cycle of products and materials and giving priority to the protection of human health. the reduction, prevention, reuse and recycling of waste should be given priority. the european commission should take the lead in drawing up a waste prevention action plan which can serve as a source of information for the prevention programmes to be drawn up by the member states. they should take measures to stabilise their waste production by 2012. to this end, it is essential to strengthen the responsibility of producers and importers for waste generated following the placing of their product on the market, in accordance with the polluter-pays principle. the thematic strategy refers to the need to clarify concepts. i have therefore tabled two amendments seeking to clarify the definitions of recovery and disposal of waste, which i hope will be adopted by the european parliament. the european parliament recently adopted reach, which provides for the member states to take the necessary measures to ensure that the collection, production, transport, storage and treatment of hazardous waste are carried out in the best possible conditions for safety and protection of the environment and human health.
mr president, the process of assessing whether turkey is meeting the criteria for accession to the european union requires a frequent assessment of the progress made, particularly in the field of human rights. in this context, the quality of the report by emine bozkurt shows that she has paid great attention to the development of the situation of women in turkey, and for this reason the rapporteur should be congratulated. i would like to highlight some of its recommendations: the incentives for the social partners to promote the participation of women in the social dialogue, the invitation to the turkish authorities to set up a system for monitoring the drop-out of young people from the school system, the proposal for a quota system that works in several countries, from iberia to scandinavia, to ensure the equitable representation of women on electoral lists, the need to instruct judges to punish severely so-called 'honour killings' and forced marriages, the need to carry out a campaign to promote the image of women as agents and economic and social elements and the need to include the social partners and some ngos in the advisory committee on the status of women. the report by mrs emine bozkurt is thus an excellent contribution to the progress of the evaluation of the situation of women in turkey. ladies and gentlemen, i cannot help saying that there can be progress throughout europe on the situation of women. just yesterday in portugal, with the vote of the portuguese women and the portuguese men, the discrimination against voluntary termination of pregnancy was approved in a popular referendum. a great day for portugal! a great day for women's rights!
in writing. it is not our purpose to comment on the validity or otherwise of this decision to repeal directive 68/89/eec, although we generally have reservations about the commission's harmonising approach, which in this case has the majority of companies and member states saying that it does not apply this directive. but it is important to give an opinion on the process in which it is involved - the 'better regulation' initiative - which, in the name of simplification, is in practice moving towards deregulation of markets at national and community level. the commission's justification is clear: "better regulation is crucial to improve the competitiveness of european businesses and to achieve the objectives of the lisbon agenda", cutting "unnecessary costs and obstacles to adaptation and innovation" and putting "the right incentives and basic market conditions in place for businesses to develop". in other words, better regulation is about benefiting businesses and not about protecting the labour, social and environmental rights of consumers. this is what we reject. we do not want to see legislation that jeopardizes the primacy of competition or the profits of companies being withdrawn and the rest being ignored.
in writing. the report raises a number of questions, some of which are even contradictory. priorities are set for waste management, with emphasis on prevention, reuse, recycling and other recovery operations, and for waste disposal. we consider this to be a positive development and hope that the final text will develop towards this position. but on the other hand, some of the positive amendments tabled to the effect that the incineration process should not be regarded as a recovery process and that the use of this method should be virtually void were not adopted, although others, which greatly limit its scope, were adopted, and therefore some contradictions were generated. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. that is why, at this first reading, we have taken stock of the aspects which have improved the commission's original proposal. but the final vote on second reading will depend on the clarification of the existing contradictions.
in writing. the question of waste treatment is of the utmost importance and must be debated with the notion that an ecological excess will result in legislative unrealism and actual impracticability, while a legislative insufficiency will result in environmental neglect and an avoidable legacy for future generations. on the other hand, it is worth being aware that, however good our intentions may be in reducing pollution, the truth is that the increase in living standards - still ongoing in the european union (not to mention the rest of the planet) - will always lead to increased consumption and, inevitably, to increased waste. we must be realistic and above all seek, as suggested here, to obtain a positive return from waste treatment, particularly in terms of energy.
in writing. we know that one of the problems of modern societies is the production of waste. we therefore stress the adoption of this document which highlights the primary objective of waste management, namely the protection of the environment and human health. we also stress the adoption of the so-called 'waste hierarchy', i.e. the establishment of the following priorities for action, with emphasis on prevention first, followed by reuse, recycling, other recovery operations, including, for example, energy recovery, and finally disposal. the increased importance of prevention is intended to reduce the amount of waste generated as much as possible. but we must not forget that, given the enormous quantity of waste produced today, the measures for reuse, recycling or disposal that can be applied are still insufficient and unable to meet the needs. the reduction of waste is therefore an essential issue. but this option implies a change in production and consumption patterns. it also involves actions to educate and raise awareness of the problem among the entire population. the commission has therefore clarified how to bear the costs of waste management, ensuring that these do not fall exclusively or predominantly on the 'weakest link' - consumers. we therefore consider the reference to the application of the 'polluter pays' principle to be dangerous.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by mrs emine bozkurt because it reinforces the need for the turkish government to take measures to allow women to participate more fully in the social, economic and political life of turkey, despite the progress already made. the report shows that there is still a long way to go in protecting turkish women against domestic violence and honour killings and calls on the turkish government to build more shelters for women who are victims of violence.
in writing. in voting in favour of this report we simply wanted to join the defence of the rights of all turkish women, including in the accession negotiations between turkey and the european union, by stressing the need to respect human rights, which include women's rights. but we do not consider that this is the only issue to be taken into account in the negotiations with turkey. our opposition to accession negotiations is well known, as long as turkey maintains its unacceptable occupation of northern cyprus. we therefore disagree with some of the points in that report. as the adopted report states, although the new criminal code, which entered into force in june 2005, has substantially enhanced the fundamental rights of turkish women, the european directives on equality between women and men have not yet been fully transposed. we also regret that in certain parts of south-eastern turkey, girls are not registered at birth, which hinders the fight against forced marriages and honour killings due to the lack of an official identity of the victims. we also join the call to the turkish government to ensure that women from the kurdish minority are equally involved in women's rights programmes.
in this debate on the contribution to the next spring council, where the implementation of the so-called 'lisbon agenda' adopted in 2000 will be assessed, it is important to take account of what has happened in these seven years in relation to the goals and challenges proclaimed at the time, whether in terms of full employment, poverty reduction, childcare infrastructure and equipment and equal opportunities for women, or the so-called most advanced knowledge economy in the world, which would be achieved in 2010. the truth is that since 2000, the european union has been affected by slow economic and employment growth, by an increasing shift of productivity gains from workers to employers and by the corresponding worsening of social inequalities. this is why we have persistently high levels of unemployment, with poverty and social exclusion affecting more than 72 million people, and why we have a proliferation of precarious work with fewer and fewer rights, and why we have more problems with new enlargements without adequate financial responses in the community budgets. this shows that our criticisms of this strategy are more than justified. the implementation of the lisbon agenda has been limited to deepening liberalization and privatisation in a wide variety of sectors, from transport, energy, post and telecommunications to services, putting essential public services at risk, now joined by labour flexibility and the so-called flexicurity, to make it even easier to lay off workers. that is why we are advocating a fundamental change in the policies that are being pursued, whether in the lisbon strategy, the stability pact, the broad economic and employment guidelines or the community budget. in the alternative resolution which our group is tabled for this debate, we therefore consider that priority should be given to a genuine pact for economic progress and social development and to a european strategy for solidarity and sustainable development based on more solidarity on the part of the more developed countries, with a better and wider distribution of community funds, aimed at economic and social cohesion, the improvement of the living conditions of all people, including immigrants, the dignity of workers and the realisation of human rights, particularly in the fields of education, health, housing and social security, without forgetting research and development.
mr president, mr president-in-office of the council, madam commissioner, in the year in which the european union is celebrating the fiftieth anniversary of the treaty of rome, in the year of equal opportunities for all, in the year in which my country, portugal, will hold the presidency of the european union, it is important to mention that the portuguese people voted last sunday in a referendum to decriminalize abortion up to the tenth week of pregnancy. i am justified in stressing the importance of this fact in this parliament and in this context for two additional reasons: firstly, because the decisive victory of 'yes' corresponds to the recommendations adopted by the european parliament for abortion to be legal and safe in all member states and, secondly, because, by happy coincidence, as has already been mentioned by my colleague bernard poignant, the spring council will begin on 8 march. as prime minister josé sócrates said, with this result portugal is taking another firm step towards building a more open, more tolerant and fairer society. in relation to the lisbon strategy, it is also necessary to strengthen the social component in all member states, in particular to allow a better reconciliation between family life and working life for european women and men, for example by creating and developing networks of childcare facilities for children and other dependants, and also affordable and of good quality. we need more and better jobs for women too, equal pay for equal work and we believe that without the participation of women the ambitious objectives of the lisbon strategy cannot be achieved.
mr president, mr president-in-office, today is the time to say that, thanks to the 2004 reform, the lisbon strategy is no longer limited to a set of unattainable targets - the priorities are clearer, the responsibilities are more defined. in this speech i want to talk about social policy in the context of the lisbon strategy. firstly, it is very clear that the lisbon strategy is not, as some people want to suggest, a liberal attempt that could threaten the foundations and values of the european social model. on the contrary, the lisbon strategy represents a vision which, while clearly reformist, seeks to preserve the values which underpin the european social model. the lisbon strategy therefore sets out a political orientation on the need to modernise social protection systems, a necessary response to what is happening in europe and the world. as a general guideline, it is well stated that social policies should not be seen as a burden but rather as a factor capable of positively influencing economic growth, not only by increasing productivity and competitiveness but also by providing higher levels of social cohesion and access to fundamental rights, thus becoming an important instrument for ensuring social peace and political stability, without which there is no lasting economic progress. because of the 2004 reform, i am now more optimistic than in the past about the implementation of the lisbon strategy. the european union has entered a phase of economic acceleration and can grow more than the united states of america. investment in the first half of 2006 alone grew by 6%; the growth in exports is expected to exceed 5%; the unemployment rate is falling and has already reached 1998 levels. 2006 was the best year of the decade and the outlook for 2007 is very positive. these values confirm, on the ground, the intended objectives of the lisbon strategy - a combined effect of sustained economic growth creating more and better jobs, a continuous improvement in the living standards of the citizens of the european union without loss of competitiveness and respect for the values of the european social model. i therefore congratulate josé manuel durão barroso and the commission on the reform they have decided to introduce in the lisbon strategy at the right time.

question no 45 by mr georgios toussas (h-1085/06) subject: the situation in the former yugoslavia subject: banking abuses the generally anti-people policy of the eu and the governments of the member states has given audacity to the illegal usurious practices of the banks which abuse huge sums from borrowers and workers in general. characteristically, the bank of greece has imposed fines of eur 25 million on credit institutions for opaque/abusive practices, but at the same time has relaxed the penalties in force for uncovered cheques and refuses to reveal the names of the banks that have been sanctioned. what is the commission's position on the publication in the media of the names of banks sanctioned by the supervisory authorities of the member states for illegal abusive practices in order to at least inform and partly protect borrowers and depositors in general?
member of the commission. as i said in my reply, we are aware of the concerns about the level of interest rates charged in greece and have responded to several written questions on this subject. but the definition of retail interest rates is mainly a matter for financial institutions and it is not as such the subject of eu rules and regulations. however, as explained in earlier responses, we have undertaken a series of initiatives that could have an impact on the level of retail interest rates in europe, including initiatives on mortgage credit and consumer credit. in june 2005 we also launched sector-specific competition inquiries in the areas of business insurance and retail banking. yes, it is known to us that the level of interest rates charged in greece are very high, but we do not have particular responsibility to make any change in that, nor is it likely that the union will have responsibility in this area in the future. in other member states where the winds of competition have blown, the interest rate charged to consumers has come down dramatically. i have personal experience in this regard from my home member state. when a retail financial institution from another member state announced that it was coming to set up shop in the member state i know best, interest rates contracted overnight.

question no 46 by mrs sarah ludford (h-0007/07) subject: the situation in the former yugoslavia subject: laundering of money the london county council has recently made a credible case that the european union's fight against money laundering - and thus potential terrorist financing - in the form of an effective deterrence and detection regime for criminal practices is being hampered by the inconsistent, uneven and inadequate application of the 2001 second money laundering directive by member states. with the implementation of the third anti-money laundering directive due in 2007, what is the commission's strategy to ensure a rapid, appropriate and uniform implementation of eu legislation on this essential matter in all member states, making the most of the possibilities to detect suspicious transactions and minimising unnecessary costs and red tape for honest customers and businesses?
member of the commission. as you are aware, member states are required to have fully transposed the third anti-money-laundering directive into national law by 15 december 2007 at the latest. this directive reinforces our actions in the fight against terrorist financing. it provides for harmonised rules under which the obliged entities and persons can apply customer due diligence procedures, taking into account the risk of money laundering and terrorist financing. in order to help member states ensure a timely and proper transposition of this directive, we are following a threefold strategy. firstly, in november 2006 we held an initial transposition workshop. the objective of this meeting was to exchange views and provide clarity on issues of interpretation or any other problem linked to transposition. secondly, we have set up a european platform between the financial intelligence units. these are the national authorities competent to prevent and counter money-laundering and terrorist financing by receiving and analysing suspicious transaction reports filed by credit and financial institutions, as well as by selected non-financial businesses and professions. the fius are directly involved in the enforcement of the directive. within the european platform, regular meetings are organised to exchange information, notably on the provision of feedback to reporting entities. thirdly, we support the work carried out by the joint anti-money-laundering task force which the committee of european banking supervisors has created in association with the european insurance supervisors and the securities markets supervisors. the objective of this task force is to enable the sharing of experience and best practices between financial services supervisors. this is crucial for a consistent implementation of the directive across the european union. the commission participates as an observer.
member of the commission. i think that what the honourable member says is quite reasonable. from my knowledge of previous directives, practice varies from member state to member state. furthermore, within member states, it probably varies between financial institutions – i am aware of that too, but you must remember it is quite early days. i know that we are now on the third anti-money-laundering directive, but people are learning and, hopefully, with the processes we have set up, such as the bodies i have just referred to, best practices can be established and then people can learn from one another. i would not rule out making some guidelines in the future, as the honourable member referred to. perhaps that will be done in the future, either by the commission or some agency on our behalf through all these processes. however, as the honourable member will understand, we have gone for the risk-based approach, which leaves a fair degree of flexibility in the hands of the entities, and that leads to some of the problems we have just outlined. on the other hand, if you went for the more prescriptive approach, line by line, it would probably take ages to get agreement between the different member states because of the different cultures in this particular area. hopefully, we are learning, and i do not rule out any future initiative that would bring greater consistency in this area, which is what, i believe, everybody desires.
questions 47 and 48 will be answered in writing.
question no 49 by mr carl schlyter (h-1081/06) subject: the situation in the former yugoslavia subject: prohibition of raw materials obtained in violation of international law for more than 30 years, the dineh and hopi indians of black mesa, new york, have been fighting against coal mining on their land and the consequences of it. earlier this year, the coal mine and the pipeline that used the indians' only water supply was shut down. unfortunately, the joy was short-lived, as there are plans for a reopening and enlargement of the mine, with subsequent forced relocations. black mesa mountain is sacred to those people and it would be like letting a company mine stones from notre dame de paris (the mountain is considered a woman). will not the demolition of sacred symbols of a religion constitute a violation of religious freedom? does the commission intend to prohibit the import of raw materials obtained in violation of international law and, consequently, to prohibit the import of products of the companies concerned if they enlarge their holdings?
member of the commission. i should like to thank the honourable member for asking this question. the european union seeks to uphold the universality and indivisibility of human rights – civil, political, economic, social and cultural – as reaffirmed by the 1993 world conference on human rights in vienna. the commission understands that the dineh and hopi indians would like to preserve their identity by controlling mining activities on their territory. while the commission is not convinced that the functioning of the coal plant would breach any relevant instruments of international law protecting religious freedom, it nonetheless takes the rights of indigenous peoples very seriously, as set out in the commission’s may 1998 working document on indigenous peoples. however, the production of coal in the united states is subject to environmental rules, and the overall issue of rights in this instance falls within the competence of the us government. on the more general issue of whether import bans of coal would be effective in upholding the rights of people in specific localities, it would be difficult to determine the specific origin of coal being imported into the european union. consequently, a ban of this sort would be difficult to implement in practice.
member of the commission. mr president, the commission understands very well that the region where the dineh and hopi indians live is very important for their religious beliefs, and i do not contend otherwise. we also understand that their rights are protected in the us constitution, and so it is principally a matter for the us courts and not for us to intervene. i would just repeat what i said, that import bans of the sort being envisaged are really not a desirable way, in the commission’s view, of dealing with such issues. an import ban would have no effect if the coal in question were exported to countries other than the european union, which would no doubt be the case, so any sanction that we introduced would, in our view, make no material difference to the objective situation of these indigenous peoples.
question 50 is therefore adjourned, since its author is not present.
since they concern the same subject, the following questions will be referred together. question no 51 by mr brian crowley, substituted by mr sean ó neachtain (h-0030/07) subject: negotiations on world trade can the european commission make a statement on the likelihood of the doha round of world trade negotiations being seriously resumed in the near future? question no 52 by mr pedro guerreiro (h-0069/07) subject: the european parliament's proposal to establish a european union agency for fundamental rights (fra) is not yet adopted. subject: negotiations within the wto. whereas several un reports have denounced the increase in income inequalities, in social and economic terms, between and within countries over the past few years, in a context where poverty and unemployment rates remain high or are increasing, while the profits of large transnational corporations are rising and wealth is being concentrated - a reality which is of course not unconnected with the sharp increase in trade and capital liberalization on a world scale; in view of the recent contacts between the eu council presidency, the european commission and the us administration, i ask the commission what proposals and timetable it is putting forward for the wto negotiations, which are currently at an impasse, particularly on agriculture, non-agricultural products (including textiles and clothing) and services.
member of the commission. mr president, i want to give this house a substantive assessment of where things stand on the world trade talks. the davos meeting of wto trade ministers in january signalled the formal resumption of work in geneva across all the negotiating groups. what lay behind this was an injection of new political commitment to the negotiations at senior levels, including from president bush. i believe this is sincere and that there is, therefore, a new level of political investment in the process, which creates a fresh opportunity for finding success. on this basis, the director-general of the wto announced in the trade negotiating committee on 31 january that negotiations in geneva should restart at multilateral level in all the negotiating groups. farm subsidies remain the gateway to a deal. but a breakthrough inside agriculture must trigger a meaningful commitment to reductions in industrial tariffs and, further down the line, specific market-opening commitments in trade in services. in these areas, we are looking for meaningful and substantial moves by emerging economies in the g-20 group, without which it will not be possible to conclude the round. in the meantime, us negotiators have started to turn the corner, but they have not reached the point of showing to us what new reduction of trade-distorting farm subsidies they intend to table. this is indispensable to the progress we are seeking. susan schwab, the us trade representative, is reaching out to the democratic congressional leadership in order to prepare the ground and to see how she can meet some of their requirements for an extension of the administration’s fast-track negotiating authority, the trade promotion authority, but she has not, so far, been ready to make the necessary jump either to agreement with congress, or convergence with the us trade partners on key aspects of the current negotiation. the administration’s preliminary proposal last week for a new farm bill was welcome but somewhat disappointing in this context. if we are to have a successful outcome in the wto, the us will need to align the new farm bill with more ambitious cuts and disciplines in trade-distorting subsidies negotiated as part of the doha round. on timing, however, the us roadmap is somewhat clearer. a breakthrough on core issues in the doha development agenda is the platform on which the bush administration says it will request a new or extended tpa before its expiry in june. that implies a breakthrough in the next few months on the big numbers in the key in writing. this regulation aims to clarify the fishing gear which can be considered to be driftnets by harmonising a common definition for all the relevant regulations. drifting nets have a strong impact on fisheries resources and marine ecosystems, as well as economic impacts (competitive and income reduction) on fishermen using other gear, including artisanal gear. the european union has incorporated into its acquis (regulation no 354/1992) un resolution 44/225 on the implementation of a moratorium on the use of driftnets (although it contains some regional exceptions at community level). we have therefore supported the content of this report as a way of improving the control and reducing the impact of these gears in national waters, particularly in the exclusive economic zones of the azores and madeira, as these are frequented by fleets from other member states which use these gears for targeted fishing for tuna and other marine species, either through regulatory omissions or illegally.

in writing. as we have said before, the central point is that the commission's proposal is not a proposal for genuine modulation, i.e. a proposal to increase aid to those who receive the least or receive nothing, by reducing support to those who receive a lot, in order to ensure greater equity in the distribution of aid between producers, countries and products and to support small and mediumsized farmers and family farming. we are in favour of the commission putting forward a new proposal to create a genuine, compulsory modulation, making it more equitable and freeing up financial resources, introducing a ceiling on aid per holding (cap) and a percentage increase in aid for farmers who receive less aid from the cap (modulation), such as proposing a 15% or 20% increase for small and mediumsized farmers who receive less than € 5 000 in aid and, even from this value, taking into account various situations. without this, we risk widening existing inequalities. we therefore insist that the commission should reformulate its proposal to prevent a decision in this area from justifying the renationalisation of the cap's costs. but so far the commission has not done so. that is why we abstained.
in writing. the european parliament had already rejected the commission's proposal for a voluntary modulation of direct payments under the cap of up to 20%. the proposal would have the effect of using the money for farmers in the second pillar of the cap - rural development - i.e. it would be transferred to the national budgets of the member states which decided to apply this modulation. the abolition of support to farmers would raise competition issues between farmers in countries that would not apply modulation and farmers in countries that did, and also between them, depending on the level of modulation chosen. i therefore agree with the rapporteur, mr goepel, that the commission proposal should be rejected again.

the report by mrs marie-hélène aubert, on behalf of the committee on fisheries, on the implementation of the european union action plan against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing (2006/2225 (ini)) (a6-0015/2007) follows.
your protest will be noted.
i would also like to congratulate the rapporteur on her work. large-scale illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing has contributed significantly to the difficulties faced by the fisheries sector. large-scale illegal fishing not only affects marine ecosystems and fisheries costs, but also reduces the income of fishermen who fish legally and comply with the rules, in particular in the field of conservation of fisheries resources. large-scale illegal fishing, as the report states, is undermining the income of fisheries-dependent populations in different countries, with the worst consequences for those who have the least means to control their exclusive economic zones. large-scale illegal fishing also contributes to the deterioration of working and hygienic conditions on board vessels and the labour rights of crews. in this connection, we believe that illegal fishing, which generates substantial illicit profits for large-scale fleets, for financial groups linked to fishing and even for organized crime networks, should not be confused with the infringement of the common policy of fishing for small-scale and artisanal fleet segments, which is often carried out because of the economic crisis they are facing. it is worrying that despite the fao 2002 plan and its rapid transposition into the community acquis, with the consequent implementation, large-scale illegal fishing continues to increase due to gaps or inaccuracies in the existing rules. the fight against illegal fishing is hampered by the use of flags of convenience, failures in controls at sea, transhipments on the high seas, lack of controls in ports and lack of cooperation and coordination between relevant authorities. given that illegal fishing has its greatest impact on fleet segments operating on the high seas and on continental shelves, in particular in economically less developed countries, cooperation between states and between international fisheries organisations in combating this type of fishing is vital by providing the necessary means, including financial, for the implementation of the necessary measures such as effective control of fishing activities. the reinforcement of deterrent measures must be accompanied by improvements in the traceability of fishery products, as has already been stressed, and eco-labelling is relevant here. it is also important, as the report states, to strengthen port state controls on landings and transhipments of third country vessels. we believe that the existing measures already cover the main issues, but that they now need to be implemented more rigorously and fairly and that there needs to be greater international coordination. the question is not simply whether to introduce more and more restrictive measures for the fishing industry, particularly if their impact or unilateral nature has the perverse effect of further benefiting vessels operating illegally. vessels from third countries operating in the exclusive economic zones of the member states should be subject to the rules of the common fisheries policy and existing national requirements. it is obvious that it is always possible to improve existing rules and to supplement them where they are omitted or incomplete. in this respect, we consider this report to be an important contribution which, with one or other reservation, deserves our general agreement. however, we consider it to be at least premature to place the fight against illegal fishing within the framework of a future maritime policy for the european union, which we are only now beginning to discuss in the framework of the green paper presented by the commission. we agree with greater international cooperation and coordination and at the level of the european union, but we must avoid centralizing situations and safeguard the exclusive powers of control of the member states, which are the ones who know each of their exclusive economic zones best.
madam president, commissioner, chairman of the committee on fisheries, we must all join in congratulating our rapporteur, who has done an excellent job, and we must all start by saying that the situation we are in today is absolutely unacceptable. we cannot tolerate that, for example, in the case of bluefin tuna, which is the most studied fish from this point of view, the quantity of illegal, unreported and unregulated fish exceeds by 50% the quantity of those that are legally traded. this leads to a total degradation of resources and also to a degradation of the value at which fish is sold and thus to the ruin of fishermen. this is a situation which the community cannot tolerate any longer. of all the measures that have been suggested here as a way of tackling the problem, i would like to highlight, in fact, traceability as the essential key to success. that is the measure we have to ensure is adopted in the very short term and if it is done rigorously i am sure we will have a very different situation shortly.

the rapporteur. i would first like to thank all the members of the committee on economic and monetary affairs and the rapporteurs for the opinions of the various committees which have delivered opinions on this report, for their support and for the quality of their contributions. i also thank commissioner almunia for the encouragement he has given me on several occasions. we have recently heard the president of the commission say in parliament that europe cannot have the audacity to speak with one voice to the world on energy policy when it is absolutely incapable of speaking with 27 voices at home. this is probably also the most important message that is conveyed with the report under consideration and this message has a certain addressee: the european council and the member states and an appropriate date to be received, the spring summit to be held in brussels on 8 and 9 march. it is therefore time to move from mere declarations of intent to the pursuit of facts and this change of attitude must take place now or it will never take place. this is certainly not the best time to make a demanding analysis of the nature, causes and consequences of the various energy shocks. the report has a lot to say on these matters, and even if it did not, we would all be able to distinguish the distinguishing features of each of the four oil shocks that the european economy has experienced over the last fifty years. it is clear that from the point of view of the new economic paradigm, which we can call 'globalization', and from the political/strategic point of view, which we can call 'lack of multilateralism', we are in a completely different situation today from that which existed in the middle of the last century. but it is precisely for this reason that we must have the intelligence and the humility to recognize that different problems always require different solutions and that the most complex problems require the most ambitious and radical solutions. it is undeniable that the turbulence on energy markets and the volatility of prices have resulted in a slower rate of economic growth and a higher rate of price increases, and it is unthinkable that these disadvantages have not been enhanced by strong speculative movements in the price of raw materials in the energy sector. it is clear that strong integrated economic areas, such as the european union, can, fortunately, absorb shocks in the short term and pursue their most important objectives through the appropriate use of economic policies. but it is also true that the loss of growth and competitiveness inevitably and always results in a lack of job creation, and it is equally true that the jobs that are not created today will never be recovered by the jobs that we will eventually create tomorrow. the european union is made up of member states with different growth rates and production structures, which correspond to very different levels of dependency, and the difficulties experienced by some of these member states will always have to be added to the overall difficulties experienced and paid for by the entire economic and political area in which they are integrated. the commission has warned us of a reality that will inevitably arise if immediate action is not taken: the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment is a very good one, and i would like to thank the rapporteur for the work he has done. the energy question is therefore a nuclear question for the future of europe and is above all a political question which requires answers and commitments at this level and with this dimension. even the most technical issues, such as the discovery and development of new alternatives or the creation of articulated regulatory systems, can only be successfully tackled if they are addressed with a supranational dimension, otherwise it is not possible to mobilise the enormous financial resources that are needed for research and development. it is therefore suggested that the union, through its institutions, engage in a comprehensive and mobilizing debate with economic operators, representative organisations in the sector and citizens on this matter and then proceed to assess the real impact of the use of the different energy sources and their possible combinations on economic growth, environmental protection and the reduction of the negative impacts on climate change. at this stage, as recent events have shown, the member states are not individually in a position to respond to these problems. a genuine common european energy policy is needed, as suggested by the commission, but this depends only on the explicit will of the european council. the european union is, as we know, dangerously dependent on the energy it imports, but moreover, it does not even have the security of the energy it needs to pursue its objectives of growth and the well-being of its citizens. much can be done within the european area by saving, by improving efficiency and diversifying sources or by protecting the environment. but the essential can only be achieved through dialogue with all the other regions of the world, whether they are predominantly energy producers or those which are progressively continuing to consume the same energy. the diplomacy of this new century, as far as the european union is concerned, must give priority to the energy dimension and, to be successful, must be based on three essential elements: solidarity with the european union and its structural principles and values, solidarity with developing countries and solidarity with the environmental dimension of the world in which we live and without which we cannot survive. the european parliament, by adopting this report, as it has done on other occasions, is demonstrating its willingness and fulfilling its duty to intervene in a matter which is essential to the well-being of citizens despite all the difficulties. we hope that the spring summit of heads of state and government will be a moment of progress and progress and not just pious declarations which do not solve any of the present problems and only serve to create and strengthen future problems.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report because i consider it to be an excellent piece of work by the rapporteur on a subject of extreme importance, relevance and timeliness. measures are needed to reverse the current trend of increasing import dependence of europe's energy supply, including through incentives for investment in renewable energy, which would allow the objectives of the kyoto protocol to be achieved. it is urgent to define a global strategy to reduce energy consumption, especially in the transport sector, which accounts for 56% of oil consumption in europe.
in writing. the sharp rise in oil prices, which have reached peaks of around usd 80 per barrel, is structural and permanent. unlike the oil shocks of the 1970s, caused by a supply-side breakdown, the current "shock" is the result of a sharp increase in demand from developing countries such as china or india, and also from the world's largest consumer, the usa, which is coupled with the forecast of shortages of this "finite" resource in the medium term. living with high oil prices exacerbates recessionary effects and imbalances in the balance of payments, aggravates production costs, inflation and interest rates, as well as penalizes low-income households and provokes wars for control of oil, as in iraq. whether technological solutions can contribute to increasing energy efficiency, to the emergence of new types of fuel and new forms of energy, the central question is the change in the capitalist mode of production which causes waste and inefficiency. the answer must be to reduce the energy intensity of gdp, to promote quality public rail transport and to promote production for local markets. the rapporteur has certainly made some positive proposals, but we cannot agree to the creation of an internal energy market and its liberalisation.
in writing. the report stresses the impact of the increase in oil prices on the transport sector, which accounts for 56% of total oil consumption, but it is regrettable that it does not refer to other sectors, such as fisheries. the fuel price increases have affected the fisheries sector particularly negatively, aggravating its socio-economic crisis, in particular its operating margins and economic viability. between 2004 and 2006 alone, fuel prices increased by almost 100%, and in some segments of the sector they represented almost 50% of total operating costs. fishermen have seen their incomes fall, a situation made all the more serious by the fact that the sector's activity is concentrated mainly in regions with a weak economy. several studies point to the risk of thousands of fishing businesses and thousands of jobs being lost due to the increase in fuel prices. this is why urgent and extraordinary measures are needed to support the sector, in particular the creation of a guarantee fund, shared at community level, to guarantee the stability of fuel prices. pending that decision, it is urgent to grant transitional compensatory compensation to the fisheries undertakings concerned.

the rapporteur. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, it has been an honour and a great responsibility for me to draw up the report on social services of general interest. i have tried to draw up an initial report which would express both the lines of my analysis and the proposals on the subject, and which would not only have the agreement of the parliamentary group of which i am a member, but would also be able to guarantee a wider agreement by its structure, style and design. this agreement was aimed not only at the debate in the committee on employment and social affairs but also at the european parliament's own plenary session. it also wanted to secure the support of the majority of the european council and the european commission itself. i would also like to see the majority of the social organisations which have helped me so much in the preparation of this report see it as a useful instrument for legal clarification in the social sector and a way of giving a new visibility and a new impetus to social services of general interest at european level. in november i wrote that this explanatory statement and the report presented were intended to contribute to strengthening the social dimension of the process of european integration by ensuring the necessary legal certainty for the social sectors and public authorities, financial transparency, the necessary compatibility with the rules applicable in the internal market, and the improvement of the quality of the services provided, in compliance with the principle of subsidiarity, taking into account the need to implement the lisbon strategy in the social field. the latter therefore requires significant parliamentary support for this report and requires the involvement of the social organisations of europe and the union and relevant support in the european commission, the european council and the various member states. the report which is before you today for your vote refers to a multitude of important aspects for proper work in the field of social services of general interest. they allow me to underline the following: social services of general interest are an appropriate means of strengthening the social dimension of the lisbon strategy, achieving the objectives of the social agenda and addressing challenges such as globalisation, industrial change, technological progress, demographic change, migration or changing social and working models, thus contributing to the development of a social europe. in the report, the european parliament calls on the commission and the member states to respect the diversity of the ways in which social and general interest services are organised and managed, and the resources and methods of financing these services. the european parliament also notes that in some member states the decentralisation of powers to regional or local authorities for the provision of social services of general interest has not been accompanied by sufficient budgetary resources to allow for an optimal quantitative and qualitative level of service provision. the european parliament therefore urges the member states to ensure that any transfer of powers to regional or local authorities for the provision of social services of general interest is accompanied by adequate budgetary resources. the report also recommends that a forum be convened, at the instigation of the european parliament, bringing together european social organisations, representatives of the european commission and the european council, so that this forum can monitor the conduct of this process. ladies and gentlemen, with your support this process will move forward towards the strengthening of the european union and the social dimension of europe. i believe that we have the political conditions to involve the european commission, the european council and the social organisations, as well as the member states, in this process and to have the participation of companies, trade unions and the social partners in the most useful and appropriate way. with our full commitment, the necessary steps will certainly be taken to clarify the legal status of social services of general interest, and i believe that this parliament should pass this matter shortly. i am convinced that from this week we can move forward to a new stage towards clarifying the role of social services of general interest and strengthening the social dimension of the european union.
mr president, i would first of all like to support the report by mr hasse ferreira, whom i congratulate on his work. social services of general interest are today an important instrument that can contribute to greater economic, social and territorial cohesion and can be seen as a decisive lever to achieve the objectives set out in the lisbon strategy. such services play a key role in responding to certain social needs which the market is not always able to satisfy. these services have particular characteristics in terms of target audience, management, organisation and financing which are different from those of traditional services. social services of general interest have been gaining momentum as they face new challenges and have been changing the european social landscape, with the result that social services of general interest are now being forced to adapt to a much more demanding reality. there are cases of social services of general interest which can be seen as a good example of flexible labour market management, which should be followed up as there are cases of very successful experiences. as these are services close to the user, i understand that regional and local authorities, in collaboration with civil society, can take on tasks in the context of the provision of social services of general interest. i am convinced that these services are best placed to act at local level. and in this respect, regardless of the adoption of best practices and the healthy exchange of experience between member states, i believe that the different cultural patterns that exist in the european union should be respected and the development of social services of general interest should be structured and developed in accordance with the specific characteristics of each community. i therefore share the view that, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, the diversity of the models of organisation, management and financing of social services in the member states should be respected.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place on tuesday at 12 noon.
the report by richard howitt, on behalf of the committee on employment and social affairs, on corporate social responsibility: a new partnership (2006/2133 (ini)) (a6-0471/2006) follows.
mr president, the main function of companies is to create wealth, but a company can, under certain circumstances, be more than a kind of mechanical structure capable of simply creating value. a company can also be seen as a community where people live and interact, making the company the place of professional achievement and often even personal happiness. the successful companies, the ones that are able to create wealth, are the ones that typically have a good level of relationship with their employees, customers, suppliers and the community in which they operate. successful companies are those which adopt criteria of transparency in their relations with the authorities and guide their actions on the basis of codes of conduct and ethics, in some cases with a very high level of demand. when the life of a company is prolonged over time, it can be compared to living beings, and in this case we can find cases of companies which develop their activities on the basis of a strong personality inherent in a culture which they have been able to create and develop and which identifies and distinguishes them from the rest. you could say they're companies with emotions and feelings. in this case, these companies decide to devote to the community some effort which goes beyond their traditional functions and therefore take on an added responsibility which we can call 'social responsibility'. but i understand that corporate social responsibility cannot be decreed or imposed. the social responsibility of a company must be the result of a will voluntarily assumed. corporate social responsibility can never be imposed. if so, there is a serious risk that its role will be reduced to that of a public relations tool designed to obfuscate or obstruct the responsibility of companies for social and environmental problems. in this case, corporate social responsibility would be a fraud because it would not be authentic. i support the report because in its final version my view of the problem was finally taken into account.
madam president, we know how far we have come in the fight for equal rights and equal opportunities. for portuguese women, there was an important positive event on march 8th this year: the law on the decriminalization of voluntary termination of pregnancy, if carried out by the woman's choice in the first 10 weeks of pregnancy in a legally authorized health facility, was finally passed. but there are still many inequalities between women and men, whether in the social sphere, particularly in access to work, professional promotions and pay, or in political life and family life itself. the commission must not confine itself to a statement of general principles in the area of equality, which will always be called into question as long as liberal policies are pursued with the liberalizations and privatizations contained in the so-called lisbon strategy, to which flexicurity is now added to facilitate unjustified dismissals. this will continue the discrimination against women. maternity and paternity, which are fundamental social values, must be protected by the state, which must take the necessary measures to eradicate discriminatory behaviour within companies, as is still the case in portugal. and so, as happened on 2 march in lisbon, women will continue to fight for more jobs with rights, against the closure of maternity hospitals, for more day nurseries and kindergartens. they must be answered positively.

and mavrommatis must be applauded. the freedom of choice of authors and composers by the collective management society as to what they intend to be represented by it is as fundamental a principle as in writing. the main objective of this proposal to amend several directives as regards procedural rules and prudential assessment criteria for acquisitions is to promote crossborder mergers and acquisitions (m&a) in the banking and financial sector, i.e. to promote the concentration and centralisation of capital at european level by improving the penetration capacity of foreign capital and the integration of financial markets. thus, prudential assessment is seen as a barrier to cross-border m&a, following a commission study presented in november 2005 on the barriers to consolidation of the financial sector in the internal market. the proposal, in addition to maximum harmonisation, among other technical details, aims to create shorter time limits for the prudential assessment by the national competent authorities and banking supervisory authorities, i.e. to reduce the current 65 days to 30 days. the compromise proposal, which is an extension of the commission proposal, allows for the existing deadline to be reduced. we voted against all of this.
in writing. what is happening in most european union countries at the moment, with the proliferation of precarious and low-paid work, with the exploitation of migrant workers, whether from third countries or from the european union itself, as has happened to portuguese workers in the netherlands and spain, for example, and now in the united kingdom, shows that the social responsibility that companies assume is becoming less and less. the fact that multinationals, even when they have significant productivity levels, relocate so many times because they only want to make more and more profits and show a complete lack of concern for the thousands of unemployed they cause is proof that most large companies do not practice any social responsibility. it is symptomatic that they have rejected the proposals we have tabled for the plenary, which stress the incongruence between the objectives assigned to csr and the policies put forward by the commission on employment, in particular flexicurity, to liberalize unfair dismissals, support the proliferation of precarious work and devalue collective bargaining and employment with rights. so despite the positive proposals in the report, until there is political will and real monitoring of labour law and ilo standards, little will change in practice.
in writing. in a perfect market, both the economic performance and the social or environmental impact of a company would be taken into account in determining its value and public image. in a perfect market, consumers would choose the products that best serve them directly, while also serving their other interests best indirectly. obviously, there is no such market. some, in the wake of an ever-intervening understanding, will therefore advocate more regulation and more legislation. that's not the path i'm advocating. even though i know that the market is not, and will not be, perfect, i prefer its mechanisms and the solutions that stimulate them. in this sense, i believe that interventions that promote and disseminate good practice and, above all, that foster a culture of demanding consumer demands together are preferable. the question of competitiveness remains. the idea that there is always an opposition between profit, or simple economic viability, and the environment, employment, social responsibility, does not convince me. profit is not a bad thing, it is a good thing, provided it is obtained in accordance with rules, particularly those laid down in the market, which result from increased consumer demand. these are the ones we should encourage.
in writing. the vote in plenary rejected all the proposals we had put forward to clarify the causes of the discrimination which still persists, of which i would highlight: - insisting on the need to change the economic policies of the european union so that all women, men and children can live in dignity and without the threat of poverty; - to stress the importance of establishing community indicators on childcare facilities and on the gender pay and other income gap by sector, including atypical and parttime work; - stresses the need to work towards mainstreaming the gender perspective in the economic guidelines, including in the accession process, in order to avoid the negative effects on gender equality of the processes of privatisation, liberalisation and cuts in public expenditure in the social sectors, and reaffirms that quality public services are essential, calling for increased budgetary resources in social areas to prevent social exclusion and combat trafficking in women; - fears that policies focused on increasing the eu's competitiveness may harm the interests of women in other regions of the world. hence our final abstention vote.

member of the commission. mr president, before going into the details of the report, i would like to thank the rapporteur mrs bourzai and the committee on agriculture and rural development for their very good work carried out on this fairly sensitive issue, namely the marketing of bovine meat at an age lower than 12 months. the report is a response to the request made by the council in the middle of 2004 towards a harmonisation of the definition of veal within the european community. it follows a lengthy consultation process involving different stakeholders and member state experts, during which the commission has demonstrated its readiness to take into account, to the greatest extent possible, traditions and habits in different member states. the commission has also considered the main feature of the consumption and the production of veal within the european union. it allows the main problems as regards the marketing of the meat of these young animals to be addressed, and i think it offers a balanced response to most of the concerns that have been raised. for the first time, it is now possible to reach an agreement on this difficult issue. many of the amendments that have been proposed or introduced aim to simplify the commission proposal in order to try to cut red tape, to reduce the administrative burdens and the cost as much as possible, and in principle these amendments should not raise any problems. i am looking forward to listening to the discussion, and hopefully we can find a solution.
the commission's proposal is a good one, but it is not enough to say that the commission is not prepared to accept the proposal. the establishment of precise sales descriptions according to the age of the slaughter, which is a criterion easier to control than the feed, to be used by all member states, will facilitate consumer understanding and avoid possible distortions of competition. it is particularly important that the designation 'veal' and others defined in the commission proposal cannot be used for the labelling of meat from animals over 12 months of age. another aspect which i consider essential is the subjecting of meat imported from third countries to the provisions of the proposed regulation, which will make it possible to avoid any risk of distortion of competition. i share the view of the rapporteur, mrs bourzai, whom i congratulate on her excellent work and the dialogue she has initiated, that this is a good proposal from the commission and that the matter deserved a solution long ago. we also both feel that the letters discussed by the commission for the identification of carcasses are not the most appropriate, as they can give rise to confusion about the sex of the animal. this and other aspects of the proposal for a regulation have been improved by amendments adopted by the committee on agriculture and set out in the report under consideration in this house. i should like to say that any reservations that may exist about certain traditions, which raise doubts about the new provisions, should not be taken to the extent of calling into question the work done by the commission and the european parliament. finally, i would remind members that the designations proposed by the commission were obtained after consultation with organisations in the various member states, as the commissioner has already pointed out, and that the proposal for a regulation provides for the possibility of amending the list of designations in annex ii in the future.
