in writing. the evolution of community migration and asylum policies and legislation requires statistical information of a much higher quality than currently exists. i therefore support this initiative which follows on from the thessaloniki european council in 2003, which recognised the need to create more effective mechanisms for collecting and analysing information on migration and asylum in the european union. i welcome the report by mrs klamt which seeks to create a common framework for the collection and compilation of community statistics in this area, which should enable the member states to make the best use of the data available for the production of statistics which correspond as far as possible to harmonised definitions. it should thus improve the exchange of statistics and enable common analysis to be carried out in order to develop fair and effective community policies on migration and the free movement of persons.
in writing. the civil aviation responsibilities of each member state have been gradually transferred to the 'community'. the proposed amendment to regulation (ec) no 1592/2002 is another step in this direction. such a process of transferring and alienating powers is all the more negative when it is carried out in a framework in which its limits are not clearly defined. in this case, the european aviation safety agency (easa) would also be responsible for the certification of aircraft and pilots, which is currently the responsibility of each national authority. the national authorities currently comply with and enforce the applicable civil aviation requirements resulting from international agreements. cooperation between member states and third countries is already a reality and could even be further encouraged and developed, but with due regard for the sovereignty of each country, workers and their rights (ensuring social harmonization by applying the most favourable conditions) and the rights of users. in essence, this initiative is another step towards the actual implementation of the so-called 'single european sky', which we oppose. the negotiating process on the amendment of this regulation is now under way and we will continue to monitor this matter, always safeguarding national sovereignty.
in writing. the adoption of this report is an important step towards ensuring that the rights of workers in the maritime sector are respected. the international labour organisation (ilo) maritime labour convention 2006 aims to ensure decent working and living conditions on board ships by bringing together in a single text the maritime labour conventions and recommendations adopted by the ilo since 1919 and thus constitutes the first draft of a universal maritime labour code. the ratification of the convention by the member states is therefore essential for all efforts to ensure that it is effectively complied with. given the strategic importance of the sector, which handles 90% of world trade and 40% of intra-community trade, and the number of workers involved, this measure was long overdue. we therefore voted in favour of this report and look forward to its rapid ratification and implementation by the various member states.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the need to draft a first universal maritime labour code. with the adoption of the ilo convention 2006, minimum standards in the area of health, training, working conditions and social security for maritime workers have been established, ensuring decent working and living conditions on board international ships. it is now up to the member states to ratify this convention. i therefore urge the portuguese authorities to ratify this ilo convention in order to ensure more uniform minimum employment conditions. i welcome this convention for introducing innovative mechanisms such as the maritime labour certificate issued by the state to ships flying its flag after verifying that the working conditions on board comply with national laws and the rules of the convention. i hope that this convention will contribute to the stabilization of the maritime transport sector, which is faced with the pressure of global competition from less socially active operators and the threat of offshoring of seafarers' recruitment to the detriment of european employment, including in intra-community traffic.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it is an important subject for european citizens and because i share the rapporteur's view: services of general interest (sgis) are one of the fundamental pillars on which the european social model is based and are an appropriate means of reinforcing the social dimension of the lisbon strategy and of meeting the challenges of globalisation, industrial change, technological progress, demographic change, migration or changing social and working patterns.
in writing. the pandora's box of attacks on public services, opened by the directive on the creation of the internal market for services (the infamous bolkestein directive), continues in this report on services of general interest. the commission has already accepted the division of services of general interest into general economic services and social services of general interest. secondly, by failing to defend clearly the right of each member state to define the public services it wants and the way in which they are organised and financed. thirdly, by allowing private undertakings to provide services of general interest, it opens the way to the privatisation of essential public services and thus calls into question in practice the principles of equality, universality, social cohesion and, above all, the possibility of realising fundamental human rights in practice. finally, there is also the rejection of all the proposals we have put forward, in particular our call on the member states to reverse the so-called 'reforms' which have institutionalised market-based social protection models, subject to competition and tendering obligations, and to stop promoting public-private partnerships or outsourcing social services to the private sector, as these strategies are misleading.
in writing. the european union has nothing to gain from a rigid model for defining economic activities and determining their public or private nature. the modern economy, and the european economy in particular, needs flexibility. on the other hand, the best model of european integration is one which leaves room for each member state to choose the paths which its citizens prefer, even leaving them room to make mistakes. the possibility of error is part of the freedom of choice. i therefore agree with the need for a clear definition in legal terms of what is meant by economic services of general interest and social services of general interest. their correct identification is important so that when adopting standards the european union does not impose or prohibit what it is not in a position to determine. in this respect, i am in favour of much of what is said in this report. i also agree with the rapporteur that the social services of general interest should be given sufficient funding. this is undeniable, even if we have different views on the means of financing. and that in each member state there is a different understanding of what their duty is to the citizens.
in writing. one of the objectives of the conclusion of this preliminary agreement on air transport between the european community and the united states of america is to reduce to a minimum the disparities which currently exist, at different levels, between airlines from the eu and those from the united states. however, we are concerned about its celebration. the assumption that the community has the competence to conclude such agreements and not the member states calls into question the sovereignty of each state in a matter of great strategic importance, all the more so when the assumption underlying this agreement is to 'set the pattern for greater liberalization and regulatory convergence at world level', which we consider unacceptable. the advantages of multilateral agreements are obvious, since they help to improve the conditions under which services are provided, particularly for passengers, the routes available and the prices charged, to simplify procedures and to minimise environmental impacts, and to safeguard and promote the rights of workers in this sector and to ensure respect for the internal order and sovereignty of each country.

mr mandelson, this initiative of the commission has the merit of initiating a debate on a subject too complex to call for simple answers. there are sectors in europe which are more attached to the more demagogic and populist responses of all quarters who think they have simple answers to this question. they're simple answers, but they're wrong. the key question is precisely how the european union should use the trade defence instruments at its disposal to ensure that the rules of fair trade are respected and to participate actively in the process of regulating international trade. we must defend a european economic and social model, but always with the limit of not falling into the protectionist trap. this is the fundamental question facing the european union today. we have already seen that there are natural differences and conflicting interests within the european union itself. the interests of producers do not necessarily coincide with the interests of large importers, and the immediate interests of consumers do not necessarily coincide with the interests of one another. what is needed is a guideline that always takes account of one fundamental principle: how the european union will participate actively, seriously and intelligently in the process of regulating international trade, seeking to project to the international level, within the framework of the wto itself, some basic values that identify it, a competitive economy and at the same time a more solidary and more cohesive society and very attentive to the preservation of some fundamental environmental values. this is the challenge facing the european union today, and i believe that the commission is right to promote this debate.
mr president, fundamental rights are the benchmark for all political action in the european union. since the treaty of rome democracy has been the condition for this union of peoples and the basis for consensus, and no one can deny that democracy requires that all institutions obey an ethic of rights, that democracy itself is born of an ethic of rights. the charter of fundamental rights, formalised in the treaty of nice, is nothing more than the explicit expression of this genetic matrix of the european union. let us therefore avoid the mystifications. the european union has never existed without an essential link to fundamental rights. only by this bond does the union guarantee its loyalty to itself. the european commission's methodology of self-monitoring legislation is therefore welcome: respect for fundamental rights as an integral part of the control of the legality of legislative proposals, and an entirely new assessment of the impact of this legislation on fundamental rights. fresh air and more transparency for the commission's offices. this is a more structural solution and a happier one than the new fundamental rights agency, because this method proposed by the commission assumes that human rights are transversal to the union's policies. all the policies. that's his strength. in a democratic society, the control of rights begins precisely with the self-control of the institutions over their political practice. however, the virtualities of this methodology are limited, since it does not cover the council of the european union or decisions in the field of intergovernmental cooperation, in respect of which the commission has no initiative. if there are matters which today lack qualified attention in the light of a culture of rights, it is the third pillar, criminal law and criminal procedure. the threat of terrorism and the unrest of public opinion create in the states the temptation to a security drift which sometimes enters into a limiting relationship with freedom and justice. the commission's method opened the door but should also have opened the window.
to achieve the economic and social cohesion that is proclaimed, it is necessary not only to promote the real convergence of the economically less developed member states, the cohesion countries, but also to promote the reduction of regional disparities by promoting the harmonious development of the territory of each member state. in this context, it is essential to support the most disadvantaged regions and regions with structural problems, also by increasing the financial resources of cohesion policy, and to help remove obstacles to regional development arising from permanent natural and geographical disadvantages, for example in island regions. despite the recognition of the structural disadvantages of the islands, the strategy followed has not been consistent, and we therefore regard as positive aspects highlighted in this report, such as the increase in the rate of community co-financing on the basis of the existing eligibility criteria or the flexibility in authorizing the granting of state aid to these regions in order to reduce the costs of fuel, transport and energy, as a positive differentiating factor for these regions. the central issue is not the recognition of the already widely highlighted obstacles or the competition between disadvantaged regions in terms of priorities, but the insufficiency of financial means for cohesion, as demonstrated in the present financial framework 2007-2013, under which the structural funds have seen their weight reduced from 0,41% to 0,37% of gni and the liberalising and privatising objectives of the lisbon strategy have been set as a priority, which exacerbate the specific competitive advantages of these regions.

in writing. the aim of this report is, despite some reformist rhetoric, to promote the creation of a 'free trade area' (fta) between the eu and the mediterranean region. the eu is trying to achieve the liberalisation of world trade by concluding bilateral/regional agreements, overcoming difficulties in the wto negotiations. among other examples, the report advocates: the 'opening of agricultural markets', although regulated, referring in particular to the wine and fruit and vegetable sectors; the liberalisation of services, although excluding (only...) the public services which it considers to be basic (health, education, drinking water, culture and audiovisual services); the liberalisation of energy, through the creation of a euro-mediterranean market; and the liberalisation of the industrial sector, in particular the 'consolidation of a euro-mediterranean production area' for textiles and clothing, basically encouraging the relocation of a large part of production. in other words, the promotion of trade liberalization for the benefit of european multinationals and large importers, who are eager to dominate new markets and natural resources and to create new opportunities to exploit cheap labour. the fund is committed to sovereign development models based on specific national realities and needs and to a project of cooperation which is genuinely based on solidarity between these different countries.

in writing. the charter of fundamental rights is a synthesis of the common european values with which all citizens can identify, giving them a tool to defend themselves through knowledge and understanding of their rights and to better monitor the activities of national and european authorities when they enact and apply union law. i regret that it has not yet become legally binding, although it has already become a reference text both in the work of the european institutions and for european courts, such as the court of justice. it is essential that we make efforts to develop a genuine 'culture of fundamental rights' in the european union by establishing a general system of monitoring fundamental rights and by actively promoting fundamental rights and intervening in cases of violation or unsatisfactory protection of fundamental rights by member states. there should therefore be rigorous and systematic monitoring in order to find the best solutions which strike a fair balance between the objectives pursued in terms of security and the limitation of fundamental rights. the commission has also extended the procedure for complying with the charter of fundamental rights to the whole legislative process and to comitology.

mr president, mr commissioner, reflecting the right of every citizen to have recourse to the courts under any of the constitutions of the member states, article 47 of the european charter of fundamental rights enshrines an identical right in favour of every person whose rights and freedoms guaranteed by union law have been violated. the meaning of these precepts is obvious: no jurisdiction or jurisdictional pact can remove or preclude the fundamental right of a person to have recourse to the courts, even though the actual exercise of this right may, in certain situations, be precluded by what forensic language calls a 'defence by exception of jurisdiction'. however, the validity of such exceptions must be recognised by an independent and impartial tribunal previously established by law, as provided for in article 47 of the convention, which will decide on the matter in the exercise of its own jurisdiction. it is therefore not possible to consider that the bringing of legal proceedings by a natural or legal person involves any kind of disciplinary offence. the exercise of a right which is recognised by all constitutions and the european charter cannot amount to an offence of any kind. the belet report therefore enshrines the right principle by maintaining that recourse to civil courts, even when not justified in sporting terms, cannot be penalized by disciplinary regulations by condemning the arbitrary decisions of fifa in this respect. the vote on this principle will not only help to make sport more transparent, but also to reinforce the main principles on which the rule of law is based.

the rapporteur. i think it is not very popular to speak, but i just wanted to take the opportunity to convey two messages: the first to thank the cooperation of the shadow rapporteurs and commission representatives and the close collaboration with three council presidencies involved in this co-decision process (the austrian, finnish and german) with a special positive note on the german presidency which helped to solve a final problem of comitology; a second note to say that the 170 amendments are a positive aspect in the role of parliament because they reduce the administrative burden on companies at several levels: they remove minor variables, exempt some small and medium-sized companies from responding to surveys and favour the use of administrative sources. this is just one of the aspects which i think can - and should - justify parliament's approval at first reading.
in writing. this report is part of the 'third maritime safety package' whose general objectives are the prevention of accidents and the combating of their consequences. it is the responsibility of the member states to ensure that ships registered in their registers comply with international standards. any initiative taken at eu level to promote the prevention and control of maritime accidents should not undermine this competence. on this basis, we generally agree with the proposed measures, such as the verification by member states, when registering ships, of compliance with international rules and standards, in particular by the presentation of documents proving this; the development and implementation of a control and monitoring programme for ships flying their flag; and the guarantee of the training and supervision of inspectors and investigators. however, the financial means required to implement and apply these measures should be able to rely on community co-financing, which is not clear in this proposal. the memory of the recent accidents with the erika and the prestige is still vivid, and we believe that all the proposals put forward in this context should be the subject of a wide-ranging debate, ensuring the participation of workers in the sector and the general public.
in writing. following the accidents of the erika and the prestige, the latter in 2002 and at the entrance to portugal's exclusive maritime zone, the eu has drawn up several legislative proposals aimed at preventing such disasters or at least minimising their consequences and identifying the responsibilities and those responsible. this report, which was prepared by my colleague gilles savary and which i voted in favour of, deals with one of these proposals. i consider it essential because it establishes a minimum of rules common to all member states on the civil liability and financial security of shipowners (extended to all other persons liable) and others, with a view to preventing accidents and ratifying certain international conventions, in particular the convention on the limitation of liability for maritime accidents, the international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea and the international convention on civil liability for damage caused by pollution from oil-based fuels. i also welcome the proposal to set up a solidarity fund to ensure that even ships not covered by any kind of financial guarantee are given adequate protection and financial compensation.
in writing. this report forms part of the 'third maritime safety package', a package of legislative measures aimed at strengthening the prevention of accidents and pollution and the management of the consequences of accidents. the proposal aims to establish a system of civil liability for damage caused to third parties by shipowners and to lay down rules to prevent accidents. in particular, it calls on all member states to become contracting parties to various international conventions and to introduce a better guarantee of compensation for victims and crew in the event of an accident. the proposal also provides for the creation of a solidarity fund to compensate victims of damage caused by ships not covered by a financial guarantee certificate, since such compensation should not be borne by the member state in which the accident occurred. it is up to the member states to ensure that all the criteria are met and to impose penalties in the event of non-compliance. these are essentially positive measures which we support. however, it is possible that in future the control measures will not be the responsibility of the member states but of a community body which is proposed here - the community registry office - which raises serious doubts for us.
in writing. although the commission proposal for a regulation and the report adopted by the committee on agriculture represent a positive overall contribution to the definition of the common principles and rules applicable to organic production, with the essential aim of improving consumer confidence, there are still a number of aspects which fall short of our concerns. however, since we regard the question of the contamination of organic products by gmos as a key issue and because the amendment tabled by the pes group, which is sensible and realistic, setting a maximum threshold of 0.1% allowed only for accidental reasons, was well received, we voted in favour of the report.
in writing. it is known that about 70% of european consumers do not want to consume gmos. the fact that the regulation authorizes the presence of up to 0.9% of genetically modified organisms in organic products is unacceptable and is a blow to organic farming. to tolerate the 0.9% in the report (or the 0.1% that some have proposed and which was accepted in plenary) of contamination by gmos is to accept the transgenic contamination of organic products, which will have undeniable consequences for consumers and constitutes a serious and unacceptable threat to the survival of the organic production sector. consumers choose organic products because they are produced in a more sustainable way, without the use of pesticides, and because they are completely free of genetically modified organisms. the introduction of these substances, even in small quantities, is a way of manipulating consumers with serious consequences for the environment and for health in general. contrary to the path that this report opens, there is a need for more sustainable forms of agricultural production, based on the productive diversity of each country and each region, on the value of small and mediumsized farmers and family farming, rejecting the "productivist" model that is being sought.
in writing. i believe that products labelled as 'organic' should not contain any percentage of gmos and consumers are entitled to this guarantee when they buy a certain product labelled as organic. moreover, if products with a 0.9% gm content were to be labelled as organic, we would risk seeing the emergence of another type of labelling - 'gmo-free' - calling into question the status of organic farming. i therefore voted in favour of the amendments to ban the use of gmos in organic farming and the labelling of organic products altogether. i also voted in favour of the amendment which introduces products such as salt, wool, preserved fish, cosmetics, food supplements and essential oils under the regulation in question, since these products are linked, at least during one of the production stages, to the natural environment.
in writing. unfortunately, violence at football matches is not an isolated phenomenon, but one that has been happening in succession over the last few years (for example, at the 2006 world cup in germany and the recent incidents at national championships in italy, spain, croatia and england). it is therefore necessary to adopt the necessary and appropriate measures to ensure that such sporting events can take place as calmly as possible, without gratuitous manifestations of violence and racism. i therefore support this initiative by austria to update the decision on the establishment in each member state of a national football information point to serve as a contact point for the exchange of police information relating to football matches. it is essential that competent authorities are able to strengthen their cooperation and to professionalise the exchange of information, and that each member state is able to carry out an effective risk analysis. the commission has also been asked to draw up a report on the situation in the community.
in writing. the serious situation in the balkans, particularly in the serbian province of kosovo, is the result of a long process of interference, aggression and military occupation, promoted by the eu and the usa, which, exploiting real contradictions and difficulties in yugoslavia, imposed their domination in the region. the situation in kosovo is particularly significant. after the military aggression of nato, the us and the eu created a protectorate and installed important military bases in this province of serbia, not even complying with the provisions of un security council resolution 1244. the 'solution' proposed by martti ahtisaari, the un secretary-general's special envoy for the future of kosovo, is in the same direction. the end of serbia's sovereignty over part of its territory, with the (pseudo) 'independence' of kosovo under eu and us occupation, notably through the so-called 'civilian' eu presence in the framework of the esdp, supported by nato troops and the authority of a so-called 'international civilian representative' with full powers. we believe that the solution to the situation in kosovo must respect international law and the sovereignty of serbia, which is guaranteed by resolution 1244. any other (false) solution could have unforeseeable consequences in this strategic region. that is why we are voting against it.
in writing. the guidelines for what we might call the main budget of the european union - the budget of the european commission - are not only an indicator of the priorities and prospects for the coming year. as regards the guidelines for the institutions' 2008 budget, it is expected that it should remain close to the levels of previous years, in particular as regards staff policy. although a number of reports on the development of recruitment policy and the status of recruited staff have been requested by the european parliament, no information has been made available so far. however, we are concerned about the increasing substitution of service contracts for permanent contracts, the existence of a number of workers who after decades of service are still without a permanent contract, and the 'transfer' of many workers to temporary work enterprises. in fact, the precariousness of industrial relations is promoted by the destruction of workers' rights, the much-vaunted (and false) 'new social europe' to be applied to workers in the european parliament, ... this unacceptable 'flexicurity'.
in writing. we voted against the third part of paragraph 25 of the lamassoure report for two main reasons: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. what is being proposed is a real renationalisation of the cap. the proposal for co-financing, i.e. for member states to part-finance the cap's first pillar budget, is unjustified because there are other solutions which allow the financial commitments made by the council in october 2002 to be respected without having to resort to the sharing of the national budgets of the 15 member states which constituted the union until enlargement in 2004. as an alternative to co-financing, it is possible to set ceilings on the aid that is individually allocated to farmers (for example, in the usa, where this limit is set at usd 250 000), and to establish a 'compulsory modulation', that is, a percentage reduction in aid to the largest beneficiaries of direct aid from the cap, thus generating the savings necessary to honour the commitments made. (2) because there is an insurmountable contradiction in the wording of this paragraph. the commission is also proposing that the current system of community financing be abolished and national co-financing introduced. national co-financing is precisely the main instrument for renationalising the cap, giving farmers in the member states with the most budgetary resources a clear advantage over farmers in member states in the opposite situation.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because i consider the current system of the eu's own resources, which is based almost exclusively on contributions from the member states, to be lacking in transparency, efficiency and fairness. it needs to be reformed urgently, or else a situation of budgetary imbalance and inequality created by the lack of recognition that a better union can only be achieved with more and better policies, including at budgetary level, accompanied by sufficient resources, will worsen. having spoken on this in the committee on regional development, which submitted an opinion to the committee on budgets, i tabled amendments, which were subsequently adopted by a large majority, aimed at establishing a direct link between the citizen and the eu by paying part of an existing tax, so as not to increase the heavy tax burden on european taxpayers, and at ending budgetary rebates for certain countries, many of which have prosperity levels above the european average, as is the case with the united kingdom. finally, i also argued that future considerations of the eu's own resources should take account of the special fiscal provisions in the treaties for the eu's outermost regions.
in writing. the ep wants to open the debate on the eu's own resources, in advance of the discussion to be held in 2008/2009, made possible by the revision clause provided for in the interinstitutional agreement on the financial perspectives 2007/2013. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. this is because, according to the national parliaments, 'in the short term it is still premature to have a genuinely european tax'. we reject any attempt to introduce, directly or indirectly, european taxes, whether in the short or long term. we believe that a fair system of own resources should be based on national contributions in accordance with the relative wealth of each country (based on its gni), aiming to ensure that the effort in the budgetary contribution is similar for all citizens of the different eu member states, ensuring an appropriate redistributive role of the community budget, giving priority to real convergence and effective economic and social cohesion.
in writing. the report has many positive aspects, although we have doubts about the final wording of some points. we believe that the way professional football is approached needs to be taken into account. we cannot reduce everything to the framework of organised competition, leaving out the most important issues of football as a game and its contribution to the development of the capacity for anticipation, imagination, association and creativity in children and young people, especially in the knowledge and awareness of themselves and others, through themselves. the artificial division between professional and amateur sport (this is achieved in certain ways, even in a competitive context, in which the practitioners have a different profession and a different paid activity) ignores the rights that naturally have to derive from the duties inherent in this type of sporting activity towards clubs, the associative masses, their directorships, the sports associations, the rules and the standards and structures of professional football. this is a present reality, and as long as it exists we cannot bury our heads in the sand or take our wishes for granted. we therefore have a duty to help create conditions, without patronizing them, so that their workers can defend their rights, taking into account that they run all the risks also inherent in an activity of rapid wear and tear and premature social exclusion.
in writing. football equally vibrates people from the modern and sophisticated cities of the west to the far reaches of australia and the pacific, or from any lost village in central asia or the deepest part of africa. as well as passion, football is also one of the most powerful universal languages. and it is these characteristics - passion and universal language - that give it its strength and extraordinary capacity for mobilization. to be able to put this strength at the service not only of entertainment and a legitimate economy of its own, but also of social causes, of an equally universal dimension and reach, is a huge potential of football that cannot be ignored. i support this report and would like to stress that although the bodies responsible for football management may have a legitimate desire to preserve their internal procedures, recourse to the jurisdiction of ordinary courts, even when it is unreasonable in matters of sports justice, cannot constitute any disciplinary offence. i therefore recommend that football's governing bodies examine their statutes in order to strike a balance between the right that all sports actors should legitimately have to appeal to the common courts and the normal operation of sports competitions.

mr president, economic and social cohesion, which is enshrined in the treaties, should effectively guide community policies and be implemented, for example by ensuring the redistributive nature of the community budget. in this sense, regional development policy is an indispensable instrument for promoting the reduction of regional disparities and real convergence, economic growth and employment, acting as a supposed compensation for economically less developed regions and countries, in order to minimise the consequences of the internal market, the euro and the liberalisation of public services and trade in goods and services. it is noted that the current regional cohesion policy has undergone changes in its objectives and financial cuts in the current financial framework 2007-2013. the report now before us goes further into these negative trends, and it proceeds with proposals for guidelines which, if implemented, would distort and call into question a real cohesion policy. we therefore oppose proposals which, while seeking to maintain the existing financial resources, particularly in the context of future enlargements, aim to redistribute the financial resources of the regions and countries of cohesion among themselves, while the economically less developed continue to pay for enlargement, whereas the economically more developed are the ones who derive the greatest benefit from it. replace part of the financing from community funds by increasing national co-financing, access to loans or private co-financing. to set a maximum deadline for regions to have access to structural funds, to make access to cohesion policy conditional on the implementation of a national economic policy defined in accordance with the criteria of the lisbon strategy and the stability pact. contrary to these and other intentions, with which we strongly disagree, we have tabled a number of amendments to this report which, in the name of a genuine defence of cohesion policy, we hope will be adopted.

in writing. while recognising the need for europol to make internal adjustments, particularly in terms of salaries and allowances, the european parliament has consistently rejected all initiatives since 1998 when consulted on detailed matters relating to europol. in fact, such consultation could not be considered relevant as long as europol remained in the intergovernmental sphere, without democratic and judicial control. i am glad that the successive requests of the ep have finally been answered with the presentation by the commission last december of the proposal which aims to give europol a more acceptable legal framework, giving it the status of an eu agency, financed from the community budget and applying the staff regulations to its staff. although the process of transforming europol is not yet complete, i have decided to give my favourable vote to this finnish initiative on the adjustment of europol's salaries and allowances, as a sign of goodwill and full support for this process of transformation, which i hope will be brought to a successful conclusion as soon as possible.
in writing. bulgarian and romanian refineries are significantly dependent on imports of cane sugar from third countries. therefore, and in order to avoid interruption of the supply of sugar cane to the full-time refineries of those two countries, it is necessary to open the tariff quotas applicable to imports of that type of sugar from third countries into bulgaria and romania. this is the follow-up to the european commission proposal, which has no effect on refineries in other member states. i agree with the european commission's proposal, given the exceptional nature of the measure, and i vote in favour of the graefe zu baringdorf report.
in writing. in the current monopoly phase of capitalism, the financialization of the economy has been the answer to manage the contradictions of the system that lives on financial speculation, creating an ever-growing need to bring more money into the financial sphere. this directive is in line with that objective. the proposal aims to create an internal market for payment services and is part of the financial services action plan aimed at integrating the eu's financial services markets. once again, this area is marked by private initiative, notably from the banking sector, but the purpose is always the same: to promote the opening up of national markets to the provision of crossborder payment services, to weaken the prevention rules and to allow operators outside the supervision of the banking sector to provide these services, while promoting the concentration of the sector at eu level. countries which, like portugal, already have advanced payment operators and services (the case of the multibanco system) are particularly affected in this context, as the question of data transmission to information services, including external ones, is not clear. for all these reasons, we voted against this report.
in writing. we are pleased that, in the light of our proposals and intervention, they have succeeded in removing from this report some of their most burdensome proposals, which would call cohesion policy into question and would condition the debate on the mid-term review of the current financial framework and cohesion policy, in particular the rejection of:- increasing national co-financing of cohesion policy;- establishing a maximum period for receiving structural funds irrespective of eligibility criteria;- conditioning the allocation of funds on certain criteria for compliance with economic and/or budgetary policies, such as the stability pact. we also welcome, irrespective of one's position on the eu enlargement process, the fact that proposals aimed at creating a differentiated accession status for new countries, in which they would be fully integrated into the internal market but without any participation in the institutions or decision-making process, creating a neocolonialism where such aid would always be conditional on political impositions, have been eliminated from the report. however, the report still contains serious points, particularly as regards the financial means and the objectives of cohesion policy, with which we cannot agree, which justifies our vote against.
in writing. cohesion is a principle and a value of the eu at 12 or 30. firstly, because the assumption is that the partners in the same project should benefit from it in the same way; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. for this reason, i share many of the concerns raised by the rapporteur, even if i do not fully follow all the solutions proposed. but there are other aspects to consider. the kind of economic challenge that the present time brings us, with its origin in the pressures of globalisation and the accelerated modernisation of economic structures, suggests that we look for the most appropriate instruments for changing paradigms. so i believe that while we must be steadfast in our values and guiding principles, we must also be creative and innovative in responding to new challenges. preparing the economically less favoured regions for the 21st century is no longer a visionary gesture, it is a requirement of the times. the time is different, the answers must be innovative.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report because, firstly, it draws attention to the budgetary difficulties which the member states are expected to face, given the foreseeable demographic developments within the union. this is of the utmost importance because, with the enlargement of the eu, expenditure on cohesion policy would reach a politically unrealistic value. secondly, it would not be acceptable for some regions of the eu to lose out on the statistical effect of further enlargement, plus the negative effects that some european regions will experience as a result of globalisation. we are therefore faced with a question which requires great caution and i therefore support the request to the commission to assess the regional policy expenditure which the next enlargements may entail if the present criteria are applied and the consequences for the regions hitherto considered eligible. finally, i agree with the need to develop phased approaches which allow for a greater differentiation between pre-accession assistance and full membership in the context of cohesion policy.

the question period is now over (b6-0017/2007). the following questions were put to the commission. part one
question no 42 by alain hutchinson (h-0212/07) subject: blackmail of vw forest workers - reverse relocations by making the continuation of activity at the volkswagen forest plant conditional on an increase in working hours without an increase in wages and on greater flexibility, the managers of this plant blackmailed the workers with their employment. the workers had no choice but to accept, or the factory would close its doors. in its resolution of 14 march 2006 on relocations in the context of regional development, the european parliament called for measures to be taken against this kind of blackmail with employment, which can be described as 'reverse relocation', since it has the effect of lowering working conditions without relocating the company's activity. will the commission state what measures it will propose to prevent reverse relocations which lead to a deterioration in working conditions without relocating the company's activity?

on behalf of the pse group. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i would first like to congratulate the rapporteur, mr seeber, on the way he has conducted the informal negotiations. the negotiations were very fruitful and resulted in a compromise package of amendments which was largely agreed by consensus and which should be approved by the council. the socialist group supports the compromise reached, since it corresponds to the fundamental objective of this directive. ensure the protection of human health, the environment, cultural heritage and economic activities, taking into account the impact of climate change on floods. there are more and more periods of extreme drought, followed by periods of heavy rainfall, resulting in more flooding. the current proposal also seeks to ensure greater environmental protection by advocating the inclusion in risk maps of information on potential sources of environmental pollution resulting from floods. i also welcome the fact that member states are taking responsibility for promoting sustainable land use, i.e. member states should be more careful in their land-use planning policies. it also calls for the principle of solidarity, dialogue and coordination between neighbouring countries. cyclically, we know, natural disasters leave a trail of destruction and death. according to the world health organization, natural disasters kill hundreds of people every year. to avoid greater evils, we must move from a culture of reaction to a culture of prevention. better to be safe than sorry. it's more efficient and less expensive.
mr president, in a neighbourhood of baghdad, the american army is currently building a wall that, in the name of security, separates iraqis from iraqis. he does so despite protests from the neighbourhood residents and criticism from the prime minister himself. the bush administration loves walls, whether they're in baghdad or palestine or on your border with mexico, but the perspective of europeans can only be different. it was in berlin that what should have been the last of the walls fell. the euro-atlantic relations must therefore be guided by politics. it is true that for the europe of economic liberalism, politics is business, even if the depreciation of the dollar, the environmental dumping of those who do not ratify kyoto or the disparity between social rights show how dangerous the adventure of blindly removing barriers to the movement of capital in a world of walls is.

framework to be launched at the united nations-requested talks to be held in bali/indonesia in december. the commission has repeatedly supported the efforts of the various council presidencies to make
