the beginning of the german eu presidency was marked by merkel's visit to the us with the aim, at a time of great difficulties and increasing isolation of the bush administration, of renewing her proposal for an eu-germany-us strategic partnership for shared global leadership. in the context of the rivalry and concertation between the major european capitalist powers - with germany at the head - and the usa, the present moment may be characterized by an attempt to revive the so-called transatlantic relations. the us-eu summit, scheduled for 30 april, will be the corollary of efforts to overcome differences and secondary contradictions and to realign agendas on both sides of the north atlantic, whether in the political, economic or military spheres. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. these efforts - led by merkel and her right-wing/social democratic coalition government - are taking place at a time when the us is strengthening its military apparatus in europe, with the creation of new military bases and the intention to install anti-missile systems, which pose new threats to peace. imperialist movements...
in writing. this association agreement is linked to the single european sky initiative, which is already under way. one of its central aspects - which has been consistently pursued in this type of agreement - is the progressive liberalisation of transport between the contracting parties and the euphemistic adjustment of state monopolies. we therefore reaffirm the principle that it should be for each state to decide how to organise and what conditions must be respected in the provision of air transport services, including that it should be the state itself which provides this service in the first place. we also reaffirm that the principle which should govern and guide all actions to be taken within the framework of these agreements is that of cooperation, with respect for the sovereignty of each state, including in the management of its airspace. the liberalisation of air transport has led to setbacks in the quality of service provision and attacks on the rights of workers in this strategic sector. at the same time, liberalisation has served the interests of the large international operators by concentrating the sector to the detriment of smaller operators. finally, it refers to the incomprehensible involvement of the united nations interim administration for kosovo in this agreement.
in writing. the strengthening of common rules on aviation safety is a key objective of transport policy. terrorist threats must be dealt with with precision and clear objectives. the commission's proposal is to be adopted by the council on the basis of the report by mr glinne. the effectiveness, clarity and coherence of european provisions must therefore be our main objectives. even if there are a number of important issues to be resolved, such as the sharing of the costs of aviation safety, the more restrictive measures applied by one or more states or the transport of liquids on board, we must not, in order to resolve them, depart from the main objective of ensuring the safety of citizens, even if this sometimes comes at the expense of the comfort and timeliness of air transport services. it is therefore our duty to strike a balance between these two factors - safety and quality of air transport. however, what good is a quality transport if it does not meet stringent safety standards?
in writing. the objective of this directive is to establish a legislative framework for the assessment and management of flood risks, with a view to ensuring the protection of human health, the environment, cultural heritage and economic activities. a three-step approach is therefore proposed: flood risk assessment to identify areas at risk; flood risk maps; and flood risk management plans for river basins. without calling into question the principles and objectives of the proposal for a directive, the question is why a similar instrument has not been created to deal with the problem of drought, which affects millions of people in the eu every year and has particularly serious repercussions on the agricultural sector and the water supply to the population. this failure is all the more serious as it is known that there is a recommendation of this european parliament in its resolution of 18 may 2006 on natural disasters, which, among other things, calls on the commission to present a strategy on drought, which will make it possible to develop a european policy for the prevention and management of drought risks, including strategies to minimise their impacts. so while we voted in favour of this report, we regret this failure and insist on a drought strategy.
in writing. community action on climate change issues is of the greatest importance for the future. and that is why i believe that the measures taken by the community institutions and the member states cannot be individual measures, concentrating on one part of the phenomena and forgetting the others. i cannot therefore fail to call for joint action on climate change. in voting on flood risk assessment and management we are, as we all know, forgetting that floods go hand in hand with other phenomena such as drought or fires.
in writing. we reject the legal basis used by the commission for this proposal on criminal measures to ensure respect for intellectual property rights and we regret that our proposal for rejection was not adopted. the european commission has put forward a proposal for a directive based on a judgment of the court of justice on the environment, which is also the subject of some questions, which provides for criminal measures to be taken by the member states in cases of infringement of intellectual property rights. the criminal law is the exclusive competence of the member states. we therefore consider that the commission has no competence to submit legislative texts on this matter. we regret that most of our proposals were not adopted, which were intended to prevent the most negative aspects of the european commission's proposal, although there are some positive points in the report which the majority approved, but the overall balance is negative. we also consider it unacceptable that private individuals should be allowed to participate in criminal investigations, as the commission proposes. that is why we are voting against it.
in writing. since the end of 1999, european policy on maritime safety has been at the top of the european political agenda. the successive disasters (erika in 1999 and prestige in 2002) have tragically shown how weak european policy and member states' strategies in the event of a shipwreck were. i believe that this report guarantees an increase in the safety and efficiency of maritime traffic in general. in terms of the implications for the fisheries sector, this report seems to me to be balanced and guarantees the protection of smaller fishing vessels which do not appear to be obliged to install the ais system. this report deserves my vote in favour.
in writing. we consider the proposal to set up a system for monitoring and reporting on vessel traffic with a view to preventing accidents and improving maritime safety to be generally positive. however, we cannot agree with some of the amendments proposed to refer to an (pseudo) independent authority - which will not be, in the face of a conflict of interest situation, see the prestige case - the decision on the reception of ships in distress, including the designation of shelter ports. this is a responsibility of each member state. the national authorities of each state are responsible for managing the exclusive economic zones under its sovereignty. it is up to the member states to ensure the management of their marine resources. we therefore propose that any initiatives in the field of maritime safety at community level should be based on the principle that those initiatives which we consider to be relevant and necessary should be taken within the framework of cooperation between states without encroaching on their sovereign powers.
in writing. in general, we welcome this proposal on the liability of passenger shipping companies. a proposal which is essentially aimed at safeguarding the rights of passengers on this type of transport, similar to what already exists for air transport. for example, the current proposal introduces the obligation for carriers to have insurance that can be triggered in the event of an accident, and also extends the limit of liability of carriers, in particular as regards the limits of financial compensation to be awarded to passengers in the event of an accident. however, we are less pleased that in today's vote inland waterway transport has been removed from the scope of this regulation. we believe that the need to create such an instrument is also linked to the gradual lowering of safety standards, which in turn results from the elimination or reduction of state-owned carriers and the emergence of private operators. private operators who often fail to meet the standards for the quality and working conditions of their professionals - as is the case with the increasing use of precarious employment contracts. the first step in ensuring that passengers' safety is respected is therefore to ensure that workers' rights are respected.
in writing. the commission's proposal on the natural resources strategy is too narrow, as the rapporteur, kartika liotard, a member of our group of the european united left/nordic green left, has pointed out, and she has sought to extend its scope further in her proposals. it is essential goods, such as water, trees, soil, oil, that are not only vital elements of our economy but also of our very existence. we therefore consider it important that your report was adopted in support of sustainable economic development, combined with a fair and equitable sharing of the benefits of natural resources, access to resources and markets, in order to alleviate poverty and enhance people's well-being, even though we regret that not all the proposals you made, which we supported, were included in the final resolution. it is good that the prospects of re-use have been included alongside recycling and that the commission has been asked to promote technologies that focus on durable, repairable, reusable and recyclable products, as has the defence of the principle of proximity in all legislation.
in writing. the resolution on transatlantic relations - co-signed by the right and the social democrats and today approved by the majority of the ep - is a good element to take the pulse of eu-us relations. the ep majority sets out the agenda and priorities, highlighting:- the welcome for an improved climate of eu-us relations on an equal footing and the expressed desire for a shared responsibility in global governance;- the strengthening of the transatlantic market, pointing to the liberalisation of financial services as a key issue and calling for regulatory convergence and a level playing field, recalling the multilateral investment agreement; - the affirmation of the broad prospects for close cooperation with the western balkans, the south caucasus region, central asia, the middle east, afghanistan, the mediterranean, latin america and africa; - the strengthening of cooperation in the fight against terrorism and the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction as the greatest security challenge for both partners, nato being a transatlantic forum for political debate in a true partnership between equals. the agenda expresses the ambitions of the major european capitalist powers, particularly germany, vis-à-vis the united states.
in writing. as the resolution points out, transatlantic relations have improved substantially in recent years, thus returning to the quality they are expected to have, although they obviously can never be, or even are intended to be, free from problems and difficulties. you need to invest in this good relationship. we look around us, to the old world of the 1970s, 80s and 90s, or to the new world that has emerged with the fall of the berlin wall and with globalization, and in all these different moments we realize that the united states remains our main ally, our best partner, our partner in this endeavor to make the world a freer and more developed place. the importance of the alliance with the united states of america is inescapable, incomparable and cannot be called into question by political views which today, as yesterday, basically consider the united states to be the problem and not a fundamental part of the equation of peace, prosperity, democracy and freedom. in a broader context, i also agree with the epp leader's call for a large transatlantic market by 2015 and the need for parliaments on both sides of the atlantic to be more involved in translating this desire into legislation.
in writing. after being at the forefront of the disintegration of yugoslavia - remember germany's role in the recognition of croatia, after the brutal military aggression of nato, in which war returned to the european continent after world war ii - after years of military occupation of the eu/nato in the balkans, the eu (its great powers) is eager to move to a new phase of domination, absorbing politically and economically the countries of this strategic region through their "integration". the report also stresses the need to ensure that the eu's institutions are not left to the mercy of the political parties. - the continuing insistence on adopting the acquis communautaire, i.e. the neoliberal 'open and competitive market' framework - conditioning an autonomous national development project on the interests of the great powers and their large financial/economic groups - with the implementation of 'reforms' by croatia, such as opening up to 'strong private investment' and 'selling of minority and majority state holdings in companies'; this shows that, in the past as now, the interests of the workers and the peoples of this region are not what move the eu.
the european parliament has a duty to ensure that the european union is able to play a full part in the development of the world economy. 5,186 convicts await the day when they will cross the death row without a way back. on 19 april, the families of five bulgarian nurses were in parliament denouncing the obscure trial by which the libyan authorities had sentenced them to death. and when we discussed our relations with the united states this morning, there were far more references to common values than criticism of the fact that the death penalty is still in force in 38 states of that federation. in more than 100 countries, the death penalty still exists, and in several of those that have abolished it, there are those who call for its reintroduction. populism, authoritarianism and the lawless war on terrorism are plunging our societies into a security frenzy. the european initiative to apply a universal moratorium is not just a step towards abolition. in these days, it is a sign of hope against this strong and heavy trend.
it was in the heart of europe, in old königsberg, that the philosopher immanuel kant enunciated the most universal principle of justice, man is an end in himself. the european union was founded and grew up on a culture of rights, based on the view that each individual is unique and unrepeatable. it is this perspective which marks the european project, a character which is at once political and moral. today, more than ever, europe's destiny is defined by its ability to take the lead in the fight for rights in the world. europe is, in this sense, the depository of immense hope. the frontiers we have yet to cross are precisely those which separate barbarism from civilization. the european union, true to its enlightenment ideology, cannot give in to the temptations of strategic interests and real politics. we must admit that europe really has to fill the void left by other democratic powers in the fight for human rights. for that, it needs political integration, decision-making capacity, and a cosmopolitan law. it needs a constitution, with human rights as a cross-cutting theme to all measures and defended on all fronts. it is good to remember that fundamental rights are not only violated in the shadows of underdevelopment and dictatorships. democracies that claim to be advanced practice the death penalty in front of our silence. and here the european union cannot have two weights and two measures. in these days of summits between the european union and the united states, it would be good if the death penalty were to be placed on the political agenda, it would be good if the european parliament's resolution on the death penalty gained ground and ceased to be a loose chimera. because one thing is certain, the diagnosis of the big problems that threaten us has an answer in the human rights evidence. there is no dialogue between peoples, no end to conflict, no security, no freedom, except in a more just world.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i start by agreeing with my colleagues, mr díaz de mera and mr castiglione, who have praised the work of the rapporteur, mr deprez, who, as we are used to, has produced an excellent report and has made a remarkable effort to secure a compromise between all the political groups and the council with a view to obtaining an agreement at first reading. this initiative is very welcome at a time when europe is going through the most important migration crisis in its history. the massive influx of illegal immigrants to european shores has made urgent action a priority. although the regions most directly affected are those in southern europe, we cannot regard this problem as being exclusive to those member states or regions. mass irregular immigration, the humanitarian tragedy it represents, has consequences for the security and cohesion of the whole of community europe. i welcome the various operational measures relating to the management of the southern external maritime borders, such as the establishment of an operational command centre to coordinate a network of patrolling the mediterranean coasts, the creation of a central register of available technical equipment to be used for control and surveillance at the external borders, providing the necessary means (boats, helicopters, aircraft, etc.) to be used in joint operations, and i welcome the creation of rapid border intervention teams, the rapid teams, which i very much appreciate, which will provide rapid assistance at technical and operational level to member states who request it. this will increase solidarity and mutual assistance between member states. this regulation concerns the deployment of rapid intervention teams at the borders to enable rapid assistance to be provided in situations similar to those which have occurred, for example, in the canary islands. consent to be given for a limited period of time or in exceptional and urgent situations and following a request by the member state concerned. mr president, the european agency frontex should play a crucial role in coordinating this assistance. you must do so quickly and effectively. a decision is expected within five days and an operational plan is to be drawn up, which should specify the duration, geographical location, mission to be carried out, composition, number and profile of experts that each member state should make available to join the team. we all - parliament, the commission and the council - have to ensure that the necessary means are available at institutional, human and financial level to enable it to carry out its task effectively.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group, at a time when the 33rd anniversary of the april revolution is being celebrated in my country - portugal - it is a particular pleasure to be here discussing the strengthening of legislation in the field of information and consultation of workers. we know that the directives on the right of workers to information and consultation and on the european works councils provide for some information, particularly on the development of the economic and social aspects of the company and on decisions which lead to substantial changes in the organization of work or in employment contracts. but practice shows that it is not only insufficient, it fails to respond to the growing and serious problems of restructuring and relocation of companies, with serious economic and social repercussions. the situation which workers in a wide range of companies - from hightechnology companies such as alcatel-lucent, delphi and yasak, to footwear companies such as rodhe, the car industry, textiles and many others - are continually bringing to our attention calls for much more community legislation. it is necessary to ensure that workers' structures are fully informed and have a decisive role to play in the whole process, particularly in the european works councils, including the right of veto. we must prevent the promotion of flexibility and insecurity through the liberalization of dismissals and an unacceptable attack on the rights that workers have won over the years. i hope the commissioner will answer the questions that have been raised.
the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work is a step in the right direction. since then, other directives have been adopted covering areas such as workers' health, the organisation of health services at work, working conditions, the protection of young workers and temporary workers, on board ship assistance, giving expression to the ilo conventions. although almost all these and other directives require member states to send the commission a report on their practical implementation and the views of the social partners, the fact is that some member states have not submitted their reports. the proposal now under discussion is expected to give greater attention to the effective application of these directives and to working conditions, in an attempt to help reduce the millions of accidents per year, thousands of deaths and permanent disabilities in all the countries of the european union. as is now well known, the preparation of reports on practical application by the member states is provided for in several separate directives, but with different frequency: some every four years, others every five years and others there is no obligation. the commission now proposes, as we heard from the commissioner, that a single report be drawn up every five years. the proposal for a single report every five years must not be allowed to undermine or undervalue the specific aspects of each directive, which is what this report seeks to address, if it is to meet the needs of safeguarding health and safety at the workplace. we have therefore put forward a number of proposals, notably those which concern the structure of the report itself, which should be accompanied by a specific questionnaire in its content. thus, this single report should include a general part covering the principles and common aspects applicable to all directives and other specific chapters on the implementation of each of the particular aspects of each directive, with the inclusion of specific indicators where available. the five-yearly report shall assess the practical implementation of the different directives and, where appropriate and available, provide gender-discriminated data on equality between men and women. it shall also include relevant information on the prevention efforts undertaken by member states in order to allow an adequate assessment of how the legislation works in practice. we insist that a policy of genuine improvement in the practices of the various member states is required. but it is also urgent that the commission should present an in-depth report on the situation in the member states in the various areas of workers' health and safety at the workplace. finally, i would like to emphasize the close collaboration that has been possible with the members from the various political groups in the committee on employment and social affairs, as well as with the executive committee and the council, which will certainly enable us to obtain agreement at first reading. i thank you all for the work you have done.
mr president, in this european year of equal opportunities, which we hope will be for all, this report is of particular importance because it draws attention to those who are particularly vulnerable to multiple discrimination: women with disabilities. i therefore commend the rapporteur for her work and hope that the european commission and the member states will take due account of the proposals contained here. we know that people with disabilities and their families in general face increased difficulties in their daily lives and need support and measures which take account of the specificities of their situation so that they can be fully integrated into the various activities of society. it is therefore necessary to mainstream the needs of persons with disabilities and the rights of women in all policies at national, regional and local level, in particular in urban planning, education and training, employment, housing, transport, health and social services policies, including personalised support where the situation warrants it. this implies strong public policies, with significant investment in areas that are particularly sensitive, to ensure equal opportunities for women and people with disabilities, which requires changes in policy priorities. we cannot continue to give priority to the nominal convergence criteria of the stability pact and, on that basis, continue to cut public investment, as has happened in portugal, and to close maternity hospitals, emergency services, health services and schools, thus undermining the rights of people, especially the most vulnerable, such as women and people with disabilities. it is not enough to proclaim that we want equal opportunities for all, launch a propaganda campaign and then practise neoliberal policies that exacerbate inequalities and social injustices. more than proclamations, we need policy changes to prioritize social justice and real policies of social inclusion and equal opportunity for all and for all.
in writing. the health of workers and working conditions, the organisation of health services, hygiene and safety at work and the list of occupational diseases themselves were given some prominence in community affairs in 1989 with the publication of framework directive 89/391. since then, other directives have been adopted covering various areas of health and safety at work. the adoption of this report is expected to bring greater attention to the effective application of these directives and to working conditions, in an attempt to help reduce the more than four million annual work accidents and more than four and a half thousand deaths and permanent disabilities in the countries of the european union as a whole. we insist that a policy of genuine improvement in the practices of the various member states is required. it is urgent that the commission should present an in-depth report on the situation in the areas of the safety and health of workers at work and that the ilo conventions and other legislation in these areas should be applied.
in writing. we are pleased that the report adopted today incorporates all the proposals put forward by the cfp which were already included in the report drawn up by us for the opinion of the committee on regional development of the european parliament. in view of their importance, we would like to highlight the following proposals put forward by the cfp in the ep, in particular the increase in the financial envelope: - the increase of the annual financial envelope of the present scheme by eur 2 million, from eur 15 million to eur 17 million, of which eur 570 000 is for the azores and madeira; - the elimination of the limit of 75% for the compensation of transport and other related costs, ensuring full coverage (100%) of these for the european continent and for the local markets of the outermost regions; - the elimination of the lapse clause, making the compensation scheme permanent, with a five-year review; - the maintenance of the possibility for the local processing industry to use fish caught by community vessels, when the possibilities of supply by local fleets have been exhausted; - the positive differentiation of small-scale coastal and artisanal fishing; - the eligibility of internal transport from each outermost region, to deal with the problem of geographical dispersion, which is the case with the azores.
in writing. i am voting in favour of the duarte freitas report for the following reasons: 1° because the very specific situation of the fisheries sector in the outermost regions (orr) is taken into account, particularly as regards compensation for the additional costs incurred by the economic operators involved in fishing. 2° because the proposed permanent nature of the compensation scheme is consistent with the permanent nature of the constraints inherent in the fisheries sector in the oct. 3° because it proposes the possibility of supplementing the community compensation scheme with national aid. 4° because it provides for greater flexibility in the financial management of the scheme by allowing, within the overall financial limit, variations in the funds allocated to each region or member state. 5° because it proposes an increase of eur 15 to 17 million in the financial resources which will each year finance the compensation scheme over the period 2007-2013. in short, while the european commission's proposal was already positive, the european parliament's proposals substantially improve it, giving full satisfaction to the need to compensate for the additional costs of fishing in madeira and the azores, which will now have an annual financial envelope of eur 5 million for this purpose.
in writing. the completion of the internal market and the progressive removal of trade barriers have greatly benefited the strengthening of economies of scale in the outermost regions. however, the natural barriers to trade which persist in these regions weaken the position of the companies located there compared with those which fully benefit from access to the community market. the specific geographical and structural conditions of the outermost regions justify our measures to compensate for the extra costs of the outflow of products, particularly fishery products, from the outermost regions to the community mainland market. the renewal of the compensation scheme for the azores, madeira, the canary islands and the french departments of guiana and réunion for the period 2007 to 2013 therefore means that we must finally adopt a specific strategy for aid to the development of these regions, particularly in the fisheries sector, through a strengthened partnership. it should therefore be a permanent scheme, with some flexibility being possible, given the special conditions of these regions and in order to optimise its use. it is therefore essential that we give our support in solidarity to these measures.
in writing. the regional advisory councils (racs) were established following the cfp reform adopted in 2002. council decision 2004/585/ec establishes a general framework for the functioning of the jrc in order to ensure a coherent and balanced approach between them. the commission proposal, which is fully supported by the ep rapporteur, aims to provide the regional advisory councils (racs) with a more solid basis for their functioning by improving the conditions for their financing. the amendments introduced are intended to ensure that the community contribution is not decreasing, as originally envisaged. this report deserves my vote in favour.
in writing. we support this report, which improves the operating conditions of the regional advisory councils (racs), given that their inclusion in the budget means that the community contribution is no longer necessarily decreasing and that they are now subject to a single accounting method. however, the central issue that needs to be addressed is the long-term financial viability of the jrc. as these are an integral part of the common fisheries policy, community funding for their normal operation must be ensured on a permanent basis. this report applies to financing and not to other aspects of the council decision, in particular the number, composition and functioning of the racs which will be the subject of another decision revising decision 2004/585/ec. however, it is currently difficult to assess the rccs, as only 4 (out of 7) are operational. however, our support for this proposal is based on a view of the cfp as an instrument to promote the decentralisation of the common fisheries policy and to ensure the participation of fishermen and their representative organisations in the decision-making process of the cfp - which we believe is not being fully ensured - while also ensuring a pluralist and fair representation of fisheries interests among the member states.
in writing. we condemn the creation at eu level of so-called rapid intervention teams at the borders of the various countries, which is an expression of the increasingly repressive and militaristic nature of the eu. this measure is part of the current security drift and the policy of criminalizing immigration, which is a disregard for human dignity and fundamental rights. the rapid intervention teams, the walls, the immigration detention centres are instruments for the construction of a fortress europe, which we reject outright! one of the arguments to try to justify this measure is the fight against illegal immigration. the main component of the advanced policy is repression, it is stressed, while the real causes of immigration, poverty, hunger, war, the absence of a dignified life prospect for millions and millions of human beings - including portuguese - caused by capitalist exploitation and the brutal centralization of wealth are hidden. on the other hand, since the protection of its borders is one of the core competences of a state, we consider that this proposal - despite some safeguards - represents a further step towards the future creation of a european coastguard, which, if it were to come into being, would constitute an attack on national sovereignty. that is why we are voting against it.
in writing. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject of the protection of the external borders. the european union as a whole is also defined by its borders. in this context, it is clear that the external borders of the union are at the same time territories under the exclusive sovereignty of their respective member states, but they are also territories whose integrity, surveillance and protection are of interest to all, since problems arising there can hardly be considered as not affecting the other member states. think, first of all, of illegal immigration. but think also of illicit trafficking or, in another context, but for which this reasoning is equally valid, environmental threats. the sharing of the disproportionate burdens that the states with the most vulnerable external borders have to bear for geographical reasons is of the greatest justice and importance. this cooperation, while being based on the principle of solidarity between the eu member states, is above all the result of the need to ensure the greatest possible effectiveness in border protection. defending them is not to be confused with protectionism or isolationism, but only with respect for the rules.
in writing. in june 2006, following the political agreement reached in the council on the new european fisheries fund, it was decided to amend two provisions of the basic regulation revising the fisheries policy (2371/2002) concerning the management of fishing capacity of the fleet. the aim of the amendment is to allow some fleet adaptations to improve safety, working and hygiene conditions, the quality of products on board vessels and energy efficiency. the amendments will give member states the possibility to increase the tonnage of their vessels to a limited extent, thus improving safety, working conditions and hygiene, the quality of products on board the vessel and energy efficiency. this report deserves my vote in favour.
in writing. the amendment is to amend articles 11 and 13 of regulation no 2371/2002, which is the main instrument for the revision of the 2002 common fisheries policy. one of the conditions introduced by the european fisheries fund (eff) was to call into question the community aid for the modernisation and renewal of fleets, which was already provided for in the previous financial instrument. the current proposal, dated june 2006, after the eff, aims to allow, on a limited basis, aid for the modernisation of the fleet for the purpose of safety and improvement of working conditions and hygiene, as well as energy efficiency, by allowing the reuse of 4% of the withdrawn tonnage, at public expense, for this purpose, while determining that the power reduction related to the replacement of engines cannot be restored with public aid. despite our reservations about the commission's proposal, we shall vote in favour of the rapporteur's two proposals which guarantee: - 10% of the tonnage withdrawn may be used for modernisation purposes, which, if limited, will make it possible to ensure, for example, the modernisation of small-scale coastal fishing vessels (less than 12 metres), so that they are given priority;
in writing. the galileo programme (european radio-navigation and satellite positioning programme) could be an important instrument which, by ensuring the provision of a public service, will represent an opportunity for cooperation, scientific and technical progress and the exchange and accessibility of information. the project should be based on a public investment and control strategy and solutions should be found to ensure its financing, in particular in the framework of international cooperation. the galileo system is being looked at with interest by countries such as china or india, which could be important partners in this project, contributing to the end of the gps monopoly and creating, as an alternative, a project based on broad international cooperation. we believe that equal access for all users should be ensured and that the public should be able to use the information available free of charge. however, it must be reaffirmed that such a project must fully guarantee the rights, guarantees and freedoms of citizens and their non-use for military purposes - the rejection of the militarization of space or its use for military purposes - and/or security dynamics, contrary to what is currently envisaged.
in writing. the galileo programme is undoubtedly one of the cornerstones of the lisbon strategy, given its technological scope and the expected future added value, not only in terms of employment but also in terms of technological advances. the economic growth that the programme's potential enables us to foresee is of the utmost importance to the european economy, and we have a responsibility to ensure that the conditions for its realisation are created with the necessary clarity, efficiency and speed. i therefore share the concern of my colleagues that the negotiations on the concession contract have been at an impasse for several months now, as these delays will have significant consequences for the overall cost of the project. i believe it is essential at this stage to make every effort to ensure that the commission presents to the council in june this year a clear and credible road map, solutions to future financial obligations and alternative scenarios for the implementation of the programme. the council will thus have the information it needs to ensure that this process continues, so that it can make up for the delays it has suffered. that is why i support this resolution.
in writing. once again, the majority in the ep is drawing up a report on human rights in the world, which, although it contains aspects with which we agree, is characterised, fundamentally and in general terms, by a manipulative and reductive view of human rights - political, social, economic and cultural - using them as an instrument of interference and political pressure on some states, always in accordance with the interests and contextual conveniences of the eu. a strategy for the use of human rights which involves an attempt to use the un human rights council to isolate countries which do not submit to the dictates of imperialism. as we have been saying, this is an exercise in profound hypocrisy, in which the so-called friendly countries are protected and the others, those targeted by the us and the eu, are criticized. a practice with which we cannot agree! the report therefore completely omits israel, once again, and in fact whitewashes israel's brutal policy of aggression and occupation of palestine, which systematically violates international law and disrespects the inalienable right of the palestinian people to their own sovereign, independent and viable state.
in writing. among the various aspects which the report in question touches upon, there is one point which i think should be repeated exhaustively. i refer to point 10: 'reiterates that in their future annual reports on human rights, the council and the commission should examine the different ways in which human rights are dealt with in other community policies, such as the common foreign and security policy, development, trade, immigration and other relevant policies, which fall within the eu's external relations framework (...) '; the eu's role in the world - and in particular in its immediate neighbourhood - lies in its ability to use its soft power to increase universal respect for human rights. on the other hand, it is time to look seriously at the enormous threat to this purpose of expanding human rights which results from the strategy of international cooperation and aid from china, an emerging power in this field. it is time to rethink the strategy we use, to ensure that we are pursuing the most effective path and in line with the values we stand for and want to promote.
in writing. as we have said before, we support the initiative to submit to the un general assembly a motion for a resolution calling for a universal moratorium on the death penalty, which, as we have seen, already has the support of some 88 countries. the abolition of the death penalty is an aspiration of millions of men and women around the world and of an increasing number of countries which have abolished it in their domestic legal order or have established a moratorium on its application. we consider that this step represents a civilizational gain which it would be important to extend to other countries. this initiative can help to do so.
in writing. if there are causes - and there are - to which we can and must adhere without hesitation, this is one of them. the reasons are not without explanation. a society that does not regard life as the highest value, the standard, the criterion, the limit, will always be a society capable of the greatest atrocities. i am not surprised, therefore, that bloodthirsty states shamelessly kill their opponents. but i believe we have a duty, and perhaps even the ability, to stop them. i am more surprised by the democratic states which apply it, as if they suffered from a sudden lack of criteria or values. this is not the place for another discussion, but i want to say that it strikes me that you refuse to accept the death of an adult citizen, even if he is possibly guilty of a heinous crime, but you consider that the life of an unborn baby is either not life or does not deserve to be protected. i would therefore conclude by saying that this eu commitment deserves my support. it also hoped that the member states - and the eu as such - would follow through on this declaration.

in writing. the annual reports of the european parliament on public finances always present the same recipe, regardless of the economic moment - the implementation of the stability pact - one of the greatest constraints to economic and social development in the european union and in the less developed member states with economic difficulties, such as portugal. the report is clear about the objective - to use 'economic recovery to cut budget deficits and make labour markets more competitive' - i.e. to cut back on the social functions of the state and deregulate the labour market, particularly in terms of wages and safety for public sector workers. in this report, the priority objective is no longer zero deficit but budget surplus. the rapporteur is of course not happy with the pseudo-revision of the pact in 2005, when it became clear that the pact was unreasonable in the face of the economic recession in the eu. but as you know, this is a political pact, the fruit of the reigning neoliberal ideology, so the economic justification is only an alibi. this has been our position since 1997 and we have advocated the repeal of the stability pact ever since. that is why we are voting against this report.

i would like to welcome the rapporteur, mr andria, and to highlight his report, which contains aspects which deserve our support. housing policy is a national policy. it is up to the states to guarantee their citizens the right to adequate housing, using the prerogatives at their disposal. the constitution of the portuguese republic, for example, enshrines in article 65 that everyone has the right, for himself and his family, to adequate housing, in conditions of hygiene and comfort, and that preserves personal and family privacy. this right is an essential factor of social integration and inclusion and a sine qua non condition for ensuring that all citizens have a basic need that is fundamental to human development. the housing problem in community regional policy is taking on a new context in a european union of 27. it should be borne in mind that, despite the increasing contribution of the structural funds to urban renewal, in particular through a community initiative of their own, the function of the structural funds is to promote investment of a reproductive nature by promoting positive externalities for economic development, such as investment in basic infrastructure and improving the skills of the labour force. that said, we believe that the structural funds can play a significant role in supporting integrated projects to promote social, public or cooperative housing, whether for purchase or for lease at controlled costs, with controlled social facilities for urban renewal, social cohesion and the promotion of sustainable urban development, and therefore, once again, the question of increasing the funds in the community budget for cohesion policy is reaffirmed as necessary, in addition to the mobilisation of other financial instruments such as the european investment bank.
i should like to begin by congratulating mr andria on his report. the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, which everyone is trying to make constitutional and binding in the european union, states in its first article that the dignity of the human being is unviable. this right right rightly includes the right to adequate housing. although the european union, as has already been said, has no direct competence in this area, it has nevertheless an essential role to play. europe, in close cooperation with national, regional and local authorities, must work to eradicate the urban ghettos and the scourge of homelessness that proliferate not only in the big cities but also in small and mediumsized towns. it should therefore encourage the revitalization of city centres, not only in the perspective of historical preservation but also in the perspective of the recovery of the local economy and the dynamisation of urban centres where dozens of abandoned buildings are now proliferating. this vision has evolved and we now believe that the european financial instruments available to member states should allow for public-private partnerships and structured investment in smart homes, where energy efficiency and environmentally friendly construction are key criteria. there is still a lot to be done, but i believe that this own-initiative report, together with the european charter on housing adopted by the urban housing intergroup of this parliament, are two key pieces in this way of approaching housing in the european union that has set them up.
i would first of all like to congratulate mr janowski on the excellent report he has produced. the european union's regional development policy can be crucial in promoting the innovation capacity of regions, particularly the most disadvantaged. in all regions there is a potential for innovation which must be exploited and, in agreement with the rapporteur, it is important to understand innovation in a broad sense, not only that which results from the activity of research centres, universities and companies, but also that which can result, in the context of dynamic societies, from processes of continuous improvement and improvement in which the contributions of each person, each worker, each public official, each entrepreneur can be decisive. only in this way can you increase the productivity levels of an economy, the best mirror to assess the innovation capacity of a region. thus, for regional development policy to have a significant impact on innovation, it must above all contribute to the creation in the regions of an environment and culture favourable to innovation, which favours initiative, entrepreneurship, healthy competition and a taste for risk. and we must recognize that in some regions these are not always the values that are reinforced as a result of the action of the structural funds, where, on the contrary, the risk of creating a culture of subsidy-dependence is very real, a situation which must be avoided at all costs if we really want to encourage innovation in the regions.
