in writing. on this subject and in this report i think it is justified to insist on an idea which i have put forward on several occasions. with a view to promoting peace, prosperity, democracy and human rights in our neighbouring countries, both for reasons of direct eu interests and universal values, i consider it desirable that a european project, designed in partnership with our mediterranean neighbours, should create in the medium term an area of free movement in the mediterranean as close as possible to the logic of the eu model, to which surrounding countries that meet the criteria of democracy, market economy and respect for human rights (the essence of the copenhagen criteria) can join. it would be a very strengthened partnership in exchange for reforms. it would, incidentally, and without this being its greatest virtue, be a solution which, if it were in the interests of morocco, israel or tunisia, could perhaps involve turkey if it were to conclude that the accession process was in an insurmountable impasse. having prosperous, democratic neighbours, constrained by the expectation of benefits, with populations who do not need to emigrate at all costs, is a good european project. and it's not even completely new.
in writing. i voted in favour of the filip kaczmarek report (a6-0146/2007) on the horn of africa: a regional eu political partnership for peace, security and development, as i believe it is essential to consolidate the eu's presence in a region torn by three major conflicts, in sudan, ethiopia-eritrea and somalia, and where a significant part of the population, over 22%, lives below the poverty line. the partnership for peace, security and development will only be successful if it adopts a strategic regional approach, involving existing regional organisations such as the african union (au) and the intergovernmental authority on development (igad), together with other international partners, including in the un framework. on the other hand, the international community needs to support the region to make it more able to adapt to the severe impacts of climate change, because although africa is the continent that contributes least to greenhouse gas emissions, it is the continent that will suffer the most from global warming due to its underdevelopment and poverty.
in writing. we believe that the principles which should guide the approach to the complex situation in the horn of africa should be strict respect for international law and the charter of the united nations, the peaceful settlement of international conflicts and de-escalation. any genuine and real solution to the problems facing the peoples and countries of this region must not be part of or promote, even indirectly, the agenda of imperialism for this region. the european union is not only a political force, but also a political force, and it is a political force which is not only a political force but also a political force. instead of interference, outside interference in efforts to resolve conflicts and the militarization of the continent, particularly of this region, diplomatic efforts - which are far from exhausted, as the recent peace agreement between sudan and chad shows - should be promoted to resolve the problems at the root of the current serious situation, namely the unfair distribution of access to the rich natural resources in this region. the urgent humanitarian aid and real development cooperation and support policies must also be ensured.
in writing. nuclear energy has been referred to as one of the lowest carbon forms of energy, with nuclear fission being placed as one of the preferred forms of intervention in the framework of 'climate change', and the importance of savings and efficiency being secondary. however, we believe that energy saving and efficiency, as well as renewable energy, should be at the centre of any energy policy. it is in this field that more public research and investigation should be promoted and developed in order to achieve a genuine energy alternative that meets the needs of the population and the requirements of sustainable development in our society. the increasing liberalization of the energy sector, promoted in the eu in the interests of large multinationals, is putting at risk the right of people to secure energy at affordable prices. as this is a strategic sector for the development of any country, we advocate its maintenance as a public sector and reject its privatisation. we are also concerned about the assumptions in this report that nuclear energy should be promoted, given the dangers - to the environment and to the population, such as the safety of the plant itself and the reactors and the treatment and transport of radioactive waste - associated with the production of this type of energy.
in writing. there are some ideas in the report which i think are fundamental. in particular, it recalls that 'nuclear energy currently provides the european union with 32% of its electricity and is considered by the commission (...) as one of the main co2-free energy sources in europe and the third least expensive energy source', drawing the conclusion that the eu 'must defend, in compliance with the euratom treaty, its industrial and technological leadership in the face of actors who are vigorously relaunching their nuclear activities (russia, usa) and the emergence of new global nuclear players (china and india), future competitors of the european union in the medium term'. i understand and acknowledge that this is an open-ended difficulty and one which provokes negative reactions among the populations, but i believe that nuclear energy should not be excluded from our considerations of the future of energy supply. whether it's because of the costs involved, whether it's because of the environmental impact, whether it's because the technological solutions today are less risky. i believe that diversity and technological innovation are the answer to today's energy challenges and the issues associated with them.
in writing. we welcome the inclusion of our proposals, which underline the importance of social housing and the priority given to tackling the problem of the homeless, in the housing policies of the member states. investment in social housing plays a key role in providing housing for many people who would otherwise not have access to the housing market and are thus hindered in their right to housing. social housing is a way of combating property speculation, ensuring the construction of social facilities and promoting sustainable urban planning and planning. in this respect, support from the structural funds and regional policy can be important. we therefore regret that our proposal to support housing cooperatives was not included. the report also incorrectly advocates the promotion of public-private partnerships, without recognising the important role of the cooperative sector. on the other hand, prioritising the issue of the 'homeless' in housing policies is essential to guarantee all citizens a decent housing, effectively combating this growing form of social exclusion. the question of establishing quality indicators at european level defining the concept of 'adequate housing' should be considered from the top.
in writing. it is a complex task to define a concept as vague as innovation and its contribution to economic development. in this report, as in many other commission and council documents, innovation is presented as a panacea and a new model for growth, confused with technological development. although the report contains proposals with which we agree, it does not depart from or call into question the policy of the neoliberal 'lisbon' strategy, which is to commercialise knowledge, research and education. on the contrary, it defends patents (including community patents), the concentration of research in so-called 'centres of excellence', public-private partnerships and the promiscuity of companies with public research centres and universities. it refers to the 'seventh framework programme' without criticising some of its priorities and the cuts it has suffered in the current financial framework. it suggests the privatisation of regional and local public transport. it also stressed the need to increase the use of the structural funds to finance the lisbon strategy. so we cannot vote for it. finally, we would like to refer - in the light of the proposals we have already put forward - to the need to ensure broadband internet access in the outermost regions, which is mentioned in the report in a mitigated form.
in writing. despite the existence of directives on the right of workers to information and consultation and the european works councils - which provide for some information to be provided to workers, in particular on the evolution of the economic and social aspects of companies and decisions which cause substantial changes in the organization of work or in employment contracts - the cold reality shows that these are either simply not met, or, when they are, do not often ensure the rights of workers - in particular employment - in the continuing processes of relocation, restructuring, mergers and closure of companies, which cause serious economic and social consequences. we have long advocated the need to ensure that workers' structures are fully informed and have a decisive role in these processes, by improving the right to information and to genuine participation in decisions, including the right of veto, such as the possibility of annulling decisions to close companies and the right to suspend dismissals. the commission has also proposed that the community should make aid conditional on investment and on the fulfilment by firms of contractual conditions which guarantee stable and lasting employment and sustained economic development, and that flexibility and liberalization should be rejected.
madam president, i would like to welcome the day of struggle of the portuguese workers and their trade union centre cgtp-in, which will be holding a general strike in portugal on 30 may. the portuguese workers are fighting against rising unemployment, against the increasing precariousness and flexibility of work and the so-called flexicurity, against the devaluation of wages and the brutal growth of inequalities and poverty, for employment with rights, for the defence of collective bargaining, for wage increases and for the fair distribution of the wealth created. portuguese workers are fighting to defend public services, health, education, justice, social security and the public administration that provides them. portuguese workers are fighting against the policies of dismantling the productive apparatus, of breaking public investment and of subordinating the country's economic needs to the growing profits of the large economic and financial groups.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i would first of all like to congratulate all those who took part in the conciliation process on life+ and who reached an agreement which we consider very positive, particularly because the european parliament was able to secure a significant increase (+ eur 40 million) on the council's common position. we all stand to gain, especially the european environment. among the measures eligible for life+ i would like to highlight forest monitoring, information and communication actions and, in particular, awareness-raising and training campaigns for those involved in forest fire prevention initiatives. these measures are in fact in line with our concerns expressed in the own-initiative report of the committee on the environment on natural disasters, for which i was rapporteur. another very important aspect is to ensure that at least 50% of the budgetary resources of life+ are used to support projects for the conservation of nature and biodiversity, since in its common position the council had proposed to allocate only 40%, an amount clearly insufficient in view of the requirements of financing the natura 2000 network and the implementation of the habitats directive.
i would like to make three points in relation to this debate: firstly, to welcome the continuation of a specific programme to prevent and combat violence against children, young people and women, and to protect victims and groups at risk. it was a demand we supported from the beginning and we consider it very positive that this result has been achieved. the second point is that, although there is an increase in funding compared with previous programmes, i regret that the commission has not fully accepted our proposal for a further increase to take due account of the enlargement of the european union and the serious problems of violence against women, which persist, including sexual exploitation and human trafficking. thirdly, to call on the commission to present as soon as possible the proposal we have agreed on for a new european year to combat violence against women, children and young people.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group, in the light of the own-initiative reports which parliament has been presenting on the future of the european union's structural policy, which anticipate a fourth report on cohesion and the debate on the community budget for 2008-09, we have reaffirmed our view that regional development policy should be the main instrument for effectively reducing regional disparities and achieving real convergence between the various countries through economic growth and employment. to this end, the redistributive nature of the community budget should be safeguarded and reinforced, and cohesion funding should be increased and not subordinated to any other objectives such as those enshrined in the lisbon strategy. we therefore oppose any attempt to make the allocation of resources under the future cohesion policy conditional on the implementation of national policies for so-called beneficial growth, as set out in this report, because we do not agree that the allocation of funds under cohesion policy is conditional on economic performance criteria established at community level as a supplementary instrument of pressure on the way member states define their economic and social policies, which would mean a double penalty for the economically less developed.
on behalf of the pse group. madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i too would like to begin by greeting the rapporteur. europe today needs to clarify how it fits into the globalised economy. as socialists, of which i am the shadow rapporteur, we are unquestionably in favour of the multilateral framework of the world trade organisation. however, the relative stalemate of the doha negotiations has led the commission, like our main partners, to find transitional solutions through bilateral or regional trade agreements. this strategy is clearly a second option and will only be acceptable if the agreements are compatible with the success of the doha negotiations and include minimum environmental and social conditions that are in line with internationally recognised standards such as decent work. however, i would like to stress that the unilateral review of trade defence instruments, as mentioned by the rapporteur, is considered to be clearly inappropriate. in addition, it must be clearly assumed that economically strong partners with a negotiating capacity equivalent to that of the european union must be treated differently from less developed countries or countries with serious development problems. with regard to the former, such as korea, india, brazil, mexico, china and indonesia, it is time for the european union to demand some reciprocity, particularly in terms of market access, respect for intellectual property, trade rules, investment policy and competition. the european citizens are demanding it. however, this reciprocity can never be required in relation to weak or developing countries. on the contrary, the european union has a double responsibility towards them with this strategy and should strengthen the conditions for them to be able to use international trade to accelerate their development process. it is not easy to strike a balance between these various objectives. i hope, however, that a spirit of compromise and sufficient consensus can be found between the various political groups so that the european citizens we represent here feel more secure in the face of the uncertainties of globalisation.
in writing. we voted in favour of this final agreement because it enabled the european parliament to guarantee an increase of eur 40 million on the amount proposed in the council's common position. the budget for life+ is now around €1894 million. in addition, part of the life+ budget is devoted to projects on 'nature and biodiversity'. the ep has ensured that at least 50% of life+ budgetary resources will be used to fund projects supporting nature and biodiversity conservation. in its common position, the council had proposed that 40% of the total budget be devoted to these projects. finally, as mentioned in the final report, at the conciliation committee meeting, commissioner dimas read out a statement that the commission would, before the revision of the financial framework, review the expenditure authorised and planned at national and community level for the management of the natura 2000 networks. this review will be used to adapt community instruments, in particular life+, and to ensure a high level of co-financing. in conclusion, the result is far more satisfactory than any agreement reached at an earlier stage of the legislative process.
in writing. i consider the result of the reconciliation to be very positive, as the centralised approach prevailed, where the commission maintains the management of the programme in order to ensure added value for europe as a whole, equality of criteria and excellence, while reducing secondary costs by setting up entities for management at national level. i would also like to highlight other positive aspects such as the increase of eur 40 million in the general budget and the allocation of 15% of the funds to transnational projects. i therefore vote in favour of the joint text approved by the conciliation committee on life+.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by anne laperrouze (a6-0125/2007) on the proposal for a directive on environmental quality standards in the field of water policy and amending directive 2000/60/ec because i believe that the european union must continue to play a key role in protecting the environment and also because this proposal aims to protect and promote the quality of the environment in accordance with the principle of sustainable development. measures are needed, following on from the proposed water framework directive, to stop chemical pollution of water, which affects aquatic ecosystems, causes biodiversity loss and leaves humans increasingly exposed.
in writing. this new proposal for a directive on environmental quality standards in the field of water policy follows on from the water framework directive, adopted in 2000, which sets environmental quality objectives for surface water to be achieved by 2015, but without a formal assessment of the various existing legislation in this area or even an integrated approach to water policy. it is therefore a set of measures which are worthwhile, with some positive aspects and correct references to the need to take account of the scientific and technical data available, the environmental conditions of the different regions and balanced economic and social development, but in a framework of reaffirmation of neo-liberalism, making the proposed measures subject to the 'maintaining of fair conditions of competition in the internal market' and the polluter-pays principle. it also introduces vague concepts such as 'best available techniques' which can be used to make the use of patented technology and equipment compulsory, creating dependency and potentially depriving workers of production resources given the high-tech equipment prices. although the european parliament made some improvements to the commission's text, it rejected most of our group's proposals, and we therefore abstained in the final vote.
in writing. we abstained in this final vote in view of what has happened in the meantime in this whole process. on the one hand, we disagree with the commission's position, which has proposed a regulation authorising the presence of up to 0.9% of genetically modified organisms in organic products, among other negative aspects. we still consider this unacceptable, especially when it comes to organic farming. tolerating 0.9% of the proposal for gmo contamination means accepting the transgenic contamination of organic products, which will have undeniable consequences for consumers and constitutes a serious and unacceptable threat to the survival of the organic production sector. consumers choose organic products because they are produced in a more sustainable way, without the use of pesticides, and because they are completely free of genetically modified organisms. the introduction of these substances, even in small quantities, is a way of manipulating consumers with serious consequences for the environment and for health in general. but on the other hand, since it was possible to improve the european commission's proposal in the plenary, even though the council has not yet given a positive response or accepted the change in the legal basis, we abstained in the final vote, hoping that some concessions could be made with regard to the proposals that improve the initial position.
in writing. the european community and greenland have long-standing fisheries relations, with the 1985 framework agreement expiring on 31 december 2006. the new protocol, which has been in force since 1 january 2007 for a period of six years, lays down the fishing opportunities for community vessels and the financial contribution, as well as the categories and conditions of fishing activities of community vessels in the greenland eez. the main objective of the new agreement is to maintain and strengthen fisheries relations between the community and the local government of greenland by establishing a framework for partnership and dialogue aimed at improving the sustainable fisheries policy and the rational exploitation of fishery resources in greenland's fishing areas, in the interests of both parties. portugal has a particular interest in this fisheries sector and is therefore in favour of concluding this new agreement.
in writing. despite our vote in favour of this report - which approves the proposal for a regulation under consideration - we have a reservation on article 3 (2) of the proposed regulation, which allows the commission to consider licence applications from any member state when member states covered by this agreement do not exhaust the fishing opportunities to which they are entitled. we believe that in the event of under-utilisation of fishing opportunities granted to a member state under quotas and licences, the commission should consult the member states concerned on how best to ensure that these fishing opportunities are used optimally, including the possibility of transferring unused fishing opportunities to other member states. however, we believe that this possibility should not call into question the principle of relative stability. in other words, the use of this possibility should not have any consequences for the future allocation of fishing opportunities of the member states under these partnerships. we therefore supported the amendment which clarifies this point.
in writing. in principle, halting biodiversity loss by 2010 is something that needs to be supported and therefore appropriate measures are required. we know that species and ecosystems need space to develop and recover. thus, ecosystem maintenance should become an objective of all eu sectoral and horizontal policies, taking into account the vital importance of healthy ecosystems for prosperity and well-being in the european union and worldwide. so urban and rural development cannot continue to ignore nature to prevent our landscape from being dominated by cement and pollution. biodiversity is a foundation of sustainable development and therefore it is necessary to mainstream biodiversity concerns into all areas of policy-making. while there are contradictions in community policies, member states should take advantage of all the opportunities available under the cap, the cfp, the cohesion and structural funds, life+ and the seventh framework programme to support biodiversity objectives. in addition, it is imperative to give greater attention to financial needs in the 2008-2009 community budget review, during which an assessment of the (insufficiency) and availability of community funding for biodiversity, especially for the natura 2000 network, should be made.
in writing. i am voting in favour of the adamou report because i consider the loss of biodiversity to be a problem of vital importance for the future of the eu and the action plan under discussion will be a key tool in putting into practice the measures needed to halt this phenomenon by 2010, although i believe that the deadline will certainly be very difficult to meet. i agree that the consequences of climate change. ecosystem services and the specific roles of the cap and the cfp should be taken into account given their importance for meeting the targets and ensuring the long-term maintenance of biodiversity.
in writing. i voted in favour of the caspary report because, although it could be improved, i believe that most of the socialist objectives have been achieved: in particular, preference for multilateralism and the conclusion of doha, special treatment for countries with development problems, mutual recognition of standards, respect for social and environmental minimum standards by combating current dumping, protection of intellectual property, the adoption of codes of conduct and good practice by european companies and the increased involvement of the european parliament. i consider it essential that the socialist group takes an active and constructive position in the follow-up of the bilateral negotiations with major emerging economies such as korea, india, china, russia and others, calling for a broad and balanced reciprocity; however, the strengthening of the support agenda for the least developed countries, including the creation of conditions for their positive participation in world trade, requires urgent reinforcement. these aspects, as well as the important negative position on the unilateral review of trade defence instruments, have, in my view, been sufficiently addressed in the final text.
in writing. i voted in favour of the caspary report because, although it could be improved, i believe that most of the socialist objectives have been achieved: in particular, preference for multilateralism and the conclusion of doha, special treatment for countries with development problems, mutual recognition of standards, respect for social and environmental minimum standards by combating current dumping, protection of intellectual property, the adoption of codes of conduct and good practice by european companies and the increased involvement of the european parliament. as the shadow rapporteur for the pse, i consider it essential that the socialist group takes an active and constructive stance in the follow-up of the bilateral negotiations with major emerging economies such as korea, india, china and russia, among others, calling for a broad and balanced reciprocity; however, the strengthening of the support agenda for the least developed countries, including the creation of conditions for their positive participation in world trade, requires urgent reinforcement. these aspects, as well as the important negative position on the unilateral review of the trade defence instruments, were, in my view, sufficiently addressed in the final text and there was an openness on the part of the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteurs to the establishment of commitments, which i would also like to stress.
in writing. free trade and global liberalization are presented here as fallacious panaceas, in partnership with the dogmas of price stability, lower taxes on the exploitation of labour or increased competition. among other things, it states that 'bilateral and regional free trade agreements are a solution', which is not 'ideal', but should be advanced where necessary to 'improve the competitive position of eu exporters in key external markets'. these should be 'wto-compatible, global and ambitious' and 'ensure comprehensive liberalisation of services and investment, going beyond both existing multilateral commitments and those resulting from the wto'. in other words, with the wto negotiations stalled, the order is to move forward when and where it is possible to liberalise trade for the benefit and profit of the large economic and financial groups in the eu. what the report does not mention are the disastrous consequences of capitalist liberalization - with its 'structural reforms', the end of customs duties or the imposition of so-called 'intellectual property rights' - such as the glaring increase in inequalities worldwide, the growing unemployment, precariousness of work and poverty, as well as the harmful consequences for the environment and biodiversity. that's why i'm voting against it.
in writing. in a global world the concerns raised in this report are of the utmost importance. although i do not agree with some of the positions expressed, i recognize in this list of problems and possible answers an approach which is essentially realistic. and that, i think, is one of the most relevant aspects. the debate on the external competitiveness of the eu or on the eu and the global economy must be based on realism. the illusion that it is possible to close borders, to impose identical rules to ours at all latitudes and longitudes or to ignore the impact of competition on society is a mistake that costs us an unbearably high price. i therefore believe that the strategy should be one which maximises the advantages while minimising the negative effects of this new situation: to bet simultaneously on the avant-garde and on tradition, on the specific and the non-transferable and on what is attracted by the living conditions provided in the european area. the idea, in vogue, that the eurocentric world (or simply european economic and strategic relevance) died with the arrival of the global economy is not a judgment, it is an opinion that facts and political will is shaping the facts can contract.
in writing. i support this report and the adaptation of the european union's trade policies to future challenges. europe's leading position in the world market allows us to create the conditions for change in order to respond to globalisation without sacrificing our interests and our social model. however, increased trade liberalisation must be accompanied by better use of the instruments of defence against unfair trade practices. without wishing to resort to protectionism, which would not mitigate the effects of globalisation, it is essential that europe takes a strong stand on the scrupulous enforcement of its international trade agreements. we cannot accept that our competitors resort to state export aid policies, to artificial devaluations of the currency and to violations of basic environmental rules. it is equally unacceptable that these countries do not respect the rights of workers and even use child and forced labour. the opening up of international trade and the conditions for access to markets must be global and reciprocal. on the other hand, the inclusion of minimum social and environmental standards in our trade agreements must be safeguarded. it must be borne in mind that the european project is based on solidarity, respect for human rights and sustainable development.

the question period is now over (b6-0018/2007). the following questions were put to the commission. part one
question no 30 by mr david martin (h-0301/07) subject: the situation in the former yugoslavia subject: negative effects of eu biofuel targets 83% of the world's palm oil production comes from indonesia and malaysia. in part as a response to the eu's growing demand for biofuels, both indonesia and malaysia are cutting down large areas of forest - in many cases tropical forests with high environmental value - to plant palm trees for palm oil production. is the commission aware that according to a recent un report, 98% of these forests could disappear by 2022? is the commission aware of the consequences of deforestation on local fauna, such as the many orangutans that end up in rehabilitation centres with little hope of release and return to their natural habitat? according to a dutch lobby group, about 50 percent of the land for new plantings is obtained by drying and burning peat-rich land, which releases huge amounts of carbon dioxide. how can the commission reconcile the eu's target of reducing co2 emissions by 20% by 2020 with the possible increase in emissions in indonesia and malaysia (according to the same lobby group, indonesia is the third largest co2 producer in the world)? what are the commission's intentions with regard to the introduction of an eco-label for 'sustainable' palm oils? does the commission intend to examine the possibility of banning the import of biofuels into the eu?
question no 31 by danute budreikaite (h-0303/07) subject: the situation in the former yugoslavia subject: agreement between the eu member states and russia on energy the publication by the commission of the 'energy package' in january 2007 gave new impetus to the efforts of some member states to secure supplies of energy resources from russia by concluding bilateral or trilateral agreements with that country. russia, greece and bulgaria have signed an agreement on an oil pipeline that will connect the red sea to the aegean sea. construction is expected to start at the end of 2007 and be completed in 2011. hungary will build the 'energia azul' gas pipeline from turkey through bulgaria and romania together with the russian company gazprom. this pipeline will follow the eu's planned route for the nabucco pipeline. the new agreement with russia is called the "agreement on the diversification of gas supplies". what is the commission's position on such a diversification of energy supplies, since the supplier is the same 'gazprom'? what is the impact of such agreements on the implementation of the eu's common energy policy?
question no 33 by mr claude moraes (h-0298/07) subject: the situation in the former yugoslavia subject: the use of hate speech on the internet what is the commission's view on the proliferation of hate-mongering websites, in particular those promoting and inciting racist, anti-semitic and anti-roma hatred, in some cases including the names and contact details of activists who may thus be targeted? is the commission aware of any parliamentary initiatives in the united kingdom and other countries to address the problem of such websites? does the commission propose any similar initiatives?
question no 34 by glenis willmott (h-0300/07) subject: the use of the european parliament in the european parliament subject: eu-wide emergency hotline for victims of forced prostitution following pressure from the european parliament in june 2006, the commissioner for justice, freedom and security referred to plans to set up an eu-wide (multilingual) emergency hotline for victims of forced prostitution. the purpose of this hotline would be to provide first aid to victims of trafficking, allowing them to speak to an impartial interlocutor and encouraging them, through this important channel, to seek advice and support. the obstacle to the creation of this line was cited as the difficulty of reaching agreement between all the telephone companies in the then 25 member states. what steps has the commission taken to make this hotline a reality and what progress has been made in getting the telephone companies involved in this project?

question no 40 by mr papastamkos (h-0296/07) subject: the situation in the former yugoslavia subject: separation in the electronic telecommunications markets in a recent speech in brussels, commissioner reding argued that the telecommunications sector in the eu must follow the european method of separating infrastructure from services if there is to be real competition in the terrestrial infrastructure sector. as a main instrument for the national legislator it proposes 'legal separation between network infrastructures at service levels'. however, the commissioner does not rule out full operational separation for the electronic telecommunications markets. can the commission elaborate a little more on what it means by the 'european method'? does the greek telecommunications authority fall within the category to which full separation could be applied?
question no 41 by mrs batzeli (h-0310/07) subject: the situation in the former yugoslavia subject: european framework for safer use of mobile phones by children and adolescents the entry into force of the european framework for safer mobile phone use by children and adolescents, adopted on 6 february by the main companies in the sector in the eu, is welcomed as an important first step towards ensuring the protection of minors against certain risks arising from the use of mobile phones; it is even considered that this policy should be integrated into the commission's communication 'towards an eu strategy on the rights of the child' (com (2006) 367 final). what means does the commission consider appropriate for the implementation of this framework at national level in order to ensure its effective implementation and monitoring by parents, teachers and guardians of minors? since this european framework is a code of self-regulation for european companies, how will the commission participate in monitoring its proper application in the member states and evaluating its effectiveness? what are the responsibilities of the national regulatory authorities with regard to the preparation of the national self-regulatory codes by february 2008 at the latest and the supervision of their application? does the commission consider that it is appropriate to adopt a future community legislative initiative binding on member states and companies, since self-regulation alone cannot be sufficient?
question no 43 by mr bernd posselt (h-0288/07) subject: the situation in the former yugoslavia subject: situation in the vojvodina in recent years, brutal attacks against members of minorities have repeatedly occurred in vojvodina, and serb refugees have been systematically settled in villages whose residents belong to minorities in order to make them majority serb. on the other hand, there were eu funds that did not reach their intended recipients, for example for the training of minority language teachers. can the commission state whether these abuses have been stopped and what overall assessment it makes of developments in vojvodina?
question no 44 by mr dimitrios papadimoulis (h-0290/07) subject: the situation in the former yugoslavia subject: application of the convention on the law of the sea by turkey in its reply to question (e-0802/07), the commission states that the convention on the law of the sea is indeed part of the community acquis, which turkey will be obliged to adopt and apply upon its accession to the european union. however, in its reply to an earlier question (e-4160/06) on the same subject, the commission had stated that it expected turkey to have already adopted and fully implemented the acquis by the time of its accession to the european union. can the commission state why it has changed its position within a period of six months? does turkey have to adopt and apply the convention 'on accession to the european union' or 'must it have adopted and fully implemented the acquis on accession to the european union'? can the commission state the legal basis for its position?

the clarity with which mr brok has put the issues on the table and the political line he has taken lead me to congratulate him frankly. as a convinced federalist and unwavering defender of the constitution, he puts his finger on the wound and draws the european union's responsibility in today's world. i would like to focus, however, on one point in this report which relates directly to the middle east and its conflict and the european union's inaction in the face of the catastrophic state of affairs, as has emerged this afternoon from the debate on the situation in palestine. the eu's geographical priority for 2007 should be precisely the situation in palestine. so i disagree with your position. the heart of the world's problems and instability is, as is well known, the middle east. so, if we are to live in a more secure, democratic and peaceful world, the european union must take up these challenges as its top priority among the different foreign policy priorities. the defence of the objective in the israeli-palestinian conflict of two states side by side in the region, within the lines defined in 1967, is an urgent matter for the world community and for all of us.
madam president, i support the report by mrs marie panayotopoulos-cassiotou, whom i welcome and congratulate. the issue of quality of work is not just a question of workers' rights, that is a reductive view of the issue. the quality of work must be seen as a much broader area, first of all because a high quality working environment is one of the most important factors in increasing productivity and thus enhancing competitiveness. quality of work depends on sound public policies and on the actions of enterprises in different areas, such as access to infrastructure and communication technologies, education, vocational training, lifelong learning, occupational health and safety and access to the labour market. on the part of the companies it will depend on leadership capacity, career prospects and work organisation. in the meantime, i would like to stress one more reason for paying attention to this matter: the reforms that europe needs to undertake at various levels to become competitive with the outside world require a change in behaviour and attitudes on the part of both companies and workers. the greater the level of trust between the parties, the easier it will be to implement these reforms. the more intensive the dialogue, the higher the levels of trust, and the more intensive the social dialogue, the more transparency there will be in matters relating to restructuring or change processes. i believe that the political, economic and social actors in europe must therefore, in the present circumstances, seize every opportunity to promote the strengthening of the social dialogue not only at member state level but also at european level. this issue - the quality of work - also makes this great opportunity possible.
decent work for all, which is very rightly advocated by the ilo, must include the promotion of the rights of workers in a wide range of areas: employment, wages, employment relationship, health conditions, hygiene, safety at work, vocational training and promotion, social protection and social security, collective bargaining, social dialogue and the elimination of discrimination and inequalities. but it is enough to look at the reality of the growth of precarious and low-paid work, the millions of work accidents, the poor workers, unemployment and the new attacks on the rights of those who work - of which the so-called flexicurity is one of the most significant examples - to understand the contradictions in which we are involved and which lead workers to protest and struggle, as will happen in portugal with the general strike promoted by the cgtp which is scheduled for next 30 may. the commission itself is an example of the contradictions when it presents this communication and then publishes a proposal for a green paper on labour legislation. in writing. the proposal for a regulation on the granting of community financial support for the trans-european energy and transport networks, while increasing the level of community co-financing currently in force, falls short of what was originally envisaged for both the transport and energy networks, as a result of the poor agreement on the financial perspective for the period 2007-13. but there is still a question of substance. the 'trans-european networks' are implemented with community and member state funding, i.e. mainly public funding, with the aim of laying the foundations for the internal market, as stated in the first point of the council's common position: 'strong and integrated energy and transport networks are the cornerstone of the european internal market and that better use of existing networks and completion of missing links will make it possible to increase efficiency and competition'. in other words, the completion of the internal market is at the heart of these projects, with the opening up of markets and the handing over to private interests of key sectors of a country's economy, then, of course, of the public investment made. we therefore support the maintenance of these sectors as public, and reject their privatisation, since they are strategic for the development of any country.
in writing. i voted in favour of the paul rübig report (a6-0155/2007) on roaming on public mobile networks in the community because i believe that the preliminary agreement reached between the european parliament and the council presidency on the text of the regulation, in which the members of the group of the party of european socialists played a key role, represents a significant victory for consumers. i believe that these measures will be decisive for the future of the information society, saving billions of euros and serving the interests of consumers better. reducing roaming charges will make it possible to break down the barriers that persist in the internal market, thus strengthening europe's competitiveness.
in writing. the regulation states that its ultimate objective is 'to create a well-functioning european internal telecommunications market'. this is because, as the report states, "self-regulation does not work". it is interesting to note that in this case they acknowledge that the market is not functioning. hence the need to regulate prices. they therefore propose regulation of wholesale and retail prices, including the creation of a regulated retail tariff (eurotariff), which all operators must propose, in order to achieve a significant reduction in roaming prices. however, the possibility of high profit margins for large companies in the sector still remains. but there are still advantages for users: a reduction in the cost of international calls, preventing these costs from being reflected in national markets, the choice of the most favourable operator and tariff. this is another case where it has become clear that the 'market' does not protect users and consumers by imposing regulation. it is time for the commission and the member states to recognise the same in many other areas, with benefits for the people.
in writing. the current roaming charges have been a burden on users in transit through several member states and constitute an obstacle to a genuine single market. given the transnational nature of the contractual relationships arising from these services, member states have shown little capacity to deal with this problem. similarly, although it is desirable that this issue could have been resolved by self-regulation of the sector itself, it was found that this was not possible. european consumers deserve fairer and more transparent treatment. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rules are applied in a uniform manner and that the rules are not distorted. although the limits on call charges are still far from the value initially advocated by parliament, i believe that it is a first step in the right direction, and has the merit of introducing the clarity and predictability that the market so badly lacked. i hope that operators will not respond to the loss of revenue by unjustifiably increasing the price of domestic calls, but will use this opportunity to increase their billing by increasing the number of customers and improving the services provided at national and international level.
in writing. it was good that the majority of parliament rejected this report. we voted against the imposition of tax rates at supranational level because it is a condition of fiscal sovereignty and of their political choices through taxes and the budget. in the specific case of excise duties, which today constitute an important part of the income of many member states, their main objective is to moderate consumption, as is the case with excise duties on alcohol and alcoholic beverages, in order to protect health. in addition to the direct impact of this tax on the activity of the agricultural sector and a large part of the industrial sector, it should be a decision primarily taken at national level, taking into account consumer preferences, particularly for traditional products, and different social choices regarding the consumption of alcoholic beverages, as well as different choices regarding the use of tax instruments, as is the case for wine in portugal, where it is important to maintain the current minimum rate at zero euros, which was also accepted in plenary. but we have to disagree with both the commission's proposed increases in the minimum rates and the rapporteur's suggestion that there should be a maximum rate.
in writing. this own-initiative report, in line with other commission communications on health care, aims to bring health services back into the logic of the internal market in services by presenting a new proposal for a separate directive on health services. that is why we voted against this report. but we are very pleased that the proposal to include health services in the directive on the liberalization of services was rejected. access to universal and quality health services is a fundamental right of all citizens, which should be guaranteed by the national social protection systems in the european union. health services are a public good and it is the fundamental task of the public authorities in each member state to ensure equal access for all to quality health services that are adequately publicly funded. i therefore oppose the creation of a liberalised internal market in health services and the current trend towards reducing or privatising health services or making them increasingly dependent on internal market regulation or competition rules.
in writing. although the controversy generated by this report has been resolved in due course, i believe that the report as it stands confirms existing rights and encourages patient mobility. well, that's exactly what it was intended for. as can be seen from the knowledge of the different schemes in the eu member states, and the particular relevance and discussion of this subject, the cautions that should be associated with this debate are understandable. however, the most relevant thing is to make clear and viable the faculties opened by the mobility of patients. health is one of the most sensitive subjects for citizens and it is not desirable that solutions be imposed on member states by means of community legislation which breaches the rules agreed upon by citizens and policy-makers. however, this does not prevent the introduction of rules to facilitate the use of this freedom in a free area such as the european union, where there is a tradition of mobility in various subjects. i therefore believe that the result achieved is positive and in the interests and rights of the citizens.
in writing. underlining that the report aims to contribute to the debate on the future of cohesion policy in the eu, we cannot but underline our disagreement with important aspects of the report, such as:- the conditionality of the allocation of funds under cohesion policy to the fulfilment of economic performance criteria set at community level, as a supplementary instrument of pressure on the way member states define their socio-economic policies;- the establishment of mandatory ceilings on the way structural funds should be used at community or member state level, such as 'reserving at least 20% of the structural funds for the promotion of r & d & i by the member states from the close of the programming period';- the advocacy of the use of the structural funds for the financing of private investment, in particular through public-private partnerships; - or the use of new cohesion indicators - employment, gdp disparities between neighbouring regions, decentralisation and accessibility, infrastructure and transport, research and innovation, education and training and the diversity of productions - without ensuring that gdp per capita should continue to be used as the basic indicator of eligibility under eu cohesion policy.
in writing. the idea of cohesion, which has been present since the treaty of rome, is one of the structural paradigms of the european union. in short, the development of one is the development of all. this idea, which is both generous and realistic, has been tested and approved by the passage of time, and it still is today, both for the states that have recently joined and those that have been members for years. i therefore share the rapporteur's view and that of the majority of european policy-makers that the value of cohesion must be promoted and defended. and i also think that the wording needs to be updated. what were objectives ten or fifteen years ago which were outside cohesion, or which could be because of more significant shortcomings and divergences, are now matters which clearly must be included in the face of an economy with a high rate of competitive acceleration. this requires cohesion to promote the strengthening of r & d skills on the one hand. and secondly, the support of the most competitive in each area. cohesion is not uniformity; cohesion is above all investing in exploiting specificities and ensuring the sustainability and durability of this investment to ensure harmonious development.
in writing. in our view, eu 'aid' cannot and should not be seen in the context of 'trade liberalisation', as the rapporteur proposes, or even that it should be used as 'one of the most effective guidelines for economic growth' in the poorest countries, for two reasons in particular. first, because aid is conditional on the adequacy of these countries' 'internal policies' and a 'real improvement in good governance capacity' in the interests of powerful multinationals, both in the eu and the us. in other words, the development of these countries is conditioned by 'aid', using their structural weaknesses arising from historical processes linked to colonialism, to the benefit of eu capital itself. the production for export is required, especially of products with low added value and low financial return, whose prices do not match the costs of production, as is the case with many agricultural products, forcing them to lift their customs barriers to the entry of foreign products. secondly, because this guideline establishes a hierarchy between countries, further deepening the gap between the so-called rich and poor countries, with consequences at the internal level of eu countries, as in the so-called third countries, ... in writing. as the report says, 'trade liberalisation is one of the most effective drivers of economic growth, which is indispensable to reduce poverty and promote economic growth and employment for the poor, as well as an important catalyst for sustainable development worldwide'. it is not, of course, a matter of saying, and i would not agree with it, that we can just liberalize trade and then we will see stable democracies flourish in free and pluralist societies. that is not true, and the present time, with examples such as the one brought by china, but not only, proves it. however - and this is true - there are no free, pluralist and democratic societies which are not, in essence, places open to trade. it is this understanding, and not its equivocal version or the absolutely illiberal view, that should govern the eu's guidelines on aid to international trade. our efforts at international level must be directed towards promoting a constant opening up of the world to trade, without thereby leaving unprotected economies and markets which need a minimum of protection.

in writing. the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) is an international agreement whose purpose is to ensure that international trade in species of wild fauna and flora does not threaten their survival. the convention now includes 171 countries, including portugal, which ratified the text of the convention in december 1980 and entered into force in march 1981. considering the fragility of survival of many species, cites is of particular importance. currently, about 5,000 animals and 28,000 plants are protected by cites, including species existing in portuguese territory. the species included in cites are divided into 3 annexes according to the degree of protection required. the illegal trade in animals and plants has over the years posed a serious threat to many species and, despite increased control, surveillance and combat in many countries, it remains unfortunately high. as with other types of wildlife protection agreements and plans, the success of cites also depends on a balanced approach based on scientific criteria and recommendations from accredited bodies, ensuring the validity and credibility of its actions and the effective implementation of agreed recommendations.
in writing. the report views innovation as a variable of the internal market, requiring the liberalisation of markets and the systematic removal of barriers to the free movement of goods, services and capital, freedom of establishment and labour mobility, always in the logic of competition/capitalist concentration. in the face of the underfunding of the seventh framework programme for research and development (r & d), it is once again advocated that the structural funds be used to finance it, as well as 'promoting and strengthening partnerships between the public and private sectors', i.e. placing public investment at the service of private profit-making logic. what is needed is to promote public investment in research, education and innovation, based on sustainable development strategies in each country, contributing to improving the quality of life, creating jobs (with rights) and wealth (justly redistributed). strategies that reject the commercialisation of knowledge, education and research and refuse that only highly profitable research with market opportunities will see the light of day. strategies that promote greater investment in education and training at all levels and that effectively facilitate access for smes to the various existing programmes and actions. the european union has a meeting with the future at the next intergovernmental conference. a marked encounter with his own nature as well. it was here that the enlightenment proclaimed the transcendent value of human dignity and the method of a union of peoples for the realization of that value. as early as the 18th century, kant dictated the maxims for perpetual peace and said that the internal constitutions of states do not fulfill their function without an adequate external order. this is how modernity was made: anthropocentric politics, mobile institutions, power as an instrument of justice. the european constitution is one of the tasks we have to perform today to fulfil the modernity that europe has given birth to. do we want or do we not want a project of justice which is only possible on the basis of the method of political sharing? if we want to, the constitution gives us the answer. it forms the basis for a large-scale democracy, the strengthening of parliament's power, the rebalancing between the centre and the member states, the charter of rights, networked political work, rules of decision-making that give governance and effectiveness to a humane and open europe. the world is confronting us with new realities more and more. political elites have the responsibility to build new paradigms and define new ways of life. in this path to consensus - in which i would like to highlight the efforts of mr enrique barón crespo and mr elmar brok - i would like to deplore the devaluation of the symbols of europe. the devaluation of symbols does not answer any real cause for concern among citizens. it is a response to the spectre of radical political discourses, and europe is in a phase of refoundation in which it should not be without its symbolic dimension. paul valery once said that europe would be built only under the threat of decline. perhaps we can counter that europe is made by moral will and serene reason. one thing's for sure, there's no middle ground to this odyssey.

mr president, mr altmaier, on behalf of the council, mr vice-president frattini, ladies and gentlemen, may i make a few brief comments on the prüm initiative, which is being debated and scrutinized today and tomorrow by the european parliament and for which i was rapporteur in the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs. the council's proposal, which was presented almost surgically just three months ago by the european parliament, was discussed and assessed at a breakneck pace by the commission. to this end, a public hearing was organised, with the full commitment, expertise and dedication of the libe secretariat, with the aim of involving all public and private actors in order to capture as adequately as possible the concerns expressed by them, always with a view to the necessary reconciliation between the requirements of operational and effective police cooperation and the defence and promotion of fundamental rights. this exercise of balance is extremely relevant when a proposal such as this one is at stake, which establishes valuable mechanisms for action and investigation in criminal matters, but which has a potentially harmful dimension to the rights and freedoms of citizens, an aspect which cannot and should not be ignored. as rapporteur on an initiative of such importance and visibility, my main concern was therefore to find the best possible balance between the requirements of effective operational police cooperation in the fight against the main threats to the foundations of the european union itself - terrorism and crime - and the protection of the fundamental rights of individuals. we agree that achieving such a balance and transposing it into a text accepted by the overwhelming majority of members represented in the libe committee, who also come from various political quarters, was not an easy task, but it was undoubtedly fruitful. i am convinced that the proposals which are to be submitted to the plenary for a decision have substantially improved the draft presented by the council. i am therefore pleased that the amendments we have adopted, the result of a broad convergence of positions between the various political groups represented in the european parliament and of close cooperation between the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteurs, have been adopted almost unanimously in the libe committee, where only one abstention was recorded. and i hope now that you will receive the same acceptance from this house. among the amendments proposed, i would like to highlight the following, because of their relevance in the economy of what i consider should formally be a framework decision: further harmonisation of the conditions of access to biometric databases, limiting them to investigative situations and, in the case of dactyloscopic data, also to the prevention of serious criminal offences; the clear definition of the rules applying to the conduct of joint operations; the establishment of criteria of strict necessity for the transmission of personal data to be legitimate, in particular in the most sensitive situations, in large-scale events and in measures to prevent the occurrence of terrorist offences; the extension of the application of the chapter on data protection to all types of data processing, giving effect to all the recommendations presented by the european data protection supervisor in this area; the provision of a maximum retention period for personal data; the prohibition of safeguards in the context of the prevention of serious criminal offences; finally, the establishment of a third pillar of the european parliament's role in this proposal, following the establishment of the general data protection framework and the evaluation of any possible measures, and, finally, the establishment of a third pillar of the european parliament's role in this area of data protection, and the evaluation of any possible measures to be taken. as a final note, i would like to sincerely acknowledge the importance of integrating the intervention mechanisms established by the prüm treaty into the legal framework of the european union, which are undeniably important in the fight against terrorism and organised crime. but i do not cease to express my concern about the fate of the european parliament's opinion in the council. in conclusion, the adoption of the framework decision with a view to deepening crossborder cooperation, particularly in the fight against terrorism and crime, will lack obvious democratic legitimacy if the role of the european parliament is ignored in part or in full, which will in no way strengthen the confidence of the citizens of the union in the process of community construction, quite the contrary.
mr president, mr altmaier, mr vice-president of the commission, ladies and gentlemen, the strengthening of security and the fight against transnational organized crime and terrorism imply not only a strengthening of the common external borders but also a rapid and efficient exchange of information in the field of border controls and judicial cooperation. equally important are closer police and judicial cooperation in criminal matters and the creation of the visa information system. i therefore support the reports presented to us by mr fausto correia, mrs sarah ludford and mrs martine roure, with a special congratulations to mrs sarah ludford for finally reaching an agreement after two and a half years of negotiations. the proposal for the deepening of crossborder cooperation includes some of the main provisions of the prüm treaty, in particular with regard to the fight against terrorism, crossborder crime and illegal migration, while fulfilling some of the most important requirements of the hague programme. it thus includes some improvements in relation to the exchange of information and the provision of personal data which should be protected as fundamental rights. i welcome this proposal and support the position of mr fausto correia that this initiative should take the form of a framework decision, since it aims to approximate the laws and regulations of the member states. the vis should also be the third major information technology-based system to be set up within the area of freedom, security and justice. i welcome the fact that agreement has finally been reached so that we can move forward with the creation of this much-needed system, which should improve the administration of the common visa policy, consular cooperation and consultation between central consular authorities, help prevent threats to internal security and facilitate the search for the easiest visa - in writing. the aim of this commission proposal is to incorporate into the community acquis the conservation and enforcement measures adopted in nafo, to which the community is a contracting party. the commission also uses the opportunity to update and consolidate in a single legislative document all the rules which are scattered over several regulations, in line with other legislative simplification measures. the rapporteur, in turn, updates these rules with other texts adopted after the commission's proposal, in particular in the framework of the 2007 tacs and quotas regulation. the purpose of simplification is, in itself, positive. however, we believe that the consequences of some of the measures now being introduced for the production of the long-distance fishing fleet, for the fishing industry and, as a result, for national economies, must be carefully managed at community level. it should also be remembered that portugal was one of the founding members of nafo and was represented by the community when it joined in 1986 - which, let us say, did not bring it any particular advantages, but on the contrary, so that it should depend on the difficulties of the national long-distance fishing fleet.
in writing. the mobilisation of the solidarity fund to help people affected by natural disasters in greece and hungary in 2006 is an opportunity - in particular in the face of the impasse in the council over the review of this mechanism - to reaffirm the need to maintain the eligibility of regional disasters in this fund and to adapt it better so that it corresponds more effectively to the assistance needed by people affected by such disasters. it is therefore an opportunity to reaffirm that we consider it a bad thing that the scope of application of the fund is extended without, as a result, increasing its financial ceiling, or that the threshold for mobilising the fund is reduced in such a way that it is the eu countries with the highest gross domestic product that clearly benefit the most. we should also recall our proposals, which have already been approved by the ep, in particular on the recognition of the specific nature of natural disasters of a mediterranean nature - and the adaptation of the solidarity fund to the specific nature of natural disasters such as drought and fires, in terms of the time limits and the eligible actions - and the assessment of the possibility of creating an agricultural disaster fund.
in writing. draft amending budget no 2/2007 is intended to mobilise the solidarity fund to provide financial assistance to hungary and greece to help them cope with the damage caused by the floods in march and april 2006. one of the things that immediately strikes the eye - apart from the delay in the implementation of the aid, the causes of which should be ascertained - is the amount of eu financial assistance, which may be considered insignificant in view of the estimated direct losses. the overall amount of community financial assistance for disasters is about eur 24.4 million for a total of almost eur 900 million in losses (520 million for hungary and 372 million for greece). this is another example of the discrepancy between the extent of the damage and the aid given by the community, which calls into question the notion of effective solidarity with the people of the affected regions. this reinforces the need to reassess the current solidarity fund in order to adapt its eligibility criteria so that it better corresponds to the assistance needed by the disaster-stricken populations.

in writing. the adoption of this framework decision on the protection of personal data is of the utmost urgency and importance, as it is essential to create a new overall legal framework for data protection under the 3rd pillar, comparable to the standards in force in community law, in order to ensure the same level of protection. i therefore welcome the fact that a political agreement has finally been reached, and i would like to highlight the efforts of the rapporteur, martine roure, and her contribution to this result. improving data protection under the third pillar implies that this framework decision should apply to the whole of the pillar, including europol, eurojust and the third pillar customs information system. as such, i support this extension and the amendments proposed by the rapporteur, in particular the addition of an evaluation and review clause, so that the commission will present new proposals with improvements within three years. i also support the 15 general principles put forward by commissioner frattini, which reflect the essence of the acquis on the protection of personal data processed in the context of police and judicial cooperation in criminal matters.
in writing. in the age of the terrorist threat, the balance between privacy and the protection of citizens is emerging as a constant challenge that we can only overcome with clear and responsible measures. the data protection rules used for judicial and police cooperation should therefore be designed to reinforce the principle of mutual trust between the authorities involved, allowing for more effective european cooperation and ensuring the greatest possible protection for citizens with regard to the use of such data. the measures to be taken should therefore be precise and comprehensive, protecting fundamental rights and respecting the articles of the charter of fundamental rights on privacy and the protection of personal data. i therefore welcome the political agreement reached with the council, which will allow the rapid adoption of this proposal for a framework decision.

europe needs stable borders to the east, and it must be stressed that we agree with russia on one important point: we do not want russia to join the european union, nor does russia want to join. on the other hand, economic relations between russia and many eu states are becoming increasingly important in the field of energy, where stable agreements and well-negotiated supplies are needed, while clear solutions for russian investment in the european union are being negotiated and companies from the member states are vigorously penetrating russia's energy sources. the european union must maintain its support for a more balanced process and involvement of russia, not only in external trade but also in the reformulation of european cooperation programmes such as tacis. russia has financial and economic resources as well as human resources. without wishing to lecture our eastern partner, which has no long experience of political pluralism, we can say that the strengthening of trade with russia can play a very positive role. the report under consideration makes a significant contribution to the debate on trade and economic relations with russia. we know that the strengthening of these relations will contribute to a better mutual understanding and may contribute to the reduction of social and regional disparities, especially when accompanied by frank and in-depth political dialogue. i also believe that accession to the wto will lead to deeper economic integration between the eu and russia. at the same time, it is necessary to foster a favourable investment climate in russia and to encourage the russian federation to ensure decent working conditions and respect for workers' trade union rights. of course, it is also necessary not only to support but also to contribute to improving russian legislation in order to ensure the application of the law with regard to the protection of intellectual, commercial and industrial property rights. i would like to conclude by saying that all these contacts with russia can and should also contribute to freedom of movement and expression and to respect for national minorities throughout the federation. good business should make good friends.
we are living in difficult times in our relations with russia. we have an obligation to contribute to improving that relationship. between 'realpolitik' which tends to ignore principles and 'irrealpolitik', a term recently introduced into international relations by the former french minister védrine, which tends to ignore the complexity of reality, there is certainly a possible way, the way of a demanding and responsible pragmatism. i believe that is the path that is presented and pointed out in this report and i want to welcome it. a path that points to the strengthening of economic and trade cooperation and to the creation of conditions enabling russia to join the world trade organization, as a condition for a better integration of russia into the international framework in this field. at the same time, this path must also be a demanding one in terms of defending and safeguarding fundamental rights, fundamental human rights, the fundamental principles of a democracy, the fundamental principles of a state governed by the rule of law. and it is in this balance that we must seek the solution to solve in the long term the problems which still separate us from russia.
the rapporteur, in writing. madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, in the european parliament's report on competition policy in 2005, we recognised the significant efforts made by the commission to modernise competition policy. let me highlight the main recommendations of the report. in the fundamental field of energy, we support the commission's action to separate ownership of production and distribution ('ownership unbundling'). we reiterate our call on the commission to clarify at community level the public service obligations which must be imposed on operators of services of general economic interest in the field of strategic security and universal coverage. we also consider it important to ensure that the eu's external dimension is consistent with competition policy when negotiating bilateral trade agreements. despite the commission's efforts to harmonise practices and ensure transparency, it is a fact that there is incentive competition between regions and eu states which, combined with the absence of tax harmonisation, encourages the artificial relocation of companies. these and other challenges illustrate the need to strengthen the eu's capacity to ensure the effectiveness of competition rules and to refine the flexibility to respond to new challenges. this is why it is important to continue to provide the european competition authority with resources commensurate with its mission.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group, this debate on measures to assist citizens of the european union suffering from multiple sclerosis is of the utmost importance. it is important to know what measures have been taken, based on the december 2003 resolution on this disease, to increase the visibility of this problem and prevent discrimination against the more than 400 000 people suffering from multiple sclerosis in the european community alone. it is essential that the european commission gives full priority to research to accelerate the development of more effective treatment for all forms of ms and takes into account the code of good practice on this subject prepared by the ms societies of the member states and their european platform. i would therefore ask the commissioner what he intends to do to ensure equal opportunities for these people and to make the member states aware of the need to pay greater attention to this problem.
