mr president, i would first like to congratulate mrs panayotopoulos-cassiotou on her report. demographic change is the main challenge facing europe. it is a very serious problem that requires urgent action. the situation differs from country to country, but one thing is certain: the conditions must be created at social, economic and educational level so that young europeans can have the children they want without suffering negative consequences in their careers or interrupting their studies. women remain the most disadvantaged, leading to de facto discrimination in access to and pursuit of education and lifelong learning. on the other hand, young families are thrown to the outskirts of large cities, which means more time wasted on the commute home-work-school, more physical and psychological exhaustion and less follow-up with their children, with incalculable social costs. there are two major challenges that lie at the heart of gender equality policy. to close the gender pay gap and ensure the reconciliation of family life with work or education. access to education and professional development are rights for both men and women. to achieve the objectives of the lisbon strategy, the european commission and the member states should promote policies that take into account the specificities of each family, including student parents, single mothers, etc., in terms of social security systems, adequate housing, childcare facilities and flexibility in curricula, timetables and choice of educational institutions so that our young people can contribute to the knowledge society, the competitiveness of the economy, social cohesion and the renewal of european society.
the rapporteur. ladies and gentlemen, since unforeseen transport difficulties prevented me and other members from speaking in the debate yesterday, i would like to take this opportunity to thank the shadow rapporteurs for their spirit of cooperation and commitment, which has already resulted in a broad consensus. i would also like to thank the commission services, and in particular commissioner kroes, for their openness, personal interest and willingness to engage in dialogue. cooperation between the european institutions and strong involvement of the parliament are becoming more important today, at a time when european competition policy focuses on strategic sectors such as energy and services of general economic interest, covers new areas such as the environment, and much of competition has acquired a global dimension. it is therefore important that the modernisation of competition policy continues and that the spirit of cooperation that has been evident during the preparation of this report is maintained, in the interests of the european citizens.
in writing. this report concerns the fisheries protocol with são tomé and príncipe on the community fishing opportunities for 4 years (starting in june 2006). under this agreement, portugal holds five licences for surface longliners. under the new protocol, fishing opportunities were reduced by 32% overall and the financial burden on shipowners was increased from eur 25 to eur 35 per tonne of fish caught, while the financial burden on the community was reduced by the same amount. we are very concerned about the consequences of these measures for the sector. in view of these conditions, which translate at community level into protocols with fewer and fewer fishing opportunities and more burdens and obligations for shipowners, the question is what contribution do shipowners really make to the effective improvement of the economic situation of the fisheries sector in the various eu countries? finally, we have serious doubts about amendment no 2 adopted by the ep in this report, which gives the commission a discretion to refuse licences when there is a breach of obligations, and we therefore believe that the procedures in place for this type of situation should be safeguarded.
in writing. this protocol fixes the community fishing opportunities for the next six years in kiribati waters, while maintaining, in essence, the conditions of the may 2003 fisheries agreement. the exclusive tuna protocol maintains the number of licences available to the national fleet - i.e. 6 surface longliners - and the key for allocating funding, with shipowners contributing 35%. however, the reference framework has changed, with the old fisheries agreements with third countries (of a commercial nature) being replaced by the new partnership agreements (with protocols on fisheries), which are increasingly serving as development aid. it should be noted that in this context fishing opportunities are becoming increasingly scarce, the financial burden on vessels is higher and the fishing rules are more restrictive, which means that these opportunities are not fully exploited by a large part of the fleets. on the other hand, the relocation of production from european union countries is sometimes seen in this context. this is a set of issues which raise reservations and questions and which should be studied and evaluated further when these protocols are drawn up.
in writing. the new regulation on spirit drinks will bring greater clarity to the definition and production methods of these drinks. the horst schnellhardt report improves the european commission's proposal by making it clearer and introducing some spirits that are difficult to define and others that were missing from the original proposal. we support the report because it is a complete document, including the only two portuguese drinks initially forgotten by the european commission - rum and poncha da madeira. the amendment to the directive on the protection of the environment against the risks of chemical agents, which was adopted by the committee on the environment, public health and consumer protection, was adopted unanimously. we felt that this was the most appropriate position to defend traditional values and the original production of vodka, and that it is in the interests of consumers to have clear information about the products they consume. on the other hand, it is a precautionary position aimed at preventing the same from happening in the future, distorting the production and marketing of some traditional portuguese drink. although this amendment was not adopted, the report was supported and a reference was made, albeit less clearly, to the raw material used in the production of vodka.
in writing. i voted in favour of the horst schnellhardt report on the proposal for a regulation on the definition, description, presentation and labelling of spirit drinks, because i consider it essential that the consumer is not misled. i therefore think it is important that producers provide clear information on the nature of the product, ensuring greater transparency on the market. the adoption of a single regulation, which brings together the two existing regulations, is intended to adopt a well-defined policy for spirit drinks, adapting the current legislation to the new technical requirements also defined by the world trade organisation.
in writing. the european commission adopted this proposal for a regulation to update community legislation on spirit drinks, including the definition of criteria for the recognition of new geographical indications. the proposal also aims to provide clear information to the consumer on the nature of the product and requires producers to provide all the information necessary to avoid misleading the consumer. this was one of the texts which led to a number of last-minute compromises between the various political groups in order to find an acceptable proposal for a regulation on the definition, designation, presentation and labelling of spirit drinks. at the heart of the controversy was what should be understood by "vodka": while some argued that the drink should only be made from cereals, potatoes and/or sugar beet molasses, others insisted on labelling so that consumers could distinguish the raw material used in its manufacture. as regards portugal, i think there are no problems with the proposals contained in the regulation, particularly as regards the geographical indications, which include the various wine spirits, bagaceiras and pear, madeira rum, algarve and buçaco rum, portuguese gin, singeverga liqueur, portuguese anise and madeira poncha.
in writing. in view of the marketing on the community market of dog and cat fur and products derived therefrom, i consider it necessary to create an instrument to standardise the rules applicable to this trade and to prohibit completely its use, import or export within the community. this requirement is based not only on the ethical aspect of considering these animals as pets, but also on the need to ensure a level of protection and respect for the welfare of animals that is not ensured by the cruel method associated with the rearing and slaughter of these animals. the confidence of european consumers and traders in fur must be restored, which can only be achieved by a common body of legislation prohibiting this trade and clarifying the legal requirements at the level of all member states concerning the prohibition of the sale and distribution of dog and cat fur and thus removing obstacles to the proper functioning of the internal market in the fur sector in general. i am aware of the widespread concern of european citizens about this illegal and immoral trade, and i believe that the adoption of a set of concrete measures by the union in this area will strengthen the citizen's identification with the european institutions.
in writing. i voted in favour of the eva-britt svensson report because i believe that by creating a set of measures to prevent the use of cat and dog fur we will be helping to put an end to this profoundly inhumane trade. i also believe it is essential to establish at community level analytical methods which will allow effective control of the origin of cat and dog fur, and to prohibit the import and export of cat and dog fur onto the european market. it is therefore not appropriate to provide for any derogation which is intended to create exceptions to its marketing.
in writing. following a large number of petitions and concerns raised, this regulation proposes a ban on the placing on the market, and on the import and export of cat and dog fur and products containing it, at community level. the ban will replace the different existing measures applied by member states to prohibit the production and/or marketing of cat and dog fur. the proposal also aims to ensure that information on new detection methods for distinguishing cat and dog fur from other animal fur is made available to the commission and exchanged between member states. the rapporteur strongly supports this proposal, but stresses the need to clearly eliminate any legal loopholes that jeopardise the very prohibition of import and marketing, and to make customs controls and administrative - and, where possible, criminal - sanctions applied by the member states more stringent, with the aim of creating a truly dissuasive framework to stop this scandalous and illegal trade.
in writing. while we welcome the adoption of our amendment to the effect that 'general access to broadband is an indispensable condition for social development and the improvement of public services and that public authorities should make every effort to ensure that all citizens have access to broadband, thereby extending its benefits to all sections of the population, particularly in the less developed regions of the union', we regret the non-adoption of our amendments which stressed, for example: - 'that in some ultra-peripheral regions with a high geographical dispersion, there are parts of their territory that do not yet have access to essential ict infrastructures such as broadband internet, which is the case, for example, with the western group of the azores (flores and corvo), thus representing a double penalty to be added to the constraints arising from ultra-peripheralness'; and 'that account should be taken of the differences between the ultra-peripheral regions, such as the constraint that geographical dispersion represents in some of them, as is the case of the azores and the canary islands, which implies guaranteeing the right of access to essential ict infrastructures such as broadband internet in the entirety of its territory to all its inhabitants.'
in writing. the report reflects the current framework of inter-capitalist contradictions between the major powers of the eu and russia. the text develops lines of intervention vis-à-vis russia - and it can be said that it presents itself as a true guide to neoliberal policy - so that it is shaped by the interests and ambitions of the major economic and financial groups in the eu. here is the significant criticism of "the recently introduced law in the russian federation that allows the government to reject foreign proposals to acquire majority stakes in russian companies, thus prohibiting foreigners from owning more than 49% of companies operating in 39 strategic sectors". the majority of meps 'question the law itself and the choice and growing number of industries that have been considered strategic and essential to russia's national security'. and, perhaps too much to expose the real purposes of such considerations, the consideration has been withdrawn 'that such an approach will not improve the investment climate and raises fundamental questions as to the role of the state in a market economy and competition in key sectors of the economy; the committee of the regions believes that in russia, as in other countries, the market is the best determinant of the system of company ownership.' more words for what?
in writing. the eu's relevance to russia is due to a combination of factors ranging from geography and size, strategic location, importance in energy supply - notably as an alternative to energy sources located in the middle east - to the memory which is particularly sensitive in most of the member states that have been part of the eu since the last two enlargements, to trade and, of course, to the role played by russia in international relations. all these factors call for realism. but realism is not to be confused with ignorance of the difficulties or with the absence of a framework of values. today's russia, despite some significant improvements in several sectors, is far from being a free and open democracy that fully respects human rights. i therefore think it is welcome that the eu was able to speak with one voice at the last eu-russia summit, incorporating the various concerns and interests of the different member states in its speech. even if the results achieved are not ideal, an approach such as this, which recognises the multiplicity of european interests, represents them and remains true to its framework of values, is preferable.
in writing. in general, the european parliament uses the sectoral annual reports - in this case on competition policy 2005 - to present its maximalist positions. it is currently doing so in the light of the concern to ensure full liberalisation of the energy sector by 1 july 2007, tax harmonisation in relation to corporate taxation (with a common consolidated corporate tax base) and the reduction and control of state aid, which is a sui generis feature of eu competition policy. nor does it forget to change the rules of competition when they prevent the concentration and centralisation of capital. all this is done in the name of the neoliberal lisbon agenda. that is why we are voting against it. however, two points deserve to be stressed. firstly, we reaffirm our opposition to changes in strategy in the face of mergers and impacts on competition, with the aim of encouraging ever larger european multinational groups to compete globally, rather than analysing the impacts of company concentration on their national markets, while continuing to criticise 'monopolies' and public authorities. it is recorded that mergers and acquisitions in the eu have tripled in value since 2003. secondly, there is a veiled suggestion that the competition rules apply to services of general interest.
in writing. the union's competition policy is of the utmost importance in an open market economy. fair trade measures for goods and services are of the utmost importance if we are to reap the important benefits of open markets - from lower prices to increased quality and choice for consumers, and the very important development of technological innovation. we therefore vote today to promote further clarification of the competition rules and the strengthening of legal certainty so that all the measures which have been taken to improve the effectiveness, transparency and coherence of this policy can be put to good use. the current approach seeks to go beyond a merely formal view of competition rules, to be able to better assess the actual or potential effects of certain practices or structural changes in firms, and to take decentralisation as another very positive trend. i therefore voted in favour of the report by mrs ferreira.
in writing. the report stresses the importance of all young people, men and women, benefiting from quality education and training adapted to the new market requirements and from a continuous updating of their knowledge in order to enable them to enter and progress in a lasting way in the world of work. considering that the level of education is a key determinant of a society's growth and capacity for innovation, the oecd estimates that adding an extra year to the average length of education increases the growth rate by about 5% immediately, and by about 2.5% in the long term. in countries with higher average levels of education, there is less inequality between individuals, which is a major challenge for portugal, the country with the highest inequality and the lowest level of schooling in the eu. in general, the level of employment increases with the level of education attained. the employment rate for those with a higher education degree was 84% in 2001 for people aged 25-64, about 15 points higher than the average for all levels of education and about 30 points higher than for those with up to the lower secondary level.
the genocide in darfur, the serious crises in zimbabwe, somalia, ethiopia and nigeria, corruption, pandemics, desertification, the flow of arms, the race for oil and other natural resources are all factors fuelling more conflicts in africa and increasing the number of desperate people risking their lives to enter europe or wherever they find better conditions. so it is depressing to see the g8 simply repeating unfulfilled promises from gleneagles. in the meantime, as the glennys kinnock report well documents, the millennium development goals have yet to be internalized as a priority by european governments and the commission. in africa in particular, the millennium development goals will have to underpin any security and development strategy and therefore also the joint cooperation strategy to be adopted at the eu-africa summit in december, which can no longer be a mere 'photo-op'. it is necessary that this should be the basis for phased commitments to the millennium development goals by european and african authorities and strategies that go beyond governments and beyond short-sighted and unprincipled competition with china. investing in the strengthening of democratic institutions and civil societies in african countries also means investing in those who fight for human rights, women's rights and civil liberties in africa. it implies that the european union and its african partners must demand from each other that they comply with the agreements which already bind them, such as the cotonou agreement. without justice and the rule of law, there will be no good governance and much less sustainable development.

question no 44 by mr david martin (h-0373/07) subject: the situation in the former yugoslavia subject: european union objectives for the concentration of greenhouse gas emissions the european union has set itself the strictest target in the world to limit the concentration of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere. the commission believes that the 550 parts per million (ppm) carbon dioxide equivalent target will limit global warming to a maximum of 2° above pre-industrial levels. however, in a recent study, climate scientist malte meinshausen estimates that the likelihood of this goal limiting global warming to a maximum of 2 degrees is only 12 percent. a draft report by the intergovernmental panel on climate change (ipcc) says that the likelihood may even be lower. in 2005, a study by the commission itself concluded that to achieve a reasonable probability of limiting global warming to a maximum of 2°, it may be necessary to stabilise concentrations at a level well below 550 ppm co2. can the commission explain why it sets targets which it knows cannot produce the desired result? what measures does the commission propose to take to reduce the concentration of greenhouse gases to 400 ppm, the value recommended by malte meinshausen, in order to achieve the maximum probability of limiting global warming to 2°c?

on behalf of the pse group. mr president, as we all know, agriculture, unlike the rest of economic activity, is carried out outdoors, which often leaves farmers dependent on weather events they cannot control. the farmers who are victims of these calamities cannot be dependent on charity, either national or european. they must be given rights so that in similar situations, within the european area, everyone can be treated equally. it is in this spirit that, as rapporteur for the draft resolution on the agricultural aspect of natural disasters adopted a year ago, i proposed, among other measures, the creation of a european insurance system with triple financing: farmers, member states and the european union, precisely to respond to this type of situation. so, in addition to supporting the request for solidarity support, which is due to the farmers concerned, i would like to ask the commission whether it intends to implement the proposal adopted a year ago in this parliament by a large majority, aimed at establishing this insurance system, which would not, moreover, entail an increase in the community budget, and, if so, when it intends to submit a proposal to that effect.
the european union is not a party to the treaty of rome, but it is a party to the treaty of rome. so first of all i would like to say that we are in solidarity with all the farmers in poland who have been hit by the recent frosts which have destroyed most of this year's fruit and vegetable crops and for whom we are asking for the necessary support. there must be a response of solidarity from the european commission. however, we should also mention the severe hail and thunderstorms in portugal in may, which caused serious damage to farmers in murça, sobral de monte agraço, azambuja, torres vedras and alenquer, alvito, vidigueira and cuba. we must also show our solidarity and call for the support that is needed. these situations demonstrate that farmers are among the first to be affected by climate change, and it is therefore important to ensure that public policies are put in place to guarantee farmers' income, even in times of crisis and crop destruction due to climate reasons, whether frost or hail, floods or droughts. it is time to create a public insurance funded by the european community. however, it is also important to ensure the protection of agricultural product markets and to promote a new agricultural policy as part of local and regional development policies which articulate various sectoral policies and give them cohesion and coherence. a new agricultural production strategy is needed which takes account of comparative natural advantages, the need to increase productivity and production levels and the integration of production systems into the framework of the ecological and climatic characteristics of each region, which has as its reference points food quality and the promotion of effective improvement of the incomes and living conditions of farmers, ensuring the future for young farmers and the food sovereignty to which each country is entitled.
madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by congratulating the rapporteur, mrs ria oomen-ruijten, on her excellent work, which presents us with a bold, balanced and prudent proposal which clearly goes in the direction of developing a decisive component of the european project, namely more freedom of movement with more protection. ladies and gentlemen, the globalisation of the economy and the ageing of the population are two questions to which europe has not yet found a clear and convincing answer. a more globalised economy implies a willingness to change, which means more mobility. the mobility of workers implies the acquisition, retention and transfer of pension rights and is essential for the development of the internal market. on the other hand, the ageing of the population with the inherent and foreseeable increase in public expenditure requires ensuring the financial sustainability of social security models. this sustainability will be all the more guaranteed if there are more conditions for instruments complementary to the pensions financed by the state. the trend is clearly in this direction, given the financial pressure that demographic change places on public authorities. the greatest challenge facing the european union today is to maintain the core values which are the basis of the european social model and at the same time to be competitive in the world context. this will only be possible through political action and if we are able not only to reformulate some aspects of this social model but also to develop very determined action with a view to deepening the internal market, especially as regards the free movement of people, in this case. the proposal we are discussing today is a very positive and encouraging sign of that.
in 2003, the european parliament rejected two commission initiatives on this subject. i congratulate the commission for separating the issue of residence permits from the issue of visas, and i agree with the european parliament. apart from the technical issues linked to a conflict in the radio emissions on the different chips, these are in fact different issues. it is one thing to have an identity document for use within the schengen area, it is another to have a travel document for use outside the schengen area. this will allow all third country nationals legally resident in the schengen area to be identified in the same way. i would therefore like to congratulate the commission on proposing the introduction of biometric identifiers containing an image and fingerprints in an interoperable format. the use of such biometric data is the best way to prevent the use of false identities and the misuse of identities. i would, however, draw the council's attention to the need for these changes of residence to respect the same high levels of security as are required for the issuing of national identity cards. i would also draw the council's attention to the gaps in the way data are collected, especially in the case of children or people who, for various reasons, cannot provide fingerprints. finally, i would draw the council's attention to the data protection rules and the need to draw up a detailed list of the authorities who will have access to them and of the authorities responsible for carrying out checks on residence permits, in order to prevent the misuse of the most sensitive data.
in writing. as our group says, this proposal - which introduces biometric data into the uniform format for residence permits for third country nationals - 'raises concerns as regards its technical feasibility, the financial burden it implies and the risks of abuse it poses'. as underlined, it is more than questionable whether the introduction of biometric identifiers will actually increase security. on the contrary, it may, above all, be a threat to the same, owing to the risks of abuse, the technological shortcomings and the lack of transparency and data protection it entails. this is a disproportionate measure, part of a supranational dynamic and the creation of eu-level monitoring and control instruments - such as the creation of a personal database - without even being accompanied by 'particularly serious and robust safeguards, mainly concerning the way data is collected and used' and without it even being possible to ensure its use 'in a relatively safe environment'. as a consequence and an integral part of the current security drift by the eu institutions, the present proposal deserves our rejection.
in writing. the oslo-paris commission recommended in 1990 that all chlorine and mercury cell-based alkaline plants convert to mercury-free technologies by 2010. the european parliament resolution on the community strategy on mercury (march 2006) called on the commission to ensure its implementation. in addition to the current mercury emissions from chlorine and alkaline mercury cell plants, when these plants convert to mercury-free technologies, the large amounts of mercury in their cells need to be managed in an environmentally appropriate manner. in order to prevent these surpluses of mercury from invading the world's raw material markets, a proposal for a regulation was adopted in october 2006 to ban the export of metallic mercury from 1 july 2011, which was now sought to be brought forward. there are provisions for the safe storage of surplus mercury, mainly from chlorine plants and alkaline products based on mercury cells, to prevent its resale, given that there are about 12 000 tonnes of mercury in europe. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all transport services by rail, road and inland waterway.
in writing. when it comes to the transferability of pension rights, at least two fundamental aspects must be taken into account: ensuring workers' rights and the sustainability of public social security systems. in this case, it is only the supplementary pension schemes and not the public social security schemes. in the light of these two aspects, we consider the amendments tabled in the report to be negative, which amend the european commission's initial proposal to raise the age of access to supplementary pension schemes from 21 to 25 and to make the acquisition of pension rights conditional on a minimum period of five years. however, it should also be borne in mind that supplementary pension schemes cannot and should not replace public schemes. public social security schemes, based on solidarity and universality, are one of the pillars of any state and a fundamental guarantee of a more just and equal society. finally, we regret the rejection of the amendments we tabled, in particular the one which sought to combine the european commission's original position on the minimum age of 21 with the two-year entitlement period, which were more favourable to workers. hence our final vote against.
in writing. our abstention from this vote is justified by our respect for the sovereign decision of a member state to join the euro area. but our opposition to the creation of economic and monetary union and the euro zone is well known. the example of portugal shows how the euro is an instrument for promoting wage moderation and labour flexibility. by supporting nominal convergence rather than real convergence, it is becoming a factor that is detrimental to growth, employment and living conditions, and is always at the service of the large european multinationals and financial groups. it is also stressed that the question of accelerating the enlargement of the euro area is also linked to political criteria, in particular the strengthening of political integration and the euro area itself. with the two new member states - malta and cyprus - the euro area now comprises more than half the member states of the european union. this is an important 'symbolic' issue at a time when the discontent of workers and the population is growing in the eurozone and when the future constitutional treaty is being discussed. the majority therefore accepts accession, even if malta does not meet all the criteria for nominal convergence. as in the past, this is not an 'economic' decision but a political one.
in writing. it is well known that we rejected the creation of economic and monetary union and the euro, as can be seen in the vote on the european parliament's resolution of 2 may 1998, which established the euro zone, made up of the 12 founding countries, including portugal. we believe that monetary policy and the ability to issue currency is a matter for the member states alone and we have therefore rejected this transfer of sovereignty which makes it impossible to respond to the economic and social problems of each country, of which portugal is an example. at the moment, the enlargement of the euro area is also linked to political criteria, namely to strengthen political integration and the euro area itself, as this case clearly demonstrates, since malta does not meet all the nominal convergence criteria. however, with the two new member states - malta and cyprus - the euro area now comprises more than half the member states of the european union. this is an important 'symbolic' issue at a time when the discontent of workers and the population is growing in the eurozone and when the future constitutional treaty is being discussed. however, we respect the sovereign decision of a member state to join the euro area, which justifies our abstention.
in writing. we regret the significant rejection by the majority of the european parliament of the amendments tabled by our group to ensure that 'the galileo programme must not under any circumstances be used for military purposes' and that 'safeguards should be provided against any future privatisation' of this programme, especially as its implementation will be fully ensured by public funding. does this mean that, after such a large public investment, it is already considered unacceptable to conclude a concession contract for its future exploitation by a private entity? our position is clear. we believe that the galileo programme (european radio navigation and satellite positioning programme) can contribute to cooperation, scientific and technical progress and the exchange and accessibility of information. this project should be based on a public investment and control strategy in order to provide a public service, ensuring equal access for all users and free use of the information available to them. it is a project in which the rights, guarantees and freedoms of citizens must be fully guaranteed and not used for military and/or security purposes.
in writing. we need no more than the first recital in the preamble to this report and its title to justify our vote against it. the objective of community public procurement law is to open (liberalise would be the better word) the public markets of the member states to cross-border competition in order to support the development of the internal market, in line with the liberalisation agenda contained in the lisbon strategy. we are of course in favour of national rules for the transparency of public procurement, without denying the possibilities of using public markets to promote the economic fabric and national small and mediumsized enterprises, given their size and importance. but there is a substantial difference here which justifies our vote. the fact is that this matter should remain the responsibility of the member states. as regards public procurement, we note that it is also important as an instrument for promoting social and environmental policy, since it may contain criteria relating to both areas for the award of contracts. this utility cannot be restricted at a supranational level in the name of non-discrimination rules or other economic interests.
in writing. i voted in favour of the kinnock report (a6-0220/2007) on 'halfway to the millennium development goals' because i believe that we need a broad partnership to achieve the millennium development goals. it is therefore desirable that the national parliaments and civil society in the countries concerned should be involved. one of the key points for achieving these goals is to reduce poverty by 50% by 2015, with particular attention to problems such as hiv/aids, tuberculosis and malaria. gender inequalities and discrimination against women are also elements to be taken into account in development programmes.
in writing. it is good that the report recognizes the seriousness of the world situation. moreover, as the 2006 un report on the mdgs points out, progress in reducing hunger has been too slow and the numbers have actually increased in recent years, with 854 million people (17% of the world population) going hungry every day and almost 16,000 children dying every day from hunger-related causes. however, once again the report ignores the causes that are at the root of this intolerable situation. it is necessary to point out that, while 16 000 children die every day from hunger-related causes: - the us administration has budgeted for 2007 over 600 billion dollars for military spending; - i know . the 691 richest people in the world have a net worth of $2.2 trillion, or the combined wealth of the 145 poorest countries. - the 500 richest people have a combined income greater than the 416 million poorest people; - i know . the richest 8 million people have a net worth equal to 80% of the gdp of all the countries in the world. this is the root of the problem.
in writing. in the space between the explanatory statement and the vote there are two notes which i think are relevant. the first paragraph of the resolution states that 'the overarching objective of development cooperation is, and must be, the fight against poverty; it is stressed, however, that this struggle is not limited to material growth and that therefore the building of democracy, the promotion of fundamental human rights, the rule of law and the principles of justice, equity, transparency and accountability must always be central themes of such cooperation. i did not oppose this resolution because i felt that the concerns in question appeal to the highest denominator that we are capable of, but i think that the idea should be emphasized that there is no effective fight against poverty without combating its causes. and among the structural causes of poverty will always be bad government. that is why, and not because of the desire to impose any model, it is so important to do both fights simultaneously. otherwise, we are solving a problem today that will be repeated tomorrow. finally, it is regrettable that, as stated in the report, 'portugal, which is due to host the eu-africa summit during its presidency, achieved only 0.21% of oda/gni in 2006'.
in writing. as is clear from the resolution adopted here, the work of the acp-eu joint assembly in 2006 and in previous years is an excellent way of creating the structures, relations and dialogues that are indispensable for laying the foundations for a good relationship between the two parties and for the development of truly useful projects. that said, it should be noted that the path traveled is commendable, but our concerns should be based on the path to be traveled. we have an obligation (as much moral and ethical as it is in our own interests) to support the development of the associated countries, to develop with them the mechanisms for opening up economies and to make globalisation an essentially virtuous movement, and it is up to us all to avoid, reduce and make up for the shortcomings it brings. in this sense, and for some of these partners, it is of the utmost importance that the next eu-africa summit, to be held during the portuguese presidency, be consequential. realism with results is preferable to utopias without history.
on behalf of the pse group. these last few years have not given much cause for rejoicing to advocates of arms control and disarmament anchored in multilateral legal instruments. the decision by the un general assembly last december to officially open the process of drafting a global arms trade treaty (att) is indeed a rare occasion for celebration. it is not surprising that the united states of america has voted unopposed against the resolution which gave birth to this process. this treaty is not just about finding a common legal denominator for the import, export and transfer of arms, about giving a global response to a completely globalised trade and about creating uniform criteria which subject arms trade to the imperatives of human rights, stability and sustainable development. it is also a question of mobilizing public opinion in the developed countries against the opacity that defines the legal contracts for the sale of millions of arms to allied countries. the scandalous decision by the uk government to close the latest investigation into the sale of arms from that country to saudi arabia, and the corruption at the highest level that accompanied it, is a paradigmatic example of the sui generis nature of this trade. it is only in this area that a european government dares to stop a serious investigation in the name of the national interest. it is because of the special treatment that the arms trade has received from governments around the world that a treaty is needed that is specifically designed to control it. the european union can and must lead efforts in this area, striving to ensure that the lessons learned from the interpretation and application of its code of conduct, in particular with regard to the criteria of sustainable development and human rights, are applied in the new treaty, because these are two particularly linked aspects, as mrs ferrero-waldner has stressed. in this connection, the conclusions of the last general affairs council, which stress the importance of joining forces with other states and regional organisations in the preparation of a new treaty, are welcomed. the european union now has only to transform this goodwill into a diplomatic strategy towards the att, duly anchored in a common position of the council. until reason and scruples once again honor the white house with their presence, european leadership in this area is particularly urgent.

in writing. the question that inevitably arises when we discuss the subject of this report is what the european union's financial aid to palestine should be used for, what strategy it should follow. i believe that there are three certainties that must be part of this response: support for the people, encouragement of the organization of a future palestinian state in terms that are clearly democratic and respectful of human rights and, finally, promotion of peace. as regards the past, the results of the investigations of the european anti-fraud office (olaf) cannot leave us in a good mood. 'according to the information available so far in the olaf press release, there is no evidence of armed actions or illegal activities financed by ec contributions to the palestinian authority.' however, it is also known that 'there are ... serious indications that support the hypothesis that part of the funds of the palestinian authority have been used by some people for purposes other than those for which they were intended'. eu support must be visible, recognised and effective in achieving these objectives. unfortunately, it is not certain that this was the result of our initiatives. although it is fair to say that the eu's role in that region is essentially positive.
in writing. the resolution proposed by the committee on development of the european parliament is both relevant and meaningful, and it illustrates, by a few examples, what has long been known, namely that the stated objectives are often in contradiction with the policies and measures implemented. the parliamentary committee points out that, in the context of the 'regional strategy paper 2007-2013' and the 'multiannual indicative programme for asia' proposed by the european commission, and in view of the regulation establishing a financing instrument for development cooperation - which states that 'the primary and fundamental objective of cooperation under this regulation is the eradication of poverty in partner countries and regions in the context of sustainable development' - it is not understood, for example, that 'in the context of support to the association of southeast asian nations (asean), the stated objectives of the institutional support programme and dialogue between regions' include support for 'eventual negotiations for the conclusion and implementation of an eu-asean free trade agreement'. it is not clear how this intention fits in with the overriding objective of poverty eradication in the context of official development assistance. just the tip of the iceberg.
in writing. the united nations general assembly adopted a resolution last december which initiated a process which is intended to lead to the creation of an arms trade treaty. this resolution was supported by 153 countries, with the us being the only un member state to vote against the creation of the treaty. as our group in this house has pointed out - and as the 2007 sipri annual report shows - world military expenditure in 2006 was usd 1 104 billion in current prices, an increase of 3.5% on 2005, and the same expenditure increased by 37% between 1997 and 2006. in the context of this very dangerous development, there is a succession of situations which also show that the illegal arms trade has increased considerably (see the alleged payment of over £1 billion in bribes by bae systems, with the consent of the british ministry of defence, to saudi prince bandar bin sultan). however, it must be stressed that the regulation of arms trade will be more relevant if it is accompanied by a process of multilateral and reciprocal disarmament, in particular the dismantling of the huge nuclear arsenals.
in writing. my agreement with the contents of this report is substantive. states have the right and the duty to defend their populations and to guarantee the peace and integrity of their territories. on the contrary, illegal, irresponsible and unethical trade is one of the main factors in promoting conflict, war and death. the arms trade, which lacks an international code to prevent it and to condemn those who practice it, demands our active and consistent repudiation. in the future, but also today. even if the tax code at international level does not yet exist, the eu member states and our allies should not be less demanding and rigorous in this matter. there are values that cannot be compromised.
in writing. we abstained in the final vote on the report because our most important proposals were not included, namely the following: - stresses the importance of specialised training (initial and continuing) for judges working with juvenile offenders and the placement of experts from other areas in juvenile courts so that they can intervene in good time. we believe that it is necessary to give greater value and visibility to the rights of children and we think it is useful to encourage harmful intervention in the cases of young offenders, in particular by suspending the process with the implementation of behaviour plans for the child, involving him and his parents or legal representatives. we know that in most cases there are socioeconomic reasons for the phenomenon of juvenile delinquency, and that it is therefore necessary to improve the living conditions of families so that they can give more attention to children and young people. we therefore advocate a commitment to prevention rather than to legal action, as the epp tried to do, which, although it did not fully achieve its objectives, worsened the initial report.
in writing. the latest commission communication on this issue advocates a coherent approach, undertaken in collaboration with the countries of origin of immigration, in particular illegal immigration. it is a correct approach, which we welcome. in parallel - as an integral part of this policy - channels must be created to facilitate legal immigration, either by making the risks of illegal immigration and its consequences known, or by making legal channels simple and transparent. however, this perspective also implies the need to invest in creating employment opportunities in these countries. otherwise, as long as there is misery on one side and an attraction factor on the other (the possibility of getting a job), there will always be immigration, illegal if you cannot get in in another way. finally, in this context, the question of the need for reinforced and renewed cooperation with the mediterranean countries arises, not only because of immigration but also because of the need to improve the quality of life in the mediterranean.
in writing. asylum applications are increasing every day throughout the union. the desperation of many has shown us tragic consequences. it is of the utmost importance to the eu to establish common rules to avoid a repetition of such situations and to create conditions for mutual assistance within the union, since the pressures on states differ, often due to their geographical location. the establishment of a common european asylum system must therefore be based on three main pillars: the introduction of a harmonised procedure, the sharing of information on countries of origin and the strengthening of cooperation between member states in order to assist those member states which are under the greatest pressure. it is therefore necessary to promote the interrelationship between the authorities of the member states, with the ultimate aim of improving the quality of the decision-making process, which should be faster, fairer and more reliable. only then can we aim for a common asylum system by 2010.
the expression of a genuine desire for dialogue based on the european union's respect for cuba was what should actually be on the table in the european parliament. in our view, the establishment of an open dialogue on all matters of mutual interest naturally requires that the obstacles which have been created to make it difficult or even impossible be removed. this means demanding the definitive lifting of the sanctions imposed by the european union in 2003, which are now temporarily suspended, and the definitive lifting of the european union's common position on cuba. these measures would effectively open the way to the normalisation of relations between the european union and that country. however, this is not the choice of those who forced this debate onto the agenda of the european parliament, the same people who signed the motion for a resolution put to the vote today. its aim is to promote the isolation of cuba, in line with the unacceptable blockade imposed on cuba by the us administration. the aim is to promote blatant and unreserved interference in the internal situation of this country, seeking to impose, by external pressure, decisions which only the cuban people have the sovereign right to take. but reality shows that the best response to such intentions is the broad prestige, the deep significance that this country has and the active solidarity towards cuba and its people on the part of millions and millions of human beings all over the world.
author. – madam president, i headed the eu election observation mission in ethiopia in 2005. at that time, opposition leaders warned the eu that the elections would be another scam by prime minister meles zenawi to fool the international community and that they all would end up in jail or killed. we, the eu, persuaded them not to boycott the elections, promising to watch and ensure accountability. the ethiopians believed us and voted massively and in an orderly manner. however, when people protested peacefully against electoral fraud, government forces resorted to brutal repression. in june and november, hundreds were killed in massacres and thousands were wounded and imprisoned, including the leaders who had warned the eu. they are among the 38 political prisoners found guilty on 11 june of this year in a farcical trial in which they were not able to present their defences. sentences are due next july, possibly carrying the death penalty, against some of the most representative, articulate and courageous leaders of ethiopia – elected members of parliament, human rights defenders, journalists, activists for development, teachers and other prisoners of conscience. professor mesfin woldemariam, aged 77, the respected founder of the ethiopian human rights council, is one of them. the eu is the main donor of aid in ethiopia. i have seen the difference it makes there. it can do it again if the commission, council and member states stop turning a blind eye. they must act immediately, holding the government of ethiopia accountable to human rights commitments under the cotonou agreement, holding prime minister meles zenawi personally responsible and pressing for the release of the prisoners without delay and unconditionally. they must follow the recommendations made by this parliament in several resolutions, including the one we will approve today, not to further let down the ethiopian people, not to further discredit europe’s commitment towards development in africa and not to further betray our basic values of democracy and human rights.

in writing. the mandate for the intergovernmental conference (igc) on the reform of the treaties, defined at the last european council under the german presidency, confirms what we have long been denouncing, namely that those who did not accept the results of the referendums held in france and the netherlands - who rejected the content of the so-called 'european constitution' - almost immediately began to plot ways of circumventing the sovereignly expressed will of these two peoples. the mandate for the cig speaks for itself. the aim is to recover the essential content of the draft treaty which has already been rejected - overcoming the contradictions, especially those of those who, committed to holding referendums, now seek to avoid them - by disguising it as a 'reform treaty' and setting aside its 'constitutional character' to better disguise the operation. those who repeat to the end that the new draft treaty is imbued with democracy are, after all, the same people who, once again, are preparing the way to avoid the holding of binding national referendums before any ratification of a new draft treaty, a fact all the more serious as it is an attempt to recover the qualitative leap in the federalist, neoliberal and militarist project embodied in the rejected 'european constitution'. we can say that this is a doubly unacceptable process!

mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, how many amateur or professional cooks in europe or elsewhere have thought that the excessive use of flavourings can be harmful to health? very few, certainly. how many of us who enjoy the taste of oregano or cloves could imagine that in some extreme cases flavoring food could be dangerous? probably not anyone. and yet, experts say that there can be food poisoning and allergies if the use of flavorings does not meet consumer standards. consumers know, and if they do not know, they should know, that the consumption of chemical ingredients is not the same as the ingestion of natural products, and it is also known from experience that synthetic, chemical and industrial products are, as a rule, more affordable than natural ones. it is therefore necessary to inform consumers of the characteristics of flavourings and to regulate the sector. the regulations proposed by the commission and these reports are precisely in that direction. i would also like to take this opportunity to congratulate the commission and the rapporteurs, mrs westlund, mrs doyle and mrs murko, on the work they have done and on their cooperation with the shadow rapporteurs, in particular mrs murko, for whom i was the socialist party shadow rapporteur. defending public health, informing and protecting consumers are objectives which should guide all european policies. the proposal for a regulation is welcome in this respect, since it aims to update the rules on the use of flavourings to take account of technological and scientific developments in this field. the new legislation lays down clearer rules on maximum levels of substances with toxic characteristics to take account of recent scientific advice from the european food safety authority. more precise definitions are laid down for flavourings, and stricter conditions are introduced for the use of the term 'natural' in the description of flavourings. we believe that the european parliament's contribution is in line with the need for further clarification and harmonization of legislation in the field of flavourings. will the new rules make consumers more informed and protected, without harming the industry? so it's all in the benefits. the creation of a clear framework allows innovation and enables new technological developments, and the european industry itself can maintain its leading position in the field of flavourings. positive effects on public health are thus expected.

on behalf of the ppe-de group. madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by congratulating the rapporteur, mr protasiewicz, on his efforts. however, i must say that the report as it is presented to us is unbalanced. it is unbalanced because it covers, above all, the aspects of social protection - which are certainly important - but it ignores the other fundamental perspective for a reform of labour laws for the 21st century, which must address greater flexibility in the functioning of labour markets. second, the text rests on a very conservative view still fueled by a culture based on mistrust and conflict. what we need today is the opposite: a culture based on trust and cooperation between the parties. this paradigm shift, which is absolutely necessary if we are to reconcile the values of social justice and human dignity with increased competitiveness, is not taken up in this report. it would be essential that this balance, which is absent from the text of the report, be clearly expressed, because this would be the way to encourage changes in behaviour and attitudes on the part of companies and workers in order to increase levels of confidence. in short, the text of this report is somewhat disappointing, because it does not show that today's europe has the character, the talent and the capacity to become more competitive, while at the same time showing that it is capable of preserving the values which are representative of its social model. the truth is that the text in question shows no signs of rupture and shows no talent or capacity for reform. the european people's party has therefore tabled a number of amendments which, if accepted, will ensure that this report does not become a lost opportunity.
in writing. under the 2005 act of accession of bulgaria and romania, a simplified system has been established allowing their accession to conventions and protocols concluded on the basis of article 34 teu or article 293 tec, thereby eliminating the need to negotiate and conclude specific accession protocols to these conventions and thus reducing the huge bureaucracy that would be the need for ratification by the 27 member states. a list of seven conventions and protocols on justice and home affairs, which contain this convention, is therefore set out in the annex thereto. i welcome these kinds of initiatives which aim to reduce bureaucracy at community level and the excessive expenditure of time on such simple matters as this. i therefore support this council decision determining the date from which the convention of 26 july 1995 on the use of information technology in customs matters and the protocols thereto should enter into force in bulgaria and romania.
in writing. respect for the official languages of each member state of the european union is enshrined in its treaties. however, the idea is promoted that some translations are dispensable, using the financial issue as an argument and appealing to the need to define priorities and restrictions such as, for example, the length of the documents. we do not accept these guidelines because they are contrary to respect for multilingualism. we therefore reiterate our firm rejection of any attempt to limit the use of any official (and working) language in the eu on the grounds of high costs, as exemplified, as we have pointed out in due course, by the current criteria for determining the languages used during eu-acp parliamentary assemblies, which make the use of portuguese unfeasible in a discriminatory manner. we also reject the reduction in the number of interpreters and translators and the precarious or degrading working conditions for them in parliament, the commission and the council, on the pretext of fraudulent budgetary arguments, and the promotion of the outsourcing of these services, which are essential for the proper functioning of these institutions and for ensuring access to relevant information in their mother tongue for citizens of the various member states of the european union.
in writing. the establishment of a common framework for action to protect europe's critical infrastructures once again brings us face to face with the central question of the transfer of competences which are at the heart of the sovereignty of states to the eu. the definition at community level of the protection of these infrastructures, in the name of the so-called 'fight against terrorism', will place the member states before the responsibility of implementing binding measures, as is, moreover, referred to in the justification for this proposal. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. it should also be stressed, as recent events have shown, that under the pretext of the so-called 'fight against terrorism' measures have been implemented which undermine the rights, freedoms and guarantees of citizens. we hope that the concept of 'protecting europe's critical infrastructure' will not be used as an argument to curb the legitimate struggle of workers to defend their rights.
in writing. this is another step towards the liberalisation of the internal gas and electricity market in the wake of the lisbon strategy. the key words in this report are 'liberalisation' and 'market'. the basic idea of leaving is always the same. the premise that the market will solve the problem of energy supply and consumption by itself, which has already been refuted by numerous examples, is being defended with increasing fervor in an attempt to hide the fact that it is increasingly difficult to ignore that the 'market' has only worked for a few, with the accumulation of fabulous profits, but not for consumers, who are faced with the increasing price increase in the energy bill. the energy sector, as a strategic sector of a country, is vital to its independence and sovereignty. subordinating it to national and transnational private interests is an affront to the sovereignty of peoples, to the rights of workers and of the population. we therefore reject once again the liberalization of gas and electricity and advocate their retention in the public sector as the only guarantee of access to a continuous, quality and affordable service.

question no 26 by brian crowley (h-0467/07) subject: fight against youth and longterm unemployment in the eaeu what steps has the commission taken this year to combat youth and longterm unemployment in the european union and to ensure that unemployed eu citizens have access to quality training in information technology?
question no 27 by olle schmidt (h-0487/07) subject: the situation in the former yugoslavia subject: refuge for persecuted writers and journalists the european union has an obligation to support open debate in closed societies and dictatorships. in too many countries, however, freedom of expression continues to be associated with the risk of one's life. all over the world, journalists and writers are persecuted, kidnapped and murdered. freedom of expression is important for dictatorships to give way to open and democratic societies. the commission could send a clear signal of the importance of freedom of expression by offering temporary refuge to writers and journalists persecuted following restrictions on freedom of expression. the danish government has recently proposed a measure to this effect. is the commission prepared to take the initiative to offer refuge in the european union to writers threatened with persecution as a result of restrictions on freedom of expression?
question no 29 by stavros arnaoutakis (h-0500/07) subject: the situation in the former yugoslavia subject: risk of extinction of fish stocks in the aegean sea according to published scientific studies, fish stocks in the aegean sea are declining dangerously, putting fishing areas at risk of depletion. this situation is aggravated by the lack of effective measures for the sustainable management of fishing activities and by the uncontrolled use of fishing gear and practices that significantly damage the ecosystems of spawning/renewal areas of fisheries reserves. the european commission has the immediate task of protecting this region against the development of these phenomena, on the one hand to maintain at least the reserves and on the other to protect the coastal fishermen who live from fishing. how does the commission intend to deal with this serious problem?
question no 30 by marie panayotopoulos-cassiotou (h-0452/07) subject: the situation in the former yugoslavia subject: protection of children's rights in the uae's external relations commission communication on a european strategy for the rights of the child published on 4 july 2006 considers, in the context of the 'global situation' thematic unit, that some 300 000 children are fighting as soldiers in more than 30 armed conflicts worldwide. although it would be desirable if the issue of child soldiers were resolved and if the extreme situations of violation of their rights had decreased, the international press frequently refers to the phenomenon of recruitment of child soldiers with concrete examples in africa and asia. how does the commission view the use of child soldiers in military operations in its external relations? what concrete measures do you propose to take to make the fight against the military recruitment of children a priority of your political agenda in your relations with countries which force children to take part in military operations? how will the commission encourage the application of the protocol to the united nations convention on the rights of the child so that states respect the condition that they refrain from recruiting persons under 18 years of age to receive military training and to participate in armed conflict?
question no 31 by mr bernd posselt (h-0460/07) subject: the situation in the former yugoslavia subject: strategy for the black sea region what is the status of the eu's external strategy for the development of the black sea region and what role do issues related to human rights, security and external energy policy play in this context?
question no 32 by mr kirilov (h-0479/07) subject: the situation in the former yugoslavia subject: situation of bulgarian nurses and palestinian doctor in libya can the commission inform us of the current situation of the bulgarian nurses and the palestinian doctor in libya, following the recent visit to that country by commissioner benita ferrero-waldner and german foreign minister frank-walter steinmeier? can the commission draw some conclusions from this situation and present a political analysis of how the negotiations with the libyan authorities should continue to be conducted?
question no 35 by mr papastamkos (h-0453/07) subject: the situation in the former yugoslavia subject: nuclear energy in the balkans what projects have been submitted to the commission concerning the construction of new nuclear power stations in the eu member states of the balkan peninsula and in south-eastern europe in general? given the gradual closure of the reactors at the kozloduy plant and the simultaneous construction in belene, what is the energy map of the region? in view of the concerns raised by the history of intense and strong seismic activity in the region, does the commission consider that nuclear energy is the right and responsible strategic solution to meet the energy needs of the countries in the region?
question no 36 by mr papadimoulis (h-0474/07) subject: the situation in the former yugoslavia subject: maintenance of fuel stocks in greece the greek competition commission, by its decision 334/v/2007 adopted after examining the petroleum products market, put forward a series of measures and proposals in which it makes particular reference to the maintenance of reserves. the greek competition commission had already identified problems with the reservation system in a public consultation: 'the current legal regime for the maintenance of safety reserves effectively prevents the import of petroleum products and therefore competition at the refining level is limited to the two local refining units. this is because they do not face strong competitive pressures from (lower) import prices, which means that the two local refineries charge fuel companies in greece higher prices than in other eu member states despite the low cost of crude oil that local refining companies benefit from.' has the greek government adopted the measures proposed by the greek competition commission? what is the commission's view of the existing reserve system and the proposed solutions? does the commission intend to urge the greek government to adopt the above and other proposals to strengthen competition?
question no 37 by mr vincas paleckis (h-0480/07) subject: the right of asylum for refugees subject: the druzhba pipeline in july last year, russia suspended the supply of oil to lithuania and latvia through the "družba" pipeline. for almost a year now we have had no official information about the reasons for the suspension and the prospects of resuming supplies. russia justifies this by the fact that the economic and technical study on the repair of the 'družba' pipeline is still ongoing, at the end of which it will be established whether it is profitable for russia to repair the pipeline or whether a new pipeline should be built unečia velikije luki primorsk. according to the experts, the russian government has already made the political decision to abandon the "družba" pipeline, as the new pipeline would offer russia the possibility of not having to transit oil through belarusian and polish territory and instead transport it directly to the european union through the port of primorsk on the baltic sea. this runs counter to the eu's strategy of transporting less oil by sea to avoid negative ecological consequences and will have significant consequences for the oil supply of eight states, including six eu member states, namely lithuania, poland, hungary, slovakia, the czech republic and germany. in march, eu heads of state and government declared that the aim of energy policy was to ensure the security of supply of eu member states with energy sources and the diversification of their infrastructure. the closure of the druzhba pipeline will be a clear failure of this european policy. what concrete measures does the commission intend to take to remedy this situation? what are the forecasts and recommendations of the network of energy security correspondents (nesco)?

in writing. a europe which is ready to be the solution to the daily problems of its citizens can only have the best instruments and examples. so, as regards legislation on the completion of the postal services market, we see no reason to destroy systems which have been operating effectively, with economic soundness and which are in line with the beneficial development of the market and the guarantee of the maintenance of the universal service. without opposing the principle of liberalization of postal services, i think this is the appropriate place to reiterate my position that there is no economic or rational reason to exclude the 'reserved area' from the possible financing of the universal postal service. the financing through the reserved area is not only transparent, neutral, free of state subsidies, economical in transaction costs and litigation and validated by economic theories. the portuguese case is proof of this, where all services are liberalized or ready for liberalization, without this being in conflict with the financing of the universal public service through the resources coming from the reserved area, whose importance for territorial and social cohesion and for combating desertification in the most remote and difficult to reach territories we cannot ignore.

in writing. the two main trends in financial markets have been the concentration of major financial players and the exponential growth of so-called 'alternative investment activities', i.e. the derivatives market and hedge funds. today, some 30 large transnational players worldwide concentrate activity and dominate the market. the concentration of financial services at national level is continuing at an accelerated pace, with the dominance of large foreign operators in the peripheral and small markets in the new member states and in southern countries such as portugal. the use of financial instruments for pure speculative purposes, which concentrate large amounts of money, such as tax havens, together with the deregulation of the main markets and the increasing free movement of capital worldwide, implies systemic and operational risks that trigger economic and financial crises. the major multinational players are the beneficiaries of this process, and the financial services action plan at european level has contributed to this. the questions remain: why not end tax havens? why are there no taxes on capital movements?
in writing. in this vote, as we expected, the epp was able to pass some of its proposals, betting on more flexibility and fewer rights for workers. that is why, in line with our position in the committee on employment, we voted against this report. we find it very serious that this parliament, once again following the neo-liberal lines and responding to the calls of the employers' organizations, is recommending further deregulation of labour law. the assumptions in the european commission's green paper, which this report does not deny, represent a serious attack on the rights of workers won after centuries of struggle. despite some contradictions, it promotes the use and extension of flexible employment contracts with lower wages and social rights, the increase in working hours, the deterioration of social security and the retirement conditions of workers. we also regard as very serious the clear attempt to mislead workers by using as justification for this attack everything that is not currently complied with in terms of labour legislation. it is about legalizing what is now illegal. but the proof that the populations and the workers are aware of this whole situation is the various demonstrations that have already taken place against these policies, such as the recent demonstration in guimarães involving thousands of workers.
in writing. with the increasing number of cases of exploitation of workers in various countries of the european union, particularly temporary workers, it is disappointing that the european parliament has not sent a clear signal to the commission, that it does not demand an end to these situations, that it does not clearly demand compliance with the minimum standards essential for the protection of workers and the conditions of employment applicable to posted workers. the text we have adopted falls short in some respects of the text we were able to adopt here recently - the schröder report - on the posting of workers. that is why we voted against it. we regret that the proposals we put forward were rejected, in particular those relating to the requirement of a legal representative of the contracting company in the host country, those advocating that the necessary documentation be kept at the workplace or that liability be ensured in the event of illegalities and those combating the phenomenon of recruiting workers on false premises. we strongly criticise the fact that the commission's communication is unbalanced in that it considers the measures for the protection of workers to be disproportionate, but it does not consider them to be disproportionate, nor does it even analyse the insufficient implementation of the directive as a result of inadequate controls in some member states.
in writing. i support the motion because i agree with the need to promote the mobility of workers in the european union. increased mobility will help to boost the internal market, which in turn will lead to greater economic growth and more employment. the internal market of the european union still has great potential for development in a number of areas, notably in the area of freedom of movement for workers. in view of the very different social and economic realities in the various member states, i am firmly convinced that it is neither possible nor desirable to harmonise labour legislation. however, i believe that there should be an effort at union level to achieve convergence in the definition of the status of 'worker' and 'self-employed'. the commission has also taken the view that the implementation of the existing european directives, in particular on the posting of workers, should be ensured. in this particular context, it is important to improve coordination and information sharing between member states on the basis of transparent criteria.

and should serve as a model for other possible and desirable collaborations, as in the case of the acp countries. however, we can still improve cooperation between the two institutions, particularly as regards the sharing of information. parliament considers it particularly important to receive clarification on how the various national strategies can, taken together, contribute to the financial commitment to allocate 20% of the available funds to basic health care and education. as regards the priorities set out in various national strategy papers, i regret that, in general, there is no greater investment in the millennium development goals. the objective of this financial instrument is to combat poverty, in particular by achieving these objectives. several of the national strategy papers include activities related to trade, higher education, civil aviation and even the promotion of the european union in the recipient countries. parliament understands the importance of some of these actions, particularly for the authorities of the countries concerned. i think, however, that our priority, the priority of the commission, should be activities which are directly related to the achievement of the millennium development goals and which have a much more direct impact on the fight against poverty. these should be the priority. these cannot be omitted, as is the case in some
