every year, in different member states, the scourge repeats itself. in southern europe, hundreds of thousands of hectares of forest are consumed by fires, while in northern europe floods cause devastation and death. every year we repeat ourselves in the european parliament. we regret the losses and promise to correct the shortcomings. well-meaning words are not enough. on the one hand, we must prevent disasters by combating climate change and taking environmentally friendly measures, in particular by reducing greenhouse gas emissions of co2 which are responsible for global warming. on the other hand, when disasters occur, the european union must respond quickly and appropriately. this is what the citizens expect and we must recognize that the solidarity fund is not adequate to the needs and that the civil protection mechanism, which has already been perfected, does not always give the prompt response that is required.
madam president, for someone like me, who comes from the western extremities of our continent, it is impossible not to express deep respect for a people whose fate has been so often tragic, particularly throughout the 20th century, and who are now making a huge effort to find the paths of democracy and the rule of law. this was demonstrated in the streets of kiev three years ago and is still being demonstrated in the desire of the ukrainian people to join the european union one day. and we must look at this will with respect and we must send out signals, signals which involve strengthening cooperation with ukraine at the most diverse levels, supporting ukraine's development at the most diverse levels. it is true that it is not up to us to do the work that the ukrainians have to do: to consolidate their democracy, to institutionalize their rule of law fully, to overcome the problems they still face. but if it is true that this is the work of ukrainians, we must send signals, and i am convinced that this report is a good political signal that we are giving to ukraine, and for that i congratulate the author of the report.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group, first of all, i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on her own-initiative report, which highlights some points which we consider important, although we disagree with others, particularly in the context of the debate on the future of cohesion policy and the fourth report on economic and social cohesion in the european union. in this context, it is necessary to stress that disparities, particularly regional disparities, have increased very significantly with the successive enlargements of the european union, that there is evidence of the increase in regional disparities and the growth of the effects of polarization within each country, that there are currently regions and even countries in the process of divergence from the european union, and that, in general terms, there continues to be a rich centre and a poor periphery, now enlarged. in stressing these aspects, we want to highlight the need for a strong regional policy as an indispensable instrument for reducing disparities and promoting real, rather than nominal, convergence in the regions of the poorest countries of the european union. a strong regional and cohesion policy is all the more necessary as the costs of the internal market, the policy of market liberalisation and competition, economic and monetary union and the euro and its stability pact for the poorest regions and countries of the european union are accentuated. what is needed is to strengthen regional and cohesion policy, placing the proclaimed economic and social cohesion and real convergence as the central objective and policy of the european union, reinforcing the redistributive role of the community budget and adequately financing it in order to achieve the objectives it sets itself. the existence of an effective regional and cohesion policy also requires the rejection of its misuse, in particular by redirecting its funds to finance other policies and priorities which will in no way contribute to the achievement of the objectives set out above.
madam president, the report by mrs lidia de oedenberg is not only an excellent report, the result of her total openness and ability to create consensus, but it is also a reminder of the great regional disparities that exist in europe, both in the new member states and in the old ones, where many of its regions have been excluded from the group of the poorest regions, solely and exclusively for statistical reasons, statistics which are not always complete and sufficiently comparable and which therefore need to be improved. i come from an outermost region, the island of madeira, and i made a number of contributions aimed at ensuring that cohesion policy is adapted to the outermost regions, as referred to in article 29 (2), better defining the criteria for distinguishing between rich and poor regions, and strengthening research and education as a means of development, because these regions need to find ways of actually getting out of the situation in which they find themselves.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report based on the commission's green paper on the future maritime policy of the union: a european vision for the oceans and seas, because i believe that the promotion of a prosperous and sustainable maritime economy is fundamental. this report presents an integrated policy approach to this issue, with concrete proposals on shipping, maritime safety and security, tourism, fisheries, port policy, the marine environment, research, industry and spatial planning, including the proposal to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from ships and the creation of a european coast guard.
in writing. we believe that a maritime policy based on cooperation between the different member states and translated at community level into a coordination of synergies that would add more value and boost the policies and measures linked to the sea defined by each country (such as fisheries, transport, environment, energy, among others) could have a positive impact. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. in this connection, the rejection of our amendments is significant, as they indicate the principle issues we do not renounce, such as:- full respect for the sovereignty and competence of each member state in the management of its territorial waters and exclusive economic zones (eez), particularly with regard to marine resources - in particular biological ones - and the issues of safety, rescue and control of navigation in these waters;- the enhancement of the fisheries sector, given its strategic importance for different countries, such as portugal, ensuring the socioeconomic sustainability of this sector through appropriate policies and financial means; that is why we are voting against it.
in writing. the first railway package, launched with the announced objective of 'laying the foundations for modal shift' - i.e. promoting the shift from road to rail - was a 'trojan horse' but sought to hide the opening up of rail transport, including freight, to competition and private interests as the first step towards full liberalisation of the rail sector at eu level. a process whose intentions we denounced and rejected from the start. as in other liberalisations promoted by the eu, one starts by using what is wrong at a given moment (by hiding the real causes of such situations, namely the systematic policies of dismantling and atrophying the public transport sector) to justify liberalising measures and pointing to the so-called 'competition' - not understanding how and why - as the solution to all the evils, this holy miracle, but in the end, with the consequences that we have pointed out in our intervention. public investment in the railway sector is undoubtedly strategic, according to the needs and options defined by each country, but not to hand it over to the profit-making logic of the big private interests, which aim to dominate this key public sector in each country by liberalising it at the level of the eu internal market.
in writing. the first railway package, which aimed to open the market to international rail freight services by 15 march 2003, has been somewhat successful. however, we can still see shortcomings and delays in transposition by the member states. the consequences of these delays have repercussions on the restructuring of railway undertakings and the creation of a genuinely competitive market. as there are still many aspects which are not fully exploited by the first railway package, we believe that it is necessary to create the resources to correct the inadequate implementation of the legislation by the member states. will we therefore need an independent and transparent national monitoring body with sufficient resources to play an active role against existing distortions of competition? we also need measures to create genuine interoperability - the lack of which in the rail networks is still the main obstacle to the achievement of an integrated european railway area - such as the rapid installation of the ertms system, especially on priority rail corridors.
in writing. dissatisfaction with the implementation and results of european transport policy does not negate the improvements that have been made, from transport safety to quality of service or the environment. there is, however, still much to be done. the limitations of community funding are one of the main causes of the inadequacy of this policy. only innovative forms of financing, such as public-private partnerships and the co-financing of projects by the member states, can prevent projects from being delayed or reoriented. the community funds for the financing of transeuropean transport projects are limited. that is why they must concentrate on cross-border sections, the added value of which will enable the creation of an interconnected and interoperable transeuropean transport network. it is, however, essential to avoid the creation of a blanket of national network parts, and the commission should ensure, in cooperation with the member states, the application and enforcement of european transport legislation. finally, enhanced cooperation at european, national, regional and local levels is needed to link good practice and transport policy with other national or community policies such as energy, environment, tourism or innovation.
in writing. we voted in favour of this resolution because we know that the reality of cardiovascular disease is a cause for concern and that it is important to increase knowledge in the area of prevention of the factors which have a negative influence on these diseases. it is therefore important to consider the actions contained in this resolution. we know that health is complete physical, mental and social well-being. but today's society is full of contradictions, because it is steeped in constant stress, lack of time to rest, spend time with the family, take care of physical health and psychological balance, added to poor diet and lack of time for sports, loss of rights at work, in particular overtime, and reduction of the period of leave, when not unemployment or permanent threat. now, all of this has serious repercussions on people's lives, on their balance and, consequently, on the proliferation of cardiovascular disease. however, this campaign to raise awareness and prevent cardiovascular disease should not be turned into a banner of the communicalization of health. what we want is to defend the public health service and the responsibility of each member state for its maintenance and management, so as to guarantee the right to health for everyone and not just those who have the money to pay for it.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the transfer of personal data to third countries. among many deplorable aspects, it is noted that:this is based on non-binding guarantees, which can be unilaterally modified by dhs at any time. these data may be used for unspecified purposes and their retention period will be extended from 3 and a half years to 15 years. furthermore, there is no guarantee that after the retention period of 15 years - 7 years 'active' and 8 years 'latent' - the data will be permanently destroyed. the dhs will be required to provide the dhs with sensitive data (e.g. personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, and trade union membership, as well as other data relating to the health or sexual life of individuals). the agreement also refers to a possible future pnr system at eu level or in one or more of its member states, and states that this data may also be made available to the us dhs. in a word, intolerable!
in writing. the report 'welcomes the favourable economic developments achieved in 2006' in the euro area, but does not disguise some concerns and risks about future developments in the euro area. the truth is that profits as a percentage of gdp are at one of the highest levels, while wages continue to lose weight and grow below labor productivity, meaning productivity gains continue to go to the employer. the report says little about the increase in inequalities and poverty in the eu, the increasing precariousness of employment and the high number of unemployed, and ignores social tensions. but it is becoming increasingly difficult to justify further wage restraint and to call for more belt-tightening when the fruits of wealth continue to go to the same financial and economic groups as always. in fact, what they want to ignore is that the big question to stop consolidating this moment in the economic cycle is to raise wages and increase public investment in order to boost demand. the report does not do exactly that, insisting on the need for fiscal consolidation and price stability, i.e. less public investment and more wage moderation. this is a strategy which we reject and hence our vote against this report.
in writing. the situation in palestine is a matter of great concern. beyond proving that israel is not at the heart of the issue - a fact that so many have so often claimed - it also demonstrates two unfortunate truths. on the one hand, there are groups interested in and willing to do anything to obtain power by force and to exercise it violently; on the other hand, an authority whose survival is threatened is a partner incapable of making agreements and of building itself. the middle east, israel, europe, we all need to have a reliable partner at the table to negotiate and a strong partner to deliver on the deal. without these elements there will be no successful peace negotiations. but it is also impossible to achieve peace and security without determination. our unambiguous objective must be to ensure peaceful and secure coexistence between two states, nothing less. and that requires a real recognition of the obstacles to peace and security, rather than, as so often happens, assigning blame as if all actions were equal.
in writing. the present statement of vote is only to emphasize that, although the resolution mentions some of the most important aspects of the current situation in pakistan, its content ends up concealing the participation of the government of pakistan in the invasion and occupation of afghanistan by the us and its allies and its subsequent 'replacement' by nato. nothing about the pressures that pakistani officials have already admitted to having suffered from the us and its european allies to aid the attack on afghanistan. nor does it say anything about the nato bombing that has been carried out on the border between afghanistan and pakistan, which has led to the deaths of many innocent civilians on both sides of the border. an example of applying double standards...
in writing. the fact that europe, the united states and the world in general need pakistan's cooperation in the important fight against terrorism, and al-qaeda in particular, does not mean that the pakistani government, which is now a de facto presidential regime, has our unconditional support. on the contrary, i did. the fundamental values, the inalienability of democracy, deserve our defence and it will have to be in this spirit that the european union will manage its relations with pakistan, particularly on the eve of electoral events. that said, it is necessary to stress that the recent events at the red mosque prove - as if it were not yet demonstrated - that radical islam is a very real, very dangerous and very active threat.
in writing. after the doha declaration, the implementation of the mechanism for access to medicines was a failure, and it served mainly as an alibi to include the least developed countries, especially those in africa, in a negotiating agenda for the liberalization of world trade. the big pharmaceutical monopolies are not willing to lose the fabulous profits from patents and the bulky health "business". the right to life and health of millions of human beings is thus denied. research on a cure is oriented towards the "palliative", as continued illness is more profitable. capitalism is the commodification of life. the world bank and the imf condition loans/aid on the privatization and liberalization of national health sectors, increasingly in the hands of large multinational operators. health cannot be overridden by the wto, the primacy of competition and trade. the right of each country to guarantee the right to health must be guaranteed. the public sector has an irreplaceable role to play in ensuring this right, in particular by providing preventive and primary health care and promoting research for the benefit of all, but also by producing medicines and vaccines without the constraints of patents and other forms of licensing that inhibit access to essential goods for the people.
in writing. there are aspects of this report on ukraine which become recurrent whenever it comes to relations between the eu and eastern european countries, such as the recommendation to deepen internal reforms so that these countries fully adapt to the eu's neoliberal agenda. in this case, the first objective is the gradual economic integration of ukraine into the eu internal market, ensuring the creation of a competitive market economy (with particular emphasis on the energy sector), the close participation of ukraine in the eu's common foreign and security policy, and, we add, the elimination from reality (and, if possible, from memory) of any trace of the civilizational advances achieved with the first experience of building socialism in the world. despite the domination ambitions of the us/nato/eu major powers towards this country - with a particularly significant strategic importance in europe - they will always have to face those in ukraine who resist them. hence the importance of expressing solidarity with the ukrainian people and with the recent demonstrations in odessa against the us/nato military exercise - sea breeze 2007 - in that country.
in writing. we regret the rejection of our postponements which:- recommended that, in addition to paying attention to the specific situation of the regions affected by the so-called 'statistical effect' which have suffered cuts in the current financial framework, the need for its revision be put forward so that these regions receive the same level of support as they would receive if the eligibility criterion were an eu-15 benchmark; - i know . calls on the commission to speedily specify the content of the 'enhanced partnership' it has announced for the outermost regions, including the introduction of permanent, flexible and adequately funded policies and measures which are able to adapt to the needs of each of these regions and help to overcome the permanent constraints on development faced by them; or that:- urge the commission to study new ways of measuring the different aspects of regional development, not only on the basis of gdp per capita but also on other indicators such as unemployment rates and quantitative and qualitative indicators of social status (such as poverty rate, education levels and income inequalities), while improving the methodology for calculating purchasing power parities through the development of better regional and national indicators.
in writing. despite the repeatedly stated 'european crisis', one of the policies that defined its principles, values and strategies has fortunately not been called into question. in general, both european citizens and political leaders remain firmly convinced that the cohesion effort responds to a need for solidarity between partners in the same community, but also because cohesion represents an investment in the generalization of the conditions for economic growth of the whole in which we are integrated. there are, however, two notes that must be made. on the one hand, it is necessary to insist on the question of statistical error. there are several regions which have become statistically richer than they really are, simply as a result of enlargement. to exclude them from the support framework would not only be unfair but also wrong in the objectives of the policies pursued so far. finally, it is important to adapt cohesion policies to the new economic reality. the causes of backwardness and poverty, or in other words the factors contributing to this situation, are now distinct, which is why it is necessary to adapt and adapt these policies, avoiding that the current funds merely respond to old imbalances.

mr president, we all regret what has happened in greece and what has happened in the united kingdom. we all sympathize with the victims and hope that such situations will not happen again. unfortunately, as the leader of my group has already said, every year at this time the european parliament adopts a resolution deploring the natural disasters that occur during parliamentary holidays and proposing measures that take time to be adopted. we must move from words to deeds so that this situation does not repeat itself every year, as it is happening, with more violence and more victims. there is every reason to believe that the risks are increasing because of climate change and global warming. there are a number of documents which point to solutions - the barnier document and other documents presented by parliament and the commission have already been mentioned here - not only to improve the effectiveness of the civil protection mechanism at european level but also to strengthen the means at national level. as for the costs that are often cited, it is important to say that when tragedy happens it is necessary to fight it and rebuild the heritage that has been destroyed, which costs money. in fact, it's more expensive to cure than to prevent. one of the resolutions adopted by parliament provides for the drawing up of maps identifying fire risk areas, which should be taken into account in the urban management of the territory. it is also necessary to provide for various sanctions, such as not allowing construction in the burned areas for 10 or 15 years. there are member states' competences and i recall that portugal also had to deal with devastating fires in 2003 and 2005 and that this year it was fortunately able to help greece by sending airborne firefighting equipment there. it is therefore necessary to strengthen coordination at european level, but also to improve mechanisms at national level. it would be desirable if the commission were to put forward a directive on fires, as it has done with regard to floods. i would like to end by wishing commissioner dimas well.
mr president, i would like to begin by adding my words to those of all those who have expressed their solidarity with the victims of these disasters, from the canary islands in the west to greece and bulgaria in the east. i would also like to emphasize, as has already been done here, the role of the civil protection services, and in particular the fire brigades, in combating these disasters. i would particularly like to welcome the statement made by commissioner dimas on 31 july, in which he stressed the importance of the report by former commissioner barnier and its implementation in order to ensure that europe is properly equipped with a civil protection mechanism capable of providing the answers it needs. it is true that there is coordination, but we must not forget the limits of that coordination, namely that, for example, the various appeals made by bulgaria last july were not answered. the path ahead seems to me to be very clear: the commission must formalise what is contained in this report as its proposal, and we in parliament, and of course the council, must give due attention to and follow up these proposals which are extremely important for the future of european civil protection.
in writing. we are dealing here with an initiative by the republic of finland to adapt the regulation on analysis files to the legislation now in force. the 2003 protocol, which entered into force in april this year, amended title iii of the europol convention, in particular the part concerning the creation of analysis files and the collection, processing, use and deletion of personal data contained in those files. the implementing rules which have been adopted will therefore have to be amended accordingly. it is therefore a measure which, although temporary, is necessary and timely. in fact, this measure should have a short period of application, since all the previous acts should be repealed on the date on which the council decision establishing the european police office enters into force.
in writing. although we regard this resolution as positive, and therefore voted in favour of it, we stress the absence of some important proposals (which have been referred to more than once in previous ep resolutions) and the insistence on others on which we have the greatest doubts. we therefore insist on the need to revise the solidarity fund regulation to cover regional disasters and to create mechanisms to support the affected populations and reforestation, which include a component for the prevention of large-scale disasters caused by climate change. a public agricultural insurance scheme, financed by the european union, should be established to guarantee farmers a minimum income in the event of public disasters such as droughts, fires and floods. it is necessary to invest in a culture of prevention that takes account of natural disasters of the mediterranean type and a profound change in the cap to combat the abandonment of production by many small and medium-sized farmers and family farming, stimulating agricultural production, biodiversity and land use. we have doubts about the community civil protection mechanism, first of all because it can be another way of subtracting important aspects of national sovereignty, such as the management of natural resources, particularly forests.
in writing. i would like to express my deepest sorrow for the victims of the serious forest fires which occurred during the summer - particularly in greece - and my solidarity with their families and all the people affected. we must move from rhetoric to action. the eu must activate the financial instruments and means to ensure that the material needs of the affected populations are met and to promote the socioeconomic and environmental recovery of the affected regions. in the light of the debate, i would like to recall some of the proposals we put forward in 2003 and 2005 which are still very relevant: - the maintenance of the eligibility of regional disasters for the solidarity fund;- the recognition of the specific nature of mediterranean natural disasters, where more than 90% of forest fires and drought occur;- the creation of a community programme for the protection of forests against fires;- the evaluation of the possibility of creating an agricultural disaster fund;- the granting of special attention to the most disadvantaged regions in the event of natural disasters. finally, i would like to stress that if, instead of increasing military spending, the money was channelled into preventing, combating and rehabilitating areas affected by natural disasters, the impact and consequences of such disasters would be significantly reduced.
in writing. for the sake of consistency, in view of what we have said in the past and what we expect from the european solidarity fund, it is clear that my vote here would have to be in favour. but there is more than just consistency in this vote. european integration has, amongst its many advantages, the advantage of scale and, consequently, the advantage of solidarity economies of scale as well. without making the member states and their governments any less responsible, it is possible and desirable that a european solidarity effort should make it possible to deal with disasters which are more the result of nature and its increasing unpredictability than of errors in the administration of the territory. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment is a very important one, and i would like to thank the rapporteur for the work he has done. i therefore believe that it is time to review many of our policies, particularly in the field of forests and rural development, but not only that, also in the field of environmental rules, in order to prevent man from making the destructive force of nature even more destructive.
in writing. the report states that simplification of the regulatory framework to ensure the clarity, effectiveness and quality of legislation is an indispensable condition for achieving the objective of better regulation and constitutes a priority action of the european union. however, it is claimed that there are some 500 new legislative initiatives (200 of which for 2007 alone) contained in a separate continuing programme specifically targeting codifications, which demonstrates the bureaucratic complexity of the european union. it also calls for simplification at european level to be accompanied by appropriate simplification at national level to ensure that the benefits of community simplification are not compromised by national regulations or technical barriers. but it is necessary to take account of what is purely bureaucratic and what are rights that are intended to be called into question. we agree that it is proposed that the commission should definitely opt for recasting as a regular legislative technique, so that for each initiative the full text is available, even if there are specific amendments, with a clear indication of the new parts and those that have not been changed, which would make community legislation more readable and more transparent.
in writing. we agree with the rapporteur that the notion of soft law, based on common practice, is ambiguous and harmful and should not be used permanently in the documents of the community institutions, although we disagree on other points in the report. however, soft law instruments are legitimate when they can be used as interpretative or preparatory tools for binding legislative acts, but they should not be treated as legislation, nor should they be given any normative effect, and it is for each country to decide on their use, in particular when they help interpret national provisions adopted with a view to ensuring their implementation, or when they are intended to supplement community provisions with a binding character. it is clear that so-called non-binding legal instruments cannot replace existing legal acts and instruments to ensure continuity of the legislative process. the commission should therefore pay particular attention to the effects of soft law on consumers and their possible remedies before proposing any measures involving soft law instruments.
in writing. this is a report drawn up from an extremely neoliberal perspective, demonstrating once again that this european parliament wants more and more liberalization, more benefits for capital, for economic and financial groups which already have profits of 35% or more. in addition to the praise for the great benefits that the single market brings (to the large economic and financial groups), it is stressed that protectionist attitudes persist, which must be combated, and that progress must be made in other areas which are not yet fully liberalised and integrated, such as financial and tax services, in addition to transport, postal services and energy. by distorting reality, they try to hide the real effects of the single market, such as the increase in costs, the reduction in the quality of services provided, the loss of jobs, and many others. the report is an attempt to push further the liberalisation of public services, the transfer of political power from the national to the transnational level and the attack on consumer and workers' rights, and it can only be voted against.
with this own-initiative report, whose rapporteur we would like to welcome, we hope to be contributing to the definition of a strategic framework for the logistics of freight transport within the framework of our european union. we see logistics as a necessary tool for the effective planning and implementation of a balanced and sustainable use of the various modes of transport. logistics is thus at the heart of a process of rationalisation to achieve the most competitive and sustainable levels in the future. despite the benefits that modern logistics brings in the areas of economic efficiency and competitiveness, the optimisation of the use of resources, the creation of employment opportunities, and the protection of the environment and the improvement of safety, we recognise that there are still problems to be solved, including the chronic under-funding of the tens, in which the development of freight transport logistics is embedded. alternative forms of financing must therefore be explored, using public-private initiatives, the eib, the structural funds, etc. another point to be noted, introduced in a timely manner in this report, is the need for the commission's action plan to include measures to combat organized crime in the international transport of goods, promoting the safety of cargo against theft and other diversions. it is up to the public authorities to regulate these and other aspects and, on the other hand, to facilitate the multimodal transport of goods, which is essentially an entrepreneurial activity. measures such as one-stop-shops and the reduction of red tape reduce costs and introduce a healthier and more competitive economy in the sector. given the high growth rates forecast for freight transport, the future of logistics will be crucial to benefit from efficient, sustainable, affordable and safe transport. to this extent, we are sure that logistics will increasingly be an essential tool for achieving the lisbon objectives.

i have listened carefully to the communications from both the council and the commission, and i must say that i am convinced that we will have this discussion again - in the same exact terms as we are having it - in a few months' time, because for dr lobo antunes and commissioner frattini, everything that has been done is well done, it has been well done, there is no error, there is no assessment that allows us to detect a single error. we just have to insist on more of the same, and that's the first problem: you're wrong! as long as we continue to treat terrorism as a problem of police and intelligence services, we are only delaying the essential. terrorism is now closely linked to the symmetrical political logic which promotes the clash of civilizations and war, and your silence on this is deafening. for example, commissioner frattini announces measures to control explosives at a time and in an era when the war in iraq has become a private multi-million dollar business, or when the united states outsources the collection and processing of classified information. control the explosives? i know one way: nationalize production and trade. only this can prevent terrorism and counterterrorism from becoming the face and the crown of the same coin: the one that turns life and death into a business.

terrorism challenges our free and open society. sometimes it even tempts us to create a security right that is very close to eroding our civilized values. the european union must therefore urgently establish a common code that makes clear the principles and methods. first, the guarantee of the principles of human dignity and the rule of law on all fronts in the fight against terrorism. we cannot allow the moral foundations of democracy, which are based on these values, to be undermined. as simone de beauvoir said, we cannot allow our executioners to create bad habits in us. secondly, it is necessary to create uniform legislation in the member states. the union must be a union in this respect. the fight against terrorism makes it urgent to practice unity and consistency of rules; it cannot be left to the impulses of each member state and its public opinion on the occasion. thirdly, it is necessary to promote networking and to promote consensus by giving the measures legitimacy in the european parliament and in national parliaments. fourthly, the european union's efforts to establish an international united nations mechanism for monitoring emergency practices and legislation. this is a large-scale fight, not just a fight between europe or the euro-atlantic axis. finally, the fight against terrorism requires us to make an effort to create a more just and balanced international community, to diagnose the causes and the fractures, to promote a culture of rights across the peoples and to make a huge effort in dialogue between civilizations. terrorism is a complex phenomenon. we cannot answer it with a simplistic interpretation.

in writing. we believe that the sustainability of fisheries resources is necessary for the continuation of fishing activity and the viability of the fisheries sector, but we reject a fleet management policy - like the one adopted in the eu - and the encouragement of the permanent slaughter of vessels, which has as its main consequences a sharp reduction in the means of production and a radical reduction in jobs. in order to achieve the objective of a sustainable balance between fishing capacity and opportunities, account should be taken of the socioeconomic situation of the fisheries sector by implementing mechanisms for subsidising or compensating fishermen who are affected by the economic consequences of environmentally friendly fishing and measures to reduce fishing effort, in particular in the most disadvantaged regions dependent on the sector. similarly, the adaptation of fishing effort to existing resources and the protection of the marine environment - while promoting small-scale coastal and artisanal fishing and defending fishing communities - would be particularly promoted by increasing the exclusive access zone of member states from the current 12 nautical miles to 24 nautical miles and, in the case of the outermost regions, from 100 nautical miles to 200 nautical miles.
in writing. the report says that around 110 billion tonnes/km of dangerous goods - to people and the environment - are transported in the eu each year, representing around 8% of total goods transport. of these, 58% are transported by rail, 25% by air and 17% by inland waterway. the international transport of dangerous goods is regulated by international agreements. in this context, we believe that the necessary and useful cooperation at eu level should safeguard the full sovereignty of the member states over the transport of (dangerous) goods within their territory, for example through the right to regulate, issue individual authorisations and prohibit the movement of the transport of dangerous goods for reasons of national security or environmental protection. this is a matter of principle which is even more important in the context of the unbridled liberalisation of transport promoted by the eu.
in writing. creating safe living conditions for european citizens is one of the eu's basic obligations and responsibilities. the volume of inland transport within the eu is growing steadily, and with it the volume of dangerous goods being transported. it is therefore necessary to ensure the simplification and clarity of the legislation applicable to the transport of dangerous goods. the aim of including the transport of dangerous goods by rail, road and inland waterway in a single directive can contribute to co-modality and ensure, through the rules laid down, greater safety and speed by adopting new criteria for the speed of delivery of goods and the provision of associated services. this means that transport throughout the eu - including the transport of dangerous goods - must be made safer, and i believe that this will be possible if the measures in this directive are implemented.

in writing. i believe that the threat to air safety is real and that the risks involved are enormous. i also believe that there is a proportionality between the inconvenience to passengers and the goods protected and that there is no violation of rights, freedoms or guarantees in question here, but only a technical measure which has proved effective, so i think that the european parliament is rushing and exorbitant in asking for the application of the regulation on the introduction of liquids on aircraft to be abandoned if no new evidence is presented in favour of its application. the precautionary principle advises that a small inconvenience is preferable to a catastrophe. the safety principle is that you don't go easy on yourself until you're sure of the risks involved. for these reasons i voted against the motion for a resolution on the establishment of measures to implement the common basic standards on aviation safety (the introduction of liquids on aircraft).

mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, financial crises are never confined to the financial sphere. the current crisis will make credit more restrictive and, in anticipation, it has already started to become more expensive regardless of the decision the central bank will take tomorrow. the confidence of economic operators has also declined substantially and, despite the optimism of commissioner almunia, growth in the economy is neither widespread nor guaranteed. there are indeed many regions with serious economic difficulties. it is difficult today, but i would like to have some support in justifying to the citizens that the worrying increase in household indebtedness, the disincentive to public investment, the overvaluation of exports produced in europe caused by the management of the interest rate, among other aspects, are inevitable sacrifices. traditionally, to control a nonexistent inflation. the options are now more limited to the perfectly foreseeable consequences of excessive risk exposure by financial operators which we have not been able, or have not been willing, to regulate in time. i think there are two conclusions to be drawn: the first concerns the need to improve regulation, transparency and cooperation in financial markets, as has already been pointed out. the second is the urgent need to review the relationship between monetary policy and its impact on the real economy, households, investment and employment.
the commission has not yet taken a decision on the matter, but it is still in the process of being discussed in writing. it is not enough to identify the problem when it has already become visible. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. we all know that the real economy is based on the production, distribution and consumption of goods according to people's needs, even if those needs are real, imagined or created by advertising. which means that the currency in circulation should be equivalent to this real economy. but the greed of those who want more and more profits led to the creation of financial exchanges and the speculative profits of the casino economy, secondary to the productive area and promoting the financialization of the system. this is the root of the current problem that central banks have sought to mitigate by either throwing even more money into circulation or raising interest rates. these are processes which have their limits, otherwise they will fuel new speculative bubbles or further degrade the real economy by increasing the costs to households.
the green paper on climate change draws attention to natural phenomena aggravated by climate change. climate change is expected to lead to reduced rainfall, increased temperature, and increased incidence of heat waves and droughts, which will further contribute to desertification. unlike other natural disasters, the impacts of drought do not affect infrastructure, but the productive and environmental fabric, and the lives of people. one of the serious consequences of drought is the difficulty of supplying drinking water to the populations. studies reveal that droughts and floods kill more people than any other natural disaster. on the other hand, eight million people die each year from diseases related to the consumption of unsafe water, such as diarrhea, cholera and typhoid fever. lack of clean water is responsible for 80 percent of the disease and death rate in developing countries. more than 4,500 children die every day from water-borne diseases. it is no accident that the informal meeting of the ministers for the environment, held in lisbon a few days ago, was devoted to the problems of water scarcity and drought, which is, moreover, one of the concerns and priorities of the environmental programme of the portuguese presidency, as has already been mentioned by the secretary of state. the conference of the parties is expected to take the appropriate decisions to combat drought and desertification and the european institutions are also expected to contribute. finally, i would like to reiterate the proposals i made in the report on natural disasters, in particular, and which the european parliament approved: the creation of a european drought and desertification observatory, with a view to collecting information and responding more effectively; the increase in preventive measures in the field of the management of drought risks, including strategies to minimise their impacts, and their incorporation into the management strategies of watersheds.

it is now clear to 77 million ethiopians and many millions of africans that the eu does not take the cotonou agreement seriously. among the elected members of parliament, journalists and activists who were imprisoned in ethiopia following the 2005 elections, observed by a european union mission, 38 were recently released thanks to repeated pressure from this parliament and the incomprehensible silence of the council. but others, such as netsanet demissie and daniel bekele, are still in prison. will they ever believe in cotonou and the eu? madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the report we are debating deserves our support, first of all because of the extent and detail with which it analyses an aspect of great relevance to the external dimension of the european union, and i would therefore like to congratulate the rapporteur. the worst thing that could happen to the european union's commitment to the global promotion of fundamental human rights would be for this to be an isolated issue, dealt with in isolation. the alternative, the good option, i believe, is one which considers the promotion of human rights to be both an ethical duty, which is not without justification, and an interest of the european union insofar as instability, migratory flows and the political-military tensions associated with their violation provoke crises which make the world a more dangerous place. the commission has not yet taken a decision on the matter. if the european union were to relate only to countries which respect human rights, as we advocate, there would be very few countries with which we would have solid relations. on the other hand, if the european union were to always opt for the realism of economic, energy, geostrategic or other interests, it would soon find that instead of defending immediate advantages, it was creating greater future dangers. what we should expect is that the european union has a coherent strategy that involves including the promotion of human rights in its external agenda in a tangible and measurable way. spending money without evaluating the outcome of its use, or proclaiming purposes that will not materialize, is not an option. in this respect, the forthcoming eu-africa summit is an opportunity that cannot be missed. if we want to help africa and africans - member of the commission. madam president, first of all allow me to thank the rapporteur, ms fraga estévez, and all the members of the committee on fisheries for a very thorough report on the implementation of sustainable fishing based on maximum sustainable yield (msy). i am pleased to see that we are in broad agreement, in particular on the need to move away from annual decision-making allowing for a more gradual approach and for better planning by the sector. a longer-term approach will also allow for more stability and sustainability in the exploitation of fisheries resources. i am sure that we are in agreement on the objectives of urgently taking measures to improve the very poor state of fisheries resources in europe in order to bring the stocks to sustainable levels, which, at the same time, will improve the profitability of the fishing industries in the long term. apart from the benefits to industry, there is an international political commitment that should be met. in particular i appreciate and share the committee on fisheries’ view that the common fisheries policy needs a new management model for the setting of fishing opportunities, the recovery of depleted stocks and the adaptation of fishing effort levels to sustainable and profitable levels. also, and very importantly, adjusting fishing efforts to msy levels is the single most important action that can be taken to reduce discarding in european waters. i am aware that there are concerns too. i share many of these concerns and know they will need to be addressed. first of all, i know that evaluating msy is not a simple matter. there are scientific uncertainties and the matter is complicated because of eco-system effects and mixed fisheries issues. fisheries science is not yet able to predict accurately what msy for any particular stock or mixture of stocks will be. but we must not only look at the difficulties. science can tell us in which direction fisheries should move in order to improve yields and decrease costs. even if the destination is imprecise, the direction is known quite well. we should start to move in the right direction and progressively evaluate and review the msy reference points as fisheries develop. mixed fishery situations need to be studied carefully and the best possible solutions identified in relation to the potential yield of the whole fisheries system. this progressive approach will allow environmental, economic and social aspects to be explored. it is also the approach that has been adopted in the long-term plan for plaice and sole in the north sea, which was adopted this year and which i consider to be a good model for the implementation of this approach. as your report stresses, it is an urgent matter to start moving in the right direction. let me underline here that the long-term management plans in practical terms move fisheries management in the right direction: that is, away from over-exploitation and not necessarily to a fixed msy target. the plans include provisions for regular revisions of the targets that allow for the adaptation of msy targets where necessary, for example, where there is a change in the natural environment or where there is a revision of the scientific advice. secondly, i agree that it is important to address fisheries issues on a local basis and to involve the stakeholders in the important decisions concerning the choice of objectives, the rate at which we should move towards those objectives and the right combination of measures to take such as tax, effort management and technical adaptations. the commission will only prepare msy plans on a regional basis and only after a detailed consultation with the sectors involved. the region advisory councils will play an important role here and their work has already begun. economic and social analyses are also important in this process and the commission will accompany all proposals for management plans with impact assessments where economic, social and environmental aspects of the proposals will be analysed. increased support for fisheries research is a necessary part of the development of msy plans. the framework programmes, the work of the scientific, technical and economic committee for fisheries and the support of the international council for the exploration of the sea will all be important in this context, which will be a priority area for the next years. moving to msy fisheries will, in many cases, mean adjustments of fleet capacity and reductions in fishing effort. the european fisheries fund was designed so that member states can plan the development of the national fleet capacity and use co-funding from the community budget to help adjust the fleet size according to long-term objectives and taking appropriate social and economic provisions into account. i would also like to say a few words in relation to the three amendments proposed by mr schlyter. the commission believes that a gradual approach to moving to msy conditions should in fact be a general rule. there is no need in all cases to move drastically to msy. as regards scientific methodology for reaching msy, the commission will ask for scientific advice on a case-by-case basis. we should not prejudice the scientific debate by prejudging which methods may be better than others. lastly, as i have already stated, it is correct to say that the european fisheries fund provides for member states to allocate public aid so as to restructure fishing fleets in line with msy strategies. this, however, should not be seen as compensation, because the fishing industry will be the eventual beneficiaries of the new policy but as a financial incentive to make the transition. the commission will continue the dialogue with the fisheries sector and will start to discuss specific long-term plans for a number of fisheries with an msy perspective. implementing such plans will improve the stability and the productivity of stocks and of the industry. i look forward to more discussions with you about these plans at a later date, after the commission has developed impact assessments, consulted the industry and prepared our proposals. there is a lot of work to be done and i will be very grateful for your support in developing this policy area.
on behalf of the pse group. madam president, mr commissioner, mr president of the committee on fisheries, i would like to begin by congratulating our rapporteur on her excellent work and also congratulate the commission on this communication which responds to a requirement which it itself adopted at the 2002 world summit in johannesburg and which also corresponds to the first of the eight objectives which were set out at that conference. of course, much has already been done by the european commission on these eight objectives, but i would like to tell the commissioner that we are in 2007 with objectives set for 2015 by a summit in 2002. the fact that we are still debating this communication at this stage does not seem to me to be a fast enough way of responding to the scale of the challenges we are facing. i welcome the words of the commissioner when he speaks of the need for a new management model, when this proposal emphasizes the concept of ecosystem management, i think we are also moving in the right direction, but i think that by looking at this concept of maximum sustainable yield as something radically new we are here making a mistake, because this concept, which is a theoretical concept, has always been the basis for all the fixing of quotas and tacs, and it would not be possible to do so if it were not based on this concept. the problem is that its application has many problems which were, incidentally, very well pointed out by our rapporteur and also by our colleague mr doyle and we cannot just rely on its blind application, we must try to improve its effectiveness, see that by seeing where it has failed and where it has had good results and this is an exercise which i think, frankly, this communication cannot do; and we must go beyond that to all the other complementary means. that is the challenge now facing the commission, from whom i hope we will hear good news in the near future.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group, in general, following the main points of the report under discussion, which are of crucial importance for the fisheries sector, we consider it useful to highlight the differences between the long and short term in applying the principle of sustainability in fisheries. that is, long-term plans aim to set objectives or targets to achieve a stable situation that will be achieved after a relatively long period, while short-term measures are proposed set annually with the aim of correcting for a short period of time the level of fishing intensity, fishing mortality until the level proposed as a long-term objective is reached. as regards the long-term objective for fisheries, the main objective set in johannesburg, namely to achieve a maximum sustainable catch stock, can be accepted. however, it will be important to stress that in order to formulate the objective of maximum sustainable yield, scientific analysis is indispensable to determine the fishing mortality intensity that ensures the maximum catch that the fishery resource can provide in a sustainable way. to do this, it is essential to take account of the natural characteristics of each fishery resource and to know the characteristics and the way in which fishing gear works. in order to assess the level of fishing appropriate to the long-term objective, the projections proposed by scientists must be verified, which means that they must be based on reliable information, adopted by managers and accepted and complied with by the fishing industry, always safeguarding, and i always stress, the socioeconomic situation of the fishing sector and of the fishermen. in practice, the aim is to estimate long-term catches and the corresponding levels of fishing mortality intensity. this requires choosing a criterion on sustainability and determining the level of fishing that produces the maximum sustainable catch value. this is where the real debate begins. there are different fishing mortality intensity levels currently proposed for the long-term management of stocks in the exclusive economic zones of the member states. several scientists consider the fishing mortality intensity level designated as f0.1 to be preferable to, for example, fmsy, which they consider less appropriate. it should be noted that fmsy, which is a value of fishing mortality intensity, should not be confused with msy, which is the catch rate. as a final consideration, i would like to support the need for sustainability measures to be accompanied by an assessment of the socioeconomic consequences and costs of their implementation.
mr president, the simplification of legislation cannot mean a reduction in the rights of consumers. what needs to be done is not only to maintain existing rights in current legislation - including financial services - but to improve where they are not sufficiently covered, such as in the area of telecommunications and energy. as stated in the proposals put forward by my group, the existence of a horizontal instrument in this area should focus on defining a limited set of general rules common to all vertical consumer protection instruments, ensuring a high level of consumer protection and using the approved method of minimum harmonisation, coupled with the country of destination principle, so as not to compromise existing national standards. it is unacceptable that a directive on consumer rights should take up any idea of defending the country of origin as a general rule, as was intended in the initial version of the directive on the liberalization of services. the consumer must be free to choose the legislation which is most favourable to him. the report we are debating is therefore full of contradictions which must be resolved by the amendments which are before us in order to defend the principle that it is necessary to ensure that the general binding rules for the protection of consumer rights respect the rights existing in each country and do not prevent these rights from being improved. on the contrary, it should serve to promote and improve existing rights. it is also necessary to apply the rules on unfair terms to all negotiated contracts containing unfair terms, even if they have been negotiated individually, while maintaining a system of direct liability of producers in the event of non-compliance with consumer protection. and that is all we intend to be assured. if not, as has already been said, we shall vote against the report.

in writing. the problem of drug addiction requires the adoption of a set of transversal policies covering, inter alia, prevention, treatment and reintegration, as well as the fight against drug trafficking, organised crime and money laundering. public policies, which are as much a priority as drug addiction, have serious human and social consequences, particularly affecting the youngest. policies which must be accompanied by other public policies aimed at improving the living conditions of citizens by guaranteeing access to health care, food, housing, the school system, academic success, stable employment with rights, a decent wage, free creation and cultural enjoyment and sport. taking into account its objectives and actions, the specific programme on drug information and prevention promoted at eu level could contribute to the increase of knowledge, the exchange of information and the prevention of drug use, supporting and complementing the measures developed at the level of each member state. the (insufficient) approximately eur 21 million allocated to the 27 countries during the period 2007-2013 should therefore be used effectively and fully.
in writing. the international regulation adopted by the who is a new instrument aimed at protecting global health, replacing the old post-war regulation which focused on border control, including health checks on ships and their crews, and included international vaccination against yellow fever and other diseases that have been added. emerging public health issues such as tuberculosis and malaria, and even new ones such as avian influenza and the risk of pandemic influenza, have increased the urgency of international public health information and consultation. the latest epidemics and pandemic threats have shown that no country or region can be guaranteed a health fortress. this new regulation gives priority to the exchange of information and calls on countries to cooperate in responding to global threats, recognising that all countries are important and that mutual assistance is relevant. in portugal, border health surveillance and international vaccination and traveller consultations have received less and less attention, which was largely due to the current government's closure of the regional public health centres. without a proper national monitoring system, the contribution will remain mediocre.

governance and environmental sustainability. in conclusion, pollution and the post-kyoto scenario, the price of oil, moral and human rights imperatives, political and economic instability resulting from dependence on hydrocarbons, the potential of new environmental technologies to stimulate a new industrial revolution in europe and the world - all of this is conspiring around us to force the eu to develop a multifaceted but coherent external energy policy. i would like to conclude, madam president, by congratulating the rapporteur, mr saryusz-wolski.

mr president-in-office of the council lobo antunes, vice-president of the commission. ladies and gentlemen, today's discussion is based on two reports which represent two complementary approaches: the action plan on legal immigration and the priorities for combating illegal immigration. to favor one and forget the other would be a grave mistake. they're two sides of the same coin. migration is a phenomenon of great proportions today. it is estimated that there are now some 26 million migrants in the european union, both legal and irregular. migration is a phenomenon that clearly has a european dimension. not only because each member state cannot manage it effectively on its own, but above all because any change in the emigration policy of one member state will eventually have an effect on migration flows and their evolution in the other member states. i am in favour of the idea of the blue card and the creation of a european migration portal to disseminate information on the conditions and possibilities for legal migration in the european union. i welcome the strategy of abandoning the idea of a single directive which has been blocked in the council for several years and adopting a progressive approach which envisaged the submission of four sectoral directives over the next three years. i would stress the need for a policy of development aid, with the conclusion of agreements with third countries, for the effective management of emigration. cooperation with countries of origin is essential in the fight against trafficking in human beings and in combating illegal labour. finally, mr president, border control and the use of the resources already created, such as frontex and the rabbits, which must have the means to operate, must also be ensured.
in writing. i voted in favour of the paasilinna report on the european institute of technology because i believe that it will make a decisive contribution to boosting the competitiveness of the european economy by allowing for greater synergies between innovation, research and education. i therefore support the proposals put forward by the rapporteur, which seek to define clearly the sources of funding for the future european institute of technology, so that it can be operational as soon as possible and successfully fulfil its mission, in line with the objectives set out in the lisbon strategy.
in writing. our position on the creation of the european institute of technology is very critical, following the position taken by various research organizations. for example, last year the league of european research universities presented a study concluding that the european institute of technology plan was "badly conceived and doomed to failure", and euroscience, a pan-european movement of scientists and policy experts, called it "a politically determined idea based on a wrong premise". uk science adviser robert may says it is "based on a misunderstanding" of innovation. this institute will be virtual, staffed by scientists, based in eu universities, research laboratories and companies and will not award degrees, contrary to what was originally proposed. after pressure from several countries, who wanted to keep the institute, it became virtual, a kind of consulting office for scientific communities in different fields. the european parliament itself has just approved several amendments to the commission's proposal, but we do not think they are sufficient to correct what has gone wrong. as regards financing, one of the possibilities is the community budget, including funds for research, which can be another way of supporting the more developed countries, thus contributing to the aggravation of inequalities.
in writing. the european union is today at a real crossroads in its ability to compete with the rest of the world. although we have many attractive factors, whether historical and cultural, economic or touristic, we cannot escape the great challenges of global competition with the new emerging asian economies. now our capacity to be an enticing space in terms of knowledge and innovation has been called into question. with the vote on the european institute of technology, i believe that an important step has been taken towards building a framework for european action in the context of the growth and development of our economy, based on the triangle of innovation, research and education. i believe that it is neither low wages nor cheap labour that can make us attractive for investment and for the growth of our societies. the future belongs to those societies which invest in equipping their populations with specialised skills, helping their societies to interact with industries and businesses to devise the highest quality and innovative responses to the dynamic and demanding needs of markets.
in writing. agreeing that it is appropriate to allow, for 2008, the cultivation of set-aside land for agricultural purposes, we considered that a longer-term derogation should be provided for and therefore submitted a proposal for 2009 and 2010 which was approved to include 2009. this will enable farmers to plan better in the face of exceptionally high prices on the cereals market. however, this measure does not resolve the fundamental question of the need to increase production and supply in each member state and employment in rural areas. we also draw attention to the shortage of cereals on the eu market and to the negative effects of a bet on biofuels, such as the one decided by the council, both on supply and price. we reiterate the need for a thorough review of the cap to take account of the characteristics of the soil and biodiversity of each country, to adapt to a possible rotation of production and to guarantee farmers adequate incomes without compromising the interests of consumers in healthy and quality food.
in writing. i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on 'dangerous toys made in china' because i consider it essential that all the necessary legislative and administrative measures be taken to ensure that consumer goods, marketed in the eu, fully comply with the eu standards and do not endanger the health and safety of consumers. i therefore consider it desirable that the toy directive 88/378/ec be revised as soon as possible and that it include relevant and effective product safety requirements.
in writing. safeguarding the safety of products, in particular toys, is a priority concern for the protection of public health and, in particular, of children. the necessary verification and control of product quality is an essential mechanism for achieving this objective. it is for undertakings and the competent national public authorities to carry out such control and certification in a preventive manner. since the safety rules which products must naturally comply with are laid down by law, it is up to the undertakings responsible for their design, production and marketing to assume their responsibilities. the first reaction to the importation from third countries of products, including toys, which are unsafe or harmful to health, was to try to shift responsibility to others, to the extent that the financial times reported that mattel had formally apologized to the chinese government and people. it should be stressed that many of the imported products are manufactured in third countries, but they are owned by large multinational companies in the eu, which, in the interest of profit, have relocated their production. on the other hand, to focus the discussion of poor quality on imported products alone is to ignore the fact that many products produced in the eu also do not meet the standards in force.
in writing. energy is a central strategic issue of our time. the various eu countries, which are highly energy dependent, are aiming to dominate the exploitation of existing energy resources, hence the proposal to create an energy component in the common foreign and security policy, which, if implemented, would also be a way of overcoming the contradictions between their main powers. to do this, the eu should proclaim its 'market' and 'competition' and its enlargement to other countries, in the framework of so-called 'energy communities', the 'energy charter treaty' - 'guaranteeing investments' and 'the right to compensation in the event of expropriation and/or nationalisation' - or the inclusion of 'energy security clauses' in trade agreements. everything he can control, hence his dread of creating "a gas version of opec". the european parliament's resolution on the situation in the former yugoslavia, adopted on 26 june, calls for the eu to take action to prevent the further spread of the virus and to ensure that the virus is contained in the territory of the former yugoslavia. iraq, afghanistan, africa? what are you talking about?
in writing. given the growing importance of the energy sector in contemporary societies, on the one hand, and the growing international interdependence, which is also a common feature of this time, on the other hand, it is impossible to exclude energy policy from the external dimension of european policy, either at the level of the member states or at the level of the common foreign policy. i therefore agree with the resolution in that it states that 'while member states should retain their sovereign right to make strategic choices regarding energy savings, exploit their energy resources and make decisions on supply structures, it is necessary (to promote a common approach, not necessarily a single policy) to cover security of supply, transit and investment in the context of energy security and (to) promote energy efficiency and savings as well as (...) clean and renewable energy sources, in particular in relations with countries whose energy consumption is growing rapidly'. but as for the idea of a senior official for external energy policy, this dimension must be present in the action of the european foreign policy officer, because i do not think that a more specific approach makes sense than this.
in writing. although it includes important points on immigration issues which we have long advocated, the report does not denounce the current eu policies and guidelines which are criminalising and repressive in relation to immigration, but rather integrates them as one more element. the report adopts the concept of the existence of different 'categories' of immigrants - whether 'highly qualified', 'seasonal' or other - and their management according to the need for labour in the different eu countries, in particular by creating a so-called 'blue card'. a dehumanizing view of immigration and immigrants. on the other hand, the report advocates the creation of a common immigration policy, which we consider to be inadequate and unrealistic, both in view of the results of other 'common' policies and in view of the different realities in the member states. we reaffirm that immigration policy is a matter for each country and its democratic institutions. as we have said, what is needed is not a common policy but a policy, within the framework of cooperation between member states, which promotes the rights of immigrants, in particular by ratifying the un convention on the protection of the rights of all migrant workers and members of their families.
in writing. the debate on immigration too often focuses on the issues of illegal flows and often forgets legal immigration, this important contribution to our economy and to our cultural enrichment. in this perspective we agree on two fundamental concepts: a clear and effective policy on legal immigration is one of the keys to the issue of illegal immigration; a generous and commonly-based welcome that promotes the integration and adaptation of those who arrive. but it is also necessary to recognise that migration flows, immigrant communities and host countries have distinct traditions, habits and memories and that these differences cannot be ignored. another topic in this debate is skilled immigration. the idea of a blue card, which would make it easier to enter and move around, may be interesting, although it seems too complex for the time being. in any case, the central question must be that of attractiveness, particularly at the academic level. and here it is important to raise awareness among educational institutions of the need to be able to attract students from other parts of the world. and, of course, support that cause.
in writing. this report too, although it contains some points with which we agree, falls within the security and repressive vision of 'illegal immigration'. even if mitigated in some respects, the report advocates the promotion of the main pillars of the current eu guidelines and decisions on immigration, including: the so-called 'european return policy', i.e. repatriation; the work of frontex in border patrolling and control; the so-called 'temporary reception centres'; the development of biometric data collection tools; or the so-called 're-admission agreements'. the report also proposes the creation of 'european patrols', a 'european maritime border surveillance system' and an 'automated system for controlling entry and exit from the eu'. in other words, the report seeks to strengthen the eu's security policy and criminalise 'illegal immigration', transforming it into a common eu policy - repressive, with dangerous information systems, measures and infrastructures for the detention and deportation of immigrants - which we clearly reject. the application of this repressive logic culminated in the authorities of one member state charging seven tunisian fishermen with having saved 44 people at sea, in compliance with the conventions of international maritime law.
in writing. effective policy intervention in the area of illegal immigration must address two aspects of the problem. about the origin, and about the destination. or, as the adopted resolution says, 'the authorities of the countries of origin, the strengthening of the legal and criminal framework to combat trafficking networks, the fight against illegal employment and trafficking in human beings'. without firmness in these areas there will be no adequate response. even if this response involves other dimensions, such as development cooperation and action also in the field of legal immigration. in addition, and in line with what we have included in the report on the european maritime strategy, any immigration policy that is intended to be effective within the framework of the european union requires, as the adopted resolution states, respect between member states for the following principles: solidarity, shared responsibility, mutual trust and transparency. we are in full agreement on this.
