flights which the sef has been able to reconstruct. the portuguese government also did not allow the director of the secret services and his predecessors since 2002 to be heard by the european parliament mission that travelled to lisbon in december 2006. the portuguese government has not provided the national parliament or the european parliament with the repeatedly requested list of civil or military flights to and from guantanamo that pass through portuguese territory. until december 2006, the government denied such flights. but they were registered, and the compiled list included 94 overflights and 17 landings, mostly by american civilian and military aircraft, between january 2002 and the end of june 2006. there is evidence that several of these planes were transporting list, but went on to claim that the guantanamo detention centre is not synonymous with the guantanamo military base and that flights to this military base would be "normal" and under the auspices of the un or nato. the secretary general of nato subsequently denied this in writing. in january 2006, i gathered testimonies of prisoners being seen chained at the lajes base in the azores, being transferred to american planes. these testimonies were confirmed by journalists and reports were published including photographs of the buildings. mr president, a judicial inquiry is under way in portugal today. unfortunately, it was not decided by the portuguese government, it was my initiative. but the truth will come out in the face of the disturbing data collected in this parliament from the time of the barroso government to the present.

un secretary-general. all of them evoke the urgent need for an international presence in that region which must include a strong military component. and no country or multilateral organization is more suited than the european union to effectively fulfil the mandate that resolution 1778 imposes. esdp has matured and it's for these emergencies that it exists. in this respect, and with regard to the deployment of a european union military force to the region, the council and the portuguese presidency can count on parliament's support in principle. but the european parliament also expresses its concern about certain aspects of this mission. firstly, we fear that the reluctance of the member states to provide the minimum necessary manpower and military equipment will greatly reduce the effectiveness of the force. in addition, the fewer the contributions from the various member states, the more the french component of the force will be highlighted. the perception of the impartiality of this mission is fundamental to its success and france is seen as a rather neutral actor in the region. secondly, parliament called for the deployment of this force to be accompanied by a diplomatic operation, which is scheduled to last only 12 months, will not be able to make a lasting contribution to peace in the region. finally, parliament welcomes the mandate of the force which will act under chapter vii of the united nations charter. it is essential that this mandate be properly interpreted on the ground and that european troops be proactive in protecting civilians in danger, in creating paying the ultimate price for the timidity and over-scrupulousness of international troops. let us hope that one day this operation will be used as a model example of esdp and effective multilateralism in action and as a full demonstration of the european union's willingness to strengthen the united nations and to contribute to the resolution of conflicts in accordance with international law and the responsibility to protect which it already enshrines.

one of the areas of education which is still very poor in some countries of the european union, particularly in portugal, is pre-school education. i therefore think it is important to stress the call to the member states to increase investment in a public network of kindergartens with quality trained educators, capable of reaching all children, which is one of the most effective tools for developing their intellectual capacities, laying the foundations for the next levels of education, raising the general level of skills, significantly improving the equity of the education system and combating social inequalities. it is also important to focus on the quality of public primary and secondary education, which should be universal, compulsory and free of charge, with the aim of providing basic education and basic skills, contributing to the realization of social and civic values of solidarity, education for peace and equality, strengthening social cohesion and inclusion. as regards higher education, it must be recognized that it is a fundamental sector of developed societies and that it is therefore necessary to combat failure and early school leaving, as is still the case in portugal, where unfortunately about 40% of students do not even finish secondary education. budget cuts in public education, the increasingly high costs of higher education and the difficult social situation of a large percentage of families and young people prevent portugal from rapidly improving the higher education of its population, maintaining the worst rates in the european union. however, if we know from studies that for each additional year of average school attendance, productivity increases selectively by 6.2% in an average eu country, we can better understand the difficulties of countries that do not provide a high quality public education for their population.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's agricultural policy is not undermined by the excessive deficit. other as rapporteur for the committee on agriculture and rural development, i would like to stress the importance of adopting some of the proposals in our opinion which were not included in mrs kauppi's report, and ask for your support for their adoption in this plenary given their importance to millions of women farmers and rural people whose work needs to be more visible by including them in agricultural statistics rather than as household statistics. it is essential that their status as women farmers is fully recognised and that equal rights and opportunities are realised, including in social security systems. that there is effective protection of maternity and easier access to health, education, lifelong learning, child and family support facilities, including childcare centres, cultural centres and local markets, which requires greater investment and better public services in rural areas. only in this way can we help to combat the high levels of poverty and isolation of women in certain rural areas and achieve greater social cohesion.
in 2005, in my report on the lisbon strategy in a gender perspective, i warned of the various discriminations to which european women are subject. two years on, many speeches and good intentions, many debates and conferences, many reports and studies, what has changed? what progress has been made in terms of the gender pay gap or women's participation in decision-making or the reconciliation of work, family and personal life, not only for women but also for men? while there has been progress in some member states, unfortunately at european level very little has changed. the pay gap remains at 15%, and women's participation in decision-making has increased by only 1%. women continue to devote three times as much time as men to family responsibilities. and yet, women are more numerous in universities. they are slowly asserting themselves, but there is still a lot of discrimination, particularly when they are mothers and just because they are mothers. maybe that's why the birth rates are so low. and migrant and refugee women, women from ethnic minorities, elderly women, women with disabilities, these are doubly discriminated against. we need better laws, such as the equality laws that have been passed in countries like portugal and spain, but we also need existing laws to be enforced, including advertising laws, to stop degrading representations of women in advertising and the media. you have to change the laws to change the mindsets. we need fewer words and more results.

in writing. we voted against this report, although we consider that it has some positive aspects, because we disagree with the general context and positions defended in it, both as regards the objectives of higher education and as regards tuition fees, ignoring the fact that the difficulties of disadvantaged groups cannot be solved by mere financial incentives such as those announced for portugal. that's not the way to improve equity in access to higher education. even if we use the rapporteur's arguments about the influence of education on economic growth by 'increasing human capital and the capacity for innovation', considering that by increasing the efficiency of education and training, individuals and society as a whole get a return on investment that can reach 8% per year, we can see what countries lose by not decisively investing in higher education that is accessible to all segments of the population. recent studies show that 75 million eu citizens - or 32% of the workforce - are insufficiently educated. in 2010, only 15% of new jobs will be available to this group of people, most of whom come from disadvantaged sectors of society. this would justify the need to ensure effective equity in education.

in writing. the abolition of the death penalty on a global scale would be a clear sign of progress for humanity. of course, there are other horrors being committed, particularly by states that kill without even condemning, but acceptance of the death penalty corresponds to a philosophical conception that should be part of our societies. the proposal for a moratorium aimed at achieving the abolition of the death penalty therefore deserves our support and the commitment of the eu member states. in this sense, a world day against the death penalty could have the effect of 'embarrassing' states that practice it and could thus be positive. as for the idea of a european day against the death penalty, it seems to me that it is a matter of establishing a european celebration against a fact which does not exist in europe, while at the same time, as we know, it involves provoking other discussions where unanimity is lacking. for that reason, i doubt the virtue of this initiative. finally, i did not want this culture of the primacy of life to spread to other areas and other issues, where the defence of life also seems to me to be a sign of civilization.

in writing. the negotiations conducted by the commission under a council mandate have as their central objective the creation of an open aviation area (eea) between the eu and the us, going beyond the existing bilateral agreements between the member states and the us. the aim is to create a single, liberalised eu-us air transport market 'in which investment can flow freely and eu and us airlines can provide air services without any restrictions, including in the internal markets of both parties'. the eu aims to ensure reciprocity on the part of the us in the liberalisation of air transport, in particular with regard to 'the elimination of legal restrictions in force, both on the ownership and control of us airlines by non-nationals and on cabotage' or 'the right of establishment' and 'state aid'. we therefore reiterate that it is up to the member states, not the community, to conclude such agreements, especially when it is a matter of great strategic importance and the aim is to 'shaping the pattern for greater regulatory liberalization and convergence at world level'. we also reaffirm our opposition to further liberalization of this important public service in each country.
in writing. the conclusion of this agreement seeks to meet long-standing needs on both sides of the atlantic, with clear benefits for consumers from greater regulatory liberalisation and convergence at the global level. the eu will also act as a guarantor of compliance with community legislation. the work done to conclude this agreement is therefore to be commended, as the new legal framework will allow for a far-reaching agreement to create an integrated transatlantic aviation market, beneficial for consumers and businesses. however, it still shows a certain disproportion in terms of the liberalization of the conditions for control of american companies by foreigners and the non-inclusion of cabotage. the crucial suggestion of the european parliament to include the later stages, deadlines for completion and consequences of possible non-compliance in this phased approach to the agreement is therefore to be welcomed. the conditions have also been set for full reciprocity to be restored in the us-us aviation market should the negotiations not reach the balance desired by both parties. in short, a good start for goals not yet achieved.
in writing. the psd meps, although they consider that it is not a perfect solution and that it has the defect of not establishing a rule, but of forcing a new negotiation in the framework of future enlargements, support the lamassoure report on the composition of the european parliament for three reasons: 1. because some member states do not accept a mere definition of general principles and make a strict definition of the composition of the ep a condition before accepting the reform treaty, which could compromise the main objective of the portuguese eu presidency. 2. because lamassoure proposes a balanced compromise solution which respects a minimum threshold guaranteeing the pluralism of representation of small states and takes account of the demographic dimension of the others through a principle of degressive proportionality which ensures a fair relationship between states. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.

in writing. in view of the need to adapt the composition of the european parliament to successive and planned enlargements, i believe that the solution adopted in this report should be consistent with what was previously accepted (nice), not promote the predominance of the most populous states over the rest, maintaining a model of balance between states that is understandable, and be a contribution to alleviating the difficulties associated with the adoption of the reform treaty. so, although i preferred, as the vote shows, an accepted model based on the concept of citizenship rather than residence - because i believe that the link between citizens and the european union should be this and not that - i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. we voted in favour of this report, which expresses the european parliament's solidarity with women who are victims of violence all over the world, including in our countries of the european union, but which also highlights the seriousness of the situation in mexico and in some countries in central america, where there is still genuine femicide, with thousands of violent deaths of women in recent years, which cannot be attributed solely to a climate of widespread violence. in all this there are cultural causes and socioeconomic contexts unfavourable to women, a situation that is aggravated in the case of indigenous women, with high levels of economic dependence, but to which is added also the action of criminal gangs. we believe that this report can help to raise awareness of this serious situation and thus help to ensure that the necessary measures are taken in the various countries to put an end to femicide and violence against women.
in writing. in view of the rapid growth of air transport for passengers and goods, the commission decided to draw up an 'action plan on airport capacity, efficiency and safety in europe', which includes a set of measures. the european parliament's resolution, although it incorporates aspects with which we agree - for example, in relation to its references to the need to respect social standards and collective agreements, training or the needs of the outermost regions - is part of a vision of liberalising the sector and creating the so-called 'single european sky'. while pointing out that the responsibility for planning airport infrastructure lies with the member states, it advocates a 'common community approach to the need for new capacity, the limitations of future investment in additional capacity and the strategic axes'. the resolution affirms the primacy of 'community competition rules', particularly as regards the provision of groundhandling services, while not ruling out greater liberalisation. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all air carriers, including those operating in the territory of the member states. hence our critical position.
in writing. in identifying 'the construction of support airports in the vicinity of congested airports' as one of the solutions to airport congestion situations such as that in lisbon; and in noting that 'traditional airlines, low-cost airlines, charter airlines, cargo carriers and business aircraft carriers have different requirements for airport services and slot allocation', the european parliament values the options which are presented as less costly and at the same time effective in responding to the growth of air transport, taking into account the particular characteristics of this growth. i therefore voted in favour of this report, considering that its ratio is contrary to the position of the cds-pp for lisbon, which is the 'portela +1' option.

, in writing. this convention, which aims to establish the obligations of the parties with regard to the assessment of the environmental impact of certain activities at an early stage of planning and imposes a general obligation on member states to notify and consult on all major projects which may have significant harmful transboundary environmental impacts, was signed by the community and its member states on 26 february 1991 and approved by the community on 27 june 1997. parliament approved a number of amendments, notably the one which broadens the definition of 'public' in article 1 (10) of the convention, clarifying that the public which may participate in the convention's proceedings includes civil society, in particular non-governmental organisations, and the one which opens the convention to accession by countries which are not members of the united nations economic commission for europe, subject to approval by the conference of the parties, which we support. the other amendments are less important and, in principle, do not seem to me to pose any problems. we therefore agreed with the rapporteur and voted in favour of the report.
in writing. the convention on the protection of the european communities' financial interests and the protocols thereto form part of the list of conventions and protocols in the field of justice and home affairs contained in annex 1 to the act of accession. the convention and its protocols were adopted in 1996 with the aim of establishing a common basis for the criminal protection of the communities' financial interests and entered into force in 2002 following ratification by the then 15 member states. in order to avoid wasting so much time and effort with the laborious negotiation, conclusion and ratification (27 member states) of protocols of accession specific to each of the conventions, the act of accession of romania and bulgaria introduced a simplified system of accession to the conventions and protocols concluded by the member states, based on article 34 teu or article 293 tec. i therefore support this proposal for a council decision which, in a simplified form, determines the date of entry into force of this convention for romania and bulgaria.
in writing. in march 2007, france requested the mobilisation of the egf to cover the redundancies of 1345 workers at renault sa and 1057 workers at peugeot sa and its suppliers. due to the budgetary constraints imposed on this fund (eur 500 million per year), its restrictive eligibility criteria and the number of workers concerned, the amount of the community co-financing granted was eur 3 816 280. we thus find that each of the workers made redundant in connection with renault is paid eur 1 902 and each of the workers made redundant in connection with peugeot eur 1 190. the european commission estimated that between 35,000 and 50,000 workers could benefit from this fund, but eu data show that the number of workers made redundant as a result of 'restructuring' has long since exceeded half a million. this is all the more serious when most of these workers have been made redundant as a result of 'restructuring' considered to be 'within' the eu and are therefore not covered by the eligibility criteria of this fund. what is required is an end to the policy of liberalization and maximum profit which is the cause of relocations and 'restructuring' and the defence of the preservation of jobs.
in writing. the decision to use the new european globalisation adjustment fund and the response to the french state's request is an opportunity that we must follow closely to see whether this fund can actually produce the desired results. as the debate on its creation showed, the fund is intended to be an institutional reform in solidarity with the unforeseen and negative consequences of the globalisation process. it is clear that free market adjustment will always be better than the need for state intervention or similar. in any event, this fund is part of the european union and the solutions adopted by most of its member states to resolve social crises, so the challenge is to ensure that the results of its mobilisation are as expected on the one hand and, on the other, to ensure that such intervention does not send the wrong signals to the market, inadvertently promoting solutions that in the long run create even greater damage. i believe and hope that it will not, but i have voted in favour of this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by mrs christa klaß on a proposal for a european parliament and council directive establishing a framework for action at community level on the sustainable use of pesticides because it meets the objective of reducing the use of plant protection products and contributes to high safety standards for man, animals and the environment. i believe, however, that it is essential to maintain the possibility of aerial applications in situations where there is no viable alternative or where land application constitutes a higher risk situation, although in the natura 2000 zones pesticides, in addition to being prohibited, should also be restricted or the risks arising from their use minimised, which requires a specific risk assessment.
in writing. when the 6th environment action programme was adopted, it was recognised that it was desirable to reduce the effects of plant protection products on human health and the environment, stressing the need for a more environmentally friendly use of pesticides and advocating a two-pronged approach with full transposition and appropriate monitoring of the existing legislative framework and the development of a thematic strategy for the sustainable use of pesticides. the rapporteur now considers that the title of the commission proposal is misleading. the proposal for a directive concerns a certain group of pesticides, namely plant protection products. it is therefore appropriate to replace the word 'pesticides' throughout the text by 'plant protection products'. the directive aims to reduce the risks and effects on human health and the environment of the use of plant protection products. however, the measures taken to this end must be proportionate and it must not be forgotten that it is primarily for the member states to contribute to the reduction of the risks associated with the use of plant protection products in the framework of national action plans. it is the only way to take account, as appropriate, of the different conditions that exist at local level.
in writing. i voted in favour of the hiltrud breyer report on a proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council concerning the placing of plant protection products on the market, as it will ensure high safety standards for man, animals and the environment by establishing stringent but simplified procedures and by rationalising resources. the approved report respects the principle of subsidiarity, so that member states can take into account national specific conditions, in particular climatic and phytosanitary conditions, and that appropriate risk mitigation measures can be taken.
in writing. this proposal should follow the rationale of the sixth environmental action programme with the aim of applying current knowledge of prospective and retrospective risk and hazard assessment strategies for man and the environment and of creating coherence with other policies. thus, also following the thematic strategy for the sustainable use of pesticides, the regulation should ensure a high level of protection of human health and the environment, making the precautionary principle prevail, but measures should be proportionate and take into account the principle of subsidiarity. consistency with other policies needs to be more clearly ensured. therefore, the regulation should not run counter to the objectives and quality standards of the water framework directive 2000/60/ec and the directives deriving from it. this objective can be achieved by regular reviews. each member state should retain the possibility to go beyond community standards for protection standards and to take product approval decisions to achieve objectives of pesticide action plans, health programmes or environmental protection measures adopted at national level, based on national specific conditions.

commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the debate we are having is of great political importance, given the ethical importance of the subject under discussion. the dichotomy between the protection of intellectual property and the promotion of the health and well-being of the people of the least developed countries reflects a conflict of interests which can only be resolved in the field of the confrontation of values. in a rather simple way we can describe this antagonism with clarity. on the one hand, there is a certain and questionable model of intellectual property protection based on the argument of encouraging innovation and the consequent expansion of scientific knowledge, on the other, there are millions of poor human beings, inhabitants of countries with scarce resources who cannot be condemned to suffer and die for economic reasons at a time when the knowledge available can save their lives. it is clear which side the fundamental values are on in this confrontation. in view of this, several steps have been taken at different times and in different places to make the intellectual property protection regime more flexible in order to promote universal access to medicines. it is clear, however, that the path we have travelled is not enough. the mechanism under consideration is only one way of alleviating such a devastating problem. we need to go further. the european parliament has been making a decisive contribution to the european union's adoption of a position consistent with the values which inspire it. the solution now found reflects this concern and i would therefore like to congratulate the presidency of the council for the efforts it has made to achieve, through declarations and commitments, a position which is able to project europe at its best: that of a political community based always on unshakable humanist values.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the european qualifications framework for lifelong learning is a key document for making national and sectoral qualifications frameworks comparable at in writing. the costs associated with the introduction of rules for the protection of intellectual property in the pharmaceutical sector in the so-called 'developing countries' have long been known. the dramatic and unbearable situation in these countries caused by the application of so-called 'intellectual property rights' in the field of health, particularly in the fight against epidemics such as malaria, hiv/aids and tuberculosis, has long been denounced and warned of. in this sense, we believe that this report is a missed opportunity for the majority of the ep to be able, within its powers, to take a humanist position and clearly advocate a policy that would put an end to intellectual property rights in the pharmaceutical sector. the majority of the ep, taking refuge in the idea that a negotiation of the protocol would be very difficult, is giving the council a blank cheque by making sufficiently vague recommendations which will lead to a prolongation of the existing situation, creating financial and legal obstacles to countries with less resources being able to access the advances in science and technology in this field. we denounce the fact that it is the multinational pharmaceutical companies which are the main beneficiaries of this inhumane policy, maintaining their fabulous profits at the cost of many lives.
in writing. multilingualism is much more than an expression of the cultural diversity of the european union. in an organisation of sovereign and independent states which come together to seek the greatest advantages for their citizens in collaboration without at any time having abdicated their right to remain what they are free and sovereign states multilingualism is the recognition of the relationship of equality between all its members. that alone would be sufficient to justify the conditions necessary for its maintenance within the framework of the functioning of the community institutions. but there are other factors besides military. abandoning multilingual internal communication potentially reduces the conditions for political action by members of the european parliament, who have every right to express themselves in their mother tongue; on the other hand, by minimising multilingualism in external communication we are distancing an institution which spends a large part of its energies calling for the eu to be closer to its citizens. finally, the economic argument must be countered by an equally economic argument: the linguistic diversity of europeans and the knowledge of several languages must be a competitive advantage, not a cost.
in writing. this report is full of contradictions and we are critical of the commitment of the majority in the european parliament to the establishment of a european qualifications framework, although there are positive aspects, which should be safeguarded, in the recognition of qualifications between the various member states. the final text adopted, however, underlines the federalist nature of the european parliament's proposal by setting specific dates for the adaptation and correlation of the different education and training systems in force in the member states, although it mentions that the proposal will not be binding for the next few years. we stress that education policy is the sole responsibility of the member states and therefore we consider that the proposed 'adaptation' violates this principle. we regard the link with the bologna process and the path towards the consequent commodification of education as negative, with emphasis on 'employability' and the labour market perspective related to the lisbon agenda.
in writing. the globalisation of the economy is a question to which europe has not yet found a clear and convincing answer. a more globalised economy implies a willingness to change, which means more mobility. the creation of a common reference framework for the recognition, comparability and transfer of qualifications originating in different systems is fundamental to the development of a decisive component of the european project, namely the mobility of workers, in this case facilitated by the portability of their qualifications. better training of our workers combined with a homogeneous system for the recognition of their knowledge, skills and competences will enhance their mobility and the development of the internal market. more and better skills of european workers can contribute to better organisation, innovation and competitiveness of our companies.
in writing. in order to fill a gap in the implementation of the extension of the schengen information system (sis) to include the visa information system (vis), the present proposal aims to provide a temporary solution to fill the gaps and the foreseeable disruptions created by the delay in the installation of the 'infrastructure' of the 'new' system, by distributing its costs over the community budget and the member states. it is recalled that what is at stake is the extension of the sis features, developing them, extending access to new authorities and interconnecting them, adding new categories of data (such as the capture warrant and biometric data). this extension from the previous system entails high risks for the rights, freedoms and guarantees of citizens by adding new elements to a database, which is also shared by more bodies, with no full guarantee of confidentiality of the data, and the records may be 'kept for a longer period' and shared with third countries. the basic aim is to adapt the sis to the dangerous and unacceptable objectives of the current security offensive, enlargement and the increasing communitization of internal affairs in the eu, which we clearly reject.
in writing. it is known that in july 2006 the commission presented a thematic strategy for the sustainable use of pesticides, together with a proposal for a directive establishing a framework for action at community level for the sustainable use of pesticides and a proposal for a regulation on the placing of plant protection products on the market, with the aim of reducing the overall risks and negative impacts of pesticide use on human health and the environment. the risks associated with pesticide use have been reduced, but in some areas, especially in countries that have long used intensive agriculture, pesticides are still found in soil and water in undesirable amounts. this also shows that countries like portugal with more conventional agriculture should have more support to maintain less intensive agricultural production. on the other hand, we do not consider that the solution is to replace pesticides with gmos. if the undesirable effects of chemical pesticides on human health are known, the precautionary principle must be applied to the effects of gmos on human health, which have not yet been studied. this thematic strategy for the sustainable use of pesticides concerns only plant protection products, i.e. a part of the group of pesticides.
in writing. there are several positive aspects here, notably the recognition of the role of conventional energy sources and their need for energy production, the opening up of prospects for the relaunch of nuclear fission energy and the call for the lifting of restrictions on new coal-fired power stations. it also opens up prospects for carbon capture and sequestration and calls for international cooperation, including with non-eu countries such as china and india. it also emphasises the exploitation of indigenous resources and puts a more realistic plan for the contribution of renewable energies. it welcomes some criticism of the production and use of liquid biofuels and warns of the need for countries to promote more r & d in the energy sector, in particular as a way of overcoming environmental and nuclear safety problems. but it has several negative aspects, the most important of which is that the growing problems of the oil market are associated exclusively with short-term and episodic issues, the strategic issue of depletion is ignored, and the enormous potential of biomethane produced from waste is still ignored, a trend which is already taking place in several european countries. that is why we abstained.
in writing. with the launch of the energy package at the beginning of the year, the european commission made clear the need for a technological action plan for fossil fuels and also underlined the imperative of a pragmatic approach to nuclear energy. the reality is clear: there are no equally efficient and cheap alternatives to fossil fuels, which means that they will remain the central and indispensable component of energy in the eu beyond 2020. this is why we must seek new solutions to the challenge of energy supply in the eu, taking into account the issues of competitiveness, sustainability and security of supply. all investments in the development of new energy technologies are therefore of the greatest importance, both for the reduction of the impact on the environment and the safety of existing installations, and for the development of new energy sources and for a more efficient and cleaner use of fossil fuels. it is essential that the member states and the union focus their efforts on energy research, from the more efficient use of energy sources to new technologies and the cleaner use of existing energy sources, and i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. we voted against this final resolution because, moreover, it is part of the line of defence of the economic and financial groups, as the rapporteur has pointed out, who withdrew her name from the report before the final vote, calling for a vote against. the aim is to ease the rules and the way for large companies to penetrate the various markets easily, to reap the greatest profits with the fewest obstacles in any member state. we also believe that the fiscal sovereignty of the member states in the definition of their fiscal policy should be respected in any discussion on this matter, which is not the case here. a so-called common european fiscal policy promoting 'fiscal competition' would only serve the interests of big european and international capital. available data show that the average rate of taxation on business profits has fallen sharply over the past ten years, while the tax on labour has remained essentially unchanged. we regret that the proposals put forward by the rapporteur, which stressed the distributive aspect of taxation and demonstrated the transfer of the tax burden from high incomes to lower incomes, were not included in this final text.
in writing. i voted in favour of the karl-heinz florenz report on the green paper on a smoke-free europe: strategic options at community level, because i considered it necessary to take appropriate measures to curb the number of deaths and serious illnesses caused by tobacco smoke. in this respect, i support the proposal that the commission amends directive 2001/37/ec on tobacco products, which provides for the revision of the regulations on the use of additives and other substances in tobacco products, in particular as regards carcinogenic, mutagenic or toxic additives, in the light of new scientific developments.
in writing. as we have already said, the negotiations on turkey's accession to the eu raise a number of issues. this is a process promoted by the great powers, despite their contradictions, with the aim of integrating this great country into the eu's 'single market', seeking to control its economy and use its geo-strategic position for its plans in the middle east, the caucasus and central asia. the resolution is also illuminating on this issue by highlighting 'the importance of turkey as a transit platform for diversifying gas supplies to the eu' and 'energy projects involving turkey in the south caucasus' as well as 'turkey's geo-strategic position in the region' whose 'transport and logistics role will become even more important in the coming years'. among other important points to be emphasized are: - turkey has not taken any steps towards recognition of cyprus - an eu member state - and continues to occupy the north of the island militarily and to flout un resolutions; - and that the turkish authorities continue to repress the kurdish people and deny them their legitimate cultural, political, economic and social rights.
in writing. whatever the final outcome, the ongoing negotiations with turkey must promote the reforms that the country so badly needs and which are, in themselves, the most relevant aspect of a country's prospect of eu membership. in this context, we should regard the akp victory as a consecration of economic reforms rather than a vote for islamism. in the light of the latest developments, it must be stated that the kurdish question must be dealt with in collaboration with the united states, taking into account the question of iraq where the kurdish north is a peaceful region; the european union is not only a political force, but also a political force. finally, it is never too late to recall the geostrategic importance of turkey, whether in the matter of the security of europe's borders, whether in energy supplies, in particular as an alternative to dependence on russian gas, whether as a partner in the dialogue with the islamic countries or, finally, in the matter of iran. for all these reasons, the eu's strategy must be to negotiate seriously and with rigor.
i welcome maria martens for this important report at a time when the eu is redefining its relations with africa, in large part because of china's emergence as an actor in africa. but eu-africa relations can only progress if there is coherence in the development/security approach, in particular with regard to human rights, democracy and good governance. given the importance of the joint strategy of the action plan to be adopted at the eu-africa summit, i would ask the portuguese presidency to inform the european parliament in due course of the progress of the negotiation of these documents and their contents. this can be useful to ensure that the measures envisaged in the joint strategy and action plan can then be put into practice, with the support of the european parliament, in the control of the various applicable financial instruments. in the european parliament we hope that the joint strategy and action plan will reflect the commitments made by the european union, giving due priority to the fight against poverty and the millennium development goals, in particular access to basic health care and education. we want them to include joint measures to control the trafficking of small arms and light weapons, which are the real weapons of mass destruction in africa, and also measures to empower women and civil society. they are the force for change, peace and development that africa so badly needs.

is, among other things, a clear limitation on its potential. and there is a mistake that must and will be corrected in the next eu strategy, which must strengthen the role of the african union and be based on concepts of partnership and equality, pursuing a consistent concern for peace, the plight of displaced populations and the fight against major diseases such as aids and malaria. development if we contribute to the strengthening of democracy and human rights across the continent. the reformulation and renewal of a european strategy for africa must take account of new local and global circumstances. the fact that we are now in dialogue with an african union is in itself a relevant fact. on the other hand, the widespread increase in consumption, both of oil and food, implies a need acting president of the council. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by thanking you for your comments, suggestions and even criticisms of what the presidency intends to do in its programme for relations with the eu and africa. of all the suggestions, remarks, corrections, i have obviously taken due note. i should like to make it very clear that what we are proposing in terms of a new relationship with africa has two aspects which i would call innovative, or which we intend to be innovative and which actually prove to be innovative. firstly, we must establish an effective partnership with our african partners, and a partnership which also involves ownership. as i have already said, the strategy we are developing for africa is not one-sided. it is a joint strategy, a strategy which is drawn up, analysed and discussed together so that what it achieves and what it proposes is in fact what our african friends want and expect from us and what we would naturally also like to receive, in the obviously positive sense, from the african side. but we also want to broaden the range of actors involved in this strategy. we don't want it to be, as traditionally, just governments. we want to see other public institutions besides governments, parliaments, as i have mentioned, but also broad sectors of civil society, their representatives and their actors, and we want a second aspect which i think is extremely important: we want to modernise the eu-africa agenda, we want it to respond to new global challenges, to take account of the profound changes the world is undergoing and, above all, to offer africa the opportunity to integrate fully into the new global world. that is why we will discuss and debate with africa such new and modern issues, so to speak, as the energy issue, the climate change issue, issues linked to migration, mobility and employment, without, of course, neglecting issues which remain fundamental to our traditional partnership, such as peace, security, democratic governance and human rights, issues linked to science and the information society. it is an agenda, i believe, that is comprehensive, ambitious, but, as i say, above all modern. we want to modernise our agenda with africa, we want it to be able to respond effectively to what the needs are today. i would also like to say that the portuguese presidency, portugal, has never hesitated to appoint dictators in africa or anywhere else in the world and consequently to denounce them, and will always do so when it sees fit. finally, i would also like to express my appreciation for the work carried out jointly with the commission in preparing all this work leading up to the second europe-africa summit. we have received very strong support, very high quality support from the commission and the commissioners with concrete responsibility in these matters, whether in the field of trade, external action or humanitarian aid, and we are sure that we are all working towards a common goal of making a difference in africa and for africa.

majority and the opposition in zimbabwe, which should lead to fair and honest elections in march 2008. it is not over, but at any rate the last conversation i had with president mbeki opens up this prospect in a serious way. so let's not criticize south africa, they're doing the best they can, they're not doing too badly. i would simply point out that, in relation to the financial share allocated to agriculture, between the ninth and tenth european development funds, the agricultural sector has gone from eur 663 million to eur 1 100 million. what is true is that given the increase between the ninth and the tenth edfs, there is a decrease in absolute percentage but, in terms of resounding and stumbling means, there is an increase which is really substantial. and i must say that i was delighted to hear the president of the world bank, a few days ago, in washington, at the meeting i was attending, announce a much greater focus on development in agriculture, and so i completely share your concern, madam president. as regards the role of civil society and parliaments and the pan-african parliament, i can of course only express my full approval of this approach. in short, since the time is very short, i would like to deal with the question of epas again quickly, as i promised. you know my position on these agreements. they are an essential condition for africa's integration into globalisation. the asian examples show that it is not aid that is the most decisive factor for development, but economic development and integration into the world market. i believe that the epas are an opportunity for the acp to integrate into world trade in a gradual way, by first building regional markets. i would like to remind you that on 1 january 2008 we will not be seeing a pure and simple brutal liberalisation. what's this about? in fact, it is a gradual opening of markets with transitional periods of varying length depending on the products, with regional funds to provide financial support, and in particular to deal with the issue of the net tax loss following liberalisation. there are a lot of proposals that i think are interesting. we will also be able to mobilise relatively large resources in a whole series of areas which can create the optimum conditions for making this gradual liberalisation and gradual opening of markets useful, positive and productive. so i understand the apprehensions of both sides, but in relation to this request to postpone the date of the conclusion of the economic partnership agreements, i have to say that i do not see the advantage of this. the wto will not grant us - it is very good to pretend that it is possible - but the wto will not grant us an exception for the acp because our current regime is unfair to other developing countries who are demanding to be treated in the same way as their former colonies. the only alternative is the system of generalised preferences. ldcs will have access to everything but weapons, but for non-ldcs -- and there are 36, i just want to remind you -- that's a step back from their current access. the epas will continue to guarantee this preferential access to our historical partners, but above all they will help to support regional economic integration processes. and i think that's where the real potential is for trade to contribute to development. we are of course aware of the difficulties and the reluctance of our partners and the legitimate fears - i admit - of our partners. that is why we have proposed that we first conclude interim agreements which first of all resolve the trade question by including a reciprocal opening of trade compatible with the wto rules. as i have always said, the access offers of our acp partners will of course be based on the principle of asymmetry. we must remember that we are opening up our market completely and, in terms of flexibility, we will use all the room for manoeuvre available to us to take account of development concerns, including the need to protect the major part of agricultural production or the nascent industries. we are still working on that for the time being. the real challenge is to prevent non-ldc countries from being in a disastrous trade situation on 1 january. these countries obviously have trade issues which are considerable. if the question of access to markets is not settled by 1 january, it is obvious that they will be left with the system of generalised preferences, and so they will be left out, they will be left in a truly catastrophic position. so we have to push for these agreements to be at least temporary. that's it for the epas. finally, i would like to say that i fully agree with what president borrell has said in an extremely clear way. the challenge of both the summit and this strategy is to fundamentally change the nature of relations between europe and africa. to make it possible - i use his expression - to make strong partnerships between peers who respect each other, who have rights and duties towards each other, and to get out of this relationship - i would not say trivial, it is more serious than that - of this outdated, archaic, counterproductive, humiliating very often relationship, from donor to recipient.
in writing. the eu/africa summit should mark a shift in eu policies towards respect for the sovereignty and right to development of african countries and peoples, promoting a more just, peaceful, supportive and humane world. this requires, for example:- immediate measures of solidarity to ensure the most basic needs of millions of human beings;- respect for national sovereignty and independence, non-interference in the internal affairs of each country, the peaceful settlement of international conflicts;- demilitarisation of international relations, the gradual reduction of armaments and military expenditure; - fair and equitable international economic relations, against the impositions of the imf, wb and wto and the 'economic partnership agreements' for trade liberalization; - the cancellation of the external debt, already more than paid; - real policies of cooperation and active support for development in solidarity; and not relations based on neo-colonialist ambitions or paternalistic visions that try to recover the ground lost with the broad process of national liberation of the african peoples - won in the second half of the 20th century -, promote the interference and military presence of the great powers of the eu and the domination and exploitation of natural resources by transnational corporations.
on behalf of the pse group. i am speaking on behalf of the socialist group. this resolution reflects the european parliament's leading role in conventional disarmament, arms transfer controls and the deepening of international humanitarian law. we fought for the extension of the ottawa convention to all types of mines. we have advocated, well before the european council, a global arms trade treaty. the urgent need to transform the european union's code of conduct on arms exports into a legally binding instrument has also been a constant demand of this parliament. this resolution on cluster bombs is looking to the future, to what europe must do to eliminate these weapons which do not distinguish between civilians and military personnel and which take so many human lives. we propose an immediate moratorium on the use, production, stockpiling and export of these weapons. the moratorium must be transformed in due course into a legal instrument which will have the effect of banning these barbaric munitions from the arsenals and battlefields in the long term, just as anti-personnel mines are becoming scarce. in addition to calling on the european union to launch a diplomatic offensive in favour of this new instrument, we want its member states to lead by example and eliminate the use of these weapons by their armed forces, but also to permanently halt their export, production and accumulation. every day in lebanon, chechnya, afghanistan and dozens of other countries where wars have already ended, civilians pay the ultimate price for the criminal and immoral irresponsibility of armed forces which have lost sight of the ethical and legal limits which should guide the actions of civilized peoples. it is up to europe to lead a global alliance that restores, reaffirms and strengthens those boundaries. we urgently need a common position to eradicate bombs and other cluster munitions.

on behalf of the pse group. i commend rapporteur marco cappato not only for producing this useful report but also for his willingness to help make it as consensual as possible. his original intentions were laudable. it was about defeating two evils in one sitting: legalizing poppy cultivation and the production of opiates for medical purposes would not only end heroin production in afghanistan, but also the global shortage of pain medication. unfortunately, we have come up against a number of practical considerations, such as the fragility of afghan institutions and their inability to regulate opiate production, the uncertainty about the economic viability of such a scheme or the danger of allowing opium to be reintroduced in some of the 13 afghan provinces that have stopped producing it. my group's amendments have sought to refocus the report on what is fundamental: the fight against opium production in afghanistan, which does not only affect afghanistan and neighbouring countries. the drugs that this opium illegally produces are what some have called genuine weapons of mass destruction and are mainly based in europe. the fight against opium production should be sensitive to the specificities of different regions of afghanistan. only a combination of measures can succeed. firstly, it is essential to combat the rampant corruption in the afghan central administration, particularly in the ministry of the interior and the police, which has paralysed any policy to combat opium production. second, it is urgent to find, capture and prosecute the approximately 30 major traffickers identified in a 2006 un and world bank report, thus decapitating this murderous traffic. thirdly, nato must support afghan operations to combat trafficking, destroy laboratories and warehouses and prevent drug shipments. fourthly, the eradication of smallpox must be carefully and selectively applied and concentrated in areas where farmers have real alternatives. this brings us to the areas of agreement with the rapporteur. we are all against the indiscriminate spraying of poppy fields, as advocated by the united states of america, which will only add to the ranks of the taliban without affecting the production of heroin in a sustainable way. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all transport services, including the carriage of goods by road. above all, this report seeks to encourage the european council to be creative and bold in combating heroin production in afghanistan. there are no easy solutions to this challenge, but we know that the terrorism and violent obscurantism advocated by the taliban and al-qaeda will only be defeated when afghanistan is freed from the clutches of drugs. i have finished, mr president. this report should be seen as an urgent appeal to the member states to spare no effort in economic and political reconstruction of a country so marred by bloody conflicts and so important for regional and global security.
the rapporteur. madam president, commissioner, first of all i would like to thank the members who in the libe committee worked closely with me and helped me with their critical contributions, especially mr ignasi guardans, mr demetriou and last but not least mr fausto correia. mr fausto correia, of the socialist group, my portuguese colleague, leaves us all with a great deal of regret. he died after helping me with this job. i think the best tribute i can pay to him here is a kind of public promise that i will try, by my presence in the european parliament, to contribute to the realisation of his ideas about europe, europe as an ambitious project, a visionary project, a giant capable of bringing its culture of rights to the world. i would like to pay this tribute to our member of parliament, our dear colleague fausto correia. i would therefore like to sum up the issues raised in this report without wasting too much time. first of all, i would like to stress that this report is like any other an open report, open to the search for and achievement of the best solutions. the advantage of the french and german initiative, as the commissioner has already pointed out, lies mainly in two fundamental reasons. one is that by facilitating the monitoring and enforcement of alternative measures to prison sentences, we are promoting a political culture which induces a greater tendency in judicial practice to apply these measures. we are promoting the humanization of criminal law in the member states, we are promoting the quality of european criminal law. the second aspect is that this initiative will contribute to the growth of criminal law as a criminal law at european level, increasingly harmonized and less and less feudalised in national spaces. in fact, european integration, which took a fundamental step in the last treaty, the treaty on which an agreement was reached in lisbon last weekend, shows a level of integration that criminal law in the european area has not yet been able to keep up with. it is essential that a culture of not only mutual recognition but also of harmonisation of criminal law be promoted more and more in terms of the design of sentences, the manner in which they are carried out, the relationship between convicted persons and society, and even that a greater degree of equivalence be promoted between the substantive and procedural criminal laws of the member states. article 6 of the treaty on european union, by referring to a set of fundamental values which constitute the common values of the european union, clearly shows that it only makes sense that we should increasingly have a european criminal law. most of these assets are securities protected by criminal law. i would like to make only two or three fundamental remarks on this particular report: first of all, parliament's contribution stressed the need for the distribution of powers between the executing state and the sentencing state. there is a clear logic of the application of the law, each state which uses a certain jurisdiction applies its law to it; the principle of the exceptional nature of refusal in order to give the future framework decision the greatest possible effectiveness; the logic according to which it is impossible to adapt the measures on account of their nature, under the risk of calling into question the principle of strict legality of criminal law, and the need to safeguard the principle of the contradictory in cases of revocation of a suspended sentence or conditional sentence. i would like to conclude, madam president, by saying that all this progress in european criminal law will, after all, seem to us to be very little in the near future. europe will only be a reality when it has an anthropocentric and cosmopolitan legal system which cannot exclude a more harmonized and less divided idea of criminal law.
rapporteur. – mr president, i would just like to propose an oral amendment to my amendment 2, to clarify the text. i propose to delete the word ‘unacceptable’. therefore, it would read: ‘in clear infringement of the fundamental rights laid down in the european union treaties’. the political groups have already been informed.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover the transport of dangerous goods by road. while imposing restrictions on the community budget, the priorities are defined as competition policies - as exemplified by the progressive devirtuation of structural policy, placing it at the service of the 'lisbon strategy' - the communitarisation of 'internal security and immigration control' or the eu's external policy, which promotes interference and the militarisation of international relations. that is why we are voting against it. however, we note the approval of our proposals, such as: - increased funding for the structural funds, the posei (azores and madeira) and progress (equality between men and women) programmes; - support for cooperation between agricultural organisations and other rural actors, small farming and family farming; - increased funding of eur 2 million for the compensation programme for the additional costs associated with the disposal of certain fishery products from the outermost regions, which means an increase of eur 570 000 in funding for the autonomous regions of madeira and the azores.

in writing. it is essential that a common effort be made to seek to improve the standards of quality and effectiveness of justice. this is, however, a highly sensitive area characterised by enormous diversity, which highlights the need to strengthen trust in order to allow for the mutual recognition of judicial decisions, thus contributing to the progressive development of a european judicial culture. i support the excellent report by mrs assunção esteves, which, as part of the reinforcement of the principle of mutual recognition of sentences, aims to promote the social reintegration of convicted persons, while at the same time seeking to improve the protection of the victim and the prevention of reoffending. this framework decision aims to establish the rules on the basis of which a member state, within the limits of its competence, should monitor and supervise non-custodial measures (decisions relating to the enforcement of suspended sentences, alternative sanctions and additional sentences) imposed by judgments handed down in other member states. i hope that the portuguese presidency will be able to resolve the remaining issues and that a general agreement will be reached by the end of this year.
in writing. as the report states, the 1999 tampere european council identified the principle of mutual recognition as 'the cornerstone of judicial cooperation in both civil and criminal matters in the union'. a year later, the council adopted a programme of measures centred on this principle, aimed at adapting the mechanisms for the mutual recognition of final judgments and extending the application of the principle of transfer of sentenced persons to include persons resident in a member state. the hague programme later set new targets, particularly in the context of the so-called 'fight against terrorism', to advance the 'communitarisation' of this area which is at the heart of the sovereignty of states. in the light of this proposal, and as our group stresses, it is worrying that it should be stated that: 'despite the need to ensure that the sentenced person is afforded the appropriate safeguards, his participation in the proceedings should no longer be predominant, and his consent should no longer be required each time a judgment is transmitted to another member state for the purpose of its recognition and enforcement of the sentence imposed'. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the principle of equal treatment for men and women is respected.
in writing. this partnership agreement was concluded for a renewable period of six years, starting from 1 january 2007, and portugal obtained 7 fishing opportunities for surface longliners, which represents an increase of one fishing licence compared to the one stipulated in the previous agreement. the agreement stipulates, among other things, that at least 20% of the crew of each vessel must be nationals of the acp (african, caribbean and pacific) group of countries. the agreement sets out the implementation of the rules contained in the international labour organisation (ilo) declaration on fundamental principles and rights at work, which makes freedom of association and the effective recognition of the right of workers to collective bargaining mandatory, as well as the elimination of discrimination in matters of employment and occupation. the agreement also provides that the wages of crew members will be fixed in negotiations between the shipowners and the fishermen or their representatives, and the 'country of origin principle' is accepted, which introduces a factor of profound and unjust inequality. this protocol increases the contribution of shipowners by 40%, from eur 25 per tonne of fish to eur 35, thus reducing the community's share, which we do not think is acceptable.
in writing. we voted against the report as a form of protest against the way the commission intends to allocate fishing opportunities among the member states under this agreement. contrary to what has always happened in agreements of this kind, the commission intends to violate a basic principle which has been a fundamental instrument for ensuring justice and fairness between member states and, in practice, an implied agreement between them. the fact that it does not apply in this case is incomprehensible and unacceptable to us.
in writing. i abstained from voting on my report because, although i recognize the urgency of concluding the agreement and consider this proposal partly positive as regards the distribution of fishing licences, and given the impracticability of amending it, which is the responsibility of the council and the commission, i strongly disagree with the non-compliance with the principle of relative stability which has always been followed in previous agreements. i also regret that, for legal reasons, i cannot present several proposals for legislative amendments to the articles of the agreement, aimed at strengthening mozambican civil society by involving fishermen in the preparation of future agreements and at improving international rules for the occupational categories concerned, particularly as regards the fixing of minimum wage rules for acp seamen. i felt that the european parliament's political mandate is limited in this area, so i tabled other amendments, which i considered legally admissible, aimed at improving the information provided to the european parliament and requiring the parliament and the council to submit a report on the application of the agreement during the last year of the protocol and before the conclusion of any renewal agreement.
in writing. we cannot vote in favour of this fisheries agreement because we consider the allocation of fishing opportunities between the different member states defined therein to be disproportionate and inappropriate, because it does not safeguard the legitimate interests of portugal. this ec-mozambique partnership agreement entered into force on 1 january 2007 for a period of five years and provides for an increase of 2 000 tonnes in the community's tuna and tuna-like fisheries quota compared to the previous one. in the previous agreement, the level of utilisation of fishing opportunities for portugal (5) was very high, which led portugal to apply for 9 licences for surface longlining, plus the maintenance of fishing opportunities, in the demersal deep-sea shrimp freezer trawler category. however, it has obtained only 7 tuna fishing licences. this means that - in view of the previous allocation of licences and the (failure to) respect the principle of relative stability in the face of increased fishing opportunities - there is a marked imbalance in this new agreement: portugal gets only 2 more licences, while other member states get an increase of 16 (france) and 13 (spain) licences. if the council had decided unanimously, this would not have happened. that is why we are voting against it.
in writing. the regulation on business registers (council regulation (eec) no 2186/93) which compiles statistical information on businesses operating in the european union, including their number, type, size and other characteristics, was intended to provide eu policy-makers with reliable statistical data. on 1 june 2006, the european parliament gave its support to the substance of the commission's proposal at first reading, subject to 22 amendments dealing with the issue of administrative burden, clarification of the terms and conditions under which confidential data may be transmitted and, finally, a number of technical and drafting amendments. in its common position of 21 may 2007, the council fully endorsed the 22 amendments tabled by parliament. but then new bureaucracies created added difficulties to the process, so that it has dragged on until now, with all the costs involved, which is rightly denounced by the rapporteur.
in writing. the increase in food prices which has recently occurred is largely due to the successive reforms of the cap, the abandonment of production which it has promoted and, consequently, the disappearance of many small and mediumsized farms. by ignoring the specific reality of the member states in order to take account primarily of the interests of large agro-industrial companies, multinational food distribution companies and the negotiations for trade liberalization in the wto, it has contributed to changing the basis of agricultural activity with repercussions on the decline in production. on the other hand, the use of agricultural products for non-food purposes, in particular for the production of biofuels, which they seek to give priority, will not contribute to the development of agricultural activity but may, on the contrary, replace the production of foodstuffs and thus have a negative influence on the defence of food sovereignty. we therefore consider it essential to review the objectives of the common agricultural policy with a view to increasing food production, supporting small and mediumsized farms and livestock farming and moderating consumer prices by strengthening intervention mechanisms and ensuring adequate intervention prices.
in writing. although it contains aspects which we consider positive, this report avoids the analysis of the core reality of eu relations with africa, by omitting or bypassing its deep responsibilities and strategic objectives. perhaps the most striking example is its silence on the initiatives articulated within the framework of nato/usa/eu in relation to this continent, such as the creation of specific military commands (usa/africom), the conduct of military maneuvers (nato) or the growing military presence of the major eu powers ("peace support mechanisms", military missions). the report also contains elements that open the door to intervention - disguised as 'humanitarian', 'conflict management' or 'good governance' - and does not denounce the growing subordination of development policy to 'security' strategies - favouring 'development aid' provided by the military or the use of its funds for purposes unrelated to this - instrumentalising it in accordance with the strategic objectives of the great powers, namely the control of the immense natural resources, including oil, of this continent. the report also stresses the need to ensure that the economic partnership agreements are based on the 'dogma' of trade liberalisation as the basis for development. we reject such policies, while supporting the holding of the eu-africa summit.
in writing. the united nations on 17 september called on its member states to take immediate measures to deal with the terrible consequences of the use of cluster bombs, calling for the conclusion of a legally binding instrument of international humanitarian law prohibiting the use, development, production, stockpiling and transfer of such weapons. the united nations calls for the destruction of existing stockpiles of these weapons, calls for risk mitigation activities and assistance to victims, and recommends that member states, pending the conclusion of this instrument, apply a moratorium on the use and transfer of these weapons. as denounced in this resolution, there is evidence that 98% of the victims of these bombings are civilians, causing a high and brutal rate of death and injury, especially among children. the house also voted to extend the deadline for the submission of a report to the european parliament on the implementation of the eu's new energy strategy. it is urgent to put an end to the arms race. the end of weapons of mass destruction, cluster bombs, depleted uranium munitions and phosphorus shells is urgent. that is why we are supporting this resolution.
in writing. the ombudsman's records show that in 2006 he received 3830 complaints. however, the ombudsman considered that only 21.5% of the cases were within his remit and of these, 258 gave rise to an inquiry. in 2006, the ombudsman carried out a total of 582 inquiries, of which 315 had been carried over from 2005 and 9 were opened on his own initiative. it is interesting to note that, as in previous years, the institution which was the subject of the most inquiries was the commission, with a percentage of 66% of the total (387), followed by the european communities personnel selection office (epso), which was targeted at 13%, and the european parliament at 8%. the most cited vice was lack of transparency, including refusal of information (25%), followed by bias or abuse of power and a plurality of other forms of maladministration. however, as the ombudsman himself points out, there are many cases where his critical remarks clearly do not produce any effect, but they are undoubtedly a warning to existing problems, and parliament should therefore give them due attention.

mr commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, as a member elected by one of the seven outermost regions, i have to tell this house of the immense concern that the application of the directive we are now considering is causing in these regions. for one simple reason, the outermost regions are almost exclusively dependent on air transport and any increase in the cost of this service, the inevitable consequence of the application of the directive, will make it more difficult to reach these regions, aggravating their isolation, a decisive factor in the finding at european level of a specific status for the outermost regions, as enshrined in article 299 (2) of the treaties. on the other hand, the increase in the cost of air transport will accentuate the competitive disadvantage of these regions by hampering tourism, the main economic activity for most of these regions. a reduction in tourist flows and/or a decrease in spending per tourist is foreseeable, which could lead to a decrease of at least 2% in the gdp of the outermost regions, according to studies carried out by the government of the canary islands. the commission's communication on the outermost regions, entitled 'a stronger partnership for the outermost regions', which the european parliament fully supported, sets out two of the three main priorities of the european policy for the outermost regions: to make them more accessible by reducing their isolation and to promote their competitiveness. the contradiction and inconsistency with these priorities which will result from the application of this directive cannot be overlooked. i believe that for the first time we are faced with a legislative act of the european union which will have the consequence of increasing the isolation of these regions. the amendments nos 5 and 6 from the european people's party, tabled following a compromise between the rapporteur, mr peter liese, whom i congratulate on his excellent work, and mr jarzembowski and mrs christine de veyrac, are certainly moving in the right direction in terms of mitigating the impact of this directive, but they are not sufficient. i therefore call on the three institutions to find better solutions in the next stages of the legislative process to mitigate the impact of this directive on the outermost regions.
