in writing. the signing of this agreement between the european community and ukraine on the facilitation of the issuance of short-stay visas is being carried out in parallel with the signing of the readmission agreement, 'which are mutually conditional'. the report stresses that these agreements fall within the eu's 'fight against illegal immigration' and its instruments, and expressly stresses the fulfilment of the 'recommendations on the need for the ec and the european commission, in particular, to provide adequate technical and economic assistance to ukraine to achieve a high level of implementation of the readmission agreement'. what we criticize. although the agreement introduces strict procedural deadlines, establishes preferential visa fees, including a total exemption from the visa fee for certain 'categories of persons' (?) and provides for a simplified procedure for different situations, it falls short of what would be required and what thousands and thousands of ukrainian citizens need. the need, as the rapporteurs make clear, is for the effective implementation of measures to facilitate visa applications for wider groups of ukrainian society, including a visa-free regime without discrimination, as ukraine has done for citizens of the different eu countries. hence our vote.
in writing. the signing of this agreement between the european community and moldova on the facilitation of the issuance of short-stay visas is being carried out in parallel with the signing of the readmission agreement, which is 'mutually conditional', as is the case with the agreements with russia and ukraine. although the agreement introduces strict procedural deadlines, establishes preferential visa fees, including a full exemption from the visa fee for certain 'categories of persons' (such as members of official delegations, businessmen, journalists, participants in scientific, cultural and sporting events, students, participants in exchange programmes, close family members, representatives of civil society, persons visiting for medical reasons) and provides for a simplified procedure for different situations, it falls short of what would be required and what is needed by thousands and thousands of moldovan citizens. the need is for the effective implementation of measures to facilitate visa facilitation for wider groups of moldovan society, up to a visa-free regime without discrimination, as moldova has done for citizens of the different eu countries. in addition, such agreements fall within the community's immigration policies and the 'schengen area', which includes its biometric data retention instruments. hence our vote.
in writing. the commission's proposal for a new council regulation on the collection of data in the fisheries sector aims to develop long-term sampling programmes which are well integrated at regional level and include ecological, economic, environmental and social data. the revision of the data collection regulation is intended to respond to new demands arising from the need to move towards fisheries management (based on fleet and fishing areas as an alternative to fish stock management) and to apply an ecosystem approach to fisheries management. this is to ensure that the approach is more in line with the different realities of fisheries, which require different strategies to tackle a common problem. the aim is to make the procedures more transparent, ensuring that fisheries data are processed and used in a better and more effective way. the report of this parliament deserves my favourable opinion.
in writing. this proposal aims to replace, as from 2008, regulation (ec) no 1543/2003 on the community framework for the collection and management of data in the context of the common fisheries policy. the main differences between the present proposal and the current regulation are the inclusion of new types of data, the application of a more fleet-oriented approach and the distinction between different regions (fishing areas) and the drawing up of three-year national plans. the new text, among other things, clarifies the type of data to which the commission will have access, insists on safeguarding their confidentiality and provides for different levels of penalties depending on the failure of the member states to comply with the new regulation, including the conditionality of the community financial contribution to the national programmes to be drawn up by the member states. it also requests that the commission clearly define what should be understood as an 'official request for information' and an 'incomplete national programme'. it should be for each member state to adopt measures, based on the availability of reliable data and as complete as possible for scientific research into fisheries, for the sound management of its marine biological resources. however, it is a competence of each member state which is unacceptably called into question by the so-called 'reform' treaty.
in writing. the commission ensures the production of community statistics by coordinating the necessary harmonization of statistical data, the collection of which is carried out by the member states, addressing issues such as the definition of variables, discrimination, dates of application and frequency, etc. gender should also be broken down in order to have information on any gender differences. as regards health and safety at work, account should also be taken of studies and surveys by the european agency for safety and health at work and the european foundation for the improvement of living and working conditions. outside europe, greater cooperation should be established with the united nations, and in particular with the international labour organization and the world health organization. complementary funding for health and safety at work will be provided under the community programme for employment and social solidarity (progress). in principle, financial assistance should be provided to help member states to strengthen national capacities to improve and create new tools for statistical data collection.
in writing. as the report states, sport must be given full attention, because of its social and cultural aspects and the social and educational values it conveys, such as self-discipline, overcoming personal limitations, solidarity, healthy competition, respect for the opponent, social integration, combating all forms of discrimination and team spirit, as well as tolerance. thus, in a multicultural society, sport can and should be an integral part of formal and informal education, as studies have shown that regular physical exercise improves physical and mental health and, in parallel, contributes positively to the learning process. we therefore agree with the call to the member states and the competent authorities to give greater priority to the development of health in school and pre-school education programmes, by encouraging specific forms of physical activity at these ages, and also by providing greater awareness-raising by clubs and associations so that children can start physical activity as early as possible for the benefit of their development and health, so that physical education is given a status that is in line with the profile of the institution and the corresponding level of study.
in writing. the role of sport in education is a topic of relevance to a number of titles. for example, obesity is on the rise throughout europe, particularly among young people. this is an alarming fact, a public health concern, and the effects of which will be felt for the lifetime of these people. we must not forget that these citizens will have health problems for the rest of their lives, which will have major social and economic effects on the organization and future of our societies. another relevant fact is the evidence that throughout the eu the time allocated to physical education has been gradually decreasing. well, we can infer that the increase in physical inactivity has also contributed to the most alarming of the figures - in the eu-27, overweight affects almost one in four children. i voted in favour of this report which seeks to contribute to positive action in favour of the health of the younger generations.
in writing. soil is known to have a basic social function, being essential for the production of food and other agricultural crops and the storage and processing of energy and minerals, as well as acting as a natural filter for groundwater, the main source of drinking water, a habitat for a plurality of organisms living on or on the surface of the soil, a platform for human activity and an important element of the landscape and cultural heritage. so it's a key component of the earth's environment. there are already several community policies aimed at protecting these essential functions, although not the soil itself. as the impact assessment carried out by the commission shows that soil degradation is worsening, there is concern for soil protection, linked also to concern for climate change, the preservation of a sufficient supply of unpolluted water, the protection of biodiversity and the fight against desertification and deforestation. further community legislation specifically aimed at protecting soil itself must result from an exchange of information and coordination between member states and should not impose any unnecessary additional administrative burden or jeopardise agricultural production and the social function of land.
in writing. i consider the commission's analysis to be relevant and i agree with the proposed strategy on soil protection, a non-renewable resource which provides vital services for human activities and the survival of ecosystems. i support the prodi report, considering its proposals to better understand the relationship between soils and the issues of biodiversity, desertification and climate change to be particularly relevant.
in writing. the protection of the environment in europe is a politically relevant subject, the development of which has been intensifying in recent years and whose research remains a priority for the union. the protection of the environment in europe cannot therefore be achieved without the protection of soils. these are exposed to various degradation processes and the need for specific measures to protect them makes perfect sense in the context of a new european framework in this field. we recognize that land is mostly private property, but even more so that land is a natural resource of common interest and that, for that very reason, it must be preserved for the benefit of future generations. considering that soil protection is closely linked to the main environmental challenges of international dimension, there is a need to study community legislation specifically aimed at protecting the soil itself, which could provide for the exchange of information and the coordination of good practices between member states. the integration of soil protection into a future climate regime thus seems to imply the recognition of the need for greater awareness of the role of soil protection in mitigating and adapting to climate change.
in writing. i voted in favour of the peter liese report on a proposal to amend directive 2003/87/ec and to include aviation activities in the greenhouse gas emission allowance trading scheme in the community, as i consider the integration of the aviation sector in the emission allowance trading scheme to be a key measure to mitigate the effects of climate change. the contribution of aviation to climate change is substantial and growing rapidly, and this proposal for a directive is therefore an important step towards meeting the ambitious targets for reducing greenhouse gas emissions in the european union. i believe, however, that it is essential to adopt measures to adapt this directive to the reality of the outermost regions, so as to avoid the social and economic impact of the emissions regime being particularly high in these regions. i therefore regret that amendments nos 98=100/rev and 97=99/rev were not adopted.
in writing. we have serious doubts about the overall content of the proposals adopted in this resolution of the european parliament, and we have therefore not voted in favour of it. we are against emissions trading, which always protects those with the most money to buy emission rights and does not solve the problem of excess co2 emissions. secondly, because countries and regions where air services are essential, such as the outermost regions of the azores and madeira, are not taken into account. for example, both flights between these islands and flights between the continental european area and these regions are particularly important for territorial cohesion in the european union and should therefore be given special treatment. we regret that the inclusion of the outermost regions in the eu territory and of all flights arriving/departing from european airports has not been taken into account in the assessment of the impact of this directive, which will be more severe in these regions than in the european average, both in terms of the use of aircraft by their inhabitants and the impact of tourism on regional development. it has also failed to take account of the dramatic consequences for its competitiveness of a tax burden on air links from which its neighbours are exempt.
in writing. the commission's proposal to include aviation in the emissions trading scheme is an important element in the package of measures to be taken internationally. we cannot deny the significant increase in greenhouse gas emissions in the aviation sector; the solution to the problem through emission allowance trading therefore appears to be a useful instrument, especially if it is properly designed and articulated with other measures that support market stability and do not distort competition. the measures we are taking today will set a precedent for the negotiations that follow at international level, and the union must therefore have a strong position and solutions that actually have an effect on protecting the environment, while defending our industries and our freedoms. while recognising that this is a difficult exercise, the rapporteur and all of us should be commended for our efforts to seek commitments that make a real case for mitigating the effects of climate change and balancing economic and social activities in europe.
the schengen area is one of the greatest successes in the history of european integration and the most successful expression of freedom of movement, with the abolition of internal borders and the adoption of various compensatory measures, such as the reinforcement of external border controls, police and judicial cooperation and the creation of the schengen information system. schengen, like the european union, has been growing. of the five founding member states, there are now 15, including two non-eu countries, iceland and norway, and with a partial participation of ireland and the united kingdom. we are therefore facing a historic event, the largest enlargement in the history of schengen, with the simultaneous lifting of the internal borders with the new member states, the czech republic, estonia, hungary, latvia, poland, lithuania, slovenia, slovakia and malta. this is a significant fact for europe, for free movement and for these new member states and their citizens. i start by welcoming them and congratulating them. we congratulate them on their entry into this area, but we congratulate them above all on the systematic and committed effort they have shown to meet all the requirements of the strict schengen rules. the december 2006 reports, already referred to by the secretary of state, josé magalhães, had pointed out several problems which have since been overcome in their overwhelming majority. the evaluation teams were composed of experts from all member states, travelled to borders and consulates and produced comprehensive reports containing factual descriptions, assessments and recommendations, many of which required additional measures and follow-up visits in the face of problems still encountered in the vast majority of member states. i would like to congratulate the evaluation team, chaired by dr carlos moreira, not only for the demanding work they have carried out in a short time, but also for not simply fulfilling their role as an inspector, suggesting several times measures and solutions that have allowed the problems identified to be solved. the absence of internal borders, mr president, not only requires better controls at the external borders and the smooth transmission of information and data through the sis, but is above all an exercise in mutual trust in which everyone must ensure strict compliance with the rules adopted. ensuring good control at our borders is about ensuring the safety of all european citizens. the security of the schengen area depends on the rigour and effectiveness of each member state's control of its external borders and on the quality and speed of the exchange of information through sis. the fragility or improper functioning of any of these elements endangers the security of the union. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. that is why the european parliament, in the political resolution it is going to adopt, which is signed by five political groups, and also in the legislative resolution, asks to be informed in detail within six months of the details still outstanding. that is why we are also calling for a global assessment of the functioning of the schengen area to be carried out within two years, involving all the member states, both past and present. finally, i would like to thank the presidency for its commitment and spirit of collaboration, and i would like to thank in particular the portuguese government and in particular the secretary of state, mr josé magalhães, who is here, for the solution which has been the sisone4all, as already emphasized by vice-president frattini. this solution made it possible to connect the new member states to sis. if that had not been the case, we would not have been able to extend the schengen area this year, given the delay in the sis ii. i know, mr secretary of state, of the high level of your personal commitment and i would also like to congratulate dr eduarda peixeiro, to whom much is owed for the solution adopted. the commission's final two notes, the first for the european commission, are intended to remind parliament once again that the creation of sis ii remains a priority for the european parliament (the problem of not allowing new member states access to the system has already been solved by sisone4all), particularly because it will allow more efficient use of data within the community framework, improving security, both by introducing biometric data and by interlinking alerts. and as regards the council, i cannot but regret that at the beginning of this consultation process the council did not respect the principle of loyal cooperation with parliament by refusing to send the evaluation reports drawn up by experts on grounds of security. although a compromise was reached, which allowed the solution to be found for the time being, it is urgent to find a solution for the future. it is absurd to deny parliament the elements on which it exercises its legislative powers. mr president, we have taken another step forward in the march of european integration. it is up to all of us to ensure that this step leads to greater freedom but also to greater security.

madam president, in this debate it is important to stress that the success of the european union depends on the responses it can give in terms of solidarity and economic and social cohesion. when poverty in the european union is still high, reaching 17% of the population, or about 80 million people in the eu of 27, when precarious employment is worsening and the share of the working poor is increasing, the key priority must be to break with neoliberal policies and give priority to employment with rights, decent wages, increased social protection and high-quality public services for all, to support productive investment by micro and small enterprises, to make a fairer distribution of the wealth produced, in order to promote real convergence between the member states, to promote development and social progress and also to pursue a policy of cooperation with the third world countries.
the european union faces the great challenge of succeeding in the era of globalisation: how to reconcile competitiveness with social cohesion is the question, globalisation with regulation, therefore. the lisbon strategy contains the answer, and the lisbon treaty will facilitate decision-making, but success will depend above all on how europe views globalisation: as an opportunity rather than a threat. you have to understand what's going on with china and india. china has overtaken britain, france and italy as the most industrialized nation, has overtaken the united states as the leading exporter of technological products, has accumulated enormous monetary reserves. as for india, few know the name tata. however, the automobile subsidiary of tata was worth more on the stock market in 2006 than general motors, and no one had heard of the mittal group until it launched a hostile takeover bid on arcelor, causing panic in paris, brussels and luxembourg. but we must not forget the other side of the asian miracle, a story of suffering made up of the complicity of the beijing government with western multinationals who relocated their factories to take advantage of cheap labour and the absence of the welfare state. on the other hand, it is asia that will win or lose the challenge of combating global warming. in international trade, europe must be firm, demand reciprocity, but not adopt protectionist policies as a system. it is true that chinese competition is unfair because of low wages, the absence of political and trade union rights, counterfeiting or undervalued currency. all of this is true. but it is also true that there are 800 million chinese and 700 million indians who are eager to access a minimum income worthy of their human condition and to demand more social justice. challenges for a stronger europe, for a better world.
in writing. as has been pointed out, the whole of southern europe is bounded by the boundary of two tectonic plates which cross the mediterranean and extend across the atlantic ocean through some of the islands of the azores, making earthquakes one of the most frequent natural disasters in this region. the ep's report contains a diverse set of concerns and proposals which we value, particularly when it acknowledges that the outermost regions 'are regularly victims of these phenomena' or when it points, among other things, to the need to support member states' action in the areas of prevention, response and damage repair; information to the population; scientific research; civil protection and solidarity at community level. as regards coordination, the report proposes cooperation mechanisms between member states and between member states and third countries to implement the measures set out above. however, although it supports the creation of a 'european civil protection force' as a 'centralised prevention and management tool' - a line with which we disagree - it stresses that this 'will only be useful if it is based on improved national civil protection and better instruments for coordination between member states', which in our view puts the question back where it should be.
in writing. while we support a number of aspects of humanitarian aid which are highlighted in the report, we cannot support a 'consensus' on eu principles, objectives and strategy in the field of humanitarian aid in third countries which calls for the promotion of 'the right, or even the duty, to intervene in the event of serious violations of international humanitarian law (ihl) and/or human rights', considering that 'coercive measures, including military intervention', may be used as a 'last resort'. we know the results of such a policy of "good intentions", see the aggression and military occupation of iraq by the us and its allies and their hundreds of thousands of dead. as has been pointed out, the so-called 'humanitarian intervention' is often concealed by other real objectives which use it and exploit it in the interests and unscrupulous calculations of the great powers and transnational powers, thus calling into question basic principles of international law. we believe that the solution to the serious problems affecting millions of human beings depends, among other things, on respect for the sovereignty of all peoples and countries, on the peaceful settlement of international conflicts, on meeting the urgent needs of the economically poorer countries on a friendly and supportive basis and on their effective development.
in writing. i voted in favour of the cristina gutiérrez-cortines report on a proposal for a european parliament and council directive establishing a framework for the protection of soil and amending directive 2004/35/ec, because i believe that soils are a vital resource that must be protected to mitigate the effects of climate change and ensure that the activities of future generations can take place in a safe and healthy environment. in this sense, i consider that this proposal contributes to effective soil protection in that it sets out the objectives for which there is no community and/or national legislation. however, it should be for member states to decide, in the light of their specific situation, which measures should be given priority, while respecting the principle of subsidiarity.
in writing. we know the importance of soil protection, right from the start, for agriculture, which will have to produce more food and require more water, so soil protection is essential to safeguard food production and to ensure sufficient and clean water for future generations, and land has a social function which no private interest should call into question. soil is a platform for human activities, including cities and infrastructure, but also for nature and landscapes, so its protection is crucial to preserving our cultural heritage and natural resources. but the proposal put forward by the european commission is not the most appropriate one, because of its partial approach, the impositions it imposes and the little value it gives to agriculture. the european parliament has significantly amended it with proposals in defence of the principle of subsidiarity, recognising the importance of agriculture and the right of 'each member state, taking into account its climate, soil characteristics ... to decide its own agricultural policy in relation to soil' and recognising different approaches to soil protection. however, it does contain some aspects which merit our reservations. hence our final vote of abstention.
in writing. i consider it extremely important that there should be a framework directive on soil protection, since it is a non-renewable resource that provides vital services for human activities and the survival of ecosystems, especially as the issue of climate change is becoming increasingly worrying and there is no specific european legislation on soil protection at present. i therefore support the gutiérrez-cortines report and vote against all amendments which seek to reject the commission's proposal or to weaken the gutiérrez-cortines report significantly.
in writing. after several years of negotiations between the council, the commission and the european parliament, the decision amending the previous decision of 1999 on the rules for the exercise of implementing powers conferred on the commission was finally adopted in 2006. the regulatory procedure with scrutiny has thus been introduced, which is to be used for the adoption of measures of general scope designed to amend (by deleting or adding) non-essential elements of a basic act adopted pursuant to article 251 of the treaty, i.e. by codecision. this is a new comitology procedure which should be applied to a list drawn up by the commission containing 25 acts already adopted and to be adapted, including this regulation on the schengen borders code. i therefore support the technical proposals put forward by the rapporteur, mr michael cashman, which seek to take account of the specific features of the schengen borders code, since it is a development of the schengen acquis.
in writing. it is true that the long-term consequences of gmo technology are not yet known. the statements of scientists are contradictory, and many people fear possible dangers and risks. the precautionary principle should therefore be respected and its use in agriculture should not be insisted upon. however, directive 2001/18/ec on the deliberate release into the environment of genetically modified organisms covers the experimental release of gmos into the environment, i.e. the introduction of gmos into the environment for experimental purposes (such as field testing) and the placing on the market of gmos (products containing or consisting of gmos), for example for cultivation, import or industrial processing. we think it is important that there should be at least more general control of gmo technology, at least as regards the procedures, as the european parliament now wants, but we insist on the need to apply the precautionary principle, both in agriculture and in processed foodstuffs.
in writing. this directive is of the utmost importance given the growing concern about money laundering and its role in the financing of international crime and terrorism. the community approach is thus necessary, creating uniform rules, closing gaps and seeking to maintain a balance between the need for control and the requirements of the protection of the internal market and the free movement of capital. i support this initiative which aims to update directive 2005/60/ec on money laundering, in particular with regard to all the implementing measures contained in article 41 thereof. this is another case of updating the existing legislation under the new regulatory procedure with scrutiny under the comitology decision. the european parliament will have greater powers of control over the implementing powers conferred on the commission.
in writing. the proposal amends the provisions of directive 2005/60/ec on the prevention of the use of the financial system for the purpose of money laundering and terrorist financing, which provided for a temporary restriction of the implementing powers conferred on the commission in this area. in accordance with the recent decision on the exercise of the commission's powers, this restriction is abolished, but the european parliament retains the right to monitor the implementation of acts adopted under the codecision procedure. it is therefore clarified that possible amendments to this directive will be submitted, in addition to the council, to the european parliament for its consideration. however, this should not mean that national parliaments are excluded from the legislative process or merely referred to a process of transposing directives adopted in this field at community level. the european parliament has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. finally, we must point out the inconsistency of the european union, which, while advocating the fight against money laundering, is promoting the total freedom of movement of capital and tax havens.
in writing. since 2005, publicly traded companies have been required, under certain conditions, to prepare their consolidated accounts in accordance with international accounting standards. these standards were developed by a private organisation (the international accounting standards committee foundation/international accounting standards board) based in london, and were subsequently transposed into community law by means of a regulation. this resolution, although with some reservations, accepts the commission's proposal to amend this regulation by adopting a standard (ifrs 8) which in turn incorporates a north american standard (sfas 131) into community legislation. this is accepted without, as mentioned in the resolution, the impact assessment carried out by the commission having sufficiently taken into account the interests of users and the needs of small and mediumsized enterprises established in different european countries and of enterprises operating only locally. that is why we do not support this resolution.
in writing. there is much to be said about this resolution on the recent eu-russia summit, so only a few examples are highlighted as to its purpose. for example, while dismissing the us administration's initiatives and deep responsibilities in promoting a new escalation in the militarization of europe - it is emphasized, with the support of nato members - it considers that the 'statements of the russian authorities' and the 'inappropriate threat ... to withdraw from the treaty on conventional forces in europe have raised serious concerns as regards the maintenance of peace and stability on the european continent'. for example, more or less directly, it puts the emphasis on the essentials, i.e. 'the acquisition by community companies of strategic stakes in certain russian companies', 'the importance of improving the investment climate in russia' for the benefit of the major financial groups in the eu or 'equal access to markets, infrastructure and investment' based on the principles of the 'energy charter treaty'. and in line with the previous examples, it maintains political pressure on the russian federation, including by seeking to promote instruments of interference, while ignoring the unacceptable situation of the most elementary rights of the russian-speaking population in latvia, an eu member state.
in writing. the eu-russia summit, which took place after the discussion of this report but before the vote, marked the 18th anniversary of the fall of the berlin wall. eighteen years later, what was eastern europe is a democratic space where the market economy has been consistently established. on the contrary, russia is far from being democratized and transformed into a reliable partner. in energy, in kosovo, in the caucasus, in central asia, in ukraine, in moldova, in the iranian nuclear issue, russia has not been a sufficient part of the solution. the same week the european council on foreign relations presented a report which stated that in the relationship between the european union and russia, the russians have been setting the rules, while europe shows a lack of unity and strategy, and in some cases does not seem to be. the european union has been a major player in the development of the region for a long time. it is therefore rightly suggested that the eu strategy should be more demanding, so that that country respects the principle of legality. even if it is not a liberal democracy, it is necessary that russia is a predictable and reliable state. and europe must commit itself to that outcome.
on behalf of the pse group. mr president-in-office, mr commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i would first like to congratulate the rapporteur, mrs satu hassi, on her initial text and on her ability to generate compromise on this complex subject. the text we are voting on reflects a real effort by the various political groups to make the message to bali clear, effective and mobilizing. only then will it be possible to achieve the central objective of making the bali meeting the starting point for all world opinions to make clear and quantified political commitments to combat climate change by 2009. all parties have had to make sacrifices and adjustments. we shall have achieved our objective if this text is approved by parliament as a whole, and if it gives democratic legitimacy to the european union's pioneering role in environmental and climate matters before the whole world. this pioneering nature of the european union, however, gives it increased responsibilities, particularly with regard to the quality of the concrete proposals submitted. furthermore, these proposals must include either size/reduction or size/adaptation. in particular, it is necessary to take into account that the greatest costs of adaptation are already being borne by the poorest regions of the world, those which have contributed least to the problem and are least able to solve it. the proposals will also have to aim at equitable, proportionate and fair distribution of the different international burdens of responsibility for reduction. environmental commitments need to be reconciled with the development process to which the poorest countries and regions are entitled, including access to normal levels of well-being and comfort, both by the least developed countries and by the vast populations of emerging economies. european pioneering is a duty, but it should also be seen as an opportunity to gain comparative technological and innovation advantages associated with the environment. however, the truth is that this advantage will only materialize if environmental concerns and commitments gradually become the rule of the world economy. if this is not done, the union's good practice will become a source of distortion of competition and disillusionment on the part of its citizens. in this context, parliament is making concrete progress in suggesting that, in addition to national commitments, global sectoral commitments be exploited by creating internationally accepted references, benchmarks and good practices for all sectors of industry and services involved in international competition. this is a highly ambitious agenda, but the eu has the responsibilities to play a positive leadership role, which is very important for the survival of the planet we are assuming in this matter.
the role of the european union in the world today is absolutely indispensable if we are to achieve some of the essential balances in the pursuit of peace and justice on the planet. in this sense, the logic of associating some countries more specifically through bilateral agreements must not disrupt the multilateral deepening that a global vision requires of us. the unquestionable presence of universal human rights and the guarantee of fundamental freedoms in the european union's relations with the world must be the motive for any negotiable premise with any partner in the world. the mediterranean region is even more so. this region, because of its geographical proximity to europe, its ancestral affinity, its cultural diversity and its continuing political instability, must require the european union to take a very determined approach to these fundamental issues. i therefore welcome the rapporteur's emphasis on this in his report on the european neighbourhood policy. it is worth mentioning that the proposals which president sarkozy is now putting on the table for the unification of the mediterranean are completely out of context. although it is an absolutely useful proposal for the revival of the debate on the mediterranean, it proposes on the one hand the dismantling of the current partnership and on the other hand it is dissociated from the fundamental premises of the european union as regards the primacy of universal human rights and fundamental freedoms, considering them as side issues in the face of a pragmatism on a case-by-case basis that would feed a multi-speed relationship. our role is not to fuel the retreat of our partners or to fuel divisions. we must push for change and progress, particularly in the area of rights, but always ensuring that our investments provide opportunities for growth and economic development for the whole region. so ensuring the implementation of the free trade area in 2010 in the region, among all its peers, is an objective within our reach, but without ever losing sight of our essence of humanist and democratic values and rights.

mr president, commissioner, i too would like to congratulate our rapporteur, mr braghetto, on the excellent work he is doing here and i would like to start by saying that the inability of the current common fisheries policy to ensure the sustainability of this activity is most clearly illustrated by the situation we are facing today with bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and in particular in the mediterranean. and this has recently been recognised by a very interesting study commissioned by the directorate-general for fisheries, which commissioner joe borg has taken the care to make public, and for which i would like to thank him. the fact is that the harsh measures we are now seeing in this area, with the total closure of fishing before the end of the year, the attempt to slaughter a substantial part of the fleet, the prospect of total paralysis of activity, even if it may not be able to achieve its objectives, is a direct consequence of a conception of the common fisheries policy in which decisions on management have been dissociated from its implementation and control and in which fishing communities and authorities have been discharged of responsibility by an exclusive european competence which, however, has not been exercised by those who claim it. traditional fishing techniques such as the use of the pole and the hook, which are environmentally sustainable but less economically profitable, have been forced to confront modern technologies and highly sophisticated means, which are incomparably more profitable in the short term but not environmentally sustainable, and it is only now that some discriminatory measures against the latter type of vessels have finally emerged, which i would like to support and emphasize my full support for what has been said here by my comrade rosa miguélez, namely that it is essential to give priority to artisanal fishing methods. the situation of the imminent threat of commercial extinction of the rabies fishery should serve as a basis for reflection on what needs to be done in the overall common fisheries policy.
i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr alexandru athanasiu, with whom i have had the opportunity to meet on several occasions in recent months and who is now presenting the result of what i would call good work. i have in fact been following the content of the report under discussion today and the negotiations with the commission and the council since june this year, and i can say with complete confidence today on behalf of the epp-ed that we have reached a compromise text of a very high quality and very solid. if parliament adopts the amendments to the commission proposal in this plenary session, as i hope, it is known that the council has already informed us that it will also adopt the same amended proposal for a regulation. i believe that this report will prove to be a useful tool in identifying sectors in the european union where there is a need for workers and, in this respect, in promoting solvency and better management in terms of training. i would also like to point out - and this seems important - that the content of this report does not represent any more bureaucratic burden or any more inconsequential legislation, since in its current version it does not incorporate any overlapping of existing initiatives or tools. the report also shows a good balance between the need to provide information for statistical purposes and the need not to burden businesses, especially small and medium-sized ones, with unnecessary bureaucratic procedures. i therefore believe that all the conditions are met for its adoption at first reading and i recommend that this decision be adopted by this house.
the european union is not only a political force, but also a political force, and it is a political force, and it is a political force, and it is a political force. there is no doubt that more and better cooperation for development is urgently needed in a world faced with a new arms race and the increasing militarization of international relations, led by the united states and its allies. we are therefore very concerned about attempts to subordinate development aid to security strategies, and to promote its use for the more or less disguised purposes of interference, plundering of resources and neo-colonialism. in analysing the international situation, external causes should not be omitted or devalued, by fomenting and aggravating contradictions which are often at the root of the problems. the list of so-called fragile states drawn up by the world bank, which is more than subjective, is sufficient to prove this. how many situations of external interference and aggression does this not reflect? yes, there is an urgent need for an agenda for cooperation and development that responds to the most basic needs of millions of human beings, based on respect for national sovereignty and independence and the peaceful settlement of international conflicts; an agenda that promotes the demilitarisation of international relations, that promotes equitable and fair economic relations and the cancellation of the external debt that is already more than paid; an agenda that combats the policies that are the cause of deep injustices and inequalities and that builds a more just, more peaceful, more supportive and more humane world.
on behalf of the pse group. in fragile states, the interlinkage between governance, development and security is most prominent. it is essential that the eu sets strategic priorities in its relations with these states, guided by the overarching concept of human security. it is not enough to support government institutions, it is essential to invest in strengthening parliamentary scrutiny, in strengthening free and plural media, in the independence of judicial systems and in the empowerment of civil society as a priority for the empowerment of women, vulnerable groups and minorities. this requires a consistent commitment from the eu. today's somalia is a tragic example of european alienation. this also requires that causes of fragility that instigate violent conflict, further aggravating state incapacity, poor governance, extreme poverty, or human rights violations, for example, are addressed in bilateral dialogue and often the council, commission and member states fail to do so. the causes of fragility must be taken into account in the definition of strategies and in the globalisation of eu financial instruments. development aid should be people-centred and should only provide direct financial support to governments when there is evidence of commitment to conflict resolution, the building of the democratic rule of law and the improvement of governance and human security for the people. finally, and this is unfortunately the aspect omitted in the commission communication and the resolution we are about to vote on, it is essential that the eu invests more, alongside ddr and ssr programmes, in the overall control of transfers of small arms, as these fuel armed conflicts which perpetuate the fragility of many states.

in writing. as we have long argued, we consider that the areas of justice and home affairs are central competences of the states, particularly the portuguese state. we therefore reject its gradual transfer to the supranational institutions of the eu, in a process which justifies each new 'breakthrough' on the basis of the previous 'breakthrough'. this is the case with the creation of the so-called 'schengen area' and its acquis, which serves as a catalyst for the communityisation of policies or measures relating to border control - visa, asylum or immigration - or mechanisms at police and judicial level. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the european parliament's powers are not undermined by the fact that the european parliament is not a political body. as we have said, the necessary and indispensable international and european cooperation between sovereign and equal states on this whole range of issues is one thing, but the unacceptable handing over of essential components for safeguarding national sovereignty and democracy to supranational institutions dominated by the great powers of the eu for the creation of a 'fortress europe' is another. hence our vote.
in writing. the establishment of a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna at eu level is the practical implementation of one of the measures adopted by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas. the plan provides, inter alia, for the progressive reduction of the catch quota, periods of immobilization of the fleet, the increase of minimum sizes and a programme of observation on board vessels and at aquaculture stations. the adopted recommendation also provides for financial compensation to be granted to fishermen during periods of temporary technical immobilisation of the fleet. such compensation should be aimed at ensuring the safeguarding of the fleet and employment in the sector. we also consider it important to improve controls by regularly updating the quantity caught by the various vessels, in order to avoid that the allocated quotas are exceeded by some countries to the detriment of others, as is currently the case. it should be remembered that the bluefin tuna fishery was closed from september to december because it was suspected that quotas had already been exceeded by some countries, as it turned out. finally, we regret that our proposal, which emphasized that small-scale coastal and artisanal fishing, in addition to employing thousands of people, allows for the sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources, was rejected.
in writing. we voted against this resolution, which takes up the essential aspects of neoliberal policies at community level and seeks to encourage their application at world level. it is a resolution which accepts flexicurity as a concept to be developed and integrated into the national reform plans of each member state, which attempts to clarify the real implications and objectives of the lisbon strategy and its guidelines for economic and employment policies, in particular the liberalisations and privatisations associated with it. we cannot accept a resolution which welcomes the intention to develop an external dimension to the lisbon strategy, namely the promotion of the liberalization of markets on a world scale, emphasizing its neoliberal character and interference with the economic orientations of third countries. the european commission's communication on its contribution to the october meeting of heads of state and government states that the relaunch of the lisbon strategy for growth and jobs has been successful, but it should be added 'for the large national and international economic and financial groups' who have seen their profits grow exponentially, unlike workers facing reductions in their rights.
in writing. our vote against this resolution is based on our position in principle on the community of justice and home affairs, an area which is at the heart of the sovereignty of the states. the community approach to justice and home affairs is to be transformed into a common policy by the so-called 'reform' treaty. the community's role in the world economy is not limited to the economic and social spheres, but also to the political sphere. the restrictive asylum policy and the increasing difficulties faced by asylum seekers in securing their rights and guarantees are to be seen. the immigration policy is seen in its security aspect, its criminalization of irregular immigrants, its inhuman 'detention centres' and repatriation measures, its discriminatory, exploitative and predatory nature of human resources from third countries. the increasing creation of the ever-larger information and data storage tool - including biometric data - to which a wider set of entities, including third countries, have access, as exemplified by the access to air passenger data by us entities.
in writing. i voted in favour of the european parliament's motion for a resolution on limiting global climate change to 2 degrees celsius - trajectory to 2020 and beyond (cop 13 and cop/mop3). given that climate change is one of the greatest challenges facing societies today, i believe it is essential that the european union reiterates its leadership role at the bali conference and that a future global climate agreement after 2012 is reached.
in writing. amendment no 7 breaks the spirit of compromise which presided over the negotiation of the final text. the fact that it has been adopted introduces a fundamental change in a text that should preserve a broad parliamentary consensus on the challenges of bali. in the spirit of this overall objective, and although i had indicated my support for the socialist party as a shadow rapporteur, i was forced to abstain in the final vote as an individual, in protest against two aspects: the introduction into the text of amendment no 7, which supports nuclear energy; and the rejection of the method used by the epp in the face of the spirit of compromise which presided over the negotiation of the text.
in writing. it is a fact that we are witnessing unnatural climate change, resulting from many factors, but particularly from the predatory nature of the very marked and accelerated neoliberal policies, which require effective measures to adapt human societies to new living conditions. climate change predicted in a number of credible and scientifically substantiated scenarios may not be slow and progressive, depending on the measures taken in the meantime. it is therefore urgent to take further action at global level and across the board to avoid more serious problems in the future and even the multiplication of human and environmental tragedies. but we also insist that a break with neoliberal policies is necessary at european and world level, otherwise the great powers and multinationals will continue to impose their profitable interests, both in the exploitation of natural resources and in international trade, including greenhouse gas emissions, which will have very negative effects on balanced human development.
in writing. the european parliament's resolution on the situation in the middle east calls for the eu to take action to help the countries of the region to develop their economic and social development. if there are any doubts about the eu's real aims and ambitions for the enp, they will be easily clarified by reading this report. it is a genuine programme of interference and domination throughout the mediterranean area, the middle east, central asia and eastern europe. the programme sets out the following objectives: 'to encourage the governments of the enp partner countries to engage in political and economic reforms'; their assimilation of the eu's 'common policies'; their 'alignment with the eu's external policy'; and the 'establishment of a free trade area'. the report also calls for 'more joint action between the eu and the us' to 'promote democracy, improve energy security and strengthen regional security in the eu's neighbourhood', a point so elucidating that it was watered down in the plenary vote. but you'd better read it...
in writing. the eu's relations with ukraine fall within the framework of the european neighbourhood policy, which, as the report underlines, aims to support the development of market economies in the eu's neighbouring countries, i.e. capitalism. the report states that the aim is to sign a free trade agreement (fta), i.e. to integrate ukraine into the 'single eu market' by its 'gradual adoption... of the acquis communautaire'. so the report: - i know . 'requests ukraine to pay greater attention to the liberalisation of markets, ensuring the effective completion of the privatisation process, the dismantling of monopolies (public enterprises) and the independence of its central bank; it encourages 'the convergence of standards in the agricultural, industrial and service sectors' by 'compliance with community standards'; - and, in view of ukraine's conditional accession to the 'single economic area' with russia and other republics of the former soviet union, 'reminds that some provisions included in the agreement, if fully implemented, may conflict with the conclusion of an operational lca with the eu'. the report also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's external borders are not blocked. more words for what...
in writing. we consider very worrying and deeply negative some of the developments which 'will in some way shape the eu's humanitarian doctrine in the future', embodied in initiatives such as the so-called 'eu response to situations of fragility in developing countries' or the 'european consensus for development', which are mainly aimed at african countries, but also those in the caribbean and the pacific. the analysis of these initiatives raises the central question of integrating 'development' as one of the external dimensions for the achievement of the strategic objectives of the major powers of the eu (cfsp/esdp), which is to say, the assumption of 'development' as an instrument of interference and domination in a strategy which, significantly, does not exclude 'coercive military intervention'. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. there is no doubt that solidarity with many countries which have inherited disastrous colonial conditions and are victims of decades of interference is urgently needed, but such solidarity must - if it is to be effective - be based on respect for the principles of national sovereignty and independence and on an effective and genuine policy of cooperation and development aid.
in writing. we voted in favour of this report because it contains important data on the social situation: 78 million european citizens continue to live in poverty, 8% of the eu population are working poor and the gap between rich and poor is widening in many eu member states. it also includes some positive recommendations, such as the need to set a decent minimum wage, the defence of unemployment benefits and support for the disabled, although it does not go to the heart of the causes of the social situation and does not advocate a break with neoliberal policies, as we propose. it is therefore very conservative in its demands for the political changes that are required. unfortunately, it only partially incorporated the proposals in my opinion adopted in the committee on women's rights and gender equality, in which i stress the call for the community institutions and the member states to give top priority to social inclusion and women's rights and to change their policies accordingly, including income-sharing policy.
in writing. social policy is largely a member state competence and i am therefore in favour of promoting the open method of coordination and sharing best practice in the fight against social exclusion. social security systems should be based on principles which motivate their beneficiaries to seek employment opportunities and which do not favour a perverse incentive to any form of inactivity. the low level of education of the population and the high rates of early school leaving deserve careful consideration, since it is the least qualified individuals who are most vulnerable to processes of social exclusion. this situation is particularly worrying in my country, portugal, where in 2005 more than 39% of the young population (aged 18-24) had completed only lower secondary education. this trend must be reversed and citizens must be equipped with the skills needed to successfully enter the labour market. because this proposal goes against this set of ideas i voted for it.

the report under discussion, whose rapporteur i welcome, rightly points out that the tourism sector is at the crossroads of many european union policies, which has a considerable impact on growth and employment, as well as on territorial and social cohesion. it is therefore essential to put into practice some of the aspects of its policy, in line with the definition of the guiding principles set out in parliament's resolution of 8 september 2005, for which i was the rapporteur. the first aspect concerns the simplification and harmonisation of the procedures for applying for tourist visas for entry into the member states, with a view to reducing their costs and facilitating access to the european union for tourists from third countries. we think this is a positive step, but it is necessary to safeguard the security rules required to combat terrorism, organised crime and illegal immigration. we also note the need to improve the system for collecting statistical information, including the satellite accounts, since only with up-to-date and reliable data is it possible for public authorities and industry to take the most strategically appropriate decisions that will enable europe to maintain its current leading position. a further word on the more controversial question of possible harmonization of quality standards for tourist accommodation in europe. the multiplicity of hotel rating schemes intersects with the question of protecting the rights and expectations of tourists at the time of their choices. is it possible to establish minimum safety and quality standards in the european union to ensure the reliability and transparency of the information provided to these consumers? it is certainly desirable, but we think it will only be possible on a voluntary basis and by calling on all those concerned to take part in this task. the commission could play a key role in this, if it so wished. we do not have time to mention other equally important aspects of this report, such as tourism accessible to tourists with reduced mobility, passenger rights, or the external promotion of european destinations and the development of sustainable policies. it is nevertheless sufficiently demonstrated, and i conclude with this, that the european parliament has done its job and we hope that the other public authorities, in partnership with the private sector, will strengthen their spirit of cooperation and respond effectively to the challenges of developing a renewed and sustainable european tourism policy.

in writing. in this european space, it is necessary to ensure that justice does not remain confined to borders that have already disappeared physically between the member states. it is essential to ensure the same treatment for all eu citizens, regardless of the member state of which they are a national or where they reside: a suspect who does not reside in the state where the trial is to be held may not be treated differently from a suspect who resides there. at present, alternative control measures to preventive detention cannot be transposed or transferred to another member state, as there is no mutual recognition of these measures, thus undermining the judicial protection of individual rights itself. i therefore support this proposal for a framework decision on the european judicial review decision in the context of interim proceedings, which should allow for the mutual recognition of pre-trial review measures, allowing the suspect, during the investigation phase, to return to the member state where he is resident. this reduces the scope of detention (especially for minor offences) while encouraging more efficient judicial cooperation.
in writing. as in previous cases, this council framework decision on judicial review in the context of interim proceedings between member states, which the european parliament's report has just approved, is part of the attempt to deepen and complete the 'common european area of justice', following the framework set out in the tampere and hague programmes and the continuation of the 'europe without frontiers' (inward...). the proposal for a framework decision and the report, among other things, advocate the need to extend the application of the european arrest warrant to cover all offences (without setting a threshold). these and other measures are intended to extend the scope of criminal law harmonisation to the different eu member states, taking steps which, by deepening the federalist character of this european union, anticipate and find stronger support in the so-called 'reform' treaty, which withdraws new powers from the states in the area of justice and home affairs.
in writing. the illicit manufacture and trafficking of firearms, their parts and components and ammunition have serious consequences for the security of all eu citizens. the location of firearms is also of the utmost importance in the fight against organised crime. it is essential to put in place the necessary measures to prevent, combat and eradicate this type of crime. according to who data, interpersonal violence and suicide are the third and fourth leading causes of accidents and premature death among 15- to 44-year-olds, with the highest proportion resulting from the use of firearms. the aim of this initiative is to adapt the directive on the control of the acquisition and possession of weapons by establishing common rules allowing controls to be carried out in the member states on the acquisition and possession of firearms and their transfer to another member state. the commission proposal is generally positive but it merely incorporates aspects related to the 2001 un protocol. it is also important to take account of the amendments which appear necessary on the basis of the 2000 commission report.

in writing. the charter of fundamental rights adopted in nice in 2000 is a synthesis of common european values with which all citizens can identify. these values are the result of the rich cultural heritage of the different eu countries, their constitutional traditions and legal rules, and they characterize the union not only as an economic construct but as a community of common values. the european parliament has consistently called for the charter to be given the status of primary law, thereby making it a central reference point for the court of justice and national courts, and giving it a legally binding character. it is with great satisfaction that i finally see this confirmation! at the same time i am pleased to note that the draft reform treaty has preserved the substance of part ii of the treaty establishing a constitution for europe. i regret that this incorporation was made in the form of an annex and not in the body of the treaty itself, as its dignity warranted. and i also regret that the united kingdom and poland have exercised an opt-out on fundamental rights, even though recent statements by the new polish government seem to indicate a different stance and much more in line with the common spirit.

in writing. i voted in favour of the alain lipietz report on trade and climate change because i believe that europe must play a leading role in the world in the fight against climate change and therefore i believe that substantial changes are needed in the european union's trade policy to promote a low-carbon economy. this report highlights the need to develop production, consumption and trade patterns that mitigate climate change and its economic impact. measures are therefore needed, such as encouraging local production as a means of alleviating transport needs and introducing common labelling standards and schemes in the european union to raise consumer awareness of the environmental implications of different products.
in writing. we fully agree with the report when it says that 'the current economic model, which is based on the constant maximisation of consumption, production and trade, is not sustainable, as it implies an ever-increasing demand for resources and transport, as well as an increase in waste and emissions'. or when it is said that the current trading system implies 'a division of labour at a global level which entails a very high volume of transport of products' which could more sustainably be produced locally. however, we cannot fail to stress some negative aspects such as the call for an agreement to be reached in the current context of the wto doha round negotiations on the abolition of tariff and non-tariff barriers to 'green goods and services'. or that, implicitly, agreement is given to the negotiation of free trade agreements and thus contradicts what was said earlier about the current trading system. we also stress very negatively the introduction of the 'polluter pays' principle, preferably through the global extension of the emissions trading system, which we reject because of its consequences.

i am speaking on behalf of the group of the european people's party. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, as the shadow rapporteur for the epp-ed, i have been following the preparation of this report and the negotiations with the commission. this is a very important report for the planning and evaluation of regional and social policies in the various member states, and in this respect the socioeconomic profile of the european population and housing conditions are one of the most decisive aspects in assessing the improvement of living conditions. we think that the commission's approach to the indicative data which enable this type of analysis to be carried out is correct, and we support it. the coverage, quality and reliability of this type of statistical data therefore need to be further improved. however, we believe that this task must always be carried out with a good balance between cost and benefit in relation to the detail of the information to be provided, without also neglecting the privacy of the people. this report will only be useful if it contributes to the increased periodicity, comparability and accuracy of these data at the level of the european union. this requires very particular care to be taken in the provision of data by the member states, which must be consistent, complete and reliable, because only in this way can exercises and analyses be made on
