on behalf of the pse group. the ottawa convention was the result of a global and effective mobilization for a just cause that united and unites governments, public opinion and non-governmental organizations. even some non-parties, and unfortunately there are still 37, are already partially complying with the convention. this instrument thus acts as a barometer measuring the degree of participation of countries in the global community of values. and as the commissioner has already said, it is worth remembering what has already been achieved. in 10 years the ottawa states have destroyed over 41 million mines. in the past year alone, serbia, montenegro, angola, cyprus, cape verde and latvia have fulfilled their obligations and fully disposed of their stockpiles of mines. 38 of the 50 mine producing countries have ceased to do so, including four non-parties: egypt, finland, poland and israel. but the celebration of ten years of the convention's triumphs should also serve to highlight the much that remains to be done. ten of the states parties have not yet completed the destruction of their stockpiles, which amount to 14 million mines. of these 10, two states parties are distinguished by possessing considerable stockpiles of anti-personnel mines and by not providing for any measures to destroy them: ethiopia and iraq. but the overwhelming majority of mines are in the hands of the non-party state. china alone continues to cling to an arsenal of 110 million of these inhuman weapons, while continuing to produce them. more shockingly - perhaps because it is an allied country - with which european armies are fighting side by side in places like afghanistan, the united states of america, another country, another non-party state, not only continues to maintain an arsenal of over 10 million mines, but last year the pentagon asked for new funding for two new types of mines that are incompatible with the convention. let us hope that the efforts of the american congress will bear fruit in once again imposing limits on the generosity of this white house in regard to new war toys. the european union still has some glass roofs, with finland and poland still refusing to ratify the convention. but that should not prevent europe from pursuing the broadest possible interpretation of what constitutes an antipersonnel mine. it is scandalous to see how some in this parliament insist on making distinctions based on the formal military definition of engineering rather than on the nature of the damage it causes. a civilian crippled by the action of an anti-tank mine is not interested in byzantines in terms of technical terminology. colonel gaddafi, on his website and in full-page ads he placed in the portuguese press in the final days of the eu-africa summit, attacked the ottawa convention and defended anti-personnel mines as the weapons of the poor. alongside this criminal madman, some in this house are advocating an importation of the convention which allows rich countries to develop and use more sophisticated versions of mines to satisfy an alleged military need. i would like to conclude, mr president, in the face of these obscene statements: the objective of the european union must be simple: a world free of mines, of all mines and of their civilian victims.
i would also like to begin by congratulating the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteur of the pse on the work they have done, not only as shadow rapporteurs on this report but also on the own-initiative report which preceded this debate. their work well represents the spirit of compromise and the constructive stance of the socialists to find a balanced solution. the long months of debate have shown three things: the high economic and social importance of this sector, which was so badly treated in the past by the common agricultural policy; the inadequacy of the current rules with the current market situation and the changes in consumption patterns; and the need for reforms to respond to these problems. the debate also showed a high degree of consensus on the list of problems affecting the sector. but we have not agreed with the solutions proposed by the commission. the broad commitment found in the committee on agriculture, as well as the proposals from the pse, proposals for detailed amendments to supplement it on the most sensitive issues, such as the liberalization of planting rights, the grubbing up of vineyards, the question of capitalisation and aid for grape must, the maintenance of the alcohol content, which is so important for some prestigious wines, such as port, whose competitiveness must be guaranteed, crisis prevention, promotion, etc., are very revealing of the constructive position of the european parliament. the position of parliament is therefore a good stimulus and a good signal to the council and the commission as to the way forward. the general outline of parliament's position shows that a final solution is possible which will be able to respond to the general problems of the sector as well as to the specific problems of the producing regions. commissioner, as we begin to discuss the health check and, above all, the issue that concerns us, namely the post-2013 agricultural scenario, it is important that this reform be completed quickly. i hope therefore that parliament will be able to inspire the council in the decisions that are required, because parliament's position and the general outline of its recommendations are a good sign for european wine and vineyards.
mr president, we are very critical of the european commission's proposal for a revision of the common organization of the market in wine. apart from grubbing up vineyards, the proposal to liberalize planting rights is particularly serious and we consider that the report adopted by the committee on agriculture does not adequately safeguard this issue. the future of vast regions which constitute wine-producing areas with a designation of origin or a geographical indication, but also those which produce good table wines, is at stake. in defence of traditional vine and wine production, employment and biodiversity, we therefore insist on the defence of planting rights, the maintenance of support for vineyard restructuring, production control and quality control, with particular attention to family farming and cooperative wineries, support for the distillation of alcohol by mouth and the use of grape must produced in the region, but we disagree with support for added sugar.
in writing. we support the application of the principle of subsidiarity, and therefore agree that the community should not encroach on the competence of the member states. this is the case, for example, of services provided locally, which do not involve cross-border activities and therefore do not in principle affect the functioning of the internal market. in the field of indirect taxation, therefore, each state should have complete freedom of action in fixing vat rates. even if the council decides on the definitive arrangements for taxing intra-community transactions, member states should be able to apply reduced rates, or even zero rates, to goods and services corresponding to basic needs such as food and medicines, as well as to services provided locally, including services and supplies of goods related to education, social assistance, social security and culture. and even if the final taxation regime for intra-community transactions is decided by the end of 2010, member states should be able to apply reduced rates of vat in order to strengthen the existence and maintenance of locally provided services and the role they play in the formal economy.
in writing. our abstention in this report takes account of the doubts surrounding the creation of artemis, its operation and its management. the establishment of joint ventures in the framework of public-private partnerships, such as the joint technology initiative for the formation of artemis, expressed in this report, includes the idea of using public capital for private purposes and interests, while the reverse cooperation - financial or knowledge transfer - seems to be absent. the logic of this approach is that there is a clash of objectives, since the pillar of private enterprise is based on the accumulation of profits and the pillar of public service is based on serving the public interest and responding to the aspirations of the population. however, investment in research, particularly in the field of integrated computer systems, is a contribution which we consider essential to the development of technology in europe.
in writing. being a european citizen entails a set of rights, including the right to diplomatic and consular protection. any citizen of the union shall enjoy the protection of the diplomatic and consular authorities of any other member state where his country does not have an embassy or consulate in the territory of a third country. this is all the more relevant when we consider that only three countries - china, russia and the usa - have diplomatic and consular representation from all eu member states. in addition to the fact that the representation of member states in third countries can be very heterogeneous, there are also cases where it is non-existent (e.g. maldives). i support this initiative which aims to help ensure that the provisions of article 20 tec and article 46 tfeu can be effectively translated into practice, laying the foundations for a genuine harmonised fundamental right to diplomatic and consular protection for all citizens of the union, irrespective of their nationality. the creation of a european external action service with its own powers and responsibilities under the lisbon treaty is also welcome. while agreeing that it is essential to promote information for citizens, i support the creation of a single european emergency telephone number to enable european citizens to obtain the information they need, particularly in critical and emergency situations.
in writing. this seventh amending budget for 2007 brings in an additional €4 324.8 million in revenue and a further €1 651.4 million in expenditure, thus enabling the member states to reduce their contributions to the community budget by some €5 976.2 million. while the increase in revenue is largely due to the vat and gni balances, budget under-implementation is largely responsible for the significant reduction in expenditure, with cuts mainly affecting cohesion, fisheries, the environment and agriculture. the late adoption of many structural funds operational programmes for 2007-13 (and others) is the justification put forward by the commission and the council for the non-use of the funds foreseen for 2007. however, these amounts are not transferred to the 2008 budget, thus increasing the funds for these policies. it should be noted that the amounts provided for in the 2008 budget for these headings are even below those agreed in the 2007/2013 multiannual financial framework. the non-execution of these amounts from the community budget deserves the most serious follow-up and concern, given that 2007 is the first year of the new financial framework 2007-2013 and that the n+2 rule for the previous financial framework continues to apply, with the funds to be fully used by 2008.
in writing. i voted in favour of the recommendation for second reading by mrs marie-noëlle lienemann (a6-0389/2007) on the common position adopted by the council with a view to adopting a directive of the european parliament and of the council establishing a framework for community action in the field of marine environment policy (marine strategy framework directive). the compromise reached between the european parliament and the council will enable a framework to be established for the protection and preservation of the marine environment, the prevention of its deterioration and, where possible, the recovery of that environment in areas where it has been affected.
in writing. the recommendation for the second reading of the report establishing a framework for community action in the field of marine environment policy was adopted today. it would be important to have a policy for the marine environment within the framework of the necessary cooperation and coordination between the different countries, safeguarding their full sovereignty over their territory and resources, and taking into account economic, social and environmental aspects. but the central issue is respect for the sovereignty of the member states, in particular their eezs and their capacity to implement autonomous measures in defence of their resources. it is therefore important to bear in mind that there is a clause in the proposed 'reform' treaty which seeks to make the management of marine resources within the framework of the common fisheries policy the exclusive competence of the european union. on the other hand, it is also necessary to take into account that marine pollution and intensive maritime transport have impacts on fishing activity and the protection of marine resources. fishermen are therefore the main stakeholders in the protection and regeneration of the marine environment. the measures to recover resources must therefore include the necessary economic and social compensation measures for the sector and its workers, with adequate funding.
in writing. i voted in favour of the recommendation for second reading by mr holger krahmer (a6-0398/2007) on the common position adopted by the council with a view to adopting a european parliament and council directive on ambient air quality and cleaner air in europe, as i consider that the text negotiated between the ep and the council is overall positive, both from the point of view of the protection of public health and from the point of view of environmental protection. in europe, 360,000 people die ten years earlier as a result of air pollution. studies show that the effects of air pollution affect children's health in particular, so air quality plans should be able to include specific measures to protect sensitive groups of the population, such as children.
in writing. pollution of the natural resource 'air' is becoming more and more important, especially in the regions and urban centres of the european union countries where the population density is higher. air pollution is harmful to human health, respiratory and cardiovascular diseases and ecosystems. we know that children, the elderly and people who live in the most crowded and congested urban centres, or who live near major traffic lanes, are particularly vulnerable. the european parliament today expressed its position on the council's common position on ambient air quality and cleaner air in europe at second reading. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all transport services, including the carriage of goods by road. the european parliament, for its part, wants to safeguard three main objectives of its position: the setting of more ambitious target values and limit values; greater flexibility in adopting more stringent measures at source and the setting of long-term objectives.
in writing. the report aims to improve the interoperability of the rail system in the community, i.e. to improve the possibility and the permission of a train from one member state to another. apart from other important aspects of this measure, including technical aspects, the directive is intended to avoid any obstacle to the movement of 'community trains'. it is important to remember that this report is part of the strategy for the liberalisation (and privatisation) of rail transport at eu level. as we have stressed in other community legislative initiatives on transport, here too the first objective is to remove any obstacle to the liberalization of international rail transport, in this case by eliminating, through its harmonization, any differentiating standards or requirements applied to rolling stock in each country. finally, it should be stressed that the harmonization and simplification of national authorization procedures and the principle of mutual recognition should never call into question more appropriate standards already established at the level of each member state, nor alienate the prerogative of each member state to establish them.
in writing. the report we are voting on today on the interoperability of the community rail system is of the utmost importance as an incentive for investment in rail transport and a key element in the creation of genuine freedom of movement within the european territory. the proposed measures to facilitate the interoperability of locomotives in the community are measures we have all been waiting for. to create a european transport area without frontiers and which is truly conducive to the free movement of people and goods, we must create the conditions necessary for a journey from lisbon to helsinki to be feasible in all modes of transport. rail transport must be able to develop as a full partner in achieving the objectives of the common transport policy. we must not forget that this is a safe, environmentally friendly means of transport that allows the transport of large quantities of goods and passengers. it is a mode of transport that is at the forefront of combating the negative effects of air pollution, road hazards and congestion itself. i therefore voted in favour of mr ortuondo larrea's report.
in writing. we do not share the view expressed in the report that production aid should be phased out in favour of a single payment scheme for producers based on their production history, with producers being obliged to fulfil the objectives of the cross-compliance system. this system has led to the abandonment of production by many small and mediumsized farmers and family farming and the abandonment of rural areas, to losses of biodiversity and to a further detachment from the objective of food sovereignty in some member states, notably in portugal. however, we agree that the agricultural sector needs more information in order to adapt to the rules of cross-compliance. we also believe that it is essential to provide adequate training to the people who carry out inspections of farmers' activities and that inspectors should have the ability to take into account unforeseen and non-seasonal factors that compromise full compliance with the requirements through no fault of the farmer. it is necessary to take account of the importance of agricultural activity, a genuine public service that farmers provide to society, and therefore support measures, including the timely payment of aid, should be maintained.
i congratulate the portuguese presidency on this report, which describes in detail the meritorious work done, of which i would highlight the moratorium on the death penalty. but what is lacking is critical analysis and, above all, self-criticism. i am an example of the european council's failure to respond to the recommendations of this parliament and senator dick marty on the so-called cia flights. even in the face of evidence that the territory and agents of several member states are involved in the kidnapping and torture of terrorism suspects, thus evading justice, the european council and the portuguese presidency in particular have done nothing to date to fully clarify what has happened, to establish responsibility and to prevent such criminal behaviour from continuing. despite admissions and investigations in the united states, european governments persist in the ostrich policy, thus offending essential european values and interests and seriously compromising europe's credibility in promoting human rights universally.
the debate is closed.
the following are the statements by the council and the commission on the second eu-africa summit held in lisbon on 8 and 9 december 2007.
mr president, we will only know if the eu-africa summit was worthwhile when the next one is held in 2010 and whether the topics discussed there will be new or the same as today. that will be the criterion and the moment to evaluate the results of what happened this weekend in lisbon. but in the meantime, it is possible to take stock. this summit was presented as one of dialogue, of genuine bilateral partnership, of shared responsibility, and this will is meritorious. in the new relationship between europeans and africans, there can be no one leader, they are responsible for their own destiny, and it is up to us, as europe's neighbours, to be generous and consistent in our aid to their development. if by 2010 we are on track to meet the millennium development goals and there is less death, less hunger, more democracy, more respect for human rights, more fair trade and more growth and development, this summit will have been a success. if the same dictators remain in power and the same deals continue to be made, bringing many benefits to very few, then it will have been sadly a missed opportunity.
this summit was held because the portuguese presidency insisted and the african union agreed. it has lost those in europe who wanted to diminish it on the pretext of robert mugabe's presence in lisbon. but anyone who receives the saudi king in london with pomp and circumstance has little authority to speak on human rights. in parallel with the summit, numerous civic actions denounced this duplicity between words and deeds, the duplicity of those who were absent, but also of those who were there. in portugal, the summit allowed africa and its problems to be discussed, and that is the only reason why it was worthwhile. but anyone who hears the presidency and the commission will think that this was a genuine historical event, a moment in which there is a before and an after, and there is an exaggerated manifesto, even for portuguese women of a portuguese-tropical provincialism, just read the european press. progress has been made and the main thing is that african countries have made their own agenda. but beyond that, between the vanity of words and the meagerness of results, the gulf persists. the summit went better than cairo. it wasn't hard! it is difficult to respond in solidarity when one starts with the idea fixed in the economic partnership agreements.
the eu-africa summit was made possible by the diplomatic and political persistence of the portuguese presidency. europe has echoed the success, but it is doubtful that africa will, especially the men and women who are fighting oppressive and kleptocratic regimes. they know that most of their representatives are as much about respecting what they committed themselves to at the summit as legitimacy: none. the portuguese presidency has the task of testing the joint strategy and the action plan that have been approved. and since the most serious tragedies facing africa in darfur and somalia were only superficially evoked at the summit, it is time to move on to practical measures. when will the european forces advance into chad, promised for last summer? when will the eu take strong action against the sudanese regime which is obstructing the hybrid force mandated by the security council to protect the civilian population in darfur? when will the security council decide to send troops or other european contributions to bring the invading ethiopian troops out of somalia? the organisation of summits does not justify leaving behind such urgent issues, which call into question the credibility of the eu in the eyes of millions of africans and europeans. we must show that the protection of lives in sudan, somalia, eastern congo and other countries in africa is more important than the signing of contracts in the tents of the criminal gaddafi.
in writing. while it is too early to assess the real scope of the eu-africa summit decisions, and despite contradictions, the rejection of eu free trade agreements (so-called 'economic partnership agreements') by african countries is worth noting. ironically, the rejection - despite all the unacceptable pressure and blackmail from the eu - of these so-called 'economic partnership agreements' by african countries is a real example of what the eu's much-vaunted 'good governance' should be. that is, the assumption and defence by a state of control of its economy. we believe that effective development cooperation requires respect for national sovereignty, political and economic independence, the right of each people to decide its present and future, to define and build its state and its development project. such cooperation in solidarity is incompatible with the more or less concealed aims and visions of interference, exploitation and plunder of resources and political-economic domination. it was said that the eu-africa summit had turned a 'new page'. we will continue to ensure that the eu and its large transnational corporations do not continue to (re) write the neocolonialist ambitions of the eu.
mr president of the council, mr president of the commission, ladies and gentlemen, the portuguese presidency is coming to an end and can already present a series of appreciable successes. i am not one of those who overemphasize the diplomatic initiatives related to the summits with brazil and africa, among others, only time will tell if they translate into concrete measures or if they are just big events with media visibility. but i would like to emphasize the structural measures which have been taken for the good of europe during these six months. let me highlight three: the end of the institutional crisis with the adoption of the treaty of lisbon, which will be signed tomorrow; the proclamation of the european charter of fundamental rights, which will now be binding; the historic enlargement of the schengen area, with the integration of nine new member states and almost four million square kilometres; the strategic feasibility and the important galileo programme, which some people would prefer not to have, leaving the united states, russia and china alone. i would also like to highlight the fruitful legislative work in collaboration with the european parliament and the excellent understanding with the commission, chaired by mr barroso. interinstitutional cooperation has worked and produced good results. i wish you, mr president of the council, the best of luck for the council meeting on 14 december. we are still waiting for important decisions, both in the field of foreign policy, with particular emphasis on kosovo, and in the european response to the challenges of globalisation. i would like to congratulate the portuguese presidency in particular on the inclusion of the issue of european immigration policy in the council's agenda, where president barroso will be able to highlight the timely initiatives of the european commission in this regard. there are problems and challenges which clearly go beyond the dimension of each member state and call for a common approach, which is particularly obvious, as has been said, in an area without internal borders. mr president, may i conclude with a national reference. portugal has always done its best to serve the common interest when it held the presidency of the council. this was the case in 1992 with prime minister cavaco silva, then minister for foreign affairs and now mep joão de deus pinheiro, it was the case in 2000 with prime minister antónio guterres, and it is the case today with the third portuguese presidency of the council of the union. i would like to emphasize, mr secretary of state, your personal commitment, that of minister luís amado and prime minister socrates, but also that of all those who have actively contributed to the success of the presidency here in brussels and in lisbon. i would like to highlight the work of reper, mentioning the talent of ambassador mendonça e moura and thanking dr alexandre leitão for his effective liaison with the european parliament.
we are witnessing yet another repetition of the fundamental lines of neoliberal policy, which were deepened during the portuguese presidency. the signing of the treaty of lisbon tomorrow, which will take up the essence of the so-called 'european constitution', is undoubtedly the most serious issue representing a qualitative leap in this neoliberal integration which is aggravating social problems and inequalities. instead of the answers to improve working conditions, they are betting on flexicurity to intensify the precariousness of work. instead of responses to improve living conditions and tackle poverty, which affects more than 80 million people, they present an even more neoliberal version of the lisbon strategy to deepen liberalizations and privatizations of public services. as was the case on 18 october with the demonstration in lisbon, the struggle of the workers and the people will continue against this treaty and these policies and for the demand for binding referendums on the treaty after duly pluralistic debates.
tomorrow, the prime ministers and heads of state will sign their treaty in lisbon. the day after tomorrow, they'll be calling for ratification. the change is not in the text, which replicates the constitution rejected by the french and dutch. the change is in the method. now they want quick ratification without a referendum. a few days ago, mr zappatero expressed in this very room his wish that the citizens of the various states should be able to vote on the treaty which will regulate our collective future on the same day. at friday's summit the governments will have the opportunity to refute the suspicion that each of them is being held responsible for wanting the new treaty to be approved at the expense of the people. take zappatero's suggestion with both hands. mark the day. today the treaty of lisbon is yours alone. it will never be the europeans' as long as its viability depends on the non-referendum. the european parliament has a duty to ensure that the european parliament is represented in the council of ministers.
mr president, mr president-in-office, the legacy of the portuguese presidency is very stimulating, but it is also very responsible. it is this political legacy that this week's summit should consolidate and develop. the signing of the treaty of lisbon tomorrow, the solemn ratification of the charter of fundamental rights by the three institutions of the european union in a few moments, the opening of a strategic partnership with brazil without undermining the european union's special relations with mercosur, the relaunch of the periodic strategic summits with the african continent, and the push for the lisbon strategy and so many other decisive points for the future of europe are remarkable achievements, but they will only serve a purpose if the policies are successful and the objectives are achieved, which are indispensable to making europe stronger, more cohesive, more united and more decisive for world stability. this is the responsibility which the member states, the european council, the commission and this parliament have inherited from the portuguese presidency. but it is also the stimulus that will enable us all to emerge from the institutional crisis that has limited europe and its integration process over the last two years. i would like to repeat what many have already said: my sincere congratulations to the portuguese presidency, but also my wish that the next slovenian presidency will be able to continue along these lines and develop what has been achieved. the next brussels summit should have as its sole objective the creation of the political conditions for this to happen.
the rapporteur. i should like to begin this short speech by welcoming the decision of the committee on fisheries of the european parliament to draw up an own-initiative report on the common organization of the market in fishery and aquaculture products. it is well known and acknowledged that the cmo has so far failed to achieve the objectives for which it was set up, namely to ensure the stability of the fisheries markets and a fair income for producers. we therefore welcome the european commission's decision, albeit belatedly, to carry out a thorough assessment of the current cfp and call on it to undertake its urgent review in order to increase its contribution to ensuring the sector's income, the stability of the markets, the improvement of the marketing of fishery products and the increase of their added value, in particular by significantly strengthening its financial means. although some of our initial proposals did not achieve the necessary consensus in the committee on fisheries, we believe that the report now before us contains measures which should be taken into account, such as: assessing whether the current intervention mechanisms are the most appropriate and have the necessary flexibility to meet the needs of the different member states; the compensatory allowance for sardines, as is already the case for tuna; the need for the structural funds to contribute to the modernisation and creation of support infrastructures for producers in production-marketing; effective support for the establishment and operation of producer organisations, particularly in small-scale coastal and artisanal fisheries; the application of the same standards and requirements to fishery products imported and marketed on the internal market as those applied to community fishery products. these are issues which, although they may not be of significance to some members, are very important to fishermen.
in writing. the aviation agreement with morocco is the second agreement on the so-called 'common european airspace' and the first concluded in this context with a country outside the european continent. as a political note, we regret that this agreement - as was unacceptably the case with fisheries - does not explicitly clarify 'that territory under the jurisdiction of the kingdom of morocco is understood to be territory under moroccan sovereignty in accordance with international law', thus safeguarding respect for international law and the legitimate and inalienable rights of the moroccan people. the sovereignty of morocco over the territory of western sahara is not legally recognized by international law, as the international court of justice in the hague pointed out in october 1975. morocco, which illegally occupies the territory of western sahara, has consequently no sovereignty or jurisdiction over that territory. the agreement is based almost exclusively on two objectives which we oppose: the opening up of markets and regulatory harmonization to promote competition in air transport.
in writing. in june and july the commission received the third and fourth applications for the mobilisation of this fund. the applications concern two german and one finnish companies, all in the telecommunications sector, specifically in the manufacture of mobile phones. both are linked to the relocation of production to third countries, which has led to the dismissal of 4211 workers. so far, in addition to these two applications and the two french applications already approved, the commission has received further applications from italy, malta, spain and portugal. applications to be approved early next year. as we have said, the existence of this fund cannot serve as a cushion for the unacceptable socioeconomic costs of relocating companies and their redundancies. we insist on the creation of a regulatory framework to prevent and penalize the relocation of companies. we believe that public aid to enterprises should be conditional on long-term commitments by them to regional development and employment and that no aid should be granted which could be used to promote relocations. it is also essential to strengthen the role of employee representatives on company boards and in the taking of management decisions of a structural nature.
in writing. the mobilisation of the flexibility instrument, together with the amendment to the interinstitutional agreement, is an integral part of the proposal for the community budget for 2008. in addition to the correction of eur 1 600 million in the multiannual financial framework, the mobilisation of the flexibility instrument is intended to supplement the financing of the european programmes for the global satellite navigation system (egnos-galileu) by some eur 200 million. the eu's common foreign and security policy (cfsp) is also financed by the mobilisation of the flexibility instrument with a further eur 70 million. the rapporteur stresses that 'external actions in general, and the cfsp in particular, are not sufficiently covered in the long term in the light of the requirements now identified'. it is clarified that among the 'identified requirements' is the strengthening of eu 'missions' in kosovo and afghanistan. this is the impetus for the eu's increasing military interference and interventionism, supporting nato operations both in the balkans - as exemplified by the preparations to support the 'unilateral declaration of independence of kosovo', in violation of international law - and in central asia, in particular by financing these 'missions' from the community budget. militaristic policies and objectives with which we clearly disagree.
in writing. simplification of european legislation on information and promotion measures for agricultural products on the internal market and in third countries is very important for the development of a simple and easily managed cap. i welcome the commission's proposal to improve the system, in particular the consolidation of regulations which involves the merging of the two regulations on the internal market and third countries. i am voting in favour of the golik report, emphasizing its reference to the need to pay more attention to the issues of information and promotion in the wto negotiations.
in writing. the common organisation of the market in fishery and aquaculture products (cmo), one of the four pillars of the common fisheries policy, should be radically reorganised. priorities include the review of aspects related to consumer information on fishery products and a fairer distribution of the added value of fish throughout the marketing process (with particular emphasis on the first sale). the eu must also find solutions to the 'social dumping' which is now taking place in some third countries and which is taking away the competitive power of our fisheries products. the national interests are safeguarded in this report and it deserves my vote in favour.
in writing. we welcome the adoption of the report on the common fisheries policy, which sends a clear signal to the european commission that the common fisheries policy needs to be revised urgently and with ambition, so that it can make a greater contribution to ensuring the profitability of the sector, improving the marketing of fisheries products and increasing their added value, in particular by significantly increasing its financial resources. given that the cmo should effectively meet the objectives for which it was set up and that the uncertainty of income in the fisheries sector is largely due to the way in which the sector is marketed, the way in which prices are formed at first sale and the irregular characteristics of this activity, we regret that the committee on fisheries has rejected our proposals which really went to the heart of the matter, including: - the introduction of maximum profit rates; - the need for public aid and the creation of effective mechanisms for intervention in the market; - the consideration of production costs in the definition of guide prices; - the introduction of financial compensation for the temporary voluntary reduction of the catch of fish or of the fishing effort. we shall, however, continue to intervene in defence of these just measures.
in writing. as we have emphasized, national authorities have long complied with and enforced the requirements in force in the field of civil aviation resulting from international agreements. cooperation between eu member states and between them and other countries is already a reality and could even be further encouraged and developed, but ensuring respect for each country's sovereignty, for workers and their rights (in particular, ensuring social harmonisation by applying the most favourable conditions) and for the rights of users. however, the competences of each member state in the field of civil aviation have been gradually transferred to the eu, a process all the more negative when it is done in a framework where its limits are not clearly defined. the creation of the european aviation safety agency is essentially another 'breakthrough' in this direction. it should be stressed that this agency will be responsible for the tasks currently assigned to each national authority. the main aim of this measure is to achieve the so-called 'single european sky' and to liberalise air transport and air navigation at eu level. liberalisation which, in the name of financial profitability, calls into question labour rights, the quality of services and safety levels.
in writing. as with most regulations in this area, the specific objectives of this report are based on the harmonisation of the legislative and administrative provisions of the member states to promote the development of the european internal market, in this case with regard to nutrition and health claims on food. the proposal consists of two amendments to regulation (ec) no 1924/2006 of the european parliament and of the council on nutrition and health claims made on foods and aims to provide for an appropriate transitional period for health claims made on children's development and health. nutrition claims used in a member state before 1 january 2006 in accordance with the national provisions applicable to them, which are not listed in the annex to regulation (ec) no 1924/2006, may continue to be used for a period of three years after the entry into force of that regulation. health claims not related to children's development and health also benefit from transitional measures as described in article 28 (5) and (6) of the regulation. they now provide for similar transitional measures for claims relating to children's development and health.
in writing. this report contains some amendments to the proposal for a directive aimed at liberalizing the secondary market in spare parts, applying to the automobile industry, the mechanical industry and the production of capital goods and consumer goods. the commission proposal defends unprotected markets whereas this report advocates a five-year transitional period for countries with market protection, such as portugal. we know that on the one hand the protected market leads to a monopoly by large companies on the trade in spare parts, since on the protected markets the consumer has to buy any broken or damaged part from the producer of origin. the argument is that the design of the article cannot be changed, the best known example being the automobile industry, although this proposal for a directive also applies to other industries. but there are practical cases where the replacement of a single part requires a whole assembly, with the inherent costs to the consumer. however, on the other hand, in portugal there are factories, particularly those linked to the automobile sector, which continue to operate because of the manufacture of such spare parts by large brands and for which the 'liberalisation' of the market could cause serious problems.
in writing. we voted against this report because it does not significantly change the most important aspects of the european commission's bad proposal for the wine and wine sector. as we have always said, we disagree with this liberal position, which seeks to move towards the dismantling of the common organization of the market in wine, albeit with contradictions, which the european parliament itself deepens by allowing the addition of sugar, including increasing the possible graduation in relation to values still in force. but one of the most serious aspects is the opening it leaves to the hypothesis of the liberalisation of planting rights from 2013, although the report acknowledges that this measure will only serve the concentration of production in the hands of large wine companies that already benefit from large public support and other privileges. we also regret that the proposals we made to maintain planting rights, to support the restructuring of vineyards, especially family farming, small and medium-sized winegrowers and cooperative wineries, were not adopted, although we note positively the approval of some proposals, in particular the proposal which advocates the distillation of alcohol by mouth.
in writing. although i agree with the need to reform the common organisation of the market in wine and support the european commission's proposal in general terms, i believe that the castiglione report has made an important contribution by proposing some amendments which substantially improve the commission's document. i would like to highlight, among other positive aspects, the introduction of the possibility of continuing to support the distillation of alcohol by mouth. i voted in favour of amendments nos 33 and 223 because i believe that the liberalisation of the sector should not be abrupt and i rejected amendments nos 314, 347, 293 and 217 because i do not agree with the introduction of the possibility of continuing to enrich with sugar, a practice which can cause imbalances between producers, and i therefore support the original text of the european commission.
in writing. although this resolution contains criticisms, albeit mild ones, of the violations of human rights committed in the name of the so-called 'fight against terrorism' - which we have clearly and firmly denounced from the outset - it does not depart from this, nor does it dismantle it, when international law is disregarded in its name and state terrorism is practised. yes, there is certainly a need to criticise the violation of the right to a fair trial and data protection, the lack of transparency and democratic control, the refusal of the council to respond to 'allegations of abuse of power under the pretext of the fight against terrorism, in particular with regard to extraordinary renditions by the cia and secret detention centres'. however, we cannot accept that, under the guise of the so-called 'fight against terrorism', we should 'rejoice greatly at the adoption of the new reform treaty' and urge 'the member states to ratify it'; the european union is a major player in the world economy, and it is a major player in the world economy. the commission has also proposed that the powers of europol be strengthened and that it be given 'a competence of its own to conduct investigations'.
in writing. we voted against this resolution because the proposals in which we expressed our deep concern about the acceleration of the process of liberalization and deregulation in many sectors, which is endangering employment, the quality of services provided and the future of public services in the eu, were not accepted. what remains is a prejudice against the state as a provider of services of general interest, insisting on liberalisation. monetary and fiscal policy in the eu has also been restrictive, with price stability and fiscal consolidation as the overriding objective, in line with the stability and growth pact, although it is known that the process of nominal convergence has had a negative impact on economic growth and employment, economic and social cohesion, real convergence between eu member states and public investment. it also insists on the neoliberal lisbon strategy, which has been the main instrument used in the eu to promote the liberalisation and privatisation of public services and facilities, the flexibility and adaptability of labour markets, wage moderation and the opening up to private interests of the bulk of social security provisions, including reforms and health.
in writing. among the many aspects that would warrant a critical comment on this subject, i would like to focus on one of the priorities for 2008, which the president of the commission has identified as one of the most significant: the ratification of the proposed treaty on european union. the majority of meps 'welcomed the commission's commitment to supporting the ratification of the reform treaty', 'urged the commission to ... step up its efforts to develop a more efficient communication policy in order to achieve a better understanding of eu action by citizens ... and to prepare for the ratification of the reform treaty and the european elections in 2009' and 'requested the commission to clearly specify how it intends to implement the content of the priorities ... in particular as regards the reform treaty'. in view of the unacceptable role played by the commission in the referenda on the so-called 'european constitution' held in 2005, these intentions, long proclaimed and now reaffirmed, will, if implemented, represent a genuine interference in the ratification processes that will be the responsibility of each member state. what a contradiction from the president of the commission who, when asked about the ratification process, replies that it is up to each member state to decide, but who points out that one of his priorities is precisely to interfere in that decision!
in writing. since it was not possible to secure private funding to complete the funding of the galileo project as originally planned, the european union "decided" that it would be secured only with public capital, namely from the community budget. this is the reason for the amendment of the interinstitutional agreement (ia) - which established the multiannual financial framework for 2007-2013 - which increases the ceilings of commitment appropriations under subheading 1a (competitiveness and growth) for the years 2008 to 2013 by a total amount of eur 1.600 billion, in current prices, at the expense of under-budgeting and under-implementation of appropriations under heading 2 (management and preservation of natural resources, i.e. agriculture, fisheries and environment) in 2007. with this revision of the iia and the mobilisation of the flexibility instrument, the eu is ensuring the implementation of this major 'priority' by securing its financing. it is also unclear whether, once the galileo project has been realised - and, it should be noted, with public funding - it will not be subsequently 'offered' to private capital, for example, through some kind of public-private partnership, with the public bearing the costs and the profits going to private capital.
in writing. if there were any doubts about the eu's real intentions regarding the free trade agreements it intends to establish with the acp countries (africa, caribbean and pacific), the so-called 'economic partnership agreements' (epas) - which were so clearly shown at the recent eu-africa summit by the refusal of african countries to sign them - the reading of the resolution now adopted would suffice to clarify them. however, joão cravinho, portugal's secretary of state for foreign affairs and cooperation, as president of the council, had already done so at the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly in kigali on 21 november. although forced to back down (for the time being), the eu is seeking to bypass resistance by moving forward with a "two-stage negotiating approach" to the epas, "starting with trade in goods" and then "incorporating other areas such as services and investment", while waving millions and millions of euros with which it intends to mortgage the sovereignty and independence (economic, then political) of the acp countries. this is the meaning of the decision of the general affairs and external affairs council of 17 november 2007. the majority of the ep applauds and supports it. we, for our part, denounce and oppose these intentions and policies by which the eu is seeking to economically re-colonize the acp countries.
at the summit, europe spoke out about how china is perverting wto rules, violating labour rights, exporting products harmful to health, pirating technology and hindering european access to the chinese market. the chinese leaders were not used to hearing the eu speak so frankly and retaliated by withholding the joint statement for a few days, but the european leadership unfortunately did not hold the balance, not only made unacceptable concessions on the taiwan referendum, which does not contradict the "one china policy", but also refrained from confronting beijing with serious human rights problems. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a fire. the death penalty, the release of prisoners since the tiananmen massacre, are among the reasons why this parliament supports the maintenance of the arms embargo on china. arbitrary arrests and trials, corruption and forced evictions, persecution and repression of journalists and internet users, repression of tibetans and minorities, responsibility for the tragedies in darfur and burma. none of these fundamental issues were on the agenda of the summit. of course, it is not just the eu that has to hold beijing to account for hosting the 2008 olympic games. if the international olympic committee is measuring air quality, why is beijing not measuring its respect for the olympic ethic vis-à-vis its citizens and foreigners? no one, least of all the council and the eu commission, can continue to play second fiddle to the struggle for freedoms and human rights in china. that's a marathon that the 2008 olympic framework will only encourage. it affects not only millions and millions of chinese, but it will have consequences for all of humanity.
on september 6, two dozen bells in the jewish cemetery of lisbon and swastikas inscribed on the tombstones were vandalized. the two men responsible have been arrested. they are members of the national front, a portuguese skinhead far-right organisation which declares itself to be in favour of racial warfare and violent actions for the supremacy of the white race. this and other cases, including the wave of anti-muslim sentiment in several european countries and the racist violence that has recently struck the roma community in italy, demonstrate that xenophobia and violent racism are among us and that we cannot afford to minimize them. in the portuguese case, the initial temptation of the authorities was to devalue the case and declare anti-semitism as contrary to the supposedly tolerant nature of portuguese society. but the presence of the ministers of justice and the interior in the jewish cemetery for the ceremony of cleansing the fields and the visibility that this demonstration of solidarity had in the portuguese media serve as a lesson for other cases in portugal and beyond. extremism in europe can only be effectively combated if political representatives and the media take their responsibilities by giving visibility to this type of crime and identifying it as a direct attack on the essence of democracy, europe and humanity.
we appreciate the fact that this debate has taken place and that my group has made a major contribution to it. this is a debate which we want to help defend employment and activity in the textile and clothing sector, a sector which is strategic for the european union and which has been so unprotected and undervalued. as for the questions to the commission, we have nothing further to add, they have been put. as regards the joint motion for a resolution which is to be adopted by the european parliament today, we would like to stress that, although it contains a number of points which, if implemented, could defend and enhance the textile and clothing sector in the european union, others must merit our reservations. just three examples: the so-called globalisation adjustment fund should not be used as a temporary cushion for the unacceptable social and economic costs of closing down and relocating businesses, with the consequent destruction of jobs. in other words, we must look at the causes and not the effects. the current liberalization policies must be reversed and financial resources made available which make an effective contribution to the protection of employment, to the modernization of the sector and to the promotion of the establishment of other industrial sectors, including those linked to textiles and clothing, which enable industrial diversification in the regions where it is currently concentrated. it will also make little sense to urge the european union to encourage others to review their monetary policies if the european union does not first and critically reassess the policy of a strong euro and its impact on the exports of some european union countries. it is equally pointless to call for trade defence measures against china when at the same time one supports the establishment of a euro-mediterranean free trade area. it is not appropriate for this speech to recapitulate our proposals for textiles and clothing in the european union. they are expressed in our motion for a resolution. we would like to refer to some of the amendments we have tabled to the joint resolution. the commission is also proposing that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling, presentation and advertising of foodstuffs for sale to the ultimate consumer. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. the commission's proposals express concern about the commission's intention to review trade defence instruments, and we believe that it is in the interests of companies to relocate their production to countries where there are fewer low-wage workers and where low social and environmental standards are applied. proposals for a community programme to support textiles and clothing, particularly in the less-favoured regions which are currently dependent on this sector, and for support for small and mediumsized enterprises. proposals stressing the need to create a regulatory framework to penalise relocations, making the granting of public aid to enterprises conditional on long-term commitments in terms of regional development and employment, including the reimbursement of aid in the event of non-compliance. finally, proposals calling for the strengthening of the power of employee representatives on company boards and in the taking of management decisions of a structural nature. proposals which we hope will have the support of the european parliament.
globalisation has the effect in europe of producing firms losing out and technology exporting firms gaining. all this is clearly reflected in the internal cohesion. in the case of the textile industry, the small and medium-sized size of much of the sector's business fabric is a disadvantage in a market that represents 6% of all world trade and an estimated turnover of €566 billion. and many producing regions are suffering the consequences of economic restructuring processes, making it difficult for the sector to be sustainable. european production is forced to compete with those of countries which artificially devalue their currency, do not respect the rules of environmental protection or bear the costs of it, frequently violate intellectual property rights and, what is even more serious, in the social and labour field, in addition to having much lower wage costs, do not apply measures for the protection of workers as strict as the european ones. this makes it all the more urgent that the wto rules be respected and that the commission be able to monitor imports, and not allow, as has already happened, an artificial sponge to be passed over the excesses that have in fact occurred with china in relation to the entry of textile products. the commission should take all measures to safeguard the interests of the union, including, if necessary, the imposition of quotas on china, possible by the end of 2008, within the wto legal framework and also the requirement of full compliance with the fair-play rules. european producers lack incentives for research and development and the qualification of the workforce, good access to external markets and effective control of counterfeiting. intellectual property is the basis of the surplus value of the sector and must be defended at all costs to encourage high value-added production. finally, mr president, commissioner, consumer safety must not be forgotten. it is the commission's responsibility to prevent any product which is harmful to the safety of our families from entering the homes of citizens.
in writing. the agreement reached between the commission, the council and parliament on the 2008 community budget exposes the true weight of the so-called 'big countries' and 'rich countries' by responding to their demand to limit the ceiling of the community budget as much as possible. despite all efforts to downplay this fact, the truth is that both the proposals for the community budget from the commission, the council and the ep, and now this agreement, fall short of what is envisaged in the 2007/2013 financial framework for 2008. in fact, as happened last year and in the previous financial framework 2000/2006. the reality is that the current community budget for 2008 represents a reduction of more than eur 9 billion in payments compared to what was agreed in the 2008 financial framework - that is, in terms of payments, the community budget is reduced from 1.04% to 0.96% of community gni. on the other hand, the community budget has progressively been clarifying its priorities by financing the eu's neoliberal, federalist and militarist policies. therefore, we reject this agreement.

in writing. for nearly 50 years, the council of europe has been developing a system of standards, legal and judicial instruments for the protection and promotion of fundamental rights, and has become a reference in the field of human rights, the rule of law and democracy in europe. the fundamental rights agency, which is the legal successor of the european monitoring centre on racism and xenophobia, should contribute to increasing the coherence and cohesion of the european union's fundamental rights policy. since the two institutions share the same objective (the strengthening of the protection of fundamental rights), close cooperation between them is essential. this agreement aims to ensure the complementarity and added value of its activities and to avoid duplication with the activities carried out by the council of europe, as provided for in article 9 of the regulation establishing the eu agency for fundamental rights. i support the conclusion of this agreement in a spirit of cooperation, transparency and complementarity, in particular by establishing a framework for cooperation between the two, where regular contacts and meetings, an exchange of information and coordination of activities should take place, avoiding duplication and ensuring the best possible use of resources.

in writing. increasing mobility within the eu, combined with the increasing number of separating couples, has led to an increase in cross-border maintenance litigation. the current procedures for obtaining food credits tend to be too long and complicated and in many cases impossible to achieve results. in the meantime, the creditors, the vast majority of whom are children, are living in great economic difficulty and in many cases do not even have the means to survive. this initiative is therefore of the utmost importance, since it should facilitate the functioning of the internal market and freedom of movement by removing the obstacles created by the discrepancies between member states in the implementation of food obligations. it should ensure that those decisions are recognised and enforced throughout the union as quickly and effectively as possible and at the lowest possible cost. it will simplify the lives of citizens, while at the same time it should have positive social effects by allowing maintenance creditors residing in another member state to make it easier to apply for the recovery of maintenance claims before the competent court and, once the decision has been given, to have it recognised in all member states without further formalities.
